invite:0.en: The map room smelled of old paper and warm lamp-oil. Old Helm spread a faded chart across the low table and looked up at me with a slow smile. 'We don't often *invite* newcomers in here,' he said, 'but you found the Gate-word, so here you stand.'
invite:0.cnHint: 老舵长把我____到了船队珍贵的地图室里。
invite:0.hook: The chart showed an island no one had named yet.
invite:0.line: 'We *invite* you in because you have earned it.'

million:0.en: Bell pressed her ear to the brass speaking-tube and listened. Static crackled, then a tide of distant voices poured through — low, overlapping, endless. She pulled back, wide-eyed. 'A *million* voices,' she whispered, 'all saying the same word.' The lamp flickered as if in agreement.
million:0.cnHint: 领航员在通话管里听到了____个重叠的声音。
million:0.hook: None of us moved until the voices fell silent.
million:0.line: 'A *million* voices, and every one said your name.'

represent:0.en: On the wall of the chart-house hung coloured pins — one for each island the troupe had ever reached. Old Helm tapped a red pin near the edge of the board. 'This pin does not *represent* a place we found,' he said quietly. 'It marks a place that found us.'
represent:0.cnHint: 老舵长指着地图板上的一枚红针，说它____着一段特别的经历。
represent:0.hook: The red pin was warm to the touch.
represent:0.line: 'That red pin *represents* the day everything changed for us.'

surprise:0.en: I had expected a dusty, forgotten store-room. Instead the door opened onto a bright hall lined with shelves of glowing word-stones. My breath caught. Old Helm watched my face with quiet pleasure. 'The *surprise* never gets old,' he said, 'no matter how many new members walk through that door.'
surprise:0.cnHint: 推开房门的瞬间，我满心____，因为里面的景象远超想象。
surprise:0.hook: One stone pulsed with a light shaped like a door.
surprise:0.line: 'Your *surprise* is the best part of showing this room.'

topic:0.en: The crew gathered around the low table after the watch-change, maps rolled aside to make room for mugs and elbows. Bell set down a small carved stone in the centre. 'Tonight's *topic*,' she announced, tapping it twice, 'is what lies past the last marked island.' The room went very quiet.
topic:0.cnHint: 贝尔把一块刻石放在桌上，宣布今晚的讨论____。
topic:0.hook: Old Helm stared at the stone and said nothing at all.
topic:0.line: 'The *topic* tonight is the one we have always avoided.'

meat:0.en: After hours of chart-reading, Old Helm disappeared into the narrow galley and returned with a covered bowl. He set it down without ceremony. The smell alone brought everyone closer. 'Salted sky-bird *meat*,' he said, lifting the lid, 'saved for nights when the maps stop making sense.'
meat:0.cnHint: 老舵长端来了一碗珍藏的____，犒劳在地图前苦思的大家。
meat:0.hook: Bell reached in first, then froze mid-bite.
meat:0.line: 'I kept this *meat* for a night when we truly needed it.'

drink:0.en: Bell filled four small cups from a clay bottle and slid one to each of us. The liquid was pale gold and smelled of high-altitude wind. 'We *drink* this only when we find the edge of the known world,' Old Helm said, raising his cup toward the dark porthole.
drink:0.cnHint: 每当船队到达已知世界的边缘，大家就会____这种特别的饮品。
drink:0.hook: Outside the porthole, the last star blinked out.
drink:0.line: 'We *drink* together, and then we sail past the edge.'

sleep:0.en: The chart-house lamp burned low. One by one the others drifted to their bunks, leaving me alone with the maps. I thought I should stay awake, but the warmth of the room pulled at my eyes. Just before *sleep* took me, I heard the map whisper a word I had never seen written anywhere.
sleep:0.cnHint: 在温暖的地图室里，____悄悄向我袭来，就在那一刻我听到了奇异的声音。
sleep:0.hook: I woke to find a new island drawn in my own handwriting.
sleep:0.line: 'Let *sleep* come — the map will still be here at dawn.'

shop:0.en: Inside the map-room, every wall held a shelf. Old Helm moved slowly between them, lifting jars and folding charts with careful hands. 'This is my *shop*,' he said, 'where every word has a price — not coins, but courage.' I counted twelve shelves and wondered how much courage I still had left.
shop:0.cnHint: 老船长带我参观他的____，每件藏品都要用勇气来换取。
shop:0.hook: One jar on the highest shelf hummed with a strange light.
shop:0.line: 'Welcome to my *shop* — nothing here is bought with gold.'

electronic:0.en: Bell spread a thin panel across the table. Its surface lit up with soft blue lines, each one a route between islands. 'It is an *electronic* chart,' she said quietly, tracing a path with one finger. The lines shifted as she touched them, and new islands appeared where nothing had been before.
electronic:0.cnHint: 小铃展示了一张____海图，触摸它时新的岛屿会浮现出来。
electronic:0.hook: The last island on the chart had no name, only a blinking dot.
electronic:0.line: 'This *electronic* chart updates itself — watch what happens next.'

wild:0.en: Old Helm unrolled a map so old its edges had turned soft. The islands marked on it were unlike any we had visited — jagged, uneven, with no paths drawn between them. 'Those are the *wild* zones,' he said, smoothing the paper gently. 'No troupe has charted them fully. Not yet.'
wild:0.cnHint: 老船长展示了地图上那片____区域，至今无人完整探索过。
wild:0.hook: A faint handwritten note at the edge read: 'Turn back here.'
wild:0.line: 'Beyond that line, everything is *wild* — even the wind forgets its name.'

rich:0.en: The map-room smelled of old wood and something sweeter. Rows of small bottles lined one shelf, each filled with soil from a different island. Old Helm held one up to the lamp. 'This is from the green island — *rich* earth, good for growing words,' he said, and smiled as if remembering a meal.
rich:0.cnHint: 老船长展示了来自绿岛的____土壤，说它适合培育文字。
rich:0.hook: The bottle in his hand began to glow a warm, deep gold.
rich:0.line: 'Feel this soil — it is *rich* enough to grow almost anything.'

special:0.en: Bell opened a small wooden box and placed it on the table between us. Inside lay a single folded paper. 'This is a *special* pass,' she said, pressing it flat with two fingers. 'It opens the archive at the edge of the map. Only three people have ever held one.' She slid it toward me.
special:0.cnHint: 小铃拿出一张____通行证，全世界只有三人曾经持有过。
special:0.hook: My name was already written on it in ink that still looked wet.
special:0.line: 'A *special* pass like this one opens doors maps cannot show.'

text:0.en: High on the back wall hung a single page behind glass. The letters were tiny and very close together. Old Helm stood beneath it in silence for a long moment. 'That *text* is older than this ship,' he said at last. 'We have been reading one line at a time. We are still on the third line.'
text:0.cnHint: 挂在墙上的古老____至今只被读到了第三行。
text:0.hook: The third line, I noticed, ended with a question mark.
text:0.line: 'Every word in that *text* is a door nobody has opened yet.'

front:0.en: The map-room had two doors. The back door led to the deck and the open sky. But Old Helm always entered through the other one. 'The *front* door matters,' he told me, polishing the brass handle slowly. 'How you arrive shapes what you see inside.' I made a note to remember that.
front:0.cnHint: 老船长告诉我，走____门进入地图室会影响你看到的东西。
front:0.hook: Behind the front door, something shifted and quietly knocked back.
front:0.line: 'Always use the *front* door — first impressions belong to the brave.'

law:0.en: Old Helm set down his cup and looked at me steadily. 'There is one *law* in this map-room,' he said, 'and it is simple: every word you take, you must one day return — as a story.' He tapped the table once. Bell nodded from the corner as if she had heard this promise made before.
law:0.cnHint: 地图室里只有一条____：借走的每个词，都必须以一个故事还回来。
law:0.hook: Bell's quiet nod told me others had promised — and never returned.
law:0.line: 'Learn the one *law* here and the whole sky opens to you.'

thinking:0.en: Inside the map room, Old Helm spread the latest fragment across a low table. Coloured lines twisted like rivers across the page. I watched him tap his chin, lost in quiet *thinking*. After a long moment, he smiled. 'The next island is hiding behind the morning star,' he said softly.
thinking:0.cnHint: 老舵手在地图室里对着碎片陷入深深的____，终于找到了线索。
thinking:0.hook: But the morning star rises only once every seven years.
thinking:0.line: 'Good *thinking* always takes time, but the map never lies.'

cover:0.en: Rain drummed on the roof of the archive hall. Bell pulled an old cloth over the newest map fragment to *cover* it from the dripping ceiling. 'One water stain and we lose an island forever,' she warned. I helped press down the edges, heart thumping at the thought.
cover:0.cnHint: 贝尔用布把地图碎片____住，防止雨水毁掉它。
cover:0.hook: Beneath that cloth, the ink was already beginning to shift.
cover:0.line: 'We must *cover* the fragment before the next drop falls.'

earth:0.en: Old Helm kept a small clay pot on the map-room shelf. Inside was dark *earth* from the lowest island the troupe had ever visited. He said it reminded him that all maps point downward before they point outward. I pressed a finger in and felt the cool, quiet weight of far-off ground.
earth:0.cnHint: 老舵手保存着一罐来自最低处岛屿的____，作为出发的提醒。
earth:0.hook: The earth in the pot smelled of somewhere none of us remembered.
earth:0.line: 'This *earth* holds the memory of every island we have crossed.'

paper:0.en: The archive room was stacked floor to ceiling with *paper* — rolled, folded, bundled in string. Bell told me each sheet was once a spoken word, pressed flat by the island wind and carried here. I reached for the nearest roll, and a soft chime rang through the hall as if in welcome.
paper:0.cnHint: 档案室里堆满了____，每一张都曾是一个说出口的词语。
paper:0.hook: One sheet near the top began to glow a pale, restless gold.
paper:0.line: 'Every piece of *paper* here was once someone's lost word.'

art:0.en: Above the map table hung a painted ceiling. Bell said an island elder had spent forty years on it — the whole sky rendered in quiet colour. 'That is the *art* of memory,' Old Helm told me, 'turning what you fear to forget into something the eye can hold.' I stared up until my neck ached.
art:0.cnHint: 天花板上的画作让我明白了____是如何留住记忆的。
art:0.hook: One figure in the painting seemed to look back at me.
art:0.line: 'True *art* does not show what you see — it shows what you feel.'

street:0.en: A tiny model of an island market sat inside a glass case in the corner of the hall. Each carved building lined a single winding *street* no longer than my hand. Bell said the real island sank long ago, and this was all that remained. I knelt to peer at the smallest door.
street:0.cnHint: 玻璃罩里有一座微缩岛屿模型，一条小小的____是它全部的痕迹。
street:0.hook: Behind the smallest door was a light that should not have been there.
street:0.line: 'The whole island lived and laughed along this one *street*.'

talent:0.en: Silverfang visited the archive hall with a rolled chart under one arm. Old Helm asked him to read a symbol none of us could name. He glanced once and answered without pause. 'Navigation is not his only *talent*,' Bell whispered to me, looking almost annoyed that she had said it aloud.
talent:0.cnHint: 银牙轻松认出了那个符号，让贝尔不得不承认他的____。
talent:0.hook: What Silverfang read from the symbol made Old Helm go pale.
talent:0.line: 'A *talent* used only for winning races is half a talent wasted.'

overall:0.en: At the end of the evening, Old Helm laid all seven map fragments side by side. The *overall* shape they formed looked like a creature mid-flight, wings spread toward the outer dark. No one spoke. Then Bell exhaled slowly. 'We are closer than I thought,' she said, and I believed her completely.
overall:0.cnHint: 把所有碎片拼在一起后，____的轮廓让大家震惊地沉默了。
overall:0.hook: The creature-shape pointed to a place no chart had ever named.
overall:0.line: 'The *overall* picture only appears when every piece is present.'

satisfaction:0.en: Inside the old map-room, shelves rose from floor to ceiling, packed with rolled charts. Old Helm spread the last piece flat on the table. He traced its edge with one finger and let out a long breath. 'Every island we have found,' he said, 'gives me true *satisfaction*.' The candles burned low around us.
satisfaction:0.cnHint: 老舵主在地图室里展开最后一张图，感到深深的____。
satisfaction:0.hook: But one corner of the map was still blank.
satisfaction:0.line: 'Every island we find brings *satisfaction* I cannot put into words.'

cultivate:0.en: Bell sat cross-legged on the floor of the chart room, pressing tiny seeds into a shallow tray of dark soil. 'Even here, above the clouds, I *cultivate* a small garden,' she said softly. The seeds were not for eating — each one, she explained, held a word that would bloom into a new map fragment.
cultivate:0.cnHint: 领航员在图室里____着一盘小种子，每颗种子里藏着一个词语。
cultivate:0.hook: One seed began to glow before she even watered it.
cultivate:0.line: 'I *cultivate* these seeds so our maps may keep growing.'

productive:0.en: Old Helm called the whole troupe to the lamp-lit reading room after dinner. We sorted charts, matched borders, and filled three blank spaces on the great map before midnight. 'A very *productive* evening,' he said, rolling the finished section carefully. Outside, the stars moved slowly past the round window like quiet applause.
productive:0.cnHint: 晚饭后，剧团成员们在阅览室里整理图表，度过了____的一晚。
productive:0.hook: The filled spaces suddenly showed a path none of us had noticed before.
productive:0.line: 'Tonight was truly *productive* — three new paths revealed at once.'

vision:0.en: The old telescope stood in the corner of the chart room, tall and green with age. Bell pressed her eye to it and went very still. 'My *vision* reaches the edge of the sky from here,' she whispered. She turned the brass ring slowly, and the floating island at the far rim of the world came sharp and clear.
vision:0.cnHint: 领航员通过古老望远镜，____延伸到了天边的浮岛。
vision:0.hook: What she saw there made her pull back in sudden silence.
vision:0.line: 'Through this lens, my *vision* touches the very edge of the world.'

distance:0.en: Old Helm pinned a new chart to the wall of the planning room. He placed two flags on it — one for where we stood, one for the island called Silvergate. Bell measured the gap with a length of string and frowned. 'The *distance* is far greater than we thought,' she said quietly. The string nearly doubled back on itself.
distance:0.cnHint: 领航员用一段绳子量出我们与银门岛之间的____，皱起了眉头。
distance:0.hook: Old Helm smiled as if the news were somehow good.
distance:0.line: 'The *distance* is great, but our winds have always been kind.'

forward:0.en: The morning meeting was short. Old Helm unrolled the newest chart on the round table and pressed his palm flat against it. 'We move *forward*,' he said, his voice steady. No one asked questions. Bell marked our next heading in blue ink, and the lamp overhead swung gently as the ship tilted toward the brightening horizon.
forward:0.cnHint: 清晨会议上，老舵主宣布继续____出发，领航员用蓝墨水标出了新航向。
forward:0.hook: The blue ink line led straight into a cloud no map had named.
forward:0.line: 'We move *forward* — the horizon is waiting and we must not be late.'

harmful:0.en: Silverfang arrived at the door of our chart room with a rolled map under his arm and a cautious look on his face. 'I found this in the lower holds,' he said. 'Some of the symbols on it are *harmful* — they mark traps left by old map-makers.' He spread it on the table carefully, touching only the edges.
harmful:0.cnHint: 竞争船长带来一张藏在船舱深处的旧图，警告说图上某些符号是____的陷阱标记。
harmful:0.hook: One of the trap symbols matched a place we had already visited.
harmful:0.line: 'These red marks are *harmful* — do not follow them without great care.'

impossible:0.en: Bell stared at the final panel of the great map for a long time, arms folded. The island shown there floated above all the others, wrapped in a ring of cloud. 'Reaching it looks *impossible*,' she said at last, then smiled and reached for her pen. She began to draw a new route, line by careful line.
impossible:0.cnHint: 领航员盯着大地图上那座高悬云端的浮岛，觉得抵达它似乎是____的——但随即拿起了笔。
impossible:0.hook: The pen moved as if it already knew the way.
impossible:0.line: 'It looks *impossible*, yet here I am, drawing the route anyway.'

meaning:0.en: Inside the Map Hall, Old Helm spread the latest fragment across a wide table. Every symbol, every curve had a *meaning* we had to understand before moving on. I leaned close, tracing the lines with one finger, and felt the whole world quietly open up around me.
meaning:0.cnHint: 老舵手在地图厅展开新碎片，每个符号都有其____，我们细细研读。
meaning:0.hook: One symbol, however, refused to reveal its secret.
meaning:0.line: 'Every line carries a *meaning* — read them with care,' said Old Helm.

strengthen:0.en: Bell pulled out a worn chart and laid it beside the new fragment. 'Matching them will *strengthen* our route,' she said softly. Old Helm nodded, pressing the two edges together until the paths aligned and a faint glow ran along the join like a seam of light.
strengthen:0.cnHint: 领航员将旧图与新碎片拼合，以此____我们的航路，两图接缝处泛出微光。
strengthen:0.hook: The glow faded before anyone could mark the new path.
strengthen:0.line: 'Matching old and new will *strengthen* the route,' Bell said.

competitive:0.en: Silverfang arrived at the hall door without warning, arms crossed and eyes sharp. The race to collect words had always been *competitive*, but tonight the air felt tighter than usual. Old Helm did not look up from the table; he simply covered the fragment with one steady hand.
competitive:0.cnHint: 银牙突然出现在地图厅门口，收集词语的竞争一向____，今晚气氛格外紧张。
competitive:0.hook: Silverfang's eyes stayed fixed on Old Helm's covered hand.
competitive:0.line: 'This race has always been *competitive*, and I intend to win,' Silverfang said.

recently:0.en: Old Helm tapped the corner of the map where three islands clustered close together. He explained that *recently* the winds near those islands had shifted, making the old routes unreliable. Bell updated her notes at once, crossing out two lines and drawing a careful curve between them.
recently:0.cnHint: 老舵手指出，那片群岛____风向已变，贝尔立即更新了航线笔记。
recently:0.hook: The new curve led somewhere none of us had charted before.
recently:0.line: '*Recently* the winds there changed — trust the old lines no more,' said Old Helm.

nation:0.en: A large painted crest hung above the map table — the sign of a *nation* of sky-sailors who had first drawn these charts long ago. Old Helm once belonged to them, I realised. He touched the crest lightly before speaking, and his voice carried a quiet pride I had not heard before.
nation:0.cnHint: 地图厅墙上挂着一个____的徽章，老舵手轻触它时，声音里带着我从未听过的自豪。
nation:0.hook: That pride quickly turned into something that looked like sorrow.
nation:0.line: 'This crest belongs to a *nation* of sky-sailors I once served,' Old Helm said.

perceive:0.en: The hall was lit by a single lantern, and the shadows made the symbols hard to read. Bell said she could *perceive* a pattern hidden inside the border designs — small arrows, pointing inward. I stared until my eyes ached, and then, all at once, I saw exactly what she meant.
perceive:0.cnHint: 灯光昏暗，贝尔说她能____边框图案里藏着的规律，我盯着看，终于也看出来了。
perceive:0.hook: The arrows all pointed toward one blank spot on the map.
perceive:0.line: 'Can you *perceive* the tiny arrows inside the border?' Bell asked me.

pound:0.en: Old Helm placed a small brass weight on the table beside the map — one *pound*, he said, the old sky-sailor measure for how much a word fragment could carry before it cracked. He pressed it gently onto the centre of the paper, and the fragment held perfectly still at last.
pound:0.cnHint: 老舵手把一个重量为一____的铜砝码压在地图碎片上，碎片终于安静地平展开来。
pound:0.hook: Under that steady weight, a hidden line slowly appeared.
pound:0.line: 'One *pound* of pressure — just enough to hold the fragment flat,' said Old Helm.

purpose:0.en: I asked Old Helm why we kept collecting words if the map never seemed to be finished. He looked at me for a long moment. 'The *purpose* is not to finish,' he said at last. 'It is to keep moving.' Bell smiled at her chart, and I felt something settle warmly inside me.
purpose:0.cnHint: 我问老舵手收集词语的____究竟是什么，他说不是为了完成地图，而是为了继续前行。
purpose:0.hook: His answer made the unfinished map feel like a gift.
purpose:0.line: 'The *purpose* is not the end — it is the journey,' Old Helm said.

respond:0.en: Old Helm spread the latest map fragment across the wooden table inside the navigation cabin. He asked each of us where the edge of the map might lead. Bell pointed to a gap between two islands and waited. I took a breath and *responded* slowly, naming the dark gap 'the Quiet Fold.'
respond:0.cnHint: 在航行小屋里，老船长问大家地图边缘通向哪里，叙述者鼓起勇气____了。
respond:0.hook: The map fragment trembled, as if it had heard my answer.
respond:0.line: 'I *responded* because someone had to break the silence,' I said.

welcome:0.en: We arrived at a small rest station built inside a hollow island. Lanterns hung low from the stone ceiling. A woman with silver hair stood at the door, arms open wide. Her smile made it clear that strangers were *welcome* here, and the smell of warm bread confirmed it.
welcome:0.cnHint: 在一座空心岛内的休息站里，一位老人用热情的态度让旅行队感受到了____。
welcome:0.hook: But behind her warm smile, her eyes watched Old Helm very carefully.
welcome:0.line: 'Every traveller is *welcome* in my station,' she said softly.

appeal:0.en: Rain drummed on the roof of the archive hall. Bell had found an old locked chest and wanted to force it open. Old Helm shook his head. Bell turned to me with a quiet *appeal* in her eyes, hoping I would take her side. I looked away.
appeal:0.cnHint: 在档案厅里，贝尔想强行打开一只旧箱子，她用眼神向叙述者发出了____。
appeal:0.hook: Then the chest made a sound, all on its own.
appeal:0.line: 'This is my *appeal*: trust me, just this once,' Bell said.

finally:0.en: We had searched every shelf in the old library tower for hours. Dust filled the air and my eyes burned. Bell sneezed three times. Then Old Helm lifted a loose floor board and *finally* pulled out a folded word-map wrapped in pale cloth, still crisp and clear.
finally:0.cnHint: 在古老的图书塔里，大家找了很久，老船长____从地板下找到了那张字词地图。
finally:0.hook: The word written on it was one none of us had ever seen.
finally:0.line: 'We have *finally* found what the tower was hiding,' Old Helm said.

guess:0.en: Inside the instrument room, a dozen strange dials covered the walls. None were labeled. Old Helm crossed his arms and studied them. Bell leaned close to one and tapped it. 'I *guess* this one tracks wind above the cloud line,' she said, and the needle jumped.
guess:0.cnHint: 在仪器室里，贝尔看着那些没有标注的表盘，大胆____了其中一个的用途。
guess:0.hook: Every other needle in the room began to move at once.
guess:0.line: 'I *guess* the island already knows we are here,' Bell whispered.

protection:0.en: A cold draft blew through the cracks in the stone walls of the lower cabin. Old Helm handed each of us a thin woven band for our wrists. He said the bands carried a charm woven by the last troupe. Wearing them offered *protection* against the island's forgetting winds.
protection:0.cnHint: 在船舱下层，老船长给每人发了一条腕带，说它能提供____，抵御岛上让人遗忘的风。
protection:0.hook: I tied mine on, then could not remember where we had come from.
protection:0.line: 'Wear it always — *protection* is not something you borrow,' Old Helm said.

resident:0.en: The map room at the centre of the island held one long table and one old chair. In that chair sat a thin, quiet man who had not left in forty years. He was the only *resident* of the entire upper district, and he knew every word the islands had ever named.
resident:0.cnHint: 在岛中心的地图室里，有一位四十年未曾离开的____，他知道所有岛屿曾经拥有的名字。
resident:0.hook: He looked at us as if he had been expecting exactly this many visitors.
resident:0.line: 'I am the last *resident* here, and I have been waiting,' he said.

willing:0.en: Silverfang blocked the doorway of the chart house, arms folded. He had the next word-map and refused to share it. Old Helm offered a fair trade. Silverfang was quiet for a long moment, then said he was *willing*, but only if I read the map aloud first to prove I could.
willing:0.cnHint: 在海图室，银牙船长起初拒绝分享地图，最终表示____合作，但提出了一个条件。
willing:0.hook: I had never read a word-map aloud, and the room went very still.
willing:0.line: 'I am *willing* to share, but the price is your trust,' Silverfang said.

admit:0.en: The map room smelled of old wood and lamp oil. Old Helm spread the latest chart across the table and studied it in silence. After a long moment, he looked up. 'I must *admit* something,' he said quietly. 'The edge of this map leads somewhere none of us have ever been.'
admit:0.cnHint: 老船长在地图室里终于____了一件令人意外的事。
admit:0.hook: The lantern light flickered, and no one dared speak first.
admit:0.line: 'I must *admit* I have no idea what waits beyond that edge.'

association:0.en: Inside the archive hall, rows of old flags lined the walls — each one a symbol of a different island crew. Old Helm pointed to a faded banner in the corner. Our troupe was not listed there yet, but soon, he said, our *association* with the sky routes would earn us a place among them.
association:0.cnHint: 在档案大厅里，老船长谈到了我们与天空航线的____。
association:0.hook: One flag at the end of the row was still blank, waiting.
association:0.line: 'Our *association* with the sky routes will be known soon enough.'

brand:0.en: Bell found an old chest near the back of the supply room. Burned into its lid was a small mark — a star inside a circle. 'That *brand* belongs to the first crew that ever crossed the northern winds,' she said softly, running her fingers over the worn lines with great care.
brand:0.cnHint: 贝尔在库房里发现了一个刻有神秘____的旧箱子。
brand:0.hook: Inside the chest, something glowed with a cold, steady light.
brand:0.line: 'That *brand* means this chest has crossed the northern winds before.'

deep:0.en: The reading room beneath the deck was narrow and quiet. Shelves of rolled charts reached from floor to ceiling. I pulled one open and found a sketch of a canyon so *deep* that clouds gathered at its floor. Old Helm leaned over my shoulder and gave a low whistle of surprise.
deep:0.cnHint: 我在阅读室里展开一张地图，看到了一条极____的峡谷。
deep:0.hook: Old Helm tapped the canyon sketch and said nothing for too long.
deep:0.line: 'That canyon is so *deep* that no one has ever seen the bottom.'

discover:0.en: Bell was sorting through a box of old compass stones when she suddenly went still. She held one up to the lamp. 'Look at this,' she said. 'We might *discover* something important if we match this stone to the right island on the chart.' The room felt smaller and warmer all at once.
discover:0.cnHint: 贝尔在整理罗盘石时，感觉自己即将____某件重要的事。
discover:0.hook: The stone began to spin on its own, pointing north by north.
discover:0.line: 'We might *discover* something big if we match this stone now.'

essential:0.en: Old Helm laid out three small items on the table before our departure: a wind-reader, a night lens, and a folded chart. He looked at each of us in turn. 'These are not extras,' he said firmly. 'Each one is *essential*. Without all three, we cannot reach the island at the map's edge.'
essential:0.cnHint: 出发前，老船长告诉我们三样东西是绝对____的。
essential:0.hook: I picked up the night lens and saw something already moving out there.
essential:0.line: 'Each of these is *essential* — leave one behind and we are lost.'

fine:0.en: I knocked over a jar of ink in the chart room and it spread across two map sheets. Bell looked at the mess and then at me. 'You are going to be just *fine*,' she said with a calm smile, 'but you will be re-drawing those maps until sunrise.' I reached for a fresh pen.
fine:0.cnHint: 我在地图室里闯了祸，贝尔却笑着说我____的。
fine:0.hook: The fresh pen moved across the page, and the map looked different now.
fine:0.line: 'You are going to be *fine* — just start drawing before dawn comes.'

largely:0.en: Silverfang arrived at the trade hall with a rolled chart tucked under one arm. He spread it on the counter and explained that the northern routes were *largely* unknown — most crews had only guessed at them. Old Helm studied the gaps on the chart and quietly nodded, already thinking of a plan.
largely:0.cnHint: 银牙船长说北方航线____是未知的，让老船长陷入了思考。
largely:0.hook: Old Helm's finger stopped at the one gap that looked almost deliberate.
largely:0.line: 'These northern routes are *largely* unknown — that is our advantage.'

machine:0.en: Inside the map-room, a copper *machine* filled one whole wall — gears turning, needles ticking, ink tracing lines onto blank paper. Old Helm pressed his ear close and smiled. 'It draws the next island,' he said. 'Every tick is one mile closer to the edge of the known world.'
machine:0.cnHint: 地图室里，那台巨大的____正在自动绘制下一座岛屿的轮廓。
machine:0.hook: The needle stopped, and the paper showed only darkness.
machine:0.line: 'This *machine* has never drawn the same island twice,' said Old Helm.

observe:0.en: Bell lit three small candles on the chart table. 'We *observe* the custom every time we enter a new chapter of the map,' she explained, her voice gentle. Old Helm bowed his head, and even Silverfang stood still for once. The room felt larger in the quiet.
observe:0.cnHint: 每次进入地图新篇章，铃铛都要____这个古老的仪式。
observe:0.hook: Then the candles bent sideways, though the air was perfectly still.
observe:0.line: 'We *observe* this rite so the map will trust us,' Bell said softly.

fat:0.en: Old Helm pulled a candle from his coat. The wick was thick, the wax pale with *fat* from cloud-whale oil, and it burned with a steady amber glow. 'Best light for reading old charts,' he said, holding it over the faded lines. Shadows shrank away obediently.
fat:0.cnHint: 团长点燃了一根用云鲸____制成的蜡烛，用来照亮那张古老的地图。
fat:0.hook: By its light, a new coastline appeared that was not there before.
fat:0.line: 'The *fat* in this candle keeps the flame calm enough to read by,' said Old Helm.

helpful:0.en: Silverfang spread three stolen charts across the floor without a word. It was a surprisingly *helpful* thing to do. Bell knelt at once, tracing routes with one finger. Old Helm raised an eyebrow at the captain, who only shrugged and looked out the port window at the stars.
helpful:0.cnHint: 竞争船长悄悄把三张地图摊在地板上，这个举动出乎意料地____。
helpful:0.hook: One chart showed a route that led straight off the edge.
helpful:0.line: 'I can be *helpful* when it suits me,' Silverfang said with a shrug.

position:0.en: Bell moved a small carved ship across the chart, searching for their *position* among the clustered islands. 'We are here,' she said at last, tapping a dot near the eastern fold. Old Helm leaned in. The dot sat right at the border between the known and the unnamed.
position:0.cnHint: 铃铛在地图上仔细寻找我们目前的____，发现我们已经非常接近地图的边缘了。
position:0.hook: Beyond that border, the chart was completely blank.
position:0.line: 'Our *position* is closer to the edge than I expected,' Bell said quietly.

threat:0.en: A low rumble moved through the floorboards. Old Helm read the words on the old notice pinned above the door aloud: 'Every blank space on the map is a *threat* to those who wander without a word.' He stepped back. None of us laughed. The rumble came again, closer.
threat:0.cnHint: 门上那张旧告示提醒我们，地图上的空白区域对迷途者来说是一种____。
threat:0.hook: Something on the other side of the wall began to knock.
threat:0.line: 'A blank space is not scenery — it is a *threat*,' Old Helm read slowly.

trend:0.en: Bell studied the map's ink lines for a long time, then pointed. 'There is a *trend* here — every island after this point sits higher than the last, as if the world is climbing.' Silverfang crossed his arms. Old Helm nodded slowly, his eyes bright with the thought of it.
trend:0.cnHint: 铃铛从地图的走势中发现了一个____：越往前，岛屿的位置就越高。
trend:0.hook: If the trend continued, the last island would be above the clouds.
trend:0.line: 'I see a clear *trend*: the path rises with every island,' said Bell.

ultimately:0.en: We argued over which route to take for the better part of an hour. Old Helm wanted the short path; Bell favoured the scenic arch. *Ultimately*, it was the map itself that decided — the ink shifted, and one route glowed faintly gold while the other faded to grey.
ultimately:0.cnHint: 大家争论了很久该走哪条路，____还是地图自己做出了选择。
ultimately:0.hook: The gold route led toward a light none of us could explain.
ultimately:0.line: '*Ultimately*, the map always knows better than we do,' Old Helm said.

slightly:0.en: Inside the map room, Old Helm unrolled a worn chart across the table. One corner was *slightly* torn, leaving a small gap where an island should have been. Bell leaned in close, tracing the torn edge with one finger. 'The shape is still there,' she said softly. 'We can fill the rest from memory.'
slightly:0.cnHint: 老赫姆展开地图时，发现一角____破损，贝尔仔细辨认残存的轮廓。
slightly:0.hook: But memory, Old Helm feared, might lead them somewhere far worse.
slightly:0.line: 'The edge is *slightly* torn, but the island is still readable.'

vital:0.en: The lamp above the table flickered, and every face in the room looked up. Old Helm pressed a hand flat on the chart. 'This route,' he said, 'is *vital*. Without it, the troupe cannot reach the next island before the star winds shift.' No one spoke. The lamp steadied again.
vital:0.cnHint: 老赫姆告诉大家，这条航线____，错过星风就无法前进。
vital:0.hook: Then the lamp went out entirely, and something slid off the shelf.
vital:0.line: 'That route is *vital* — we cannot afford to miss the star winds.'

mention:0.en: Bell sorted a pile of old letters near the window. One envelope made her pause. She read it twice, then set it down without a word. Later, over tea, Old Helm noticed her quiet mood. 'Any news?' he asked. She shook her head. 'Nothing worth *mention*,' she said — but her hands stayed still too long.
mention:0.cnHint: 贝尔读完一封信后沉默不语，老赫姆问起，她说没有值得____的事。
mention:0.hook: Old Helm quietly pocketed the envelope she had left behind.
mention:0.line: 'Nothing worth *mention* — just an old letter with no signature.'

rare:0.en: In the back of the map room stood a cabinet full of collected words. Most glowed a soft gold. But one tile sat apart, dim and grey. 'That one is *rare*,' Old Helm said, lifting it carefully. 'We found it on an island no chart had ever named.' I held my breath just looking at it.
rare:0.cnHint: 老赫姆展示了一块特别的词语石，说它____，来自从未被命名的岛屿。
rare:0.hook: The tile pulsed once, as if it had heard its own story.
rare:0.line: 'This word is *rare* — only two troupes have ever carried one.'

useful:0.en: I found a folded paper wedged behind the cabinet and brought it to Old Helm. He spread it on the table, studied it for a moment, then smiled. 'Very *useful*,' he said, pointing to a small mark in the corner. 'That symbol tells us which winds to follow out of the next harbour.' Bell looked relieved.
useful:0.cnHint: 我在柜子后面发现一张折叠纸，老赫姆说上面的符号非常____。
useful:0.hook: The same symbol appeared, in fresh ink, on the back of my hand.
useful:0.line: 'This map fragment is *useful* — it shows exactly where the wind turns.'

blood:0.en: Old Helm placed a deep red tile on the table. The word carved into it was 'blood.' He touched it gently. 'Every troupe has a word like this,' he said. 'One that carries the weight of those who came before us.' Bell nodded slowly. 'Then we carry it *blood* and all,' she said, and meant it.
blood:0.cnHint: 老赫姆取出一块红色词语石，说每支团队都有这样承载着前人____的词。
blood:0.hook: The tile was warm, as though someone had only just let it go.
blood:0.line: 'We carry this word *blood* and all — that is what a troupe does.'

fund:0.en: The troupe's coin box sat open on the shelf, nearly empty. Old Helm counted what remained and sighed. 'We need to *fund* the next leg somehow,' he said, tapping the map. Bell pointed to a small harbour town two islands away. 'They trade in rare words there. We could sell one copy of our chart.' Old Helm considered this.
fund:0.cnHint: 团队的钱箱快空了，老赫姆说需要想办法____接下来的旅程。
fund:0.hook: Selling the chart meant giving away the one route only they knew.
fund:0.line: 'We need to *fund* the journey — one copy of the chart should do it.'

anxiety:0.en: The night before departure, I could not sit still. Old Helm found me pacing the narrow room between the shelves. He handed me a warm cup without a word. '*Anxiety* is just excitement with nowhere to go,' he said quietly. 'Give it a direction.' I looked at the map on the table and took a slow breath.
anxiety:0.cnHint: 出发前夜，我在房间里不停踱步，老赫姆看出了我的____，给了我一句温柔的话。
anxiety:0.hook: Outside, the first star wind of the season began to stir.
anxiety:0.line: '*Anxiety* is just excitement with nowhere to go — give it a direction.'

australia:0.en: Inside the map room, Old Helm unrolled a faded chart and pointed to a shape far at the bottom of the world. 'This island cluster,' he said, 'was named after a land called *Australia* — wide, warm, and full of strange creatures.' I traced the outline with one finger, already dreaming of red dust and open sky.
australia:0.cnHint: 老舵在地图室里展开一张旧图，指向世界最南端一片以____命名的岛群。
australia:0.hook: But the chart showed one island still completely blank.
australia:0.line: 'Every navigator who reached *Australia* said the stars looked upside down up there.'

authority:0.en: The map room door had a heavy brass lock, and only Old Helm carried the key. Bell told me this quietly, with a little smile. 'He does not use that *authority* to order us around,' she said. 'He uses it to keep the most dangerous words safe.' I looked at the locked drawer and felt both curious and reassured.
authority:0.cnHint: 小铃悄悄告诉我，老舵用他的____来保护最危险的词语，而不是命令别人。
authority:0.hook: Then the drawer rattled — from the inside.
authority:0.line: 'Real *authority* means protecting people, not impressing them,' Bell said softly.

confident:0.en: I had to read the old word-chart aloud to unlock the next door. My voice shook at first, but Bell stood beside me and nodded slowly. By the third line I felt *confident*, letting each word ring out clearly in the quiet room. The door gave a warm click and swung open to a flood of starlight.
confident:0.cnHint: 在小铃的鼓励下，我越来越____，大声朗读词表，终于打开了那扇门。
confident:0.hook: Beyond the door, something was already waiting, perfectly still.
confident:0.line: 'Sound *confident* even when you are unsure — the words need to believe you.'

crowd:0.en: Word had spread that Old Helm would reveal a new map fragment tonight. By the time we gathered in the chart room, every member of the troupe had squeezed inside, and the warm lamplight made the *crowd* feel like one breathing thing. Old Helm looked around, smiled, and said nothing — he just held up a single glowing word.
crowd:0.cnHint: 消息传开后，船员们把地图室挤得满满当当，形成了一个热闹的____。
crowd:0.hook: The word in his hand spelled something none of us had ever seen before.
crowd:0.line: 'A *crowd* of curious people is the best map I know,' Old Helm said with a wink.

highly:0.en: Silverfang arrived at the chart room door and set three rolled maps on the table without a word. Old Helm studied them for a long moment. 'These are *highly* useful,' he admitted, and that was high praise from him. Silverfang only shrugged, but I noticed she was hiding a small, pleased smile behind her silver collar.
highly:0.cnHint: 老舵看完银牙带来的地图后，难得地说这些图____有用，这对她来说是极大的肯定。
highly:0.hook: The third map, however, showed an island that should not exist.
highly:0.line: 'I *highly* recommend you read the warning at the edge before you step outside.'

occur:0.en: We were sorting old word-cards by the lamplight when Bell suddenly sat up straight. 'Does it ever *occur* to you,' she said slowly, 'that the islands only appear after we say the word — not before?' The room went very quiet. I looked at the card in my hand and felt the whole world tilt gently sideways.
occur:0.cnHint: 小铃突然想到一件事：岛屿是否只在我们说出词语之后才____？
occur:0.hook: Old Helm set down his pen and did not answer for a long time.
occur:0.line: 'Did it *occur* to anyone else that the star map changed while we slept?'

regularly:0.en: Each morning, Bell updated the word-log at the small desk by the window — *regularly*, without fail, even on rough-air days when the whole room swayed. Old Helm once told me that this habit was worth more than any compass. I started keeping my own small log after that, filling it one word at a time.
regularly:0.cnHint: 小铃每天早晨都会____更新词语记录，老舵说这个习惯比任何罗盘都珍贵。
regularly:0.hook: One morning the log entry was already written — in handwriting no one recognised.
regularly:0.line: 'Update the word-log *regularly* and the map will almost never surprise you.'

responsible:0.en: After I accidentally tore a corner of the oldest chart, I expected Old Helm to be angry. Instead he sat beside me and said, 'Every person here is *responsible* for one part of the journey.' He handed me a small pot of clear paste and showed me how to mend it. By the time we finished, the repair was nearly invisible.
responsible:0.cnHint: 不小心弄坏地图后，老舵告诉我，每个人都要对旅途的某一部分____。
responsible:0.hook: Under the torn corner we found a tiny second map, hidden all along.
responsible:0.line: 'Being *responsible* for a mistake means fixing it — that is the whole lesson,' Old Helm said gently.

awareness:0.en: Inside the map room, dusty charts covered every wall. Old Helm lit a candle and held it close to a blank corner. A slow *awareness* crept over me: the corner was not blank at all — tiny star-paths glowed under the warmth, revealing a route none of us had ever seen.
awareness:0.cnHint: 在地图室里，老船长的烛光让我对角落里隐藏的星路产生了____。
awareness:0.hook: The route led somewhere the oldest charts refused to name.
awareness:0.line: '*Awareness* comes when you stop looking and start feeling,' Old Helm said softly.

introduce:0.en: Bell spread a fresh chart across the long table and cleared her throat. 'Allow me to *introduce* our next destination,' she said, tapping a small island drawn in silver ink. The rest of the troupe leaned in, eyes wide, breath held.
introduce:0.cnHint: 小铃在长桌前向大家____了下一个目的地。
introduce:0.hook: The silver island had no name — only a single warning symbol.
introduce:0.line: 'Let me *introduce* you to the island at the edge of every map,' Bell said.

expense:0.en: Old Helm opened the troupe's small iron chest and counted the coins inside. Reaching the next island would come at great *expense* — fuel, food, and a fee for crossing guarded winds. He closed the chest quietly and looked at each of us in turn.
expense:0.cnHint: 老船长打开铁箱，发现前往下一座岛屿的____远超预期。
expense:0.hook: What he did not say aloud worried me far more than the coins.
expense:0.line: 'No great journey comes without *expense*,' Old Helm murmured, closing the chest.

toward:0.en: The compass on the wall had not moved in days, but tonight its needle swung slowly *toward* a corner of the map no one had touched. Bell crossed the room and pressed her finger to the spot. The paper felt warm beneath her hand.
toward:0.cnHint: 指南针的指针慢慢转向地图上从未有人触碰的那个角落。
toward:0.hook: Bell pulled her hand back — the warmth was spreading.
toward:0.line: 'We have always been drifting *toward* this place,' Bell whispered.

track:0.en: A thin silver line appeared on the floor of the map room, weaving between the table legs and up the far wall. Old Helm knelt and ran a finger along it. 'This is a *track*,' he said, 'left by someone who read this map before us.'
track:0.cnHint: 地图室地板上出现了一条细银线，像是前人留下的____。
track:0.hook: The track ended at a locked door we had never noticed before.
track:0.line: 'Follow the *track* and it will tell you who came here first,' Old Helm said.

afford:0.en: I wanted to copy every chart on the wall before we left, but paper and ink were running low. Bell reminded me we could only *afford* to copy one. I stood there a long time, trying to choose the single map that mattered most.
afford:0.cnHint: 纸墨不足，我只____抄下一张地图，选择令我犯难。
afford:0.hook: The map I finally chose trembled faintly as I lifted it.
afford:0.line: 'We can only *afford* one truth at a time,' Bell said with a small smile.

feature:0.en: Old Helm pointed to a strange mark near the island's outline — a small spiral that appeared on no other chart. 'That *feature* is why this island matters,' he said. 'Every map that shows it has led its reader somewhere they could not explain.'
feature:0.cnHint: 老船长指出地图上一个独特的____，称它是这座岛屿真正重要的原因。
feature:0.hook: None of the readers who followed it had ever returned to explain.
feature:0.line: 'Study every *feature* of the map — the small marks lie least,' Old Helm said.

innovative:0.en: Bell had built a new reading-frame for old charts — thin wires stretched across a wooden square that split the map into a neat grid. It was a simple but *innovative* tool, and under its lines the hidden paths of the island snapped into sudden order.
innovative:0.cnHint: 小铃发明了一种____的读图框，让混乱的地图路径瞬间变得清晰有序。
innovative:0.hook: The first path the grid revealed pointed straight down — below the islands.
innovative:0.line: 'An *innovative* eye sees routes where others see only old paper,' Bell said proudly.

digital:0.en: Inside the map room, Old Helm spread the latest chart across the table. Each island we had visited glowed as a tiny point of light. 'These are not ink marks,' Bell whispered, pressing a finger close but not touching. 'They are *digital* signals — the map reads our journey and updates itself.' The whole room hummed softly, alive with stored memory.
digital:0.cnHint: 在地图室里，小铃发现地图上的岛屿标记是____信号，会自动更新。
digital:0.hook: Then one point of light began to blink, fast and urgent.
digital:0.line: 'These are *digital* signals — the map reads our journey and writes itself.'

sale:0.en: The troupe's supply chest was nearly empty, so Old Helm led us to a trading post built inside a hollowed cloud. Rows of bottled starlight lined the shelves. A sign above the counter read: FOR *SALE* — ONE WORD, ONE WISH. Bell studied each bottle carefully, looking for the one that held the word we needed. The keeper watched us with calm, patient eyes.
sale:0.cnHint: 在云中的交易站，一块牌子写着每瓶星光____一个词语。
sale:0.hook: Bell's hand hovered over a bottle that was already warm.
sale:0.line: 'Everything here is for *sale*, but only one bottle holds tonight's word.'

contact:0.en: Bell had been trying to reach the sister island all morning. She pressed her ear to a smooth stone on the shelf — a listening stone, Old Helm called it. 'I finally made *contact*,' she said, eyes wide. 'Someone answered. They know our names.' Silverfang leaned in from the doorway, arms folded, suddenly very still. The stone hummed on in Bell's palm.
contact:0.cnHint: 小铃用听音石终于与对面岛屿____上，对方竟然知道我们的名字。
contact:0.hook: Silverfang's expression was not surprise — it was recognition.
contact:0.line: 'I made *contact* — and whoever answered has been waiting for us.'

failure:0.en: Old Helm pinned the torn fragment to the wall and stepped back. Three attempts, three wrong routes. I expected frustration, but he only nodded slowly. 'Every *failure* teaches the map something it did not know before,' he said. He marked the dead ends in blue ink, then smiled. Bell added a quiet star beside each mark. The room felt warmer for it.
failure:0.cnHint: 老舵主把每次____都标在地图上，说这是地图学习的机会。
failure:0.hook: The fourth route Old Helm drew led straight off the edge of the chart.
failure:0.line: 'Every *failure* teaches the map something new — blue ink, not shame.'

bird:0.en: A small creature landed on the windowsill of the chart room, ruffling bright feathers the color of a new moon. Old Helm held out a crumb and it stepped onto his finger without fear. 'This *bird* carries sealed notes between the high islands,' Bell explained. 'If it chose to land here, someone up there wants to talk.' The note tied to its leg was addressed to me.
bird:0.cnHint: 一只在高空岛屿间传递信息的____落在窗台上，腿上绑着一封写给我的信。
bird:0.hook: The note had no name at the top — only a symbol I had seen in my dreams.
bird:0.line: 'This *bird* only lands when the message is meant for someone in this room.'

official:0.en: A tall figure in a coat covered with small bronze pins stepped through the doorway. Bell straightened at once. 'An *official* from the Sky Council,' she murmured to me. Old Helm greeted him with a slight bow but steady eyes. The visitor unrolled a scroll and read a single line aloud: our troupe had been granted passage to the Outer Ring. No one spoke for a breath.
official:0.cnHint: 一位天空议会的____带来消息，我们的船队获准进入外环区域。
official:0.hook: Then Old Helm asked the one question the scroll had not answered.
official:0.line: 'As an *official* of the Council, you must know what lives in the Outer Ring.'

confidence:0.en: I nearly dropped the chart when Old Helm asked me to plot the next leg alone. My hand shook over the paper. 'Hold it steady,' Silverfang said from across the room, not unkindly. 'Map-reading is *confidence* as much as skill — the island can sense doubt.' I took a slow breath, pressed the pen down, and drew a clean line. The chart glowed faintly along the route I had chosen.
confidence:0.cnHint: 独自规划航线时，银牙告诉我画地图需要____，岛屿能感受到犹疑。
confidence:0.hook: The glow held — and a new island appeared at the end of my line.
confidence:0.line: 'Map-reading is *confidence* as much as skill — the island can sense your doubt.'

display:0.en: Bell pulled a thin panel from behind the bookshelf and set it on the table. With one touch it lit up, and every word the troupe had ever collected began to *display* across its surface in soft, rolling light — each one a place we had been, a door we had opened. Old Helm watched without speaking. I counted thirty-seven words. There was room on the panel for many more.
display:0.cnHint: 小铃展示了一块面板，将我们收集过的所有词语____出来，每个词都是一段旅程。
display:0.hook: Word thirty-eight was already forming at the panel's edge, half-finished and waiting.
display:0.line: 'Watch — it will *display* every word we have ever carried, all at once.'

experiment:0.en: Inside the Map Room, rows of coloured jars lined every shelf. Old Helm lifted one carefully. 'We ran an *experiment* last season,' he said, 'mixing sky-water with crushed star-moss to grow a living map.' The jar glowed faintly, and a tiny island shape pressed itself against the glass.
experiment:0.cnHint: 老赫姆在地图室里展示他的____成果，一只罐子里竟浮现出小岛的形状。
experiment:0.hook: The island shape inside the jar slowly began to move.
experiment:0.line: 'Our *experiment* with sky-water and star-moss gave the map a heartbeat,' said Old Helm.

nature:0.en: Bell spread a worn chart across the low table. 'Every island has its own *nature*,' she said softly, tracing the edges with one finger. Some were wild with wind, some quiet as held breath. Knowing each island's character, she explained, was the only way to find safe landing.
nature:0.cnHint: 贝尔向我解释，每座岛屿都有其独特的____，了解这一点才能安全降落。
nature:0.hook: One island on the chart had no character written beside its name.
nature:0.line: Bell said, 'The *nature* of that island changes with the stars above it.'

status:0.en: A brass board hung near the door, names and ranks etched in neat rows. Old Helm pointed to an empty line at the bottom. 'Your *status* in this troupe is still new,' he said, 'but every name here was once blank too.' He handed me a small engraving tool.
status:0.cnHint: 老赫姆指着铜牌上我那行空白，说明我在队伍里的____，并递给我刻字工具。
status:0.hook: My hand shook as the engraving tool touched the brass.
status:0.line: 'Your *status* here grows with every word you help us collect,' said Old Helm.

accident:0.en: A jar of star-moss powder fell from the high shelf and burst open on the floor. Bell looked up quickly. 'That was no *accident*,' she said in a low voice, pointing to a faint draft from a crack in the wall. The powder had already begun to form the outline of a door.
accident:0.cnHint: 一罐粉末摔落，贝尔认为这不是____，因为粉末在地板上勾勒出了一扇门的轮廓。
accident:0.hook: Behind the outlined door came a sound like distant thunder.
accident:0.line: Bell said, 'Trust me, that was no *accident* — the island wanted us to see this.'

active:0.en: Silverfang arrived unannounced, shaking rain off his coat. He dropped a folded note on the table. 'The northern vent is *active* again,' he said, 'heat and light both rising fast.' Old Helm unfolded the note and read in silence, then looked at the ceiling as though he could already feel the warmth above.
active:0.cnHint: 竞争船长带来消息，说北方的喷气口再次____了，老赫姆抬头望向天花板。
active:0.hook: Old Helm folded the note very slowly and would not meet our eyes.
active:0.line: 'The vent has been *active* for three nights straight,' said Silverfang quietly.

feed:0.en: In the corner of the Map Room sat a small iron cage, home to a cloud-moth with wings the colour of chalk. Bell opened the cage door and held out a pinch of dried starlight flakes. 'We *feed* it every evening,' she said, 'and in return it shows us where the winds are softest tonight.'
feed:0.cnHint: 贝尔每晚给笼中的云蛾____，云蛾会告诉他们今晚最温柔的风在哪里。
feed:0.hook: Tonight the cloud-moth turned away from the starlight flakes.
feed:0.line: Bell said, 'We *feed* it starlight flakes, and it guides us past the rough winds.'

principle:0.en: Old Helm drew a single straight line down a blank page. 'The first *principle* of map-reading,' he said, 'is that every line points toward something true.' He tapped the page. A troupe that ignored this rule, he warned, would wander forever without ever arriving anywhere that mattered.
principle:0.cnHint: 老赫姆用一条直线解释地图阅读的第一条____，并警告说忽视它的队伍会永远迷路。
principle:0.hook: He then drew a second line that crossed the first at a strange angle.
principle:0.line: 'Never break this *principle*,' said Old Helm, 'or the map will stop trusting you.'

article:0.en: Bell pulled a folded page from her coat pocket and smoothed it on the table. 'I found this *article* tucked inside the oldest chart,' she said. It was handwritten, only a few lines long, describing an island that appeared only when two specific words were spoken aloud at the same moment.
article:0.cnHint: 贝尔从最古老的地图里发现了一篇手写的____，上面描述了一座需要同时念出两个词才会出现的岛屿。
article:0.hook: Neither Bell nor Old Helm could agree on which two words to say.
article:0.line: 'This *article* was hidden for a reason,' said Bell, pressing the page flat.

institution:0.en: Inside the map hall, rows of glowing shelves held every chart the troupe had ever gathered. Old Helm pointed to a seal above the door: a compass inside a ring of stars. 'This *institution* has kept records of every floating island for three hundred years,' he said, his voice full of quiet respect.
institution:0.cnHint: 老舵主向大家介绍，这座地图大厅里的____已经运作了三百年。
institution:0.hook: But one shelf stood empty, and its lock was still warm.
institution:0.line: 'This *institution* has kept records of every floating island for three hundred years.'

outcome:0.en: Bell spread the final chart across the low table, and the whole troupe leaned in. Every route they had flown, every word they had found — it all led here. Old Helm looked at the *outcome* in silence, then smiled. The map was complete at last, and beyond its edge waited something none of them had imagined.
outcome:0.cnHint: 贝尔把最终路线图摊开，大家看到了所有努力的____。
outcome:0.hook: Old Helm's smile faded as he noticed one island had no name.
outcome:0.line: 'I never expected this *outcome* — the map leads somewhere even older.'

recognize:0.en: The stranger who stepped through the hall door wore a long coat dusted with star-salt. Old Helm went still. Then he stepped forward slowly, searching the stranger's face. 'I *recognize* you,' he said softly. 'You flew with us ten years ago, before the islands drifted apart.' The stranger gave a small nod.
recognize:0.cnHint: 一位陌生人走进大厅，老舵主仔细打量后终于____出了对方。
recognize:0.hook: The stranger reached into the coat and drew out a torn half-map.
recognize:0.line: 'I *recognize* you — you haven't changed since the last great drift.'

safety:0.en: The storm outside rattled the hall's high windows, and younger members of the troupe pressed close together. Old Helm moved quietly around the room, checking every latch. 'The *safety* of everyone here matters more than any map,' he said, placing the last bar across the door. Outside, the wind gave one long cry and fell silent.
safety:0.cnHint: 暴风雨来临时，老舵主关好所有门窗，确保大家的____。
safety:0.hook: Then the lights went out, all at once, without a flicker.
safety:0.line: 'The *safety* of this troupe comes before any discovery we might make.'

collect:0.en: Bell moved along the glowing shelves with a soft cloth bag, lifting each word-fragment carefully and placing it inside. 'We *collect* these pieces not to own them,' she told me, 'but so they can finally meet each other.' When the last fragment clinked into the bag, a faint hum rose from the whole room, as if the hall itself was pleased.
collect:0.cnHint: 贝尔轻手轻脚地把所有地图碎片____到袋子里，整个大厅随之发出了声音。
collect:0.hook: The hum grew words — very old words — just barely audible.
collect:0.line: 'We *collect* these fragments so the map can remember what it once was.'

door:0.en: The hall had seven passages, but only one *door* — a narrow thing of dark wood set deep into the far wall. Old Helm said no one had opened it in living memory. Bell pressed her ear against it anyway and listened for a long moment. 'Something is moving on the other side,' she said, eyes bright with curiosity rather than fear.
door:0.cnHint: 大厅里有一扇从未开过的____，贝尔贴耳上去听到了声响。
door:0.hook: A soft knock answered her from within — three slow taps.
door:0.line: 'That *door* has been sealed since before any of us joined the troupe.'

eventually:0.en: Old Helm had been staring at the unfinished corner of the chart for nearly an hour. Bell brought him tea; I refilled the lamp. He tried one route, then another, then set his pen down and closed his eyes. *Eventually* he looked up, calm and certain, and drew a single clean line that linked the last two islands. The room let out a shared breath.
eventually:0.cnHint: 老舵主反复推敲，____找到了连接最后两座岛屿的路线。
eventually:0.hook: The line glowed faintly gold the moment the ink dried.
eventually:0.line: '*Eventually* every map finds its missing piece — you just have to wait quietly.'

match:0.en: Silverfang arrived at the hall with his own set of charts tucked under one arm. He dropped them on the table beside ours, and everyone leaned in to compare. Old Helm tapped one line, then the same line on Silverfang's version. They were identical. 'A perfect *match*,' Silverfang said, sounding more surprised than proud. 'Two crews, one truth.'
match:0.cnHint: 银牙船长带来了自己的地图，竟与我们的路线完全____。
match:0.hook: But a third route, drawn in red, appeared on neither map.
match:0.line: 'A perfect *match* — I did not think two different crews could find the same path.'

attempt:0.en: Bell laid the new word-fragment on the table under the lamp. Its edges glowed faintly. She closed her eyes and began to *attempt* a reading, pressing two fingers to the surface and breathing slowly. The room grew very quiet. Outside, stars slid past the porthole one by one.
attempt:0.cnHint: 小铃在灯下____解读那块新词片段，整个房间都安静了下来。
attempt:0.hook: Then the fragment went cold, and her eyes snapped open.
attempt:0.line: 'I will *attempt* the reading once more — this word is not done with us yet.'

draw:0.en: After the evening meal, Silverfang challenged me to a *draw* at star-cards, a game where each player picks a tile from the deck and the closest number to the night's star count wins. We tied twice. He laughed and said a draw meant the sky liked us equally. I decided I liked him a little.
draw:0.cnHint: 晚饭后，银牙和我玩星牌游戏，结果以____收场，他说这是好兆头。
draw:0.hook: The third round, however, would settle something neither of us expected.
draw:0.line: 'A *draw* is not a loss — the sky is simply saying we are equal tonight.'

facility:0.en: Deep inside the island's rock, we found a small *facility* built by earlier travellers: a low room with a water pipe, a shelf of sealed jars, and a folding chart board fixed to the wall. Old Helm ran his hand along the shelf and nodded slowly. Someone had planned for those who came after.
facility:0.cnHint: 在岛屿深处，我们发现了一处前人留下的____，里面备有水和地图板。
facility:0.hook: The chart board still held a fragment none of us had ever seen.
facility:0.line: 'This *facility* was built with care — whoever made it wanted us to survive the crossing.'

firm:0.en: The word we found that morning was carved into a *firm* block of pale stone near the hearth. It would not shift when Bell pushed it, and it would not chip when Silverfang tapped it with a coin. Old Helm smiled. 'Good,' he said. 'The best words are always the hardest to move.'
firm:0.cnHint: 那个词被刻在壁炉旁一块____的石头上，任何人都无法移动它。
firm:0.hook: Yet when I read the word aloud, the stone began to hum.
firm:0.line: 'Stay *firm*, and do not let go — this island tests everyone who arrives.'

innovation:0.en: Bell had rebuilt the compass using parts from three broken ones. Old Helm called it her finest *innovation*: it pointed not just to north but to the nearest uncollected word. I watched the tiny needle spin, then settle. A new direction. A new island. A new story waiting just over the edge of the known chart.
innovation:0.cnHint: 小铃重新组装了指南针，老舵手称这是她最棒的____，因为它能指向未收集的词语。
innovation:0.hook: The needle pointed somewhere no map in our trunk had ever named.
innovation:0.line: 'This *innovation* of yours, Bell — it changes every journey we have left to make.'

multiple:0.en: Spread across the low table were *multiple* word-fragments, each a different colour and shape. Bell had sorted them by glow, Old Helm by size. Neither order made a map. I tried arranging them by the feeling they gave off — warmth, coolness, a faint hum — and slowly, one corner of a new island appeared.
multiple:0.cnHint: 桌上摆着____块词语碎片，我按照感觉重新排列，一座新岛的轮廓渐渐显现。
multiple:0.hook: The island in the corner of the map was moving — very slowly, but moving.
multiple:0.line: 'We have *multiple* paths from here — the hard part is choosing only one.'

path:0.en: The word glowed on the inner wall of the archive room: *path*. As soon as I read it aloud, a thin line of gold light crossed the old map on the table, tracing a route between two islands we had marked as unreachable. Old Helm touched the line gently. 'Every word,' he said, 'opens a door.'
path:0.cnHint: 当我大声读出这个词，地图上出现了一条金色的____，连接了两座我们以为无法到达的岛屿。
path:0.hook: The line on the map was still growing, reaching toward an island with no name.
path:0.line: 'This *path* was here all along — we simply needed the right word to see it.'

operation:0.en: Inside the chart room, Bell spread a glowing map across the table. Each island name was a step in a careful *operation* — collect the word, trace the path, unlock the gate. 'Miss one step,' she warned, tapping the paper, 'and the whole route falls apart.' I leaned in close, suddenly understanding why the troupe moved with such quiet purpose.
operation:0.cnHint: 小铃在图表室里解释，收集单词并绘制路径是一套精密的____，少一步就会全盘崩塌。
operation:0.hook: One square on the map had no word — and no island beneath it.
operation:0.line: 'This whole *operation* depends on finding every word in the right order.'

population:0.en: Old Helm pulled out a worn notebook and read aloud: the floating island ahead once held a *population* of sky-farmers who grew clouds for rain. Now it was quiet. I looked out the small porthole at the empty terraces drifting past and felt the weight of all those absent lives pressing gently against the glass.
population:0.cnHint: 老舵翻开笔记本，讲述前方小岛曾经居住着一群云农，而那里的____如今已经消失无踪。
population:0.hook: Somewhere on that empty island, a lantern was still burning.
population:0.line: 'A *population* that large just doesn't vanish without leaving something behind.'

quick:0.en: Bell's fingers moved across the navigation board in one *quick* sweep, and a new coordinate lit up gold. The rest of us barely had time to grab the railing before the ship tilted forward into the star-thick sky. Old Helm grinned. This was, I realised, a perfectly normal Tuesday for the troupe.
quick:0.cnHint: 小铃的手指____地划过导航板，飞船随即向繁星密布的天空倾身飞去。
quick:0.hook: The gold coordinate pointed straight into a cloud no map had ever named.
quick:0.line: 'One *quick* check of the board and I can find us a new path.'

scale:0.en: Hanging on the chart-room wall was a map drawn to a strange *scale*: one finger-width equalled a full day's sail. Old Helm traced a route that looked short but meant nearly a week of travel. I had read maps before, but never one where distance hid so cleverly inside such small space.
scale:0.cnHint: 图表室墙上挂着一张特殊____的地图，看上去很短的路线实际上需要航行将近一周。
scale:0.hook: At that scale, the blank edge of the map was closer than anyone had said.
scale:0.line: 'Check the *scale* before you plan — those islands are much farther than they look.'

basic:0.en: 'Navigation is not magic,' Bell said, setting three tools on the table — a compass, a star chart, and a small weight on a string. 'These are the *basics*.' She showed me how each one worked together, and within an hour I could hold a steady heading on my own. The stars, it turned out, were patient teachers.
basic:0.cnHint: 小铃把三件工具摆上桌，告诉我这些就是导航的____，并在一小时内教会了我如何保持航向。
basic:0.hook: She smiled and pointed at the one tool she had not yet explained.
basic:0.line: 'Master the *basics* first — the harder skills will follow on their own.'

constantly:0.en: The ship's compass needle was *constantly* shifting as we moved between islands, pulled by the magnetic hearts buried in each rock. Bell watched it without worry, adjusting our heading in small, calm steps. I had expected the sky to be still and simple. Instead it hummed and tugged and breathed, alive in every direction.
constantly:0.cnHint: 飞船的罗盘指针因各岛磁力的影响而____偏转，小铃却从容地不断微调航向。
constantly:0.hook: Then the needle stopped — and pointed straight down.
constantly:0.line: 'The heading *constantly* shifts here, so keep your hand near the wheel.'

favor:0.en: When we reached the map's edge and had two possible routes, Old Helm asked each of us which we would *favor*. Bell chose the eastern path for its wind. Silverfang chose the western for its mystery. Old Helm looked at me last, eyebrows raised. It was the first time the troupe had asked the newest member to choose.
favor:0.cnHint: 到达地图边缘时，老舵询问每个人更____哪条路线，而这次轮到了最新成员来做决定。
favor:0.hook: Whatever I chose, the other path would vanish from the map forever.
favor:0.line: 'I *favor* the route with more stars — darkness hides the best surprises.'

absence:0.en: The chart room felt different at night. In the *absence* of daylight, every glowing dot on the map seemed brighter, more alive. Old Helm sat alone at the table, adding a new word-fragment to the edge of the chart. I watched from the doorway, quiet, feeling how much this troupe had built out of nothing but patience and stars.
absence:0.cnHint: 夜晚，在日光____的情况下，地图上每个发光的点都显得格外明亮，老舵独自在桌旁添着新碎片。
absence:0.hook: The word he added pointed to an island that should not exist.
absence:0.line: 'In the *absence* of a clear path, we make one — that is what we do.'

character:0.en: Inside the chart room, Old Helm unrolled a faded map across the table. Strange symbols covered every corner. 'Each mark has its own *character*,' he said, tracing a spiral with one finger. 'Learn what it means, and the island speaks to you.' I leaned closer, breath held.
character:0.cnHint: 老舵在海图室里说，每个符号都有自己的____，懂它才能读懂地图。
character:0.hook: One symbol pulsed faintly, as if it were alive.
character:0.line: 'Every mark has a *character* of its own — read it carefully.'

clean:0.en: Bell spread our worn maps across the floor and began to sort them by shape. 'A *clean* map shows only what matters,' she said, setting aside three smudged sheets. The lantern light caught the fresh lines she had redrawn, sharp and true. The room felt lighter already.
clean:0.cnHint: 小铃整理地图时说，____的地图才能看清方向，她重新描了几条线。
clean:0.hook: The one map she set aside last had no markings at all.
clean:0.line: 'A *clean* map tells the truth — a messy one tells stories.'

convey:0.en: Old Helm held up a small carved tile we had found near the hatch. 'These pictures *convey* more than words ever could,' he said quietly. Bell nodded, turning the tile so the lantern caught its grooves. Each groove seemed to point somewhere new, somewhere none of us had named yet.
convey:0.cnHint: 老舵说那块刻有图案的瓷片能____某种指引，胜过任何文字。
convey:0.hook: The tile felt warm, though no fire was near.
convey:0.line: 'These small marks *convey* a direction — if you know how to look.'

distraction:0.en: The chart room was crowded with hanging tools, dried herbs, and three singing wind chimes. Bell frowned at the noise. 'Every *distraction* costs us time,' she said, lifting the chimes from their hook and setting them outside the door. Silence settled in, and the maps seemed easier to read.
distraction:0.cnHint: 小铃把风铃移出房间，说任何____都会让大家浪费时间。
distraction:0.hook: Outside the door, the chimes began to ring on their own.
distraction:0.line: 'Remove every *distraction* — the answer is already on the table.'

fight:0.en: Old Helm and Bell argued over which route the spiral symbol marked. Voices rose, hands pointed at opposite edges of the map. I watched the *fight* burn bright and then soften — Old Helm laughed first. 'Two good guesses,' he said, 'mean we have two good roads.'
fight:0.cnHint: 老舵和小铃为地图上的路线起了____，但最后笑着达成了共识。
fight:0.hook: Both roads they chose led to the same strange name.
fight:0.line: 'This little *fight* means we both care — that is not so bad.'

finish:0.en: Bell pinned the last section of the repaired map to the wall and stepped back. The *finish* was neat: every torn edge mended, every faded line redrawn in bright ink. Old Helm crossed his arms and smiled. 'Now,' he said softly, 'the map is ready to take us somewhere worth going.'
finish:0.cnHint: 小铃修复地图的工作终于有了完美的____，老舵满意地点头。
finish:0.hook: The redrawn edge showed an island none of us remembered marking.
finish:0.line: 'The *finish* of good work always looks like the beginning of something else.'

frequently:0.en: I noticed that Old Helm *frequently* returned to the same worn corner of the map, pressing his thumb gently against a tiny star symbol. Bell caught me watching. 'He has done that for years,' she whispered. 'He says the star moves a little each time, but none of us have ever seen it.'
frequently:0.cnHint: 我发现老舵____地摸地图上某个星号，小铃说他多年来一直这样做。
frequently:0.hook: Tonight, the star symbol was half a finger-width from where it had been.
frequently:0.line: 'I come back here so *frequently* because this star has not answered me yet.'

invest:0.en: Bell laid out every coin the troupe had saved and set them beside a pile of blank chart paper. 'If we *invest* our last supplies in copying this map perfectly,' she said, 'we will not need to guess again for a long time.' Old Helm nodded slowly. I started measuring the paper.
invest:0.cnHint: 小铃建议把所有积蓄____在精确复制地图这件事上，以备将来之需。
invest:0.hook: The copied map, once finished, showed one extra island on the edge.
invest:0.line: 'Let us *invest* everything we have in getting this map exactly right.'

safe:0.en: The map room smelled of old wood and candle smoke. Old Helm knelt beside a heavy iron *safe* bolted to the floor. Inside, he said, lay the final fragment — a word so rare it could open the edge of the world itself.
safe:0.cnHint: 老舵主在地图室的角落里发现了一个锁着的____，里面藏着最后的碎片。
safe:0.hook: The lock had been turned — from the inside.
safe:0.line: 'Everything we have collected belongs in this *safe*,' Old Helm said quietly.

speed:0.en: Bell spread the charts across the table and traced a route with her finger. 'At this *speed*,' she said, tapping the compass, 'we reach the last island before the stars fade.' The whole troupe leaned in, breath held, as the numbers lined up perfectly.
speed:0.cnHint: 领航员计算出飞船的____，发现他们刚好能在星光消失前抵达终点。
speed:0.hook: Then the compass needle spun, and would not stop.
speed:0.line: 'We cannot lose any more *speed*, or the stars will vanish before us,' Bell warned.

burden:0.en: I found Old Helm alone, staring at the pile of word-fragments we had gathered. He looked tired. 'Each word we carry is a gift,' he said softly, 'but so many together become a *burden* even an old captain feels in his bones.' He smiled anyway.
burden:0.cnHint: 老舵主独自凝视着收集来的碎片，感叹这些碎片带来的____越来越重。
burden:0.hook: One fragment on the table glowed, as if answering him.
burden:0.line: 'I will not let this *burden* fall on you alone,' I told him firmly.

former:0.en: Silverfang unrolled two charts side by side. 'The *former* shows where the islands were,' she said, pointing left, 'and this one shows where they drifted.' The difference was enormous. Our carefully planned route was already out of date before we had even begun.
former:0.cnHint: 银牙船长对比两张地图，指出____上标注的岛屿位置早已发生了变化。
former:0.hook: The island marked on the old chart was simply gone.
former:0.line: 'The *former* map was drawn in a time when the sky stood still,' Silverfang said.

oppose:0.en: Old Helm announced we would sail straight into the cloud bank at midnight. Bell did not *oppose* him, but she set a second anchor quietly, just in case. I watched her hands move with calm certainty and decided that silence could sometimes be its own kind of courage.
oppose:0.cnHint: 老舵主宣布午夜出发，领航员没有____他，却悄悄多备了一根锚绳。
oppose:0.hook: The cloud bank flickered with a light no storm could explain.
oppose:0.line: 'I will not *oppose* your plan, but I will prepare for the worst,' Bell said evenly.

unable:0.en: I reached for the last word-fragment on the shelf and found I was *unable* to lift it. It was not heavy — it simply would not move, as though the island itself was holding on. Old Helm watched me struggle and nodded slowly, as if he had expected this.
unable:0.cnHint: 叙述者试图取下最后一块碎片，却____将它移动分毫。
unable:0.hook: 'Only the right question,' Old Helm said, 'will set it free.'
unable:0.line: 'I am *unable* to explain why, but this word does not want to leave,' I admitted.

unusual:0.en: The reading room on the lower deck had one *unusual* feature: the books arranged themselves overnight. Each morning a different title sat open on the table, as though something in the wood was choosing what we needed to know. Tonight's open page showed a map of the sky's edge.
unusual:0.cnHint: 下层阅览室有一个____之处：书本每晚会自动排列，翻到新的一页。
unusual:0.hook: Tonight's page showed a door none of us had ever opened.
unusual:0.line: 'It is *unusual*, yes, but every wonder here has a reason,' Old Helm said with a grin.

apart:0.en: We laid all the word-fragments on the long table, and Bell arranged them carefully, keeping each one *apart* from the next. 'They must not touch,' she warned, 'until we know the right order.' The room felt charged, as if the words themselves were eager to join together.
apart:0.cnHint: 领航员把所有碎片摆在桌上，让每一块彼此____，等待找到正确的排列顺序。
apart:0.hook: One fragment slid an inch closer on its own.
apart:0.line: 'Keep them *apart* for now — the wrong order could close the map forever,' Bell said.

announce:0.en: Inside the map room, Old Helm unrolled a worn chart on the wide table. He cleared his throat, and every member of the troupe went quiet. 'I have something important to share,' he said, then stood tall to *announce* our next destination: the Island of Echoing Glass.
announce:0.cnHint: 老舵在地图室里向大家____了下一个目的地。
announce:0.hook: But the island's name made Bell's compass spin wildly.
announce:0.line: 'I *announce* to all of you: we sail at first light.'

appropriate:0.en: Bell spread three route maps across the floor of the navigation room. Each path had its own risk. After a long silence, she tapped the middle one. 'This feels *appropriate*,' she said softly, 'not too fast, not too exposed.' Old Helm nodded, and the troupe began to prepare.
appropriate:0.cnHint: 小铃认为中间那条路线是最____的选择。
appropriate:0.hook: Then a soft knock came from behind the locked storage door.
appropriate:0.line: 'The middle route is *appropriate* for our current supplies.'

chief:0.en: The records room was full of old scrolls. I found one with a seal I did not know. Bell read the faded title aloud: 'Report to the *chief* navigator of the Northern Isles.' She looked up slowly. 'That title,' she whispered, 'belongs to someone who disappeared forty years ago.'
chief:0.cnHint: 小铃在档案室发现了一封寄给____领航员的古老信件。
chief:0.hook: The seal on the scroll was still warm to the touch.
chief:0.line: 'Only the *chief* navigator could have written this map.'

clearly:0.en: Old Helm held the lantern close to the cracked wall of the inner cabin. Strange markings covered the surface. After a moment, he smiled. 'I can *clearly* see a path drawn here,' he said, tracing the lines with one careful finger. The troupe leaned in, eyes wide with wonder.
clearly:0.cnHint: 老舵在船舱内壁上____看到了一条隐藏的路线。
clearly:0.hook: The path led straight to a room none of us knew existed.
clearly:0.line: 'Look — you can *clearly* see the next island marked here.'

communicate:0.en: The signal flags were tangled, and the speaking tubes were blocked with dust. Bell frowned at the mess in the back room. 'How do we *communicate* with the outer islands now?' she asked. Old Helm picked up a small glass sphere from the shelf and held it to the light.
communicate:0.cnHint: 小铃担心通讯设备损坏后，大家无法____外岛的同伴。
communicate:0.hook: The sphere flickered once, then showed a face none of us recognised.
communicate:0.line: 'We must find another way to *communicate* before nightfall.'

emphasis:0.en: Old Helm read the old instruction scroll aloud in the quiet study. Most lines were plain enough, but one was underlined twice. He paused there, his voice dropping. 'Notice the *emphasis* here,' he said, tapping the line. 'This warning is not decoration. It means exactly what it says.'
emphasis:0.cnHint: 老舵提醒大家注意古老卷轴中一处特别____的警告。
emphasis:0.hook: The underlined words described a door that must never be opened at night.
emphasis:0.line: 'The double line is the *emphasis* — do not ignore it.'

emphasize:0.en: Bell stood at the front of the small meeting room, facing the whole troupe. She spoke calmly but chose each word with care. She wanted to *emphasize* one rule above all others: never trade a word fragment without checking its match. Old Helm crossed his arms and gave a slow, approving nod.
emphasize:0.cnHint: 小铃向大家____了交换地图碎片时必须遵守的最重要规则。
emphasize:0.hook: Someone in the back of the room did not look convinced.
emphasize:0.line: 'I want to *emphasize* that this rule protects every one of us.'

england:0.en: Inside the dusty archive room, I found a small tin box marked with faded letters. Bell opened it gently and lifted out a folded paper. 'This map style,' she said quietly, 'comes from *England* — see the compass rose and the careful ink lines.' Old Helm went very still, deep in thought.
england:0.cnHint: 小铃认出档案室里一张地图的绘制风格来自____。
england:0.hook: The map showed an island that matched none of our known charts.
england:0.line: 'A cartographer from *England* drew this — look at the detail.'

male:0.en: Inside the map room, Old Helm spread a worn chart across the table. He pointed to two figures drawn in the corner — one *male*, one female, both holding lanterns. 'These are the first explorers who mapped this island,' he said. Bell leaned in close, eyes wide, tracing the faded lines with one finger.
male:0.cnHint: 老舵手向我展示地图上画着的第一批探险者，其中一位____的探险者手持灯笼。
male:0.hook: But one lantern on the map was still glowing.
male:0.line: 'The *male* explorer on the left — he found the hidden stairway first.'

fish:0.en: The map room had a small tank built into the wall, and inside it swam a single silver *fish*. Bell told me it had been there longer than anyone could remember. 'It never eats,' she whispered, 'but it never dies either.' Old Helm just smiled and added another word to the chart.
fish:0.cnHint: 领航员向我介绍地图室里那条神秘的____，据说它从不进食却长生不死。
fish:0.hook: Then the fish turned and looked directly at me.
fish:0.line: 'That *fish* only swims when we are near the right island.'

fashion:0.en: Old Helm pinned a new word to the wall in his usual *fashion* — slowly, carefully, as if each pin was a promise. The word shimmered and a soft line appeared on the chart, stretching toward an island none of us had seen before. Bell clapped her hands once. I held my breath and watched the line grow.
fashion:0.cnHint: 老舵手以他一贯的____将新词语固定在墙上，地图上随即延伸出一条新的航线。
fashion:0.hook: The line stopped just short of the island's edge.
fashion:0.line: 'He always does it in this *fashion* — slow, then all at once.'

weather:0.en: A glass ball hung from the ceiling of the map room, and Bell said it tracked the *weather* above every floating island at once. Tonight it glowed a pale yellow — calm skies ahead. Old Helm crossed his arms and nodded, satisfied. I stared up at it, wondering which colour meant a storm.
weather:0.cnHint: 地图室天花板上悬挂着一个玻璃球，可以追踪每座浮岛上方的____状况。
weather:0.hook: While we slept, the ball slowly turned grey.
weather:0.line: 'Watch the ball — it shows the *weather* three hours before we feel it.'
