farm:0.en: An old drawing pinned to the back wall showed a sky *farm* — rows of tall plants growing in wide baskets hung between two islands, fed by rain and starlight. Bell said someone had tried it once, long ago. Old Helm grew quiet. I looked at the drawing and imagined waking up to green rows above the clouds.
farm:0.cnHint: 地图室墙上钉着一幅古老的图画，描绘了悬挂在两座浮岛之间的天空____。
farm:0.hook: The basket in the drawing was marked with our troupe's old symbol.
farm:0.line: 'A *farm* between the clouds — can you imagine anything more hopeful?'

drug:0.en: On a high shelf sat a row of small bottles, each labelled in careful script. Old Helm explained that one contained a *drug* brewed from cloud-moss that helped sailors stay awake during long night crossings. He kept it locked and only used it on the longest routes. Bell gave me a look that said: not for us, not tonight.
drug:0.cnHint: 地图室高处搁架上有一瓶从云苔中提炼的____，专供漫长夜航时帮助水手保持清醒。
drug:0.hook: One bottle had already been opened tonight.
drug:0.line: 'This *drug* is for emergencies only — it costs three days of good sleep.'

heat:0.en: A iron lamp in the corner of the map room gave off a steady *heat* that kept the old charts from curling in the damp night air. Bell stood close to it, warming her hands after a long shift at the wheel. Old Helm rolled out a fresh map, and I felt the warmth settle around us like a quiet invitation to stay.
heat:0.cnHint: 地图室角落里一盏铁灯散发着稳定的____，防止古老的航海图在潮湿的夜晚卷曲受损。
heat:0.hook: But the lamp burned brightest just before it went out.
heat:0.line: 'Stay near the lamp — the *heat* keeps the oldest charts safe and flat.'

immediately:0.en: The map room was warm and cluttered with old charts. Old Helm unrolled a new piece of sky-paper, and *immediately* the edges began to glow, tracing paths to islands none of us had seen. Bell leaned in close, eyes wide. Even the dust in the air seemed to hold its breath.
immediately:0.cnHint: 老舵展开一张新地图，它____开始发光，照亮了未知岛屿的路径。
immediately:0.hook: One glowing path pointed somewhere even Old Helm had never dared name.
immediately:0.line: '*Immediately* after I unroll it, the map starts breathing — do you see that?'

improvement:0.en: Bell spread her navigation tools across the table and studied the old route marks. She had redrawn the course twice already. 'This is a real *improvement*,' she said softly, pressing a finger to the new line. The room felt a little brighter just from her quiet pride.
improvement:0.cnHint: 小铃重新画好了航线，她轻声说这是一个____，房间里的气氛也随之轻松了许多。
improvement:0.hook: The new route curved toward an island that had no name yet.
improvement:0.line: 'It is not perfect, but every small *improvement* gets us one step closer.'

afternoon:0.en: In the long golden *afternoon*, when the light came sideways through the porthole and turned everything amber, Old Helm would sit at the big desk and sort the word-fragments we had gathered. I watched from the corner and tried to learn his system. No one else was allowed to touch them.
afternoon:0.cnHint: 在漫长的____时光里，老舵独自整理我们收集到的词语碎片，没有人被允许触碰它们。
afternoon:0.hook: Today, for the first time, he slid one small fragment across the desk toward me.
afternoon:0.line: 'Every *afternoon* I count them — today there is one more than yesterday.'

expand:0.en: Old Helm pressed the word-fragment flat against the map, and we all watched the paper begin to *expand*, its edges reaching out like slow fingers toward blank space. A new island took shape — round, green, impossibly real. Bell grabbed her compass before the ink had even dried.
expand:0.cnHint: 老舵将词语碎片贴在地图上，地图开始____，一座新岛屿的轮廓慢慢浮现出来。
expand:0.hook: The island that appeared was one Bell had dreamed about but never mentioned aloud.
expand:0.line: 'Watch — the moment we place the word, the whole map will *expand* by one island.'

regardless:0.en: Silverfang arrived at the door of the chart room just before midnight, hair wild, grinning. She had crossed two storm-clouds to get here. '*Regardless* of the weather,' she announced, dropping a word-fragment on the table, 'I said I would bring it, and here it is.' Old Helm almost smiled.
regardless:0.cnHint: 银牙不顾恶劣天气，____赶回来，把一块词语碎片放在了桌上。
regardless:0.hook: The fragment she brought was shaped like a door, and it glowed along all four edges.
regardless:0.line: '*Regardless* of the danger, I always keep my word — always.'

rid:0.en: The chart room had been full of old, wrong maps for years. One evening Old Helm decided to *rid* the shelves of every chart that led somewhere false. He stacked them carefully, not angrily. 'A clean shelf thinks more clearly,' he said. Bell and I helped without being asked.
rid:0.cnHint: 老舵决定____书架上所有错误的旧地图，让空间变得清晰，小铃和我主动帮了忙。
rid:0.hook: Behind the last wrong map, we found a door that had no handle.
rid:0.line: 'Help me *rid* this shelf of old lies so the true maps have room to breathe.'

dog:0.en: A small island *dog* had followed Silverfang aboard three ports ago and now lived under the chart table. It had a habit of sleeping on word-fragments, keeping them warm. Old Helm pretended not to notice. Bell left it a piece of bread every morning without saying a word about it.
dog:0.cnHint: 一只小____藏在地图桌下，它喜欢睡在词语碎片上，大家都默默接受了它的存在。
dog:0.hook: That night the dog sat up straight and stared at a blank corner of the map.
dog:0.line: 'That *dog* found the fragment we lost — it was under its paw the whole time.'

busy:0.en: The chart room was at its most *busy* just before a new island was plotted. Everyone moved at once — Bell called out numbers, Old Helm pressed fragments into place, and I passed tools across the table without being asked. For those few minutes, the whole troupe felt like one thing, moving together.
busy:0.cnHint: 每次绘制新岛屿前，地图室变得最为____，所有人默契地各司其职，整个队伍像一个整体。
busy:0.hook: In the silence after, Old Helm looked around and said one quiet word: 'good.'
busy:0.line: 'Stay *busy* with the tools — we only have a few minutes before the ink sets.'

intelligence:0.en: Inside the map room, Old Helm spread the latest fragment across a wide wooden table. 'Every symbol here is a clue,' he said softly. The troupe leaned in, studying each mark. It took real *intelligence* to read these signs — not just learning, but the deep kind that comes from years of wonder and listening.
intelligence:0.cnHint: 老船长在地图室里说，读懂这些符号需要真正的____。
intelligence:0.hook: One symbol on the edge glowed faintly, waiting to be understood.
intelligence:0.line: 'It takes *intelligence* to read what the map is truly saying.'

uk:0.en: Bell found an old brass compass tucked beneath a loose floorboard. Engraved on its back were the letters *UK*, a mark from a distant island nation the troupe had only heard of in old sailors' songs. 'Someone from very far away passed through here,' Bell whispered, turning the compass slowly in the firelight.
uk:0.cnHint: 小铃在地板下发现了一个刻有____标记的旧铜罗盘。
uk:0.hook: The compass needle spun once, then pointed toward the darkest corner of the room.
uk:0.line: 'This *UK* mark means someone crossed half the world to reach here.'

user:0.en: The ancient lamp in the corner of the archive room flickered when anyone approached. Old Helm explained that the lamp chose its *user* — it would only burn bright for someone who came with honest questions. I stepped closer and the light steadied into a warm gold, casting long shadows across the shelves of rolled maps.
user:0.cnHint: 老船长说，这盏古老的灯会选择自己的____，只为心怀真诚的人发光。
user:0.hook: Behind the brightest shelf, something rustled in the dark.
user:0.line: 'The lamp has found its *user* — it has chosen you tonight.'

park:0.en: The troupe had decided to *park* their sky-vessel inside a large stone hangar at the island's heart for the night. Warm lanterns hung from iron hooks above the ship's deck. Old Helm walked the length of the hull slowly, checking each rope. The hangar smelled of pine resin and old rain — safe and still.
park:0.cnHint: 夜晚，船队决定把飞船____在岛屿中心的石库里休整。
park:0.hook: Just before dawn, a second shadow appeared beside the ship's own.
park:0.line: 'We will *park* here tonight and leave before the stars fade.'

reward:0.en: After the troupe decoded the final symbol on the fragment, a hidden drawer in the map table slid open on its own. Inside lay three small crystal keys — a *reward* for those clever and patient enough to read the map to its end. Old Helm smiled quietly and placed one key in each of our hands.
reward:0.cnHint: 成功解读地图碎片后，暗屉打开，里面是给大家的____。
reward:0.hook: Each key felt warm, as though it had been waiting a very long time.
reward:0.line: 'This is your *reward* — the map kept it safe until you were ready.'

credit:0.en: When word spread that the troupe had found the lost northern fragment, Silverfang arrived at the archive door with a thin smile. 'I helped plan that route,' he said lightly. Old Helm shook his head. 'The *credit* belongs to those who did the work — every step of it.' Silverfang's smile faded and the room went quiet.
credit:0.cnHint: 消息传开后，银牙想分享____，但老船长并不认同。
credit:0.hook: Silverfang's eyes moved slowly to the crystal keys on the table.
credit:0.line: 'The *credit* belongs to those who walked every step of the journey.'

progress:0.en: Bell pinned each decoded fragment to the wall in the order the troupe had found them. Together they formed a rough trail across the sky-map. 'Look how far we *progress* each night,' Bell said, tracing the path with one finger. The trail curved toward a region none of us had ever seen, drawn in silver ink on the oldest paper.
progress:0.cnHint: 小铃把所有碎片拼在一起，看着队伍如何一点一点____。
progress:0.hook: The silver-ink region had no name — only a single blinking dot.
progress:0.line: 'See how we *progress* — each fragment brings us one horizon closer.'

snack:0.en: Late in the archive room, after hours of decoding, Old Helm set a small wooden tray on the table. It held dried fruit, thin crackers and a pot of warm tea — a simple *snack* to keep tired minds going. The troupe reached for pieces quietly, still thinking, still turning symbols over in their heads without a word.
snack:0.cnHint: 经过数小时的解码工作，老船长端来了一份简单的____让大家恢复精神。
snack:0.hook: Between two crackers on the tray lay a folded note no one had placed there.
snack:0.line: 'Have a *snack* — a sharp mind needs something warm to work on.'

extreme:0.en: Inside the map room, Old Helm unrolled a chart so old it crinkled like dry leaves. The cold at the island's edge was *extreme* — no lamp stayed lit there, no voice carried far. He traced the border with one finger and said nothing for a long moment.
extreme:0.cnHint: 老船长在地图室里描述边境地带____的严寒，令众人沉默。
extreme:0.hook: Something beyond that border had erased every name.
extreme:0.line: 'The *extreme* cold out there swallows sound, light, and hope alike.'

style:0.en: Bell spread her navigation tools across the low table, each one arranged with quiet care. Her *style* of planning was unhurried — she drew small circles, added tiny notes, then stepped back to look at the whole picture before touching anything again. We all watched and learned.
style:0.cnHint: 领航员小铃独特的____让大家见识到什么叫做从容规划。
style:0.hook: One circle on the map had no island inside it.
style:0.line: 'My *style* is slow thinking first, fast moving second.'

color:0.en: The lanterns in the supply room cast a warm amber glow, but Old Helm pointed to the map pinned on the wall. One region glowed a deep red — a *color* none of us had seen on any chart before. Bell leaned closer and whispered that red meant the sky there never went dark.
color:0.cnHint: 地图上某片区域的____令小铃低声惊叹，那里的天空从不变暗。
color:0.hook: Red on a map always means something no one wants to say aloud.
color:0.line: 'That *color* appears only when a place refuses to sleep.'

meeting:0.en: We gathered around the folding table as the wind rattled the cabin walls. It was a short *meeting*, no chairs, no tea — just Old Helm pointing at three routes and asking each of us which felt right. Bell chose the middle one. I stayed quiet and hoped no one noticed.
meeting:0.cnHint: 在颠簸的船舱里，一场简短的____决定了我们接下来走哪条路。
meeting:0.hook: The route Bell chose had no recorded end.
meeting:0.line: 'This *meeting* has one rule: silence means agreement.'

volunteer:0.en: Old Helm asked who would enter the archive room first. It was cramped, dark, and full of old dust. No one moved. Then Bell nudged my arm gently. I took a slow breath and raised my hand — the first *volunteer*, heart loud, feet uncertain, but moving forward anyway.
volunteer:0.cnHint: 面对昏暗狭小的档案室，我成了第一个____，鼓起勇气迈步向前。
volunteer:0.hook: Something inside the archive room had already been opened.
volunteer:0.line: 'I will *volunteer* — someone has to go in first.'

deliver:0.en: Silverfang arrived at the cabin door with a rolled tube under one arm. He had promised Old Helm a rare coastal chart three weeks ago. 'I always *deliver*,' he said, placing it on the table with a small bow. Old Helm said nothing, but the corner of his mouth moved upward.
deliver:0.cnHint: 竞争船长银牙终于____了他承诺已久的珍稀海岸地图。
deliver:0.hook: The chart showed a coast that matched no island any of them knew.
deliver:0.line: 'I always *deliver* — even across three storms and a broken mast.'

engineering:0.en: Bell pulled out a thick notebook filled with diagrams of the ship's lower deck. She called it her *engineering* record — every pipe, pulley, and plank drawn by hand in careful ink. Old Helm had once laughed at it. Tonight, with the engine coughing below, he asked to borrow it.
engineering:0.cnHint: 当引擎出问题时，老船长终于正视小铃那本____记录本的价值。
engineering:0.hook: Page forty-seven had a diagram no one remembered drawing.
engineering:0.line: 'Good *engineering* means knowing the ship before the ship knows trouble.'

retire:0.en: The map room aboard the troupe's sky-barge was warm and lamp-lit. Old Helm spread the newest fragment across the table, traced its edges with a careful finger, then announced it was time to *retire* for the night. 'The islands will still be there at dawn,' he said, rolling the parchment gently.
retire:0.cnHint: 老舵查看完新地图碎片后，宣布要____了。
retire:0.hook: But under the door, pale light crept in from somewhere it should not.
retire:0.line: 'We should *retire* now — clear eyes read maps better than tired ones.'

sea:0.en: High above the clouds, the floating islands drifted like thoughts. Bell stood at the bow, eyes wide. Far below the lowest island, through a rare break in the mist, a vast *sea* of deep blue spread to every edge of sight. None of us had ever looked down on an ocean before.
sea:0.cnHint: 小铃在船头望见了云层之下的____。
sea:0.hook: Then a shape, far too large, moved just beneath its surface.
sea:0.line: 'That *sea* below us — it goes further than any map we carry.'

town:0.en: The barge docked at a platform island no bigger than a courtyard. At its centre stood a tiny *town* of six crooked buildings, each leaning slightly toward the others as if sharing secrets. A lantern swung above the only door. Old Helm knocked twice and waited, smiling at the quiet.
town:0.cnHint: 气艇停靠后，大家发现平台岛上有一个只有六栋房子的____。
town:0.hook: The door opened — and behind the stranger stood a face we recognised.
town:0.line: 'Every *town*, no matter how small, holds at least one useful word.'

gap:0.en: Bell guided the barge toward a cluster of three islands that almost touched. Almost. A narrow *gap* of open sky ran between the middle two, barely wide enough for our hull to pass. Old Helm watched in silence. I held my breath. The wood groaned once, then we were through.
gap:0.cnHint: 小铃操控气艇穿过两座岛屿之间险窄的____。
gap:0.hook: On the far side, something gold was spinning slowly in the air.
gap:0.line: 'Mind the *gap* — one hand on a rope at all times, everyone.'

generation:0.en: Inside the map room, shelves lined every wall, each holding rolled charts left by travellers long gone. Old Helm touched one gently. 'A whole *generation* of sky-farers passed through here,' he said softly, 'each one adding a little more to what we know.' The room smelled of old paper and distant places.
generation:0.cnHint: 老舵看着前人留下的地图，感叹某____旅行者的贡献。
generation:0.hook: One chart at the back was dated only three days ago.
generation:0.line: 'Each *generation* leaves a piece of the sky behind for the next.'

guide:0.en: The island had no signs, no paths, no lights — only a small carved figure standing at the centre, one arm raised. Bell called it a *guide* stone, placed by whoever had mapped this island first. We followed the direction of its raised arm and found a hidden stairway cut into the rock below.
guide:0.cnHint: 小铃发现了一块指向隐藏楼梯的____石。
guide:0.hook: At the bottom of the stairway, a door stood open and breathing.
guide:0.line: 'Let it *guide* us — whoever carved it knew this island better than we do.'

household:0.en: A warm glow came from the only occupied building on the island platform. Through the window I saw shelves of jars, a low table, a sleeping cat. It was a perfectly ordinary *household*, floating two thousand metres above the ground. Bell laughed softly. 'People make a home wherever they can,' she said.
household:0.cnHint: 大家透过窗户看到了一个漂浮在高空中的普通____。
household:0.hook: Then the cat opened one eye and looked directly at us.
household:0.line: 'A *household* up here — someone decided the sky was home enough.'

luxury:0.en: After three nights sleeping on rope hammocks, Old Helm led us into a docked rest-barge where soft cushions covered every bench and hot tea waited on a low table. Bell sighed and sank into the nearest seat. 'This is a rare *luxury*,' Old Helm admitted, pouring three cups with a pleased expression.
luxury:0.cnHint: 停靠休息后，大家享受到了难得的____——软垫和热茶。
luxury:0.hook: Then a note beneath the teapot read: 'You were expected.'
luxury:0.line: 'I will not pretend — a little *luxury* now and then keeps the crew happy.'

moment:0.en: Inside the Map Room, Old Helm spread the newest fragment across the long table. The ink still smelled fresh. Everyone held their breath. For one *moment*, the whole troupe forgot the cold wind outside and simply stared at the glowing lines tracing a path toward the edge of all known islands.
moment:0.cnHint: 在地图室里，老舵主展开新的碎片，整个队伍屏住呼吸，共同凝视那____。
moment:0.hook: Then one glowing line began to move on its own.
moment:0.line: 'This *moment* right here — this is why we travel,' said Old Helm softly.

nice:0.en: Bell laid out three compasses on the workbench and studied each one. The *nice* difference between the second and third — a hair-thin gap in the needle gap — told her which one would read true above the cloud layer. She packed the third compass without a word.
nice:0.cnHint: 小铃在工作台上仔细比较三个罗盘，凭借____的差异选出了最准确的那个。
nice:0.hook: But the compass she left behind kept spinning on its own.
nice:0.line: 'The *nice* gap here is the only thing that matters at altitude,' Bell said.

peer:0.en: Old Helm lit the single lamp and handed it to me. I had to *peer* through the thick green glass of the archive jar to make out the word floating inside — it twisted like smoke, refusing to stay still, but at last I read it: 'Farhollow.'
peer:0.cnHint: 我在昏暗的档案室里____进玻璃罐，费力辨认出漂浮其中的神秘单词。
peer:0.hook: The word 'Farhollow' was not on any map we owned.
peer:0.line: 'You have to *peer* close — the word hides from bright light,' Old Helm warned.

pretty:0.en: The trophy shelf held small wind-chimes, painted stones, and odd buttons — every *pretty* the troupe had collected across a hundred islands. Old Helm never sold any of them. 'Each one marks a place we survived,' he said, running one finger along a blue glass bead.
pretty:0.cnHint: 老舵主的奖杯架上摆满了旅途中收集的各种____，每一件都记录着一段经历。
pretty:0.hook: One of the pretties was still warm to the touch.
pretty:0.line: 'Every *pretty* on that shelf has a story sharp enough to cut,' Old Helm said.

recommendation:0.en: Silverfang arrived uninvited, snow still on her coat, and dropped a folded note on Old Helm's desk. 'A *recommendation* from the Sky Council,' she said. The note named a cartographer no one had heard of and an island that appeared on no current chart. Old Helm read it twice.
recommendation:0.cnHint: 银牙带来了天空议会的____，上面写着一位无人知晓的制图师的名字。
recommendation:0.hook: The cartographer's name matched a word on our newest fragment.
recommendation:0.line: 'A *recommendation* from the Council is not a request — it is a warning,' Silverfang said.

strange:0.en: The archive room felt *strange* to me — not frightening, but unfamiliar in the way a song sounds when you hear it in a language you do not yet know. The shelves curved inward, the floor sloped gently upward, and every book faced the wall instead of the reader.
strange:0.cnHint: 档案室对我来说感觉十分____，一切布置都与我熟悉的地方截然不同。
strange:0.hook: Then I noticed every book title was in handwriting I recognised.
strange:0.line: '*Strange* is just the word we use before we understand something,' Bell said quietly.

widespread:0.en: Bell unrolled the weather report across the floor. Red ink marked *widespread* cloud cover stretching from the Amber Banks all the way to the Rim. 'We cannot fly through that,' she said, tracing the red edge with her finger. 'We go under, or we wait three days.'
widespread:0.cnHint: 小铃展开天气报告，发现____的云层封锁了飞往边缘的航路。
widespread:0.hook: Waiting three days was time the fragment's ink simply did not have.
widespread:0.line: '*Widespread* cloud like this only forms when something big is moving beneath it,' Bell said.

wonderful:0.en: I expected the Word Vault to be dark and serious. Instead, it was bright and warm, full of soft humming that came from the jars themselves. Old Helm watched my face and smiled. 'Yes,' he said, 'it is *wonderful* — and it still surprises me every single time I open that door.'
wonderful:0.cnHint: 藏词库里温暖明亮、充满低鸣，老舵主看到我惊讶的表情，说这里依然____。
wonderful:0.hook: But one jar in the corner had gone completely silent.
wonderful:0.line: '*Wonderful* things have a way of hiding their teeth,' Old Helm said, still smiling.

disadvantage:0.en: The map room was small and packed with rolled charts. Old Helm spread the newest one flat on the table. 'Every island we have not named is a blank space,' he said. Being last to join the troupe was a clear *disadvantage* — I knew none of the old names, and the blank spaces meant nothing to me yet.
disadvantage:0.cnHint: 我作为最新成员加入船队，面对地图上的空白，感到自己处于明显的____之中。
disadvantage:0.hook: But one blank space had a faint, trembling glow.
disadvantage:0.line: 'Your *disadvantage* is also your fresh pair of eyes,' Old Helm said.

discuss:0.en: Bell laid three route cards side by side under the lantern light. 'We cannot choose until we *discuss* the risks,' she said firmly. Old Helm nodded, and even the youngest crew pulled their stools closer. The hum of careful voices filled the low-ceilinged room like warm smoke.
discuss:0.cnHint: 小铃坚持在选定路线前，大家必须坐下来____风险。
discuss:0.hook: Then a fourth route card slid in from under the door.
discuss:0.line: 'We *discuss* first — then we fly,' Bell said.

psychological:0.en: After three nights of strange fog, two crew members refused to leave their hammocks. Old Helm sat beside them quietly. 'The fog is gone now,' he said, 'but the *psychological* weight of it still sits on your chest like a stone.' He brewed tea and waited, patient as the stars outside.
psychological:0.cnHint: 连续几夜的奇异迷雾消散后，老船长注意到组员们仍承受着____上的压力。
psychological:0.hook: One of them finally sat up and reached for the cup.
psychological:0.line: 'A *psychological* burden is real, even when the danger has passed,' Old Helm said.

request:0.en: A folded note appeared on the table before dawn. Bell read it aloud to everyone. It was a *request* — quiet and polite — from Silverfang's crew on the island below, asking to share our star charts for one night. The room went still. No one had expected Silverfang to ask for help.
request:0.cnHint: 黎明前，银牙的船员送来一张纸条，提出了一个令人意外的____。
request:0.hook: Old Helm picked up a pen, then slowly set it back down.
request:0.line: 'A *request* from Silverfang — that alone tells us something has changed,' Bell said.

symptom:0.en: The navigation crystal had been flickering all morning. Bell tapped it gently and frowned. 'Flickering is a *symptom*,' she said, tracing the hairline crack along its base. 'Something deeper is wrong with the island's core.' We gathered around in silence, staring at the pale, unsteady light in her hands.
symptom:0.cnHint: 小铃发现导航晶石的闪烁是更深层问题的____，众人紧张地围了过来。
symptom:0.hook: The crack spread one more millimetre before our eyes.
symptom:0.line: 'The flickering is only a *symptom* — look for the real cause,' Bell said.

upon:0.en: Old Helm unrolled the oldest chart and pressed its corners flat with smooth river stones. *Upon* the yellowed surface, dozens of tiny islands were drawn in faded ink, each one labelled with a single word. 'Every word here was a door someone once opened,' he said softly, and the room felt larger.
upon:0.cnHint: 老舵手展开最古老的地图，____泛黄的纸面上密布着用单词命名的小岛。
upon:0.hook: One island label had been carefully scratched out by someone long ago.
upon:0.line: 'Look closely *upon* this corner — there is a name within a name,' Old Helm said.

argument:0.en: Bell and Silverfang stood on opposite sides of the chart table, voices low but sharp. The *argument* was about which path through the night winds was safer. Neither would look away. Old Helm let them talk. I noticed he was quietly writing down every point both of them made.
argument:0.cnHint: 小铃和银牙为哪条风道更安全展开了一场____，老舵手却悄悄把双方的理由都记了下来。
argument:0.hook: Old Helm finally set down his pen and smiled at both of them.
argument:0.line: 'This *argument* has given us two good answers — we needed both,' Old Helm said.

crisis:0.en: The lantern oil ran out before midnight, and with it the power for our chart-mapping tool. Bell called it a *crisis* — without the tool, we could not record the new island we had just found. In the sudden dark, someone struck a match, and someone else reached for a pencil. We started drawing by hand.
crisis:0.cnHint: 灯油耗尽导致制图工具失灵，小铃宣布这是一场____，但黑暗中大家立刻各自行动起来。
crisis:0.hook: The hand-drawn lines were rough — but somehow more alive.
crisis:0.line: 'A *crisis* shows you what the team is truly made of,' Bell said.

destroy:0.en: Inside the map room, Old Helm unrolled a brittle chart across the long table. A single wrong fold, he warned, could *destroy* the only record of the eastern islands. I held my breath and kept my hands very still.
destroy:0.cnHint: 老舵警告说，一个错误的折叠会____这张珍贵的地图。
destroy:0.hook: One corner was already beginning to tear.
destroy:0.line: 'One careless move can *destroy* what took ten years to make,' Old Helm said.

drop:0.en: Bell set a glass bottle on the shelf above the charts. She tipped it slowly until one tiny *drop* of blue ink fell onto the blank centre of the map. Where it landed, a new island appeared, glowing faintly.
drop:0.cnHint: 小铃让一____蓝色墨水落在地图上，一座新岛屿随之出现。
drop:0.hook: The glow spread faster than any of us expected.
drop:0.line: 'One single *drop* — and look, a whole new island,' Bell whispered.

efficiency:0.en: Old Helm watched Bell sort the word-fragments and timed her with his old pocket watch. 'Your *efficiency* has doubled since last week,' he said, clearly pleased. She stacked the last fragment and the room filled with a soft chime.
efficiency:0.cnHint: 老舵称赞小铃整理碎片的____比上周提高了一倍。
efficiency:0.hook: The chime meant a sealed door somewhere had just unlocked.
efficiency:0.line: 'Your *efficiency* today may have saved us three days of travel,' Old Helm said.

italian:0.en: Among the loose papers on the table lay an old letter written in a flowing hand. Bell read it aloud, pausing often. 'This is *Italian*,' she said, surprised, 'but the map coordinates are drawn in our own sky-script.'
italian:0.cnHint: 小铃发现桌上的那封信是用____写的，却附有天空文字的坐标。
italian:0.hook: Whoever wrote it had been here long before the troupe.
italian:0.line: 'The letter is *Italian*, yet the map inside is clearly ours,' Bell said.

newspaper:0.en: Wrapped around a bundle of star-charts was a yellowed *newspaper* none of us recognised. The date printed at the top matched no calendar we knew. Old Helm smoothed it flat and read the headline twice, his face going pale.
newspaper:0.cnHint: 老舵展开一张陌生的旧____，发现它的日期与已知历法完全不符。
newspaper:0.hook: The headline named an island that should not exist yet.
newspaper:0.line: 'This *newspaper* is dated fifty years from now,' Old Helm murmured.

piece:0.en: Bell found a small *piece* of the missing chart tucked inside a cracked lantern on the wall. She fitted it to the main map like the last part of a puzzle, and the whole surface lit up gold.
piece:0.cnHint: 小铃在旧灯笼里找到了失落地图的一____，拼上后地图整个发出了金光。
piece:0.hook: Gold light poured through every crack in the floor.
piece:0.line: 'This one *piece* was all the map needed,' Bell said softly.

target:0.en: Old Helm planted his finger on the glowing centre of the chart. 'This peak,' he said firmly, 'is our next *target*.' The name beside his finger was written in letters too bright to read without squinting.
target:0.cnHint: 老舵指着地图上发光的中心，宣布那座山峰是我们下一个____。
target:0.hook: The letters seemed to shift each time I looked away.
target:0.line: 'Mark it clearly — that summit is our *target* for tomorrow,' Old Helm said.

actual:0.en: I had imagined the map room as grand and vast. The *actual* space was barely bigger than a supply closet, its walls covered floor to ceiling in overlapping charts. Somehow, standing inside it, I felt the whole sky grow small.
actual:0.cnHint: 我原以为地图室很宏伟，但____的房间却小得像储物间，四壁贴满了地图。
actual:0.hook: Small rooms, Bell once said, hold the largest secrets.
actual:0.line: 'Forget what you pictured — this is the *actual* heart of our journey,' Old Helm said.

analysis:0.en: Inside the map room, Old Helm spread the torn fragments across the floor. He studied each edge carefully, matching colours and symbols. 'My *analysis* shows three islands hidden behind the Storm Wall,' he said, tracing a line with his finger. The room hummed with quiet excitement.
analysis:0.cnHint: 老舵在地图室里对碎片进行了仔细的____，发现了风暴墙后的秘密。
analysis:0.hook: But the line his finger traced led somewhere none of us expected.
analysis:0.line: 'My *analysis* shows three islands hidden behind the Storm Wall.'

application:0.en: Bell sat at the wooden desk, pressing her seal onto a folded letter. 'This *application* asks the Island Council for passage through the northern gate,' she explained, blowing the ink dry. Without approval, our troupe could not cross. The candle flame leaned as if reading over her shoulder.
application:0.cnHint: 小铃正式提交____，请求议会允许船队通过北方大门。
application:0.hook: The council had rejected every application for the past ten years.
application:0.line: 'This *application* asks the Island Council for passage through the northern gate.'

living:0.en: Old Helm hung a small painted sign above the troupe's indoor stage: WORDS ARE OUR *LIVING*. He turned to us with a grin. Every word we collected bought food, fuel, and a bed for the night. The sign swayed gently, as if agreeing with him.
living:0.cnHint: 老舵用一块牌子解释了"词语"对于整个队伍____的意义。
living:0.hook: Then someone knocked the sign down, and a hidden door appeared behind it.
living:0.line: 'Words are our *living*, and we guard them well.'

proposal:0.en: Silverfang stepped into the warm hall and laid a rolled paper on the table. 'Read my *proposal*,' she said, arms crossed. It suggested the two troupes share the next map fragment rather than race for it. Old Helm read it twice, his expression unreadable. The fire crackled between them.
proposal:0.cnHint: 银牙向老舵提出了一份关于共享地图碎片的____。
proposal:0.hook: Old Helm set the paper down and asked one very quiet question.
proposal:0.line: 'Read my *proposal* before you say no, Old Helm.'

relevant:0.en: I searched the shelf of old logbooks for clues about the Storm Wall. Bell leaned over and tapped one dusty cover. 'That one is not *relevant*,' she said softly. 'The wall moved ten years ago. Only the newer logs matter.' I slid the old book back and reached for the next.
relevant:0.cnHint: 小铃告诉我，书架上某本旧航海日志与我们当前的任务并不____。
relevant:0.hook: The newer log, however, had three pages carefully torn out.
relevant:0.line: 'That one is not *relevant* — the wall has moved since then.'

senior:0.en: A *senior* member of the Island Council, white-haired and steady, met us in the reading room. He had mapped more sky-routes than anyone alive. Old Helm bowed first, which he almost never did. The old councillor smiled and set a small glowing stone on the table between us.
senior:0.cnHint: 一位资历最深的议会____在阅览室接待了我们的队伍。
senior:0.hook: The glowing stone began to pulse the moment Old Helm touched it.
senior:0.line: 'As a *senior* of this council, I have waited for your troupe.'

table:0.en: We gathered around the low *table* in the centre of the inn's back room. Bell pinned the newest map fragment to its surface, and we all leaned in. The edges matched perfectly with the piece Silverfang had brought. For a moment, nobody spoke. The shape of the next island appeared before us.
table:0.cnHint: 大家围在____旁，把新旧地图碎片拼合在一起，轮廓渐渐清晰。
table:0.hook: The island's outline matched a shape Old Helm had drawn in his sleep.
table:0.line: 'Gather around the *table* — I think the map is finally whole.'

campus:0.en: The word we collected that day was CAMPUS. Old Helm held it up to the lamp. 'A *campus*,' he read aloud, 'is a place of learning, full of paths and quiet corners.' The fragment glowed and a new island rose at the edge of our sky-chart: wide, green, and full of towers.
campus:0.cnHint: 队伍收集到"____"这个词语后，一座布满高塔的新岛屿出现在星图边缘。
campus:0.hook: The towers were lit, as though students were still studying inside.
campus:0.line: 'A *campus* full of towers just appeared on our chart, Old Helm.'

pursue:0.en: Inside the map room, Old Helm spread a chart across the long table. 'Every troupe must *pursue* something bigger than coins,' he said, tracing a line toward the far edge. I leaned in, heart loud. Beyond that line, the chart was blank — a silence shaped like a question.
pursue:0.cnHint: 老舵在地图室里说，每个剧团都应该____比金币更重要的东西。
pursue:0.hook: The blank edge of the chart seemed to breathe.
pursue:0.line: 'We *pursue* the horizon, not the reward,' Old Helm said.

site:0.en: Bell pinned a glowing fragment to the wall — a tiny island, no bigger than a thumbnail. 'This *site* once held the oldest word ever spoken,' she said softly. The room went quiet. Dust drifted through the lamplight, and somewhere outside, wind moved through the ropes.
site:0.cnHint: 小铃指着地图上一个古老的____，说那里曾保存着最古老的词语。
site:0.hook: No one had visited that island in a hundred years.
site:0.line: 'That *site* holds a word older than any map,' Bell said.

absorb:0.en: Old Helm handed me a small crystal tile — a word fragment. 'Hold it and let your mind *absorb* what it carries,' he said. I closed my eyes. Images filled me: tall towers, a silver bridge, a sky I had never seen. Then the tile went cold and dark.
absorb:0.cnHint: 老舵让我握住水晶碎片，让思绪____它所承载的记忆。
absorb:0.hook: The image of that silver bridge refused to leave me.
absorb:0.line: 'Let your mind *absorb* it slowly,' Old Helm said, watching.

advance:0.en: Bell unrolled a new section of the map each morning — that was the rule. 'One square of *advance* per day keeps the route honest,' she explained, tapping the fresh edge with one finger. Tonight's square showed a door drawn in red ink, standing alone with no walls around it.
advance:0.cnHint: 小铃说，每天一格的____才能让航路保持诚实，而今晚的新格里有一扇孤立的红色门。
advance:0.hook: A door with no walls — what could it possibly open?
advance:0.line: 'One square of *advance* each morning, no more,' Bell said.

capable:0.en: Silverfang arrived at our map room door without warning, boots still wet. Old Helm did not look surprised. 'She is the only navigator *capable* of reading tide-charts this far out,' he told me quietly. Silverfang said nothing, just spread her own charts on top of ours.
capable:0.cnHint: 老舵悄声告诉我，银牙是唯一____在这么远的地方读懂潮汐图的领航员。
capable:0.hook: Her charts showed a route no one in our troupe had dared.
capable:0.line: 'She is the only one *capable* of this,' Old Helm said.

dollar:0.en: A trader knocked and offered us a rumoured map for a single silver *dollar* — one small coin stamped with a flying fish. Old Helm turned it in his fingers for a long time before he paid. The map the trader left behind was blank on both sides.
dollar:0.cnHint: 一个商人只要一枚银____就愿意出售一张据说很神奇的地图，但老舵买回来的却是一张空白地图。
dollar:0.hook: An empty map might still carry something invisible.
dollar:0.line: 'One *dollar* for a secret — seems almost too easy,' I said.

double:0.en: I copied our route onto a second chart — a *double* of the original — so we could leave one behind as a guide for any troupe that followed. Bell watched me work. 'Kind idea,' she said, and smiled. Outside, the stars were very bright against the dark.
double:0.cnHint: 我为路线图制作了一份____，这样跟随而来的剧团也能找到方向，小铃微笑着称赞了我。
double:0.hook: Someone would follow this route — but who, and when?
double:0.line: 'A *double* of the map protects every troupe behind us,' I said.

federal:0.en: Old Helm showed me an old seal on the back of the main chart — a circle of small islands, each one linked by a dotted line. 'This was a *federal* alliance of island-towns,' he said. 'They shared one word, one rule, one sky.' The seal had a crack running through its centre.
federal:0.cnHint: 老舵给我看地图背面的旧印章，讲述了一个曾以____形式联合起来的岛屿城镇同盟。
federal:0.hook: That cracked seal meant the alliance had broken — but why?
federal:0.line: 'A *federal* bond once held all these islands together,' Old Helm said.

campaign:0.en: Old Helm unrolled a wide cloth map across the table. 'Every island we have visited,' he said quietly, 'is part of one long *campaign* — a journey to gather every lost word before the sky closes.' I counted the ink marks. There were so many more ahead than behind.
campaign:0.cnHint: 老舵主在桌上展开地图，讲述这场漫长____的意义。
campaign:0.hook: The last mark on the map glowed faint and cold.
campaign:0.line: 'This *campaign* has taken us ten islands, and we are not done yet.'

hurt:0.en: I knocked a glass jar off the shelf. It hit the floor and cracked. Bell knelt beside it, picking up the pieces with careful hands. 'Things break,' she said softly. 'What *hurts* more is losing the word inside.' A single folded paper had slipped out, already fading.
hurt:0.cnHint: 小铃捡起碎罐，说失去里面的词才是真正的____。
hurt:0.hook: The fading paper held only half a word now.
hurt:0.line: 'It does not *hurt* to fail — it hurts to stop trying.'

initiative:0.en: No one had told me to sort the word-jars by colour, but I did it anyway. Old Helm noticed and raised an eyebrow. 'Good,' he said. 'On a floating island, waiting for orders can cost you the wind.' Bell smiled at me. Taking *initiative* had earned me my first real nod from the troupe.
initiative:0.cnHint: 没人吩咐，我主动整理了词罐，老舵主因此对我的____表示认可。
initiative:0.hook: Bell slid a small brass key across the table toward me.
initiative:0.line: '*Initiative* like that is worth more than a full night of wind.'

jump:0.en: The old rope bridge between the store room and the chart hall had finally snapped. I stood at the edge, holding a heavy folder of maps. '*Jump*,' Bell called from the other side, arms open and steady. I bent my knees, trusted her voice, and leapt across the gap without looking down.
jump:0.cnHint: 绳桥断了，小铃在对岸呼唤我____过去。
jump:0.hook: The gap beneath me was nothing but stars and open air.
jump:0.line: 'Just *jump* — I have caught everyone who trusted me so far.'

lie:0.en: The word-jar labelled 'North' had been sitting in the wrong box for weeks. I moved it to its right place on the shelf and stepped back. 'Funny,' Old Helm mused, leaning in his chair. 'So many answers *lie* hidden in plain sight, waiting for someone patient enough to look.' I agreed quietly.
lie:0.cnHint: 老舵主感叹，许多答案就____在显眼之处，只待有心人发现。
lie:0.hook: One jar on the shelf still had no label at all.
lie:0.line: 'The truth does not hide — it *lies* in the place we forget to look.'

lunch:0.en: We gathered around the low table at midday, passing bread and warm soup. Old Helm set a new word-jar in the centre as if it were a dish. '*Lunch* is also a lesson,' he announced cheerfully. 'Study the word, then eat.' Bell groaned, but she was already reading the label with bright eyes.
lunch:0.cnHint: 老舵主把新词罐放上____桌，宣布边吃边学。
lunch:0.hook: The word on the label was one none of us had ever seen.
lunch:0.line: 'Every *lunch* in this troupe comes with a lesson — that is the deal.'

necessarily:0.en: I asked Bell whether every word we collected had to be rare and difficult. She shook her head slowly. 'A word does not *necessarily* need to be hard to matter,' she said, tidying the shelves. 'Some of the simplest ones unlock the widest doors.' She held up a tiny jar. Inside it was the word 'open'.
necessarily:0.cnHint: 小铃告诉我，一个词____要难才有价值，简单的词也能开启大门。
necessarily:0.hook: The tiny jar began to hum the moment she held it up.
necessarily:0.line: 'Rare does not *necessarily* mean powerful — remember the jar marked open.'

psychologist:0.en: A strange traveller had left a journal behind in the chart room. On the first page she had written her name and title: a *psychologist* who studied why people feared losing words more than losing anything else. Old Helm read it twice. 'She understood us,' he said quietly, 'before she even met us.'
psychologist:0.cnHint: 图表室里有位____留下的日记，记录了人们对失去词语的恐惧。
psychologist:0.hook: The last entry in the journal was written in a shaking hand.
psychologist:0.line: 'A *psychologist* once told me that words are the maps inside our minds.'

gather:0.en: The map room smelled of old paper and candle smoke. Old Helm spread the newest fragment across the long table, and we began to *gather* around it, shoulder to shoulder, each pair of eyes tracing the dotted lines toward a cluster of islands none of us had named yet.
gather:0.cnHint: 团员们在地图室里____在桌边，望着从未见过的岛屿群。
gather:0.hook: One island on the edge had no name — only a question mark.
gather:0.line: '*Gather* close,' said Old Helm, 'this piece shows something new.'

imagine:0.en: Bell pressed a finger to the blank corner of the fragment. 'Try to *imagine* what lies beyond that cloud wall,' she said softly. The candle flame bent as if agreeing. I closed my eyes and saw tall towers of pale stone rising from nothing, waiting.
imagine:0.cnHint: 小铃让大家____云墙之外的世界，烛火也似乎在点头。
imagine:0.hook: Whatever waited there had never appeared on any map before.
imagine:0.line: 'Can you *imagine* towers rising straight out of the clouds?'

instance:0.en: Old Helm had seen strange things before — a singing compass, a bridge made of frozen light. 'This,' he said, tapping the fragment, 'is another *instance* of a place that should not exist by any rule we know.' He said it calmly, as though the impossible were simply Tuesday.
instance:0.cnHint: 团长说，这又是一个按常理____不该存在的地方。
instance:0.hook: Bell quietly wrote the word 'impossible' in her log, then crossed it out.
instance:0.line: 'This is one more *instance* of a place the old charts never imagined.'

numerous:0.en: I pulled open the wide drawer beneath the table and found *numerous* smaller fragments, each one a different colour, some no bigger than my palm. 'How long have you been collecting these?' I asked. Old Helm smiled without answering, which felt like an answer all its own.
numerous:0.cnHint: 抽屉里有____张不同颜色的碎片，团长只是微笑着没有回答。
numerous:0.hook: One fragment was still warm, as if someone had just let it go.
numerous:0.line: 'There are *numerous* pieces still missing, but we are getting closer.'

puzzle:0.en: Bell laid four fragments side by side and frowned. They should have fitted together — the colours matched, the edges looked right — yet a gap remained in the centre, shaped like a small door. The whole arrangement felt like a *puzzle* designed to ask a question rather than give an answer.
puzzle:0.cnHint: 四块碎片拼在一起，中间仍留着门形空隙，整体像一道____。
puzzle:0.hook: The gap was exactly the size of the word we had found that morning.
puzzle:0.line: 'This *puzzle* will only open when the right word fills the centre.'

remind:0.en: The faded ink on one fragment showed a courtyard with a great tree at its heart. Something about the curved roof around it made me pause. Bell noticed and leaned over. 'Does it *remind* you of somewhere?' she asked quietly. I nodded, though I could not yet say where.
remind:0.cnHint: 碎片上的庭院图案____了我某个说不清的地方，小铃轻声问我。
remind:0.hook: The memory hovered just out of reach, like a word on the tip of my tongue.
remind:0.line: 'Does this courtyard *remind* you of anything from the last island?'

truly:0.en: Old Helm held the largest fragment up to the lamp. The light passed through it and threw pale shapes onto the ceiling — outlines of islands, rivers, even tiny figures walking. 'Now,' he said, 'you can *truly* see what the map is trying to tell us.' I held my breath.
truly:0.cnHint: 团长把碎片举向灯光，天花板上浮现出岛屿轮廓，让我们____看懂了地图。
truly:0.hook: One of the tiny figures on the ceiling seemed to be pointing straight at us.
truly:0.line: 'Only in lamplight can you *truly* read what this fragment hides.'

valuable:0.en: Bell wrapped the assembled fragments in a soft cloth and placed them in the iron chest beneath the table. 'More *valuable* than anything else we carry,' she said, patting the lid. She was not talking about treasure you could sell. She meant the kind that opens new sky.
valuable:0.cnHint: 小铃把碎片锁进铁箱，说它们是队伍所有物品中最____的东西。
valuable:0.hook: Outside, the wind shifted, and somewhere above us, a new island drifted closer.

insist:0.en: The map room smelled of old wood and lamp oil. Old Helm spread the newest fragment across the table and studied it for a long time. 'We must go north,' he said quietly. Bell started to suggest another route, but Old Helm would *insist* — his finger pressed firm against the glowing edge of the map.
insist:0.cnHint: 老船长____一定要走那条路，贝尔的建议被挡了回来。
insist:0.hook: The map edge shimmered, as if agreeing with him.
insist:0.line: 'I *insist* we follow this road — no other way is safe.'

investigation:0.en: A locked chest sat in the corner of the map room. No one remembered putting it there. Old Helm called it a gift from the last island; Bell called it trouble. I knelt beside it and began a careful *investigation*, checking every latch and marking while the lamp threw long shadows on the wall.
investigation:0.cnHint: 我在地图室里对那只神秘箱子展开____，试图弄清楚它的来历。
investigation:0.line: 'A proper *investigation* will tell us more than guessing ever could.'

limited:0.en: Our supply shelf in the map room held only three candles, half a jar of ink, and a small loaf of bread. Old Helm looked it over and sighed. Our time and our resources were both *limited*, yet the next fragment still needed to be copied before morning light reached the window.
limited:0.cnHint: 地图室里物资____，老船长皱着眉头盯着那排空荡荡的架子。
limited:0.hook: The last candle began to flicker.
limited:0.line: 'Our time is *limited*, so let us work without a single wasted moment.'

listen:0.en: Bell sat cross-legged on the floor of the map room, eyes closed, ear pressed gently to a hollow wooden tube connected to the hull. She called it her speaking pipe. 'You have to *listen*,' she whispered to me. 'The wind tells you which island is breathing tonight.'
listen:0.cnHint: 贝尔教我用那根奇怪的木管____，说风声里藏着岛屿的秘密。
listen:0.hook: A low hum rose through the pipe, clear and strange.
listen:0.line: '*Listen* closely — the island is already trying to tell us something.'

master:0.en: On the shelf above the charts hung a small framed paper. Bell told me it was Old Helm's certificate from the Sky Navigation School, marking him as a *master* of aerial cartography. He never mentioned it himself. He just kept drawing maps, quiet and steady, as if the title meant nothing at all.
master:0.cnHint: 架子上挂着老船长的____证书，但他从不提起那件事。
master:0.hook: The certificate was dated forty years ago, almost to the day.
master:0.line: 'A true *master* of maps never stops learning new ones,' Old Helm said softly.

newly:0.en: I found a *newly* drawn chart pinned to the side wall of the map room, still damp at the edges where the ink had not quite dried. No name was signed on it. The lines were careful and clean, showing an island none of our older maps had ever named.
newly:0.cnHint: 地图室的墙上多了一张____绘制的海图，没有署名，岛屿陌生而清晰。
newly:0.hook: Someone had drawn it here while we slept.
newly:0.line: 'This *newly* made chart appeared overnight — who among us drew it?'

north:0.en: The map room had one small round window, and every night I noticed the same bright star sitting perfectly in its frame. Bell laughed when she saw me staring. 'That is your anchor,' she said. 'True *north*. As long as you can find that star, you can always find your way home.'
north:0.cnHint: 贝尔指着圆窗里的那颗星告诉我，那就是真正的____方向。
north:0.hook: That night, the star moved — just slightly, but enough.
north:0.line: 'Follow true *north*, and the islands will always lead you somewhere worth going.'

obviously:0.en: Old Helm unrolled the new fragment and placed it beside the old one. The two edges matched perfectly, like two halves of a broken plate finding each other after years apart. He looked up at Bell and me with calm eyes. *Obviously* the road ahead led to the place marked only as The End of the Map.
obviously:0.cnHint: 两张碎片拼在一起，____指向了那个只写着"地图尽头"的地方。
obviously:0.hook: None of us spoke, but we all started packing.
obviously:0.line: '*Obviously* this is the path — the map has been telling us all along.'

pose:0.en: Old Helm spread an old map across the low table and asked each of us to stand still. 'Hold that *pose*,' he said, studying our shadows against the lamp-lit wall. He believed the shape of a person's shadow could point toward the next island.
pose:0.cnHint: 老舵主让大家保持静止的____，观察影子指向下一座岛。
pose:0.hook: My shadow stretched toward a door none of us had noticed before.
pose:0.line: 'Hold that *pose* — your shadow is telling us something.'

stimulate:0.en: Bell unrolled a chart covered in tiny glowing dots inside the map room. She said the dots would *stimulate* a reader's memory, pulling half-forgotten routes back to the surface. I stared until shapes began to bloom in my mind like slow fireworks.
stimulate:0.cnHint: 小铃说这份图上的光点会____读者的记忆，让迷失的路线重新浮现。
stimulate:0.hook: One route bloomed clearest of all — and it led straight down.
stimulate:0.line: 'These lights *stimulate* your memory; let the shapes come to you.'

switch:0.en: The lantern in the chart room flickered twice, then went dark. Old Helm reached up and gave a small lever a firm pull to *switch* to the backup light. A warm amber glow replaced the darkness, and the floating maps above us trembled like waking birds.
switch:0.cnHint: 老舵主拉动小杠杆____到备用光源，地图们像惊醒的鸟儿一样颤动。
switch:0.hook: In that new light, one map showed an island that had not been there before.
switch:0.line: '*Switch* to the backup — I need to see every corner of this map.'

treatment:0.en: Silverfang arrived at our door dripping wet, holding a jar of pale blue paste. He said the island healers had given him the *treatment* after a cold fog had settled in his chest, and now he wanted to trade the recipe for a safe passage chart.
treatment:0.cnHint: 竞争船长带来了岛上治疗师给他的____，想用配方换一张安全航线图。
treatment:0.hook: Old Helm eyed the jar and asked who, exactly, had made it.
treatment:0.line: 'This *treatment* cleared the fog in my chest in one night — trade?'

union:0.en: Old Helm pinned three small flags to the centre of the map table. He explained that years ago a *union* of island captains had agreed on shared sky-roads, and those roads still held if you knew the old signs. Bell traced the lines with one quiet finger.
union:0.cnHint: 老舵主讲述当年船长们组成的____所约定的天空航道，那些路线至今仍在。
union:0.hook: Bell's finger stopped at a sign no captain had claimed to know.
union:0.line: 'The *union* drew these roads — follow them and you will not be lost.'

acknowledge:0.en: I laid my rough sketch on the table beside Bell's careful chart. She studied both for a long moment, then gave a small nod to *acknowledge* that my lines matched hers in two important places. That quiet nod felt like the warmest welcome I had received.
acknowledge:0.cnHint: 小铃轻轻点头____我的草图与她的图在两个重要位置吻合。
acknowledge:0.hook: Old Helm leaned over and circled one of those matching points in red.
acknowledge:0.line: 'I *acknowledge* your map — those two lines are exactly right.'

alike:0.en: Bell held my sketch next to her own chart under the amber lamp. The coastlines were *alike* in every curve and bend, though hers was drawn in careful ink and mine in soft charcoal. Old Helm whispered that two maps agreeing so closely was a rare sign.
alike:0.cnHint: 小铃发现我和她的海岸线____，每一个弯曲都相互吻合，老舵主说这是罕见的征兆。
alike:0.hook: Rare signs, he added, always meant something big was very close.
alike:0.line: 'They are almost perfectly *alike* — who taught you to read coastlines?'

analyze:0.en: Old Helm spread four overlapping maps on the table and asked Bell to *analyze* the patterns where they crossed. She bent low, drew small circles, and muttered numbers under her breath. After ten quiet minutes she stood up straight and said only three words: 'One island, hidden.'
analyze:0.cnHint: 小铃仔细____四张地图重叠处的规律，最终说出了三个字：有一座隐藏的岛。
analyze:0.hook: She tapped the blank space at the very centre of all four maps.
analyze:0.line: 'Let me *analyze* the overlaps — I think something is hiding in plain sight.'

writer:0.en: Inside the map room, scrolls covered every wall from floor to ceiling. Old Helm unrolled the newest one with careful hands. 'Every island was first imagined by a *writer*,' he said softly, tracing the inked paths. 'Words made these places real before any of us set foot on them.'
writer:0.cnHint: 老舵在地图室里展开一张新卷轴，告诉大家每座岛屿都源于一位____的想象。
writer:0.hook: One scroll at the far end had no name on it.
writer:0.line: 'Every island we sail to was first born in a *writer*'s mind,' said Old Helm.

addition:0.en: Bell spread the new map piece on the table beside the old ones. The fit was perfect. 'This *addition* fills the gap we have been guessing at for weeks,' she said, pressing it flat with both palms. The joined map now showed a cluster of islands none of us had ever named.
addition:0.cnHint: 小铃把新地图碎片拼入旧地图，这块重要的____让一片从未命名的群岛显现出来。
addition:0.hook: One island on the new section glowed faintly in the lamplight.
addition:0.line: Bell said, 'This *addition* finally completes the eastern quarter of our map.'

alternative:0.en: The lantern oil was almost gone, and the map room was growing dark. Old Helm looked around the shelves. 'We have one *alternative*,' he said, holding up a jar of pale liquid. 'Star-moss fuel. It burns blue, but it burns.' He lit the wick and the room turned a soft, cool colour.
alternative:0.cnHint: 灯油快用完了，老舵找到了唯一的____，点燃后整个地图室变成了柔和的蓝色。
alternative:0.hook: In the blue light, the maps seemed to show different routes entirely.
alternative:0.line: Old Helm said, 'There is only one *alternative*, and I hope it lasts the night.'

amazing:0.en: Silverfang stepped into the map room for the first time and stopped in the doorway. Her eyes moved slowly across the hundreds of scrolls. 'This is *amazing*,' she said at last, her voice unusually quiet. 'I have sailed half my life and never once guessed so many islands still waited to be found.'
amazing:0.cnHint: 银牙第一次走进地图室，看到满屋卷轴，忍不住说这景象真是____。
amazing:0.hook: She reached for one scroll, then pulled her hand back.
amazing:0.line: Silverfang whispered, 'It is *amazing* — there are more islands than stars I have counted.'

ease:0.en: After a long day of sailing, the map room felt like shelter. I settled into the old chair by the lamp while Bell sorted scrolls. There was a quiet *ease* in that room that existed nowhere else on the ship — no wind, no creaking wood, just soft paper and steady light.
ease:0.cnHint: 漫长的航行之后，叙述者在地图室的椅子上感受到了一种别处没有的____。
ease:0.hook: Then a scroll rolled off the shelf on its own.
ease:0.line: Bell smiled and said, 'You look like you have finally found some *ease*, new one.'

frequent:0.en: Old Helm noticed the marks on the doorframe — small nicks left by *frequent* visitors over many years. 'Every navigator who ever sailed with us stood here,' he said, touching one nick gently. The wood was worn smooth at shoulder height. I added my own small mark with a coin, just below the rest.
frequent:0.cnHint: 老舵发现门框上刻满了历年____到访者留下的痕迹，叙述者也悄悄加上了自己的记号。
frequent:0.hook: One nick was far older than the ship itself.
frequent:0.line: Old Helm said, '*Frequent* visitors leave marks — now you belong to this wall too.'

hope:0.en: I found a folded note tucked inside the oldest scroll. The handwriting was faded but readable: 'If you found this, my *hope* is that you sail further than I did.' There was no name. Old Helm read it over my shoulder and was quiet for a long moment before he smiled.
hope:0.cnHint: 叙述者在最古老的卷轴里发现了一张便条，写便条的人留下了自己的____，却没有留下名字。
hope:0.hook: Old Helm recognised the handwriting, though he said nothing.
hope:0.line: Old Helm read aloud, 'My *hope* is that you sail further than I ever could.'

imply:0.en: Bell pointed to a symbol repeated at the edge of three different maps. 'What does it mean?' I asked. 'The symbol itself says nothing,' she replied, 'but its position seems to *imply* there is a fixed point in the sky above all the floating islands — something that does not drift.' We stared at the maps in silence.
imply:0.cnHint: 小铃发现三张地图边缘有同一个符号，它似乎____所有浮空岛上方存在一个不会漂移的固定点。
imply:0.hook: None of our charts had ever shown what lay directly above.
imply:0.line: Bell said quietly, 'Three maps share this mark — does it not *imply* something watches from above?'

belong:0.en: Inside the map room, Old Helm spread the collected fragments across a wide table. He studied each piece in silence. 'These small scraps of paper,' he said softly, '*belong* together — like members of a family separated by a long journey. Place them right, and they show us the next island.'
belong:0.cnHint: 老赫姆在地图室里将碎片拼在一起，说它们____在一起。
belong:0.hook: But one fragment was missing, and the gap pointed somewhere none of us expected.
belong:0.line: 'These pieces *belong* together — place them right and the path opens.'

beneficial:0.en: Bell had found a warm corner of the chart room and hung bundles of dried herbs from the low ceiling. 'The air in here is dry and cold,' she explained, arranging her jars. 'Breathing these herbs is *beneficial* — they keep our minds clear when we read the old maps for hours.'
beneficial:0.cnHint: 领航员贝尔在地图室挂上草药，说吸入草药的气味对我们____。
beneficial:0.hook: Then one jar tipped over, and a strange silver mist curled toward the oldest map on the wall.
beneficial:0.line: 'Breathing these herbs is *beneficial* — your mind will stay sharp all night.'

characteristic:0.en: Old Helm pointed to the border drawn around each fragment. 'See this thin double line? It is a *characteristic* of maps made on the northern islands — every cartographer there was trained to mark borders this way. So this piece did not come from the south. It came from far above us.'
characteristic:0.cnHint: 老赫姆指出地图边框的双线是北方岛屿地图的____。
characteristic:0.hook: If the fragment came from that far north, then someone had traveled far beyond any known route.
characteristic:0.line: 'That double border is a *characteristic* of every northern island map I have seen.'

director:0.en: A stranger arrived at the chart-room door just before midnight. Old Helm introduced him simply: 'This is the *director* of the island archive — he keeps every recorded map ever drawn.' The man stepped inside, looked at our table of fragments, and went very still, as if he recognized something he thought was lost.
director:0.cnHint: 午夜前，群岛档案馆的____来到地图室，看到碎片后神情凝固。
director:0.hook: He whispered a single word under his breath, and Old Helm's face went pale.
director:0.line: 'I am the *director* of the archive, and I know exactly where that fragment belongs.'

emerge:0.en: Bell lowered a fragment into a shallow tray of warm water, something she called the old reader's trick. Slowly, faint lines began to *emerge* beneath the surface pattern — a second map drawn in ink that only showed itself when wet. The hidden chart spread like a branching river across the paper.
emerge:0.cnHint: 贝尔将碎片泡入温水，隐藏的线条慢慢____出来。
emerge:0.hook: The hidden lines formed the outline of an island that appeared on no known chart.
emerge:0.line: 'Watch closely — the real route will *emerge* the moment the paper gets wet.'

exact:0.en: I tried to copy the hidden lines onto a fresh sheet, but Old Helm stopped my hand. 'The *exact* position of each mark matters,' he said quietly. 'One millimetre off, and the island moves by a full day's flight.' He took the pen from me with great care and began again from the first dot.
exact:0.cnHint: 老赫姆叫我停笔，说每条线的____位置都至关重要。
exact:0.hook: Even his steady hand paused at one mark, as if the line refused to be copied.
exact:0.line: 'The *exact* position of each mark — one mistake and we fly the wrong way entirely.'

guest:0.en: Old Helm set out a third cup of tea without being asked, then turned to the archive director still standing by the door. 'You are a *guest* in our chart room tonight,' he said warmly. 'Sit down. Whatever you know about these fragments, share it at your own pace. We have time.'
guest:0.cnHint: 老赫姆请档案馆长坐下，说他今晚是我们地图室的____。
guest:0.hook: The director sat, wrapped both hands around the cup, and said: 'I drew those fragments myself.'
guest:0.line: 'You are a *guest* here tonight — please, sit and tell us what you know.'

massive:0.en: At the center of the table, when all the fragments finally lay in their correct places, a single island filled the joined map from edge to edge. It was *massive* — wider than any island our troupe had ever visited, its peaks tall enough to scrape the underside of the cloud layer above the floating world.
massive:0.cnHint: 所有碎片拼合后，中央出现一座____的岛屿，大得令人屏息。
massive:0.hook: Old Helm traced its outline with one finger and said nothing for a very long time.
massive:0.line: 'That island is *massive* — I have sailed thirty years and never seen its equal.'

mix:0.en: Inside the map room, Old Helm spread three kinds of old paper across the table — each piece carried part of a route. 'A *mix* of sea charts, wind records, and island sketches,' he said. Together they formed something neither alone could show: a path to the edge of the known sky.
mix:0.cnHint: 老舵在地图室里将三种纸张拼在一起，发现它们合成了一条通往天边的航路。
mix:0.hook: But one piece had a symbol none of us recognised.
mix:0.line: 'This *mix* of charts is the only map we have left.'

necessity:0.en: Bell pressed her ear to the wall of the archive room and listened. 'There is a hollow space behind this shelf,' she said quietly. She pulled out the heaviest books with careful hands. Moving them was a *necessity* — the door we needed was hidden behind them, sealed with a lock shaped like a star.
necessity:0.cnHint: 小铃在档案室发现书架后方有暗门，搬开那些书是____的。
necessity:0.hook: The star-shaped lock began to glow before she even touched it.
necessity:0.line: 'Reaching that door is a *necessity* if we want to move on.'

stuff:0.en: The storage loft above the common room was packed floor to ceiling. Rolls of rope, jars of dried roots, folded sky-maps — all the *stuff* of a long journey crammed into one small space. Old Helm climbed up and pushed things aside until he found, beneath a woolen blanket, a single glowing compass.
stuff:0.cnHint: 老舵在公共房间上方的储物阁里翻找，在一堆旅行____中发现了一枚发光的罗盘。
stuff:0.hook: The compass needle pointed straight down, through the floor.
stuff:0.line: 'All this *stuff* and the one thing we need was at the bottom.'

translate:0.en: On the reading table lay a stone tablet covered in marks that looked almost like letters but were not quite. Bell traced each mark with her finger. 'I think I can *translate* this,' she said slowly. 'Each symbol stands for a direction — not north or south, but up or further up.'
translate:0.cnHint: 小铃在阅览桌上发现一块石碑，尝试将上面的符号____成方向指示。
translate:0.hook: The last symbol pointed somewhere no island was supposed to be.
translate:0.line: 'Give me an hour and I will *translate* every mark on this stone.'

wander:0.en: I was not supposed to leave the main corridor, but my feet began to *wander* through the lower halls of the archive on their own. Each room held shelves of sealed jars, each jar holding a folded map. The air smelled of cedar and old ink, and the lamps burned a soft amber that made everything feel dreamlike.
wander:0.cnHint: 叙述者独自在档案馆下层____，发现每个房间都摆满了装有地图的密封罐。
wander:0.hook: Then I opened a door and found a room that held only one jar.
wander:0.line: 'Do not *wander* too far — some halls here have no way back.'

warn:0.en: Old Helm held up his hand before we stepped into the chart room. 'I must *warn* you,' he said, voice low and steady, 'the maps in here are not fixed. They change when someone reads them. Look at a route long enough and it will shift to match what you fear most.' We all stood still for a moment.
warn:0.cnHint: 老舵在大家进入图表室前____众人，那里的地图会随阅读者的内心而改变。
warn:0.hook: I looked down and my map had already started to change.
warn:0.line: 'I *warn* you — do not stare at any single map for too long.'

advocate:0.en: A visitor sat in the corner of the reading room, wrapped in a coat the colour of cloud. She introduced herself as an *advocate* for old routes — someone who spent her life arguing that forgotten paths should be recorded and kept. 'Every erased road,' she told us, 'is a story the sky loses forever.' Old Helm nodded slowly.
advocate:0.cnHint: 阅览室里有位旧航路的____者，她认为每一条被遗忘的路都是天空失去的故事。
advocate:0.hook: Then she unrolled a map that showed a route nobody alive had sailed.
advocate:0.line: 'I am an *advocate* for every road the world has tried to forget.'

cite:0.en: Bell pulled a small worn book from her coat and opened it to a dog-eared page. 'I want to *cite* this,' she said, reading aloud a passage about sky-islands that appear only when two stars align. Old Helm crossed his arms, unsure. But the passage matched the stone tablet exactly, word for careful word.
cite:0.cnHint: 小铃从书中____一段关于双星对齐时才会出现的空中岛屿的描述，与石碑内容完全吻合。
cite:0.hook: Old Helm uncrossed his arms and reached for the tablet.
cite:0.line: 'Let me *cite* one passage — it changes everything we thought we knew.'

content:0.en: Inside the map room, Old Helm spread the latest chart across a wide table. Every island we had visited glowed with a soft mark. I looked at the completed corners and felt quietly *content* — not finished, not settled, but at peace with how far we had come.
content:0.cnHint: 老船长把地图铺开，我看着走过的路，感到____。
content:0.hook: Then one glowing mark began to fade.
content:0.line: 'I am *content* with what this map shows — for now,' said Old Helm.

divide:0.en: Old Helm traced a long ridge on the chart pinned to the cabin wall. 'This valley does not connect the two islands,' he said. 'It *divides* them — one side holds cold winds, the other holds warm light.' Bell leaned in, marking both halves with a different colour.
divide:0.cnHint: 老船长解释地图上有道山脊，把两座岛____开来。
divide:0.hook: Neither side showed a safe path through.
divide:0.line: 'See how the ridge *divides* the whole island into two worlds,' Old Helm said.

generate:0.en: Bell crouched beside a small crystal lantern fixed to the floor of the chart room. 'Touch the word fragment to its surface,' she said. I pressed the paper shard against the crystal, and it began to *generate* a warm hum, drawing lines of light that slowly shaped the next island on our map.
generate:0.cnHint: 小铃让我把文字碎片贴近水晶，它开始____出光芒，绘出新的岛屿。
generate:0.hook: The light drew an island none of us recognised.
generate:0.line: 'One small word can *generate* enough light to chart a whole new sky,' Bell said.

operate:0.en: The ship's steering wheel had seized up during the night. Old Helm opened a panel behind it and began to *operate* on the tangle of gears inside, hands steady, breath slow. Bell held the lantern close. I handed him each small tool in silence, afraid that one wrong move would leave us drifting.
operate:0.cnHint: 舵轮卡住了，老船长打开面板，开始____里面的齿轮。
operate:0.hook: Outside, the island we were aiming for began to drift away.
operate:0.line: 'I can *operate* on these gears, but keep the ship perfectly still,' Old Helm said.

properly:0.en: I tried to fold the new map fragment on my own, but the edges refused to line up. Silverfang appeared in the doorway of the chart room, arms crossed. 'You have to crease it *properly* first,' she said, taking it from my hands with care and folding it into a neat, flat square in three quick moves.
properly:0.cnHint: 我折地图折不好，银牙出现并教我如何____地折叠它。
properly:0.hook: The square glowed the moment it was folded right.
properly:0.line: 'Fold it *properly* or the map will never show the true path,' Silverfang said.

render:0.en: Old Helm held the torn fragment up to the lantern. The heat did not burn it. Instead it seemed to *render* the pale ink visible — shapes of cliffs and bridges rose from what had looked like a blank page. Bell whispered that some maps only revealed themselves under warmth, like secrets meant for patient hands.
render:0.cnHint: 老船长把碎纸片靠近灯光，热度____隐藏的地图清晰可见。
render:0.hook: The last shape to appear was a door with no island around it.
render:0.line: 'A little warmth can *render* even the most hidden lines visible,' Old Helm said.

resolve:0.en: The map showed a gap — a wide, empty sky between two island chains with no marked route. We stood around the table in silence. Then I felt a quiet *resolve* settle in my chest, the kind that does not shout but simply decides. I picked up the pen and drew a small question mark where the gap was, as a promise.
resolve:0.cnHint: 地图上有一段空白，我心中升起一股____，拿起笔在空白处做了记号。
resolve:0.hook: The question mark began to glow on its own.
resolve:0.line: 'I have the *resolve* to cross that gap, even without a road,' I said.

seemingly:0.en: The fragment we found that morning was *seemingly* blank — pale, thin, without a single line. Bell turned it over twice and set it aside. But when Old Helm placed it at the centre of the assembled map, every surrounding piece shifted, and the blank sheet filled with the clearest chart we had ever seen.
seemingly:0.cnHint: 那张____空白的碎片让小铃放弃了，但拼上后它变成了最清晰的地图。
seemingly:0.hook: The centre of the chart showed our own ship, moving.
seemingly:0.line: 'It is *seemingly* empty, but never trust a blank page,' said Old Helm.

teenager:0.en: Inside the map room, a shelf held glass jars, each sealed with wax. Old Helm lifted one and smiled. 'This word was left by a *teenager*,' he said softly — someone young enough to wonder at everything, old enough to write it down. The jar held a single folded card. On it: a new island's name.
teenager:0.cnHint: 老舵手打开一个封蜡玻璃罐，发现里面藏着一个____留下的地图线索。
teenager:0.hook: The name on the card matched no island any of us had ever heard of.
teenager:0.line: 'This word was found by a *teenager* who sailed here alone at dawn.'

patient:0.en: Bell sat cross-legged on the floor of the chart room, tracing ink lines with one finger. She had been *patient* for hours — still, calm, unhurried — while the rest of us grew restless. Then she looked up. 'Got it,' she said. 'The passage only opens at low tide.' The room felt lighter at once.
patient:0.cnHint: 贝尔在海图室里____地等待，终于找到了航道开启的规律。
patient:0.hook: Low tide was less than one hour away.
patient:0.line: 'You have to be *patient* — the map only speaks when the room is quiet.'

classroom:0.en: The old building at the island's heart had once been a *classroom*: rows of small wooden desks, a blackboard still chalked with star charts, dusty books stacked in the corners. Old Helm walked the rows slowly. 'Someone taught navigation here,' he murmured. Under the teacher's desk, we found a sealed word-jar.
classroom:0.cnHint: 在小岛中心的旧____里，老舵手找到了一个藏有地图碎片的密封罐。
classroom:0.hook: The chalk star chart on the board matched our next destination exactly.
classroom:0.line: 'Every great sailor once sat in a *classroom* just like this one.'

vehicle:0.en: The floating barge in the dock bay was unlike anything I had seen. Silverfang called it a *vehicle* — a means to carry not just people but whole stories from island to island. Its hull was painted with faded words. Bell pressed her palm to the wood and whispered, 'It still knows the way.' We climbed aboard.
vehicle:0.cnHint: 银牙船长指着码头里的旧驳船说，那是载运故事的____，船身上写满了褪色的词语。
vehicle:0.hook: The barge began to move before anyone touched the wheel.
vehicle:0.line: 'This old *vehicle* has crossed every gap on our map at least once.'

remote:0.en: Old Helm spread the new chart across the table. One island sat far from the others, ringed by clouds. 'That one is *remote*,' he said — so far and hard to reach that no one in the troupe had visited it. The word-jar we had just opened pulsed with faint light. It was pulling us toward that very island.
remote:0.cnHint: 老舵手在海图上指出一座____的孤岛，刚打开的词罐正发着光，把大家引向那里。
remote:0.hook: No route on any chart led directly to that distant island.
remote:0.line: 'The most *remote* islands always hold the rarest words — trust me.'

zoo:0.en: The lower deck of the station house smelled of hay and warm fur. Someone long ago had kept animals here — a private *zoo* of island creatures, each pen labelled in neat hand-writing. Most were empty now. But in the last pen, curled asleep, was a small silver fox. Beside it lay a word-jar, still sealed.
zoo:0.cnHint: 在驿站下层，一排标着名字的动物围栏让大家想到了____，最后一格里睡着一只小银狐，旁边放着词罐。
zoo:0.hook: The fox opened one eye and looked straight at me.
zoo:0.line: 'Old Helm once told me this station used to be a tiny *zoo* for sky-creatures.'

card:0.en: Bell slid open the narrow drawer beneath the map table and found a single *card* inside — stiff paper printed with an island's outline, a number, and three stars. She held it to the lamp. 'This is a passage card,' she said. 'It grants entry to a locked isle.' None of us had seen one before. Old Helm's eyes went wide.
card:0.cnHint: 贝尔在地图桌抽屉里发现了一张____，上面印有一座锁定岛屿的通行信息。
card:0.hook: The locked island's name was the one word none of our maps had ever shown.
card:0.line: 'Whoever holds the *card* holds the right to open the next door — guard it well.'

gene:0.en: The science corner of the island library held jars of pressed plants and careful notes. One notebook described how certain sky-flowers passed their glow from parent to child — a kind of *gene*, a secret carried in the seed. Old Helm read aloud quietly. Bell smiled. 'So the light is inherited,' she said. 'The island remembers its own.'
gene:0.cnHint: 图书馆科学角的笔记记录了天空花卉如何将光芒通过____一代代传递下去。
gene:0.hook: The notebook's last page held a map to the valley where the flowers still bloomed.
gene:0.line: 'Bell says the glow is written in their *gene* — the flower cannot help but shine.'

childhood:0.en: Inside the map room, Old Helm spread a worn chart across the table. A faded drawing caught my eye — a small figure on a floating island, arms wide open. 'That was me,' he said softly. His *childhood* home had once drifted here, above these very clouds.
childhood:0.cnHint: 老舵在地图室里指着一幅旧图，讲述他____时期曾住在这片浮岛上。
childhood:0.hook: But the island on the chart had no name.
childhood:0.line: 'My *childhood* taught me that every island holds a secret.'

equal:0.en: Bell laid two map fragments side by side on the wooden floor. She measured each edge with a thin cord, brow furrowed. After a long pause, she smiled. The lengths were *equal* — the two pieces fit together perfectly, opening a path we had never seen before.
equal:0.cnHint: 小铃发现两块地图碎片的边长____，它们竟能拼在一起。
equal:0.hook: The joined map glowed once, then went dark.
equal:0.line: 'No road is *equal* to the one you have never walked.'

inspire:0.en: Old Helm pinned a new word to the board at the centre of the map room. Just seeing it seemed to *inspire* every member of the troupe — Bell began sketching routes, and even the quiet cook started humming. One small word, and the whole room came alive.
inspire:0.cnHint: 一个新单词被钉在公告板上，____了船员们各自行动起来。
inspire:0.hook: No one noticed the word slowly rising off the board.
inspire:0.line: 'Let this place *inspire* you — we move at dawn.'

narrow:0.en: The map room had one small window, and the passage leading to it was *narrow* — only one person could enter at a time. Old Helm went first, then Bell, then me. I had to turn sideways and breathe in just to squeeze through.
narrow:0.cnHint: 地图室的入口十分____，大家只能侧身一个接一个进入。
narrow:0.hook: Something on the other side was breathing.
narrow:0.line: 'A *narrow* door never stopped a curious mind.'

quantity:0.en: Scattered across the map table lay a huge *quantity* of word-fragments — more than I had ever seen in one place. Bell sorted them into small piles by colour, her fingers moving fast. Old Helm watched and said each one was a door waiting to be opened.
quantity:0.cnHint: 桌上摆着大____的单词碎片，小铃正忙着将它们分类整理。
quantity:0.hook: One pile kept growing, though no one added to it.
quantity:0.line: 'The *quantity* of words we carry decides how far we sail.'

sustainable:0.en: Old Helm pointed to the glowing lanterns that lined the map room walls. 'Starlight feeds them,' he explained. As long as the troupe kept moving and collecting words, the light would never go out. It was a *sustainable* system — energy born from curiosity itself.
sustainable:0.cnHint: 地图室的灯靠星光运转，老舵说这是一种____的能源方式。
sustainable:0.hook: Then one lantern flickered and turned a deep red.
sustainable:0.line: 'A *sustainable* journey depends on wonder, not on fuel.'

delay:0.en: A thick fog had rolled in around the island, and Bell warned that setting off now would be dangerous. The troupe gathered in the map room, restless but patient. Old Helm said any *delay* was just time spent learning, and handed each of us a new word to study.
delay:0.cnHint: 浓雾让队伍不得不____出发，老舵却说这段等待时间同样有意义。
delay:0.hook: Outside, something moved through the fog toward us.
delay:0.line: 'Do not fear the *delay* — the sky always clears.'

identity:0.en: On the far wall of the map room hung a board covered in small tags. Each tag held a name and a word. Bell explained that every troupe member chose one word to mark their *identity* — a sign of what they believed in. Mine was still blank, waiting for me.
identity:0.cnHint: 地图室的墙上挂满名牌，每块牌子代表一位成员的____，而我的还是空的。
identity:0.hook: Someone had already written a word on my tag.
identity:0.line: 'Your chosen word becomes your *identity* on these islands.'

therefore:0.en: The map room smelled of old wood and lamp oil. Bell spread three torn pieces of sky-chart across the table and studied them in silence. Two pieces matched — their star patterns lined up perfectly. 'These two islands share the same wind current,' she said, 'and *therefore* this third fragment must lie between them.' She pressed the pieces together, and a new island name glowed faintly on the joined edge.
therefore:0.cnHint: 小铃在地图室里拼合星图碎片，用逻辑____出第三块碎片的位置。
therefore:0.hook: But the glowing name was one Old Helm had crossed off long ago.
therefore:0.line: 'Two currents meet here, and *therefore* the island cannot be far.'

truth:0.en: Old Helm kept a small journal locked in the map room cabinet. One evening he left it open by mistake. I only read one line before I looked away: 'The word we seek may not be a place at all.' I closed the journal and said nothing. But the *truth* of that line settled into me like a stone into still water, heavy and quiet, changing the shape of everything below.
truth:0.cnHint: 我在地图室意外看到老掌舵的日记，一行字揭示了令人不安的____。
truth:0.hook: That night, the map fragment in my pocket felt suddenly very different.
truth:0.line: 'We have chased many rumours — but this, at last, is the *truth*.'

protein:0.en: Bell had organised the map room shelves with surprising care. Jars of dried beans, folded notes on island climates, and a worn notebook titled 'Long Voyages.' She opened it to a page of meal plans. 'Every sailor needs enough *protein* on a long crossing,' she said, tapping a careful list of seeds and fish, 'or your hands shake when you need them steady.' I reached up to help sort the jars, feeling like I finally belonged.
protein:0.cnHint: 小铃在地图室里展示她的航行准备笔记，解释长途旅行中____的重要性。
protein:0.hook: On the last shelf, behind the jars, sat a jar labelled with a star name I did not know.
protein:0.line: 'No *protein*, no steady hands — and no steady hands means no safe landing.'

traffic:0.en: The map room had one small round window that looked down on the dock island below. Old Helm stood at it every morning, watching. 'More boats than last week,' he murmured.
