bean:0.en: The kitchen was warm and steaming. Bell stood over a wide pot, dropping in handfuls of a small dark *bean* she had traded for on the last island. 'One cup of these,' she said, stirring slowly, 'and you can stay awake long enough to watch an entire constellation move across the sky.'
bean:0.cnHint: 贝尔在厨房里用她用以物换物得来的____煮了一锅能让人保持清醒的饮料。
bean:0.hook: Old Helm appeared at the door, eyes wide and eager.
bean:0.line: 'This little *bean* holds more energy than a full night of wind in our sails.'

birthday:0.en: A small paper banner hung across the storage room doorway. Old Helm had written on it in careful letters: FOR BELL. 'Today is her *birthday*,' he whispered to me, eyes bright. The whole troupe had gathered inside, holding a lantern each. When Bell stepped through the door, the room filled with soft golden light.
birthday:0.cnHint: 老舵手悄悄在储物室里为贝尔准备了一个____惊喜，全团的人都举着灯笼等着她。
birthday:0.hook: Bell pressed a hand to her heart and said nothing at all.
birthday:0.line: 'A *birthday* on a floating island — I cannot imagine a better place to grow older.'

flight:0.en: Old Helm pinned a chart to the wall of the planning room. It showed a long curving line from island to island — the troupe's next *flight* across the open sky. Bell traced it with one finger. 'Twelve stops,' she said quietly. 'Each one a word we have not yet learned.' The room held its breath.
flight:0.cnHint: 老舵手在规划室里挂出了旅队下一段____的航线图，贝尔数出了沿途十二个未知的停靠点。
flight:0.hook: The last stop on the chart had no name — only a question mark.
flight:0.line: 'Every *flight* we make is a sentence the sky is writing about us.'

female:0.en: Inside the map room, a small cage held a tiny creature with bright orange wings. Old Helm leaned close and whispered that the *female* of this species carries a seed in her feathers — one that, once planted, grows into a new island. We had to earn her trust first.
female:0.cnHint: 地图室里，老舵主告诉我，这只小生灵的____身体里藏着一粒能生出新岛的种子。
female:0.hook: The creature tilted her head and seemed to be choosing us.
female:0.line: 'This *female* holds a secret no map has ever shown,' said Old Helm.

holiday:0.en: The troupe had stopped at the Lantern Inn for what Bell called a well-earned *holiday*. Paper lights floated along the ceiling beams, and warm soup filled every bowl. I had never seen Old Helm laugh so freely. Outside, the wind carried the next word to us on a folded leaf.
holiday:0.cnHint: 在灯笼客栈，贝尔宣布大家享受一段____，老舵主笑得前所未有地开怀。
holiday:0.hook: The folded leaf landed in my soup, trembling with urgency.
holiday:0.line: 'Even on *holiday*, the map finds a way to reach us,' Bell said.

pain:0.en: Bell pressed her fingers against the old compass wound on her palm and breathed slowly. 'Every *pain* teaches direction,' she said quietly, tracing the scar across the wooden table. Old Helm placed a warm cup beside her hand. The compass on the wall began to spin, pointing somewhere new.
pain:0.cnHint: 贝尔看着手心的旧伤，说每一处____都教会了她辨别方向。
pain:0.hook: The spinning compass stopped, aimed at a place none of us knew.
pain:0.line: 'Every *pain* I have felt has pointed me somewhere important,' Bell said.

player:0.en: A board game covered the entire floor of the inn's back room. Old Helm explained that each *player* must trade a word-token to move forward, and the one who reaches the centre wins a fragment of the lost sky chart. I placed my token down, heart thumping, and the board lit up.
player:0.cnHint: 旅馆后室铺着一张巨大棋盘，老舵主说每位____都要用词语换取前行的机会。
player:0.hook: The board lit up, and a hidden door clicked open beneath it.
player:0.line: 'Every *player* here has wagered something real,' Old Helm said with a grin.

production:0.en: Rows of glowing jars lined the shelves of the island's only workshop. Old Helm explained that the *production* of these sky-lamps required a single spoken word sealed inside each jar, and without that word the light would simply die. I held one up and felt the word hum against my fingers.
production:0.cnHint: 工坊里，老舵主解释说每盏天灯的____都需要在罐中封入一个词语，否则灯光就会熄灭。
production:0.hook: The jar in my hand flickered, as if it had already heard my secret.
production:0.line: 'The *production* of one lamp takes one true word,' Old Helm said.

secure:0.en: Bell knotted the last rope across the hatch and stepped back to check her work. 'The chest is *secure*,' she said, satisfied. Inside it rested the three map fragments we had collected since morning. A low rumble passed through the floor, and the walls of the inn swayed like a slow breath.
secure:0.cnHint: 贝尔把箱子上的绳索系好，确认碎片已经____，但随后地板传来一阵震动。
secure:0.hook: The walls swayed, and the locked chest slid an inch toward the window.
secure:0.line: 'Nothing leaves this room until that chest is *secure*,' Bell said firmly.

audience:0.en: Old Helm spread a worn map across the table and cleared his throat as though addressing a grand *audience*. Bell and I leaned in, the only listeners in the quiet room. He traced a silver line to an island shaped like a crescent and told us it only appeared during a storm.
audience:0.cnHint: 老舵主展开旧地图，清了清嗓子，仿佛面对众多____，向我们讲述那座月牙形的岛屿。
audience:0.hook: Outside, the first drops of a coming storm tapped the window glass.
audience:0.line: 'Even an *audience* of two deserves the full story,' Old Helm said warmly.

borrow:0.en: I needed a word-lens to read the faded inscription, but mine had cracked that morning. Silverfang stood in the doorway and offered hers without hesitation. 'You may *borrow* it,' she said, 'but bring it back before the stars shift.' I pressed the lens to the page and the old letters blazed gold.
borrow:0.cnHint: 我的词语透镜碎了，银牙船长主动让我____她的，条件是星象变化前归还。
borrow:0.hook: The gold letters rearranged themselves into a name I already knew.
borrow:0.line: 'You may *borrow* it, but every lens remembers what it has read,' Silverfang said.

burn:0.en: Inside the map-room, Old Helm unrolled a chart so old its edges had turned brown. A candle had once fallen on it, leaving a dark *burn* across the southern islands. 'That mark,' he told me quietly, 'shows where the sky-fire touched the world and left its scar.'
burn:0.cnHint: 老舵主展示那张古老地图时，地图边缘有一道____的痕迹。
burn:0.hook: Something beneath that scar was still glowing faint and warm.
burn:0.line: 'This *burn* is the oldest mark on any map we own,' Old Helm said.

cook:0.en: Bell spread ingredients across the narrow table and began to *cook* a simple soup for the whole troupe. The smell of herbs drifted through the cabin and drew everyone in from their corners. Old Helm said a warm meal before a long journey was its own kind of wisdom.
cook:0.cnHint: 领航员在船舱里为大家____了一锅热汤，让所有人聚在一起。
cook:0.hook: But Bell had added something strange to the pot this time.
cook:0.line: 'I will *cook* enough for everyone — sit down and rest,' Bell said warmly.

corporate:0.en: Old Helm pulled out a sealed letter stamped with a heavy wax seal. 'It is a *corporate* order,' he said, 'signed by the island council as one body, not any single person.' Bell frowned. A ruling made by an entire council was harder to argue with than a lone captain's word.
corporate:0.cnHint: 老舵主收到一封盖有印章的____命令，让整个小队感到为难。
corporate:0.hook: Someone on that council, though, had slipped in a secret warning.
corporate:0.line: 'A *corporate* seal means every elder agreed — we cannot simply ignore it,' Old Helm said.

dangerous:0.en: The inner room of the archive held the oldest word-fragments of all. 'It is *dangerous* in there,' Bell warned me, gripping my sleeve. 'The shelves shift on their own, and more than one navigator has walked in and never found the door again.' I stepped forward anyway, lantern raised.
dangerous:0.cnHint: 领航员警告我，档案室深处十分____，曾有人进去后再没出来。
dangerous:0.hook: The door swung shut behind me with a soft, final click.
dangerous:0.line: 'It is *dangerous* to go alone — take the lantern and stay close,' Bell said.

debt:0.en: Old Helm set the ledger on the table and traced a column with one finger. 'We have a *debt* to the word-keeper of Crestholm,' he said quietly. 'She lent us the northern chart when we had nothing, and we have not yet returned the favour.' The cabin felt heavier after he said that.
debt:0.cnHint: 老舵主翻开账本，说明小队对某位地图守护者还有一份____未还。
debt:0.hook: Crestholm was the next island on the route, and she would be waiting.
debt:0.line: 'A *debt* like this one should be settled before we go any further,' Old Helm said.

discipline:0.en: Bell ran the morning check with quiet *discipline*: instruments tested, charts rolled, every lamp trimmed. There was no shouting and no wasted motion. Watching her, I understood that keeping a sky-vessel in order was not about strict rules but about care repeated every single day without fail.
discipline:0.cnHint: 领航员以严格的____完成每天早晨的例行检查，让我深感敬佩。
discipline:0.hook: Yet today one instrument gave a reading she had never seen before.
discipline:0.line: '*Discipline* in small things is what keeps us alive up here,' Bell said evenly.

error:0.en: I had copied the word-fragment onto the new chart, but Bell checked my work and tapped the page gently. 'There is an *error* here — you shifted the marker half a degree east.' Such a small mistake, yet at the speed we travelled it would have carried us over empty sky instead of solid ground.
error:0.cnHint: 我抄写地图时出了一个小____，领航员及时发现，避免了迷航。
error:0.hook: Bell did not say how many times that same error had doomed others before.
error:0.line: 'Correct the *error* now, while we are still close enough to check it,' Bell said.

gym:0.en: Below the main deck there was a low-ceilinged room Old Helm called the *gym*. Ropes hung from the beams, and a worn wooden floor showed the scuff-marks of a hundred mornings of practice. 'Every member of this troupe trains here,' he said. 'Strong legs and steady hands keep you alive in a hard landing.'
gym:0.cnHint: 老舵主带我参观船上的____，告诉我每个团员都要在这里训练。
gym:0.hook: A pair of old boots in the corner suggested someone had left in a hurry.
gym:0.line: 'The *gym* looks simple, but it has saved more lives than any map,' Old Helm said.

mile:0.en: Inside the chart room, Old Helm unrolled a wide map across the table. A thin red line marked our path from island to island. 'We have travelled nearly a *mile* of sky,' he said softly, tracing each stop with one careful finger. The room smelled of old paper and distant wind.
mile:0.cnHint: 老掌舵人在图表室里展开地图，用手指沿路线一一描过，感叹我们走过的____。
mile:0.hook: But the red line stopped — and beyond it, the map was blank.
mile:0.line: 'We have come nearly a *mile* of sky, and the hardest part is still ahead.'

movement:0.en: Bell stood at the wide window inside the navigation post, watching the clouds below. She pressed one hand flat against the glass. 'There,' she whispered. A slow *movement* rippled through the distant fog — something large turning beneath it, like a sleeping island waking up. No one else had noticed yet.
movement:0.cnHint: 小铃在领航室的窗前凝视云雾，发现远处云层中出现了神秘的____。
movement:0.hook: Whatever moved down there was heading straight toward us.
movement:0.line: 'That *movement* in the fog — it is not wind, and it is not clouds.'

party:0.en: We gathered in the warm lamp-light of the common room. Old Helm called us a travelling *party*, which made Bell laugh and me feel proud. He spread three small word-stones on the table — each one a fragment of tonight's destination. Together we studied them, voices low, the fire crackling between us and the dark.
party:0.cnHint: 老掌舵人在公共室里把我们称为一支旅行____，并摆出三块字石让大家研究。
party:0.hook: One stone glowed faintly — a colour none of us had ever seen.
party:0.line: 'Every great *party* needs a navigator, and Bell, that is you tonight.'

rescue:0.en: Rain hammered the roof of the shelter hut. Old Helm had found the small wooden box wedged under a broken beam — inside it, a folded note. Someone had planned a *rescue* here long before we arrived, leaving rope, a lantern, and dried food for a person who never came. The lantern was still warm.
rescue:0.cnHint: 在避难小屋里，老掌舵人发现了一个木箱，里面藏着一份为某次____而备下的物资。
rescue:0.hook: The name on the note — was Bell's.
rescue:0.line: 'Someone prepared this *rescue* kit knowing exactly who would need it.'

writing:0.en: I found a leather journal tucked behind a loose stone in the archive room wall. The pages were full of small, careful *writing* — maps, notes, lists of words collected island by island. The hand looked familiar. Bell leaned over my shoulder, went very quiet, then said, 'That belonged to my teacher.' Her voice did not shake.
writing:0.cnHint: 我在档案室的夹墙中发现了一本皮革日记，里面满是关于岛屿的____。
writing:0.hook: On the last page was a single unfinished sentence, ending mid-word.
writing:0.line: 'This *writing* is older than the troupe itself — someone knew our route before us.'

bite:0.en: Old Helm set a small loaf of bread on the map table and told us to eat before studying. I took one *bite* and tasted something unexpected — a faint sweetness, like the fruit from the island we had just left. 'The baker there traded us flour,' Bell explained, smiling. Even bread could carry a memory.
bite:0.cnHint: 老掌舵人让大家在研究地图前先吃东西，我咬了____面包，尝出了熟悉的味道。
bite:0.hook: Then Old Helm tapped the map and said, 'That island should not have had fruit trees.'
bite:0.line: 'Take a *bite* — you will need the strength before this night is over.'

capture:0.en: Bell had set up a small glass box near the porthole. Inside it, a scrap of cloud drifted in slow circles. 'I managed to *capture* a bit of the storm we flew through,' she said proudly. The cloud glowed faint blue. Old Helm studied it for a long time, then asked where, exactly, she had collected it.
capture:0.cnHint: 小铃在舷窗旁摆了个玻璃盒，她设法____了一小片穿越风暴时的云。
capture:0.hook: Old Helm's face went still — that shade of blue meant only one thing.
capture:0.line: 'I tried to *capture* its light, but it changed colour the moment it was inside.'

cope:0.en: The archive room was full of boxes, and Old Helm looked tired. I watched him sort through a stack of faded word-stones, one by one. 'How do you *cope* with so many lost maps?' I asked. He paused, then smiled. 'I treat each one as a new beginning,' he said, 'not a lost ending.' The lamp flickered softly.
cope:0.cnHint: 档案室乱成一团，我问老掌舵人是如何____这么多残缺地图带来的压力的。
cope:0.hook: Then he handed me the oldest stone — and it was warm in my hand.
cope:0.line: 'You learn to *cope* by remembering why you started the journey in the first place.'

housing:0.en: The inn on Amber Isle had low ceilings and warm lantern light. Old Helm spread the map across a crooked table. 'This whole district was built on cloud-stone,' he said, tapping a drawing of tight-packed rooftops. 'Decent *housing* keeps a crew sharp — cold bones make poor navigators.' I pulled my coat closer and decided he was right.
housing:0.cnHint: 老舵手说，好的____能让船员保持状态，我们在一家矮屋顶小旅馆里研究地图。
housing:0.hook: But one room on the top floor had a locked door no key could open.
housing:0.line: 'Good *housing* keeps a crew sharp — remember that.'

behaviour:0.en: Bell set the new word-fragment on the common room table and we all leaned in. The fragment glowed a soft amber. Old Helm watched it in silence, then looked at me. 'A map responds to *behaviour*,' he said. 'Greedy hands dim it. Patient ones let it breathe.' I kept very still. The glow brightened, and a new island outline appeared at the edge.
behaviour:0.cnHint: 老舵手告诉我，地图碎片会对人的____做出反应，贪婪的手会让它变暗。
behaviour:0.hook: The outline shifted, as if the island itself was deciding whether to let us in.
behaviour:0.line: 'The map always reads your *behaviour* before it shows the way.'

husband:0.en: The keeper of the Amber Isle inn was a round-faced woman named only as 'Keeper.' A small portrait hung behind her desk — a man in a sky-captain's coat. 'My *husband* charted half these islands before the clouds took his ship,' she said, without sadness. 'He left me his logs. That is how I know which guests to trust.' She handed Old Helm a folded page.
husband:0.cnHint: 客栈老板娘说，她的____曾绘制过这片群岛的地图，并留下了他的航行日志。
husband:0.hook: The folded page had a name on it that matched our newest word-fragment exactly.
husband:0.line: 'My *husband* left charts that still guide good travellers today.'

tourist:0.en: A traveller from the lower islands sat near the fire, sketching cloud shapes in a small book. 'Just a *tourist*,' Bell whispered to me, as if that settled something. But Old Helm pulled out a chair and sat beside the stranger. 'Every tourist sees what locals stop noticing,' he said. The traveller looked up and smiled, then pointed at our map. 'That path is wrong,' she said simply.
tourist:0.cnHint: 贝尔低声说那人只是个____，但老舵手却认为旁观者往往能发现本地人忽略的东西。
tourist:0.hook: Her finger rested on the exact stretch of sky-road we had been arguing about for two days.
tourist:0.line: 'Even a *tourist* can see what tired eyes miss, so listen.'

agent:0.en: A thin man in a grey coat found our table before we had ordered anything. He placed a card face-down between us. 'I am an *agent* for the Isle Council,' he said quietly. 'They know you carry word-fragments, and they want to make an arrangement.' Old Helm did not touch the card. He simply said, 'We collect for the map, not for councils.' The man in grey picked up his card and left without another word.
agent:0.cnHint: 一个自称是议会____的人找到了我们，想就碎片一事谈条件，但老舵手直接拒绝了。
agent:0.hook: Through the window we watched him step into a sky-skiff that bore no flag at all.
agent:0.line: 'I am an *agent* of the Council — they have an offer you should consider.'

cash:0.en: The inn charged three copper tokens a night, and Bell counted them out slowly while Silverfang looked on with crossed arms. 'Hard *cash* is harder to find the higher you sail,' Silverfang said. 'Up near the star-tier islands, people trade in favours and map-rights.' Bell pushed the coins forward anyway. I made a note to myself: carry more favours, fewer coins, the next time we flew high.
cash:0.cnHint: 银牙船长说，越往高空的岛屿飞，____就越难找到，人们更多以人情交换。
cash:0.hook: Silverfang's remark about map-rights hung in the air longer than it should have.
cash:0.line: 'Hard *cash* runs thin the higher you sail — learn that early.'

competition:0.en: The common room cleared a space after dinner, and two young pilots set up a word-guessing game on a round board. Old Helm watched with quiet amusement. 'Healthy *competition* sharpens the mind,' he told me. 'That is why the islands reward the curious, not just the strong.' I joined the next round, lost badly, and learned four new words. Somehow, that felt like winning.
competition:0.cnHint: 老舵手看着两个年轻飞行员比赛，说适度的____能让人头脑更敏锐。
competition:0.hook: The winner was awarded a tiny map-chip that no one in the room had ever seen before.
competition:0.line: 'A little *competition* sharpens the mind better than any textbook can.'

farmer:0.en: The last guest in the common room was a broad-shouldered man who kept his boots muddy even indoors. He grew sky-moss on a platform island one tier below us. 'People picture a *farmer* as someone who stays put,' he said, stirring his tea. 'But I move my whole field when the light shifts. Roots travel too, if you give them a reason.' Old Helm wrote something in his log and underlined it twice.
farmer:0.cnHint: 一位种植天空苔藓的____告诉我们，他会随着光线变化移动整片田地，根也可以旅行。
farmer:0.hook: Old Helm's underlined note turned out to be the exact phrase hidden in our next word-fragment.
farmer:0.line: 'A *farmer* who never moves learns nothing new about the soil.'

collection:0.en: Inside the map room, Old Helm spread his arms wide. Shelves climbed every wall, each one holding glass jars full of glowing letters. 'This,' he said proudly, 'is our *collection*.' Every word we had ever found sat there, quietly shining. I counted at least forty jars before I lost track.
collection:0.cnHint: 老舵主向新成员展示了满屋子装着发光字母的玻璃罐，那是旅团多年积累的____。
collection:0.hook: But one jar at the very top sat cracked, and its word had already escaped.
collection:0.line: 'This *collection* took twenty years to build — treat every jar with care.'

depression:0.en: Bell found me sitting alone on the cold floor of the storage cabin, staring at a blank map fragment. She set a warm cup of tea beside me without a word. 'First island failure brings a *depression* like fog,' she said softly, sitting down next to me. 'It lifts. It always lifts.'
depression:0.cnHint: 小铃发现叙述者独坐在小屋里，因第一次任务失败陷入____，便默默陪在身旁。
depression:0.hook: Then she pointed to a faint glow creeping under the cabin door.
depression:0.line: 'A *depression* this deep means you cared enough — that is a good sign.'

foot:0.en: The library ladder was old and narrow. Old Helm warned me to test each rung before trusting it. I climbed carefully, but near the top my *foot* slipped on a loose step. I grabbed the shelf just in time. A single glowing letter fell, drifted slowly, and landed in Bell's open hand below.
foot:0.cnHint: 叙述者爬上图书室的旧梯子时，____突然打滑，险些摔落，却意外掉下一个发光字母。
foot:0.hook: Bell turned the letter over and whispered that it was exactly the one they had been missing.
foot:0.line: 'Watch your *foot* on that third rung — it has surprised everyone at least once.'

graduate:0.en: On the wall of the chart room hung a long roll of names. Bell told me it was the list of every *graduate* of Old Helm's troupe who had gone on to captain their own vessel. The list was longer than I expected. Old Helm caught me reading it and smiled, saying nothing, which felt like a very full answer.
graduate:0.cnHint: 叙述者在海图室的墙上发现了一长串旧团员____的名单，老舵主的微笑意味深长。
graduate:0.hook: My own name was nowhere on the list — not yet.
graduate:0.line: 'Every *graduate* on that wall once stood exactly where you are standing now.'

intake:0.en: The engine room hummed with warm air. Silverfang showed me a copper pipe running along the ceiling. 'That is the star-dust *intake*,' she said, tapping it twice. 'It pulls light from outside and turns it into fuel.' A soft blue glow moved through the pipe like a slow river, and the whole ship breathed steadily around us.
intake:0.cnHint: 银牙向叙述者介绍发动机房的铜管，那是飞船将星尘转化为燃料的____装置。
intake:0.hook: Then the glow stuttered once, and Silverfang's expression shifted to something careful.
intake:0.line: 'Cut the *intake* valve if the glow ever turns red — do not wait to ask.'

screen:0.en: Bell had built a thin paper *screen* across one corner of the navigation room to block the starlight while she read the maps. Painted on it were small birds mid-flight. I sat on the other side of it, listening to the soft rustle of charts, and for a moment the whole ship felt like a quiet reading room drifting through the sky.
screen:0.cnHint: 小铃在导航室角落支起一扇画着飞鸟的纸质____，隔开星光，专心研读海图。
screen:0.hook: Then one of the painted birds seemed to move, and Bell went very still.
screen:0.line: 'The *screen* keeps the starlight out when I need to read the faint lines.'

chair:0.en: At the centre of the map room stood a tall wooden seat that nobody sat in. Old Helm called it the *chair* of first words, and said it was for the person who discovered a new island. Every troupe member had taken a turn in it at least once. He looked at me slowly. I suddenly felt both very small and very ready.
chair:0.cnHint: 地图室中央有一把"初语____"，专属于发现新岛屿的人，老舵主意味深长地看向叙述者。
chair:0.hook: Old Helm placed one hand on its back and said my name, quiet as a question.
chair:0.line: 'No one sits in that *chair* until they bring back a word that opens a new path.'

court:0.en: Silverfang spread a wide map across the table and pointed to a blank square near the edge. 'Go there with the wrong word,' she said, 'and you *court* real trouble. The winds read intent.' Old Helm nodded. Bell added the new fragment we had found, and the blank square slowly filled with the outline of an island none of us had ever seen.
court:0.cnHint: 银牙警告叙述者，带着错误的词前往地图边缘会____危险，随后新岛屿的轮廓浮现出来。
court:0.hook: The island's outline kept shifting, as if it had not yet decided what shape to be.
court:0.line: 'Use the wrong word out there and you *court* the kind of storm no sail can outrun.'

salary:0.en: Inside the troupe's map room, Old Helm spread coins across the table and frowned. 'We found three words this week,' he said, 'but our costs are climbing.' Bell looked up from her charts. A fair *salary* for every member kept the troupe loyal and moving — without it, the islands ahead would stay forever out of reach.
salary:0.cnHint: 老舵手在地图室里计算团员的____，担心费用不够支撑接下来的旅程。
salary:0.hook: One coin was missing — and only Bell had been alone with the chest.
salary:0.line: 'A fair *salary* keeps every good navigator at her post,' Old Helm said.

shopping:0.en: The supply dock on Amber Isle smelled of spice and sawdust. Bell handed me a list and a small purse. '*Shopping* here is the only way to restock before the next jump,' she said with a wink. I moved from stall to stall, trading words — the troupe's strange currency — for rope, dried fruit, and a new lantern.
shopping:0.cnHint: 贝尔让我在琥珀岛的补给码头____，用"词语"换取旅途所需的物资。
shopping:0.hook: The last stall keeper studied my list and slowly shook her head.
shopping:0.line: '*Shopping* with words instead of coins — only our troupe does that,' Bell laughed.

tendency:0.en: Old Helm tapped the wall chart and sighed. 'Notice anything?' The paths we had taken all curved left. Bell nodded: 'We have a *tendency* to follow the warmer wind, even when the cold route is shorter.' It was a small habit, but habits shape journeys — and some islands only appeared on the cold side of the sky.
tendency:0.cnHint: 老舵手发现团队有一种____，总是选择温暖的风向，却因此错过了某些岛屿。
tendency:0.hook: The cold route glowed faintly on the chart — as if it had been waiting.
tendency:0.line: 'That *tendency* of ours has cost us three islands already,' Old Helm said quietly.

tough:0.en: The repair bay was dim and smelled of engine oil. Bell wrestled with a bent rudder bar, her hands white from effort. 'This metal is *tough*,' she muttered, 'but so am I.' Old Helm passed her a heavier wrench without a word. By the time the stars outside had moved a hand's width, the bar was straight again.
tough:0.cnHint: 贝尔在修理舱里费力修复弯曲的舵杆，材料十分____，但她毫不退缩。
tough:0.hook: The rudder held — yet a second crack ran deeper than the first.
tough:0.line: 'The metal is *tough*, but we leave at dawn no matter what,' Bell said.

tour:0.en: 'Before we chase the next word,' Old Helm announced, 'we *tour* the archive floor.' He led us through long shelves of glowing jars, each holding a story left by a previous traveller. The air hummed softly. I reached for a jar labelled 'sky harbour' and felt warmth pulse through my fingers like a distant heartbeat.
tour:0.cnHint: 老舵手带领大家____档案室，那里的每个发光罐子里都封存着前人的故事。
tour:0.hook: One jar had no label — and it was already warm when I touched it.
tour:0.line: 'We *tour* this archive so we remember those who mapped before us,' Old Helm said.

wake:0.en: Long after the others slept, I kept *wake* beside the navigation table, watching the star-map slowly turn. Old Helm had taught me that night hours carry whispers — small clues the busy day drowns out. By the third hour, I noticed a pattern in the stars: a gap shaped exactly like the missing fragment of our map.
wake:0.cnHint: 深夜，我独自____在导航桌旁，在寂静中发现了星图里隐藏的规律。
wake:0.hook: The gap in the stars blinked once — and then a new island appeared below it.
wake:0.line: 'Your *wake* through the night just saved us a week of searching,' Bell whispered.

annual:0.en: Old Helm unrolled a large scroll marked with small suns. 'This is the *annual* drift chart,' he explained. 'Every year the islands shift, and whoever maps the shift earns a new word.' Bell traced one curving line with her finger. The drift brought certain islands close only once a year — and tonight was exactly that night.
annual:0.cnHint: 老舵手展示____漂移图，解释岛屿每年移动的规律，今晚正是难得的接近时机。
annual:0.hook: The island was close enough to touch — but the window lasted one hour only.
annual:0.line: 'Our *annual* chart says we have until midnight — not a minute more,' Old Helm said.

charity:0.en: A traveller with torn boots stood in the doorway of our map room, hands empty. Old Helm waved her inside without hesitation. 'We do not give *charity*,' he told me later, 'we give a fair trade — her story for our shelter.' She told us about a hidden door on the island of Pale Moss, and we added it to our map.
charity:0.cnHint: 一位破靴旅人来到地图室，老舵手收留了她，并解释这不是____，而是公平的交换。
charity:0.hook: Her story matched a blank space on our map that had puzzled us for weeks.
charity:0.line: 'Call it *charity* if you like — I call it the best trade we ever made,' Old Helm smiled.

couple:0.en: Inside the map-room, Old Helm spread the latest fragments across a wide table. A *couple* of pieces fit together perfectly, revealing a bridge between two islands we had never seen before. Bell leaned in close, eyes wide. The rest of us held our breath, waiting to see what new path had just opened.
couple:0.cnHint: 老赫姆把地图碎片拼在一起，发现了一座____座桥梁连接着两个未知的岛屿。
couple:0.hook: But the bridge on the map was already fading.
couple:0.line: 'A *couple* of these fragments match — look at this bridge, Bell!'

definition:0.en: Bell held a glowing word-fragment up to the lantern light. Its edges were sharp, every line full of *definition*, unlike the blurry pieces we usually found. Old Helm said that meant the island it pointed to was close and real, not a dream-place. We all gathered around, suddenly very quiet.
definition:0.cnHint: 贝尔发现一块轮廓格外清晰、____极高的地图碎片，老赫姆说这意味着目标岛屿近在咫尺。
definition:0.hook: Then the fragment began to hum softly in her hand.
definition:0.line: 'The *definition* on this piece is perfect — this island is real and near.'

imagination:0.en: Old Helm told us the map-room itself had been built by a traveller whose only tool was *imagination*. Every shelf, every drawer was shaped like a word. I pulled open one carved like 'horizon' and found three fresh fragments inside. Even the walls seemed to lean in, listening.
imagination:0.cnHint: 老赫姆说，这间地图室完全靠____建造而成，我在一个抽屉里意外找到了新的碎片。
imagination:0.hook: The drawer carved like 'storm' was still sealed shut.
imagination:0.line: 'Pure *imagination* built this room — and it still hides its secrets.'

journey:0.en: We gathered around the long table as Old Helm traced the route with one careful finger. 'This *journey* has taken us through seven islands,' he said softly, 'and the map still shows blank space ahead.' I counted the word-fragments we had collected — twelve, each one a place we had lived in, if only for a day.
journey:0.cnHint: 老赫姆回顾了我们____的路线，地图上依然有大片空白等待探索。
journey:0.hook: The blank space at the map's edge seemed to breathe.
journey:0.line: 'This *journey* has already changed every one of us, hasn't it?'

nearby:0.en: Silverfang spread a rival chart on the table beside ours. 'A supply island sits *nearby*,' she said, tapping a small mark just off our current course. Old Helm raised an eyebrow; our own map showed nothing there. The two charts disagreed, and only one of them could be right.
nearby:0.cnHint: 银牙船长指出，按她的地图，____有一个补给岛，但我们的地图上却没有。
nearby:0.hook: One map was lying — we just didn't know which.
nearby:0.line: 'The supply island is *nearby*, trust my chart this once.'

perspective:0.en: Bell climbed to the top shelf of the map-room and looked down at all the fragments we had spread across the floor. 'From this *perspective*,' she called out, 'they form a shape — like a hand pointing west.' None of us had seen it from below. Old Helm smiled as if he had been waiting for someone to look up.
perspective:0.cnHint: 贝尔爬到高处，从新的____俯视地图碎片，发现它们拼出了一只指向西方的手。
perspective:0.hook: West was exactly where our charts had always gone blank.
perspective:0.line: 'From this *perspective*, the whole map finally makes sense!'

requirement:0.en: Old Helm unrolled an old scroll beside the map table. It listed the *requirement* for entering the island at the map's edge: a traveller must bring one word freely given by a stranger. We looked at each other. In all our collecting, every word had been found, traded, or won — never simply given.
requirement:0.cnHint: 古老的卷轴揭示了进入边境岛屿的____：必须持有一个陌生人自愿赠予的词语。
requirement:0.hook: None of the words in our bag had ever been freely given.
requirement:0.line: 'The *requirement* is one freely given word — do we have that?'

signal:0.en: A small light on the wall of the map-room began to blink in a slow rhythm. Bell recognised it at once. 'That blinks to *signal* that a new fragment has landed on the outer deck,' she said, already moving toward the door. Old Helm rolled the charts quickly. Whatever had arrived, it had found us first.
signal:0.cnHint: 墙上的灯光开始闪烁，贝尔说这是____有新碎片降落在甲板上的提示。
signal:0.hook: Something had sent the fragment — and it knew our location.
signal:0.line: 'Those blinks *signal* a new fragment — someone sent it to us.'

strength:0.en: Inside the map room, Old Helm spread the newest fragment across a wide wooden table. The island marked on it was enormous — five times bigger than any we had crossed. 'We need real *strength* to reach it,' he said, tapping the edge with one finger. The others fell quiet, measuring themselves against those dotted lines.
strength:0.cnHint: 老舵主摊开新地图碎片，指着一座巨大的岛屿，说明抵达它需要足够的____。
strength:0.hook: The dotted lines led somewhere none of us had ever returned from.
strength:0.line: 'We need real *strength* to reach it, not just a good wind.'

survive:0.en: The record books in our cabin went back a hundred years. Bell turned page after page, tracing routes that old crews had tried. Most lines ended mid-ocean with a red cross. 'Only two ships managed to *survive* that crossing,' she said softly, closing the cover. The lamp above us flickered once.
survive:0.cnHint: 贝尔翻阅旧航海记录，发现能____那段航程的船只寥寥无几。
survive:0.hook: She did not say what happened to the others.
survive:0.line: 'Only two ships ever *survived* that crossing — and both lost half their crew.'

touch:0.en: Old Helm kept one small glass box on the shelf above his bunk. Inside it lay the very first word-fragment the troupe had ever found. No one was allowed to open the box. 'Even a single *touch* can fade the ink,' he told me when I asked. I pulled my hand back and stared through the glass.
touch:0.cnHint: 老舵主警告我，哪怕一次____都可能让珍贵碎片上的字迹消失。
touch:0.hook: But the ink had already begun to look a little pale.
touch:0.line: 'Even a single *touch* can fade the ink — so look, never handle.'

trap:0.en: Bell found a loose board under the map table and pried it open. Beneath it sat a small iron box fitted with three spring-loaded latches. 'Whoever built this room made a *trap* for careless hands,' she said, pointing to a thin needle behind the first latch. We used a long quill to press it safely aside.
trap:0.cnHint: 贝尔在地图桌下发现一个机关盒，那是专门针对粗心之人的____。
trap:0.hook: The second latch had not been touched — not yet.
trap:0.line: 'Whoever built this room hid a *trap* for anyone who reached in too fast.'

tv:0.en: In a side room of the harbour inn, a battered screen sat in the corner — the only *tv* on this floating island, the landlord said proudly. Old Helm stared at the moving images for a long moment, then shook his head. 'Still no signal from the deep-sky zone,' he muttered. We were truly at the edge of things.
tv:0.cnHint: 港口客栈的角落里摆着这座岛上唯一一台____，老舵主盯着它若有所思。
tv:0.hook: The screen then cut to static, and stayed there.
tv:0.line: 'This old *tv* is the only window to the world they have out here.'

victim:0.en: The innkeeper showed us a wall of pinned notes — messages left by travellers who never came back. 'Each one a *victim* of the last storm season,' she said quietly, smoothing a corner that had curled away. Bell counted seventeen notes. Old Helm read each name aloud once, then turned and walked to the window without a word.
victim:0.cnHint: 客栈老板娘指着失踪旅人留下的纸条，说每一张背后都有一个____。
victim:0.hook: Bell's finger stopped on a name that matched our ship's old log.
victim:0.line: 'Every note on this wall belongs to a *victim* of the storm that took the east passage.'

zone:0.en: Old Helm unrolled a second chart and drew a wide circle with chalk near the top. 'This ring is a dead *zone*,' he said. 'Compass needles spin, word-fragments go dark, and nobody who enters knows which way is forward.' Bell marked it in red. I studied the circle's edge, looking for any gap we might slip through.
zone:0.cnHint: 老舵主在海图上画出一片罗盘失灵的____，贝尔用红色标注了它的边界。
zone:0.hook: The only possible gap was barely wider than our ship.
zone:0.line: 'Stay clear of that *zone* — your compass will spin and never settle again.'

afraid:0.en: I admitted to Bell that I had not slept well since seeing the red crosses in the record books. She did not laugh. 'I am *afraid* too, every single morning,' she said, pouring two cups of warm tea. 'The difference is I let the fear wake me up properly.' She handed me a cup and smiled at the map.
afraid:0.cnHint: 贝尔告诉我，她每天早上也会____，但她让这种感觉帮助自己清醒过来。
afraid:0.hook: Then she pointed to the one route no one had yet dared mark.
afraid:0.line: 'I am *afraid* too — but fear is just a compass pointing toward what matters.'

cent:0.en: The map shop on the second floor smelled of old paper and lamp oil. Bell counted the coins in her palm — not a single *cent* left after buying the last chart. She turned to Old Helm with a small shrug. He laughed and pulled a hidden coin from behind her ear.
cent:0.cnHint: 贝尔买完地图后，手里连一个____都不剩了。
cent:0.hook: Yet the shopkeeper slid one more rolled chart across the counter.
cent:0.line: 'Not one *cent* remains, but somehow we always find a way.'

commercial:0.en: The hall buzzed with traders hawking routes and star-charts. Old Helm frowned at the noise. 'This place has grown too *commercial*,' he muttered, tucking our precious word-fragment inside his coat. 'People sell paths now instead of walking them.' Bell nodded, eyes already searching for a quieter door.
commercial:0.cnHint: 老赫尔姆对这个变得过于____的大厅感到不满。
commercial:0.hook: Behind the loudest stall, a door stood slightly open.
commercial:0.line: 'Everything here has turned *commercial* — even the stars have a price.'

death:0.en: The old lighthouse keeper's log lay open on the reading table. The last entry read: 'Island adrift — *death* of the eastern anchor chain.' Old Helm traced the words with one finger. 'An anchor chain,' he said quietly, 'is not so different from a word. Lose it and you drift.'
death:0.cnHint: 航海日志记录了一条铁链的____，暗示着某座岛屿的漂移。
death:0.hook: The next page had been torn away by someone in a hurry.
death:0.line: 'The *death* of one small chain can unmoor an entire island.'

escape:0.en: The storage room door had jammed tight. Bell pressed her ear to the wood and heard Silverfang's crew outside. Old Helm scanned the room and spotted a hatch in the low ceiling. 'Our *escape* is up,' he whispered, eyes bright. I climbed first, pulling the others after me into cool, open air.
escape:0.cnHint: 门被卡死了，老赫尔姆发现了天花板上通往____的舱口。
escape:0.hook: Silverfang's voice reached us just as the hatch clicked shut.
escape:0.line: 'Our only *escape* is through the ceiling — follow me now.'

expose:0.en: Silverfang unrolled a stolen chart under the lantern light. 'I will *expose* every hidden route your troupe has collected,' she announced, tapping the parchment. Old Helm crossed his arms but stayed calm. Bell leaned over to me and whispered, 'Let her look. She will only see what we choose to show.'
expose:0.cnHint: 竞争船长扬言要____我们收集的所有隐秘路线。
expose:0.hook: The chart under her finger showed a coastline none of us recognised.
expose:0.line: 'I will *expose* your secret routes before the next tide turns.'

floor:0.en: The map room was three storeys underground. Old Helm led us down a spiral stair and stopped at the lowest *floor*, where the walls were covered in tiny hand-drawn islands. I pressed my palm to the stone and felt a faint hum, as if the whole place was remembering every traveller who had passed through.
floor:0.cnHint: 老赫尔姆带我们来到地下最底层的____，墙上布满了手绘的岛屿。
floor:0.hook: One island on the wall was still being drawn by an invisible hand.
floor:0.line: 'On this *floor*, every island ever discovered has left its mark.'

foundation:0.en: The engineer spread her diagrams across the workbench. The floating island's lift-stone had cracked. 'If the *foundation* weakens any further,' Old Helm said, studying the drawing, 'the whole island tips.' Bell was already sketching a repair — a word-fragment pressed into the stone like a key, sealing the crack with meaning.
foundation:0.cnHint: 如果浮岛的____继续弱化，整座岛将会倾覆。
foundation:0.hook: Bell's sketch showed a second crack no one had noticed yet.
foundation:0.line: 'A strong *foundation* is all that keeps an island from falling.'

persuade:0.en: The map room was full of dust and old light. Old Helm spread the charts across a low table and traced a faint line with one finger. I was ready to turn back, but he began to speak softly about what lay beyond the next island — and somehow, without my noticing, he *persuaded* me to stay. By the time he finished, my boots were already pointed at the door.
persuade:0.cnHint: 老舵主在地图室里用温和的话语，____了我留下来继续旅程。
persuade:0.hook: Beyond that door, something older than the map was waiting.
persuade:0.line: 'I can *persuade* even the wind to change its mind,' Old Helm said quietly.

preference:0.en: Bell pinned three possible routes to the wall of our small cabin. Each path led to a different island, each with its own colour on the chart. Old Helm asked me which I liked best. I felt my heart pull toward the blue one. 'That is your *preference*, then,' he said, and smiled as if he had already known.
preference:0.cnHint: 贝尔把三条路线贴在舱壁上，老舵主问我的____是哪一条。
preference:0.hook: The blue island shimmered, as though it had heard its name.
preference:0.line: 'My *preference* is always the road no one else has chosen,' Bell said.

reliable:0.en: Silverfang arrived at the cabin door just before midnight, shaking rain from his coat. He dropped a small compass onto the table — old, dented, but still spinning true north. 'This is the only *reliable* thing I own,' he said. Old Helm picked it up, turned it once, and placed it at the very centre of our map.
reliable:0.cnHint: 竞争船长带来了一枚他认为最____的罗盘，把它放在了地图中央。
reliable:0.hook: The compass needle trembled, then pointed somewhere the map did not show.
reliable:0.line: 'A *reliable* tool is worth more than a lucky one,' Silverfang said firmly.

suspect:0.en: Someone had moved the word-fragments in the night. They were arranged in a new order on the table, spelling nothing we recognised. Old Helm walked slowly around the room, eyes low. 'I *suspect* the wind did not do this,' he murmured. Bell and I looked at each other. The cabin door had been bolted from the inside.
suspect:0.cnHint: 地图碎片在夜里被人移动了，老舵主____这不是偶然发生的。
suspect:0.hook: The bolt was still shut, but the room felt one person larger.
suspect:0.line: 'I *suspect* someone reached us before we reached the island,' Old Helm said.

yield:0.en: The old chest in the corner had been locked for years. Bell worked at the latch with patient hands while Silverfang and I watched. At last, with a low groan, the lid began to *yield*. Inside, folded like a sleeping bird, lay a map made entirely of pressed star-flowers — each petal a different island name.
yield:0.cnHint: 箱子的锁终于____了，里面藏着一张用星花压制而成的地图。
yield:0.hook: One petal was still warm, as if someone had just placed it there.
yield:0.line: 'Even the oldest locks will *yield* if you are gentle enough,' Bell said softly.

abandon:0.en: The lower deck was flooded with cold fog. Old Helm told us we had to leave everything that would slow us down. I looked at my extra pack — full of small comforts I had carried since the first island. Then I set it down. It is never easy to *abandon* what you are used to, but the next word was calling, and the horizon does not wait.
abandon:0.cnHint: 为了追上下一个线索，我不得不____我的备用行囊，轻装前行。
abandon:0.hook: The fog swallowed my pack, and somehow I felt lighter than ever.
abandon:0.line: 'We *abandon* what holds us back, not what made us strong,' Old Helm said.

anxious:0.en: Bell had been quiet all evening, running her thumb along the edge of the newest word-fragment. I sat beside her on the deck step. 'Are you all right?' I asked. She gave a small nod. 'A little *anxious*,' she admitted. 'This word points somewhere none of us have been.' Above us, the stars pressed closer, as if listening.
anxious:0.cnHint: 贝尔盯着新碎片，有些____，因为它指向一个所有人都陌生的地方。
anxious:0.hook: The stars seemed to lean in, waiting for her next move.
anxious:0.line: 'I feel *anxious* only when the map runs out of islands,' Bell admitted.

assess:0.en: Old Helm stood at the centre of the room, eyes moving from chart to chart. He did not speak for a long time. This was how he always began — still and quiet, letting his mind *assess* every detail before he committed a single step to the plan. At last he placed one finger on the map and said, 'Here. This is where we go next.'
assess:0.cnHint: 老舵主沉默地____了所有地图信息，然后做出了下一步的决定。
assess:0.hook: His finger rested on a spot the map had never shown before tonight.
assess:0.line: 'We must *assess* the path before the path decides for us,' Old Helm said.

beautiful:0.en: Inside the map room, Old Helm unrolled a chart so old its edges crumbled like dry bread. Ink lines showed islands no one had visited in years. 'Look,' he said softly. Every curve of the coastline was *beautiful* — delicate as a whisper, precise as a promise.
beautiful:0.cnHint: 老舵主在地图室展开一张古老海图，让我第一次见识到它的____。
beautiful:0.hook: But one island on the chart had no name at all.
beautiful:0.line: 'Every line on this chart is *beautiful*, and every line is a door.'

combine:0.en: Bell spread three torn map pieces across the reading table, frowning. Each piece alone showed only fog and unmarked sea. 'We must *combine* them,' she said, pressing the edges together carefully. The moment they touched, a faint glow ran along the joins, and a new island took shape.
combine:0.cnHint: 领航员把三块碎片____在一起，图上竟然浮现出一座新岛屿。
combine:0.hook: The island glowed — and then it moved.
combine:0.line: '*Combine* the pieces now, before the light fades completely.'

complicated:0.en: Old Helm handed me a brass instrument covered in tiny dials. Reading it, he explained, required knowing both star positions and wind memory. I turned it over and over. The instructions were *complicated* — twelve steps, each depending on the last — but somewhere inside the tangle was our next destination.
complicated:0.cnHint: 老舵主给我一件仪器，操作方法____极了，但答案就藏在里面。
complicated:0.hook: Step seven, I noticed, referred to a star that no longer existed.
complicated:0.line: 'The method is *complicated*, but the answer it gives is always honest.'

crash:0.en: We heard it before we saw it — a deep, hollow *crash* from the lower deck, like a heavy crate falling on stone. Bell grabbed a lantern and ran. In the storage hold, a sealed chest had toppled from its shelf and split open, scattering small glass bottles across the floor.
crash:0.cnHint: 船舱里传来一声____，一只密封箱子摔开，里面散落出许多玻璃瓶。
crash:0.hook: Each bottle held a folded slip of paper with a single word on it.
crash:0.line: 'That *crash* came from the hold — nobody move until I check it.'

creature:0.en: One of the glass bottles from the broken chest held something unexpected: a tiny drawing, no bigger than a thumb, of a feathered *creature* with four wings and wide, calm eyes. Old Helm studied it under his lens for a long time and said nothing. Bell quietly wrote its shape into her log.
creature:0.cnHint: 一只破碎玻璃瓶里藏着一幅画，画中是一种从未见过的奇异____。
creature:0.hook: Old Helm finally whispered, 'I have seen this before.'
creature:0.line: 'This *creature* appears on no chart I have ever read.'

crime:0.en: Bell found a folded note inside the chest, sealed with red wax. When she read it aloud, the room went very still. Someone had once stolen a map word and sold it to a rival troupe. The note called it a *crime* against every traveller who depended on shared knowledge to find their way.
crime:0.cnHint: 一封旧信揭露了一个人曾经出卖地图词语的____。
crime:0.hook: The note was signed with a name we all recognised.
crime:0.line: 'Selling a map word to strangers — that is a *crime* I will not forgive.'

deeply:0.en: Silverfang arrived at our door just before midnight, hood up, voice low. He had heard the crash, he said, and wanted to make sure no one was hurt. Old Helm looked at him *deeply*, the way you look at someone when you are reading more than their words, then stepped aside and let him in.
deeply:0.cnHint: 银牙半夜到访，老舵主____地打量着他，然后让他进门。
deeply:0.hook: Silverfang's eyes went straight to the open chest.
deeply:0.line: 'I look at every chart *deeply* — that is how I find what others miss.'

demonstrate:0.en: Silverfang picked up the brass instrument I had struggled with all evening. Without a word he set the dials, held it toward the star map on the wall, and read out three numbers. He turned to me to *demonstrate* the final step, guiding my hand slowly until the needle settled at true north.
demonstrate:0.cnHint: 银牙亲手____仪器最后一步的用法，引导我找到了正北方向。
demonstrate:0.hook: The needle pointed not north — but straight down, through the floor.
demonstrate:0.line: 'Let me *demonstrate* once — then you will never need to ask again.'

preserve:0.en: Inside the archive room, shelves of glass jars lined every wall. Each jar held a glowing word, floating in pale liquid. Old Helm lifted one carefully. 'We must *preserve* these fragments,' he said, 'or the map dissolves and every island we have found disappears with it.' I held my breath.
preserve:0.cnHint: 在档案室里，老舵解释为何要把发光的词语____在玻璃瓶中。
preserve:0.hook: One jar near the back had already gone dark.
preserve:0.line: 'We must *preserve* these fragments, or every island we have found will vanish.'

procedure:0.en: Bell spread a worn chart across the long table and tapped it twice. 'There is a strict *procedure* for adding a new word to the map,' she said. 'Miss one step and the fragment burns out.' I watched her hands move through each careful action, determined not to make a single mistake.
procedure:0.cnHint: 小铃在桌前向我说明把新词语加入地图的____。
procedure:0.hook: The next step required a tool none of us could find.
procedure:0.line: 'Follow the *procedure* exactly — one wrong step and the fragment is gone.'

reasonable:0.en: Silverfang arrived at our door with a trade offer: two rare star-charts for one glowing word. Old Helm studied the charts for a long moment. 'That seems *reasonable*,' he said slowly, 'but only if the charts show the eastern drift lanes.' I leaned in, hoping he would agree.
reasonable:0.cnHint: 银牙提出交换条件，老舵认为这个价格____。
reasonable:0.hook: Silverfang's smile suggested the charts showed something far more valuable.
reasonable:0.line: 'That seems *reasonable* — but only if the charts cover the eastern drift lanes.'

reduction:0.en: The word-jar we opened in the archive room gave off a cold mist. Bell read the label aloud: 'Reduction.' She explained that this word described the *reduction* of a whole island into a single seed of light — a way of folding a place small enough to carry in your pocket. My mind raced with the possibilities.
reduction:0.cnHint: 小铃解释一个词语描述的是把整座岛屿____为一粒光种子的过程。
reduction:0.hook: There was already a seed in the jar — glowing and warm.
reduction:0.line: 'A *reduction* of the whole island — folded into one seed of light.'

season:0.en: Old Helm pointed to the calendar pinned above the archive door. 'We are in the star-bloom *season*,' he said, 'when new words rise to the surface of the sky and wait to be found.' Outside the small window, faint lights were already drifting upward. It felt like the best possible time to set out.
season:0.cnHint: 老舵说现在正处于星花____，新的词语会浮现在天空中等待被找到。
season:0.hook: The season lasted only seven more nights.
season:0.line: 'The star-bloom *season* is short — we must leave before dawn.'

sector:0.en: Bell divided the sky map into six parts and handed me a pencil. 'Mark every word we have collected in its own *sector*,' she said. Each section held a different cluster of islands, and the words inside it shaped what those islands looked like. I drew the first mark and felt the map come alive under my hand.
sector:0.cnHint: 小铃让我把收集到的词语标注在地图各____中，每个区域对应不同的岛屿群。
sector:0.hook: One sector had no marks at all — and no islands drawn either.
sector:0.line: 'Fill in each *sector* carefully — the islands take shape from the words inside.'

setting:0.en: The archive room itself was remarkable. Soft amber lanterns, low wooden shelves, and the faint hum of stored words all came together to create a *setting* that felt part library, part dream. Old Helm said the room had been designed this way on purpose — calm surroundings helped the words stay bright longer.
setting:0.cnHint: 档案室的____令人印象深刻，老舵说平静的环境能让词语保持更久的光亮。
setting:0.hook: At the far end, one shelf glowed brighter than the rest.
setting:0.line: 'The *setting* matters — calm surroundings keep the words bright far longer.'

shrink:0.en: Bell placed a word-fragment on the test plate and pressed a small button. We all watched the glowing shard begin to *shrink*, folding itself smaller and smaller until it was no bigger than a dewdrop. 'Perfect,' she said softly. 'Now it will fit the last empty slot in the map.' I let out a long, relieved breath.
shrink:0.cnHint: 小铃让发光的词语碎片开始____，直到它小得能嵌入地图最后一个空槽。
shrink:0.hook: The dewdrop of light pulsed once — and the map shuddered.
shrink:0.line: 'Watch it *shrink* — when it fits the slot, a new island will appear on the map.'

strike:0.en: Inside the map room, Old Helm spread the latest fragment across the table. The dock workers on the island below had called a *strike*, and no supply boats were moving. Without fresh ink and paper, our next map would stay blank. The whole troupe held its breath.
strike:0.cnHint: 码头工人发起____，补给船停运，船队的下一张地图面临危机。
strike:0.hook: One blank map could mean the end of everything.
strike:0.line: Old Helm said, 'A *strike* this long will leave us stranded.'

television:0.en: We found a dusty old *television* bolted to the wall of the island's rest house. Old Helm stared at the static on the screen and said it once showed weather patterns across the sky-sea. Bell tapped the side gently, and for one bright second, a map of unknown islands flickered into view.
television:0.cnHint: 旧休息站里有一台____，小铃轻轻敲了一下，屏幕上短暂出现了未知岛屿的地图。
television:0.hook: That flickering image was gone before anyone could trace it.
television:0.line: Bell whispered, 'The *television* just showed us somewhere none of us have been.'

youth:0.en: Old Helm opened a small chest and lifted out a folded map, its edges soft with age. 'I drew this in my *youth*,' he said quietly, smoothing it against the light. The lines were rough, but every island marked on it was real. Our newest word fit perfectly into the empty corner.
youth:0.cnHint: 老船长拿出一张他____时期绘制的旧地图，新词语恰好填补了空白的角落。
youth:0.hook: But one island on the old map had no name at all.
youth:0.line: Old Helm smiled and said, 'I chased these skies in my *youth*.'

alter:0.en: Bell noticed it first: the compass on the wall had begun to *alter* its reading every few minutes, swinging slowly between two directions. Old Helm crossed his arms and studied it. 'The map fragment is pulling at it,' he said at last. We marked the shifting angle and gained a new heading.
alter:0.cnHint: 罗盘开始不断____指向，小铃最先发现了异常，这为船队指出了新的方向。
alter:0.hook: Two directions meant two islands — and only one could be safe.
alter:0.line: Bell said, 'Watch how the needle begins to *alter* when we hold the fragment close.'

approximately:0.en: The fragment we collected was *approximately* the size of a playing card, yet it held detail enough for a dozen sailing days. Old Helm measured it against his thumb and nodded slowly. 'Small maps sometimes hold the biggest secrets,' he told us, pinning it carefully to the centre of the board.
approximately:0.cnHint: 新碎片____只有一张扑克牌大小，老船长说小地图有时藏着最大的秘密。
approximately:0.hook: The tiniest mark on its edge pointed somewhere none of us expected.
approximately:0.line: Old Helm murmured, '*Approximately* the size of my palm — yet it changes everything.'

attractive:0.en: The rest house keeper had laid out trade goods on a low shelf: rope, dried fruit, blank paper. Among them sat a small lantern with a moving star pattern inside — by far the most *attractive* item in the room. Bell reached for it first. Old Helm was already checking whether it hid a word.
attractive:0.cnHint: 休息站里陈列着各种物品，其中一盏会转动星图的小灯笼最____，小铃第一个伸手去拿。
attractive:0.hook: Hidden beneath the lantern was a folded slip of paper.
attractive:0.line: Bell laughed, 'I knew the most *attractive* thing in here would hold a clue.'

bag:0.en: Old Helm emptied his worn leather *bag* onto the map table, and out tumbled a dozen word-fragments, each one glowing faintly at the edges. He sorted them by colour with sure hands. Three of them clicked together at once, forming a corridor of islands none of us had ever seen before.
bag:0.cnHint: 老船长把皮____里的词语碎片全部倒出，三块碎片自动拼合，显现出一条未知的岛屿走廊。
bag:0.hook: The corridor pointed straight toward the edge of every map we owned.
bag:0.line: Old Helm said, 'Everything we need is already inside this *bag*.'

beat:0.en: Bell tapped the old drum by the door to call the troupe together, each *beat* steady and low. We gathered around the central table as Old Helm unrolled the final piece of the chapter map. The rhythm stopped. In the silence, the map seemed to breathe, its edges lifting like something alive.
beat:0.cnHint: 小铃敲响鼓声，每一____沉稳有力，众人聚拢后老船长展开了本章的最终地图。
beat:0.hook: When the last echo faded, the map began to glow.
beat:0.line: Bell said, 'Listen — every *beat* tells us we are closer.'

employment:0.en: Old Helm unrolled the new contract on the kitchen table, smoothing its edges with care. 'This word,' he said, tapping the paper, 'is our next map piece.' *Employment* — the act of giving someone work — had opened three islands already, and the faint glow rising from the ink told us it would open at least one more.
employment:0.cnHint: 老舵手在室内展开一份合同，发现新的词语碎片让整个小队对接下来的旅程充满期待，这个关于____的词将解锁新岛屿。
employment:0.hook: The ink began to glow before he even finished reading it.
employment:0.line: '*Employment* of every skill we have — that is what this next island demands.'

entire:0.en: Bell spread the star-chart across the floor, and for the first time I saw the *entire* map — every island, every current, every gap we had yet to cross. The room felt smaller somehow, as if the world had grown too big to hold inside four walls. Old Helm whistled softly and pointed at the far edge.
entire:0.cnHint: 小铃在室内展开星图，小队成员第一次看到了____的地图全貌，远处的边缘令人心跳加速。
entire:0.hook: One island near the edge had no name, only a question mark.
entire:0.line: 'The *entire* route is here — and one path none of us has ever tried.'

gift:0.en: Silverfang dropped a small box onto the table without a word. Inside lay a compass that spun not toward north but toward the next unread word. 'A *gift*,' Old Helm said quietly, 'from someone who crossed these skies long before us.' I held it and felt it pull, steady and sure, toward the window.
gift:0.cnHint: 竞争船长带来了一个神秘小盒，里面是一份意义非凡的____，指引小队走向下一个词语碎片。
gift:0.hook: The compass needle trembled, then locked onto something just beyond the clouds.
gift:0.line: 'Call it a *gift*, but it will ask something of you in return.'

kitchen:0.en: The word arrived written in steam on the *kitchen* window — thin letters forming just as Bell lit the stove. She froze, pot in hand, and read it aloud. The moment the last letter left her lips, the steam thickened into a glowing shape: a new island rising on the horizon outside the glass.
kitchen:0.cnHint: 在____里，小铃点燃炉灶时窗上出现了神秘文字，读出最后一个字母后新岛屿在窗外升起。
kitchen:0.hook: The island outside the glass had lights — and they were moving.
kitchen:0.line: 'Every time I stand in this *kitchen*, something impossible decides to happen,' Bell said.

mystery:0.en: Old Helm kept a locked drawer no one was allowed to open. Tonight, by accident, I found it sitting wide open and empty — except for a single word card glowing gold. The *mystery* of what had been stored there, and who had taken it, hung in the still air like smoke long after he came back.
mystery:0.cnHint: 老舵手那个从未开启的抽屉今晚被人打开了，留下的一张金色词卡让这一切更添____色彩。
mystery:0.hook: The word on the card matched the name of an island we thought was only a legend.
mystery:0.line: 'Some *mystery* is not a puzzle to solve — it is a door to walk through.'

opposite:0.en: Bell pinned two word-cards on the wall: one read calm, the other read storm. 'They are *opposite* forces,' she explained, tracing a line between them on the chart, 'but the island we need sits exactly where they meet.' Old Helm nodded. Silverfang said nothing, but I saw the corner of his mouth lift just slightly.
opposite:0.cnHint: 小铃在室内将两张含义____的词卡并排钉上墙，指出我们要找的岛屿就在两股力量的交汇处。
opposite:0.hook: The line Bell drew began, very slowly, to glow.
opposite:0.line: 'Stand at the *opposite* end of the deck and you will see what I mean,' said Bell.

permanent:0.en: Silverfang carved a small mark into the wooden doorframe — not a word, just a notch. 'Every island we unlock,' he said, 'I leave one.' I counted the notches: eleven. Old Helm looked over and added, 'No word we collect is *permanent*, but the places they open — those stay with you.' I understood then why Silverfang kept carving.
permanent:0.cnHint: 竞争船长在门框上刻下记号，老舵手说词语或许会消逝，但它开启的地方却是____存在于心中的。
permanent:0.hook: I found a twelfth notch that none of us remembered making.
permanent:0.line: 'Nothing in these skies is *permanent* — except the memory of where you have been.'

plenty:0.en: The supply shelf was bare when we landed, but by morning the islanders had left baskets outside the door — bread, dried fruit, small jars of something golden. 'There is *plenty* here,' Bell said, eyes bright, lifting a jar to the light. Old Helm smiled and added that generosity was always a sign we had found the right island.
plenty:0.cnHint: 补给架原本空空如也，但清晨岛民在门外留下了____的食物，让小队感到无比温暖。
plenty:0.hook: Tucked beneath the last basket was a word-card no one had left behind before.

frame:0.en: The map room smelled of old wood and starlight. Old Helm lifted a cracked *frame* from the wall — inside it, a pressed leaf held the shape of an island none of us had visited yet. 'Every border tells a story,' he said softly. I traced the edge with one finger, and the leaf began to glow.
frame:0.cnHint: 老舵从墙上取下一个旧____，里面的叶子竟然发出了光芒。
frame:0.hook: The glow spread until the whole ceiling looked like a living map.
frame:0.line: 'This *frame* has held that island's secret for fifty years,' Old Helm said.

friday:0.en: Bell kept a small notebook where she marked every day at sea. She tapped the page and said, 'It is *Friday* — the word we found last week finally opens the lock.' She pressed the word-stone to the cabin door. A soft click, and behind it lay a passage lit by pale blue lanterns, leading down into the hull of the island.
friday:0.cnHint: 小铃说今天是____，上周找到的那个词语终于能打开那把锁了。
friday:0.hook: The blue light pulsed once, as if the island itself had taken a breath.
friday:0.line: 'Every *Friday* we unlock one door — that is the rule Old Helm set,' Bell said.

grain:0.en: Inside the storage cabin, sacks lined every wall. Old Helm opened one and let the contents run through his fingers — each tiny *grain* was golden and hummed faintly when touched. 'These are not for eating,' he said. 'Grind them and you get ink. Write the right word, and a new island appears on the chart.' I stared at the pile, already thinking of what to write.
grain:0.cnHint: 老舵解释说，这些会发光的____磨成粉后可以用来书写，写出正确的词就能让新岛屿现身。
grain:0.hook: Somewhere in those sacks, the next destination was waiting to be written.
grain:0.line: 'One *grain* of this is worth more than a full sack of rice,' Old Helm told me.

implication:0.en: Bell spread the old chart across the table. 'Look at the gap here,' she said, pressing her finger to a blank space. 'The *implication* is clear — there is a hidden island between these two.' No one had noticed the gap before. Silverfang leaned in, eyes sharp, and for once said nothing, which told me Bell was right.
implication:0.cnHint: 小铃指着地图上的空白，说这个____很明显：两座岛之间藏着另一座岛。
implication:0.hook: Silverfang's silence was the loudest agreement I had ever heard.
implication:0.line: 'The *implication* of this blank space is that someone erased it on purpose,' Bell said.

incredible:0.en: Old Helm unrolled the oldest map in his chest. It covered the whole cabin floor, and every island on it was named in a script none of us could read. 'The person who drew this visited over a thousand islands,' he said. I looked at the tiny careful lines and felt something open up in my chest. That anyone could do all that — it was simply *incredible*.
incredible:0.cnHint: 老舵展开那幅古老的地图，上面密密麻麻的岛屿令人感到____。
incredible:0.hook: If one person drew this, then the sky above us held far more than we had dreamed.
incredible:0.line: 'It is *incredible* that one pair of hands drew every island on this floor,' Old Helm said.

net:0.en: Rain hammered the cabin roof. Bell had strung a fine *net* across the open skylight to catch the star-seeds that fell with the rain — tiny bright specks that could be traded for new word-stones at the next harbour. By morning the net was full, glittering like a piece of the sky had come inside to rest.
net:0.cnHint: 小铃在天窗上挂了一张____，用来接住随雨水落下的星种。
net:0.hook: One seed was larger than the rest, and it pulsed with a colour I had no name for.
net:0.line: 'Check the *net* before you sleep — star-seeds dissolve by dawn,' Bell warned me.

obtain:0.en: Silverfang spread a hand of cards across the table and smiled. 'To *obtain* the next word, you must win it from me.' Old Helm sighed. Bell hid a grin. I had never beaten Silverfang at cards, but the word glowed on the table between us, and the next island was worth the risk. I picked up my hand.
obtain:0.cnHint: 银牙说，要想____下一个词语，就必须在牌局中赢过他。
obtain:0.hook: The word on the table flickered as if it too was watching who would win.
obtain:0.line: 'You cannot simply ask — you must *obtain* the word by earning it,' Silverfang said.

bottom:0.en: The archive room was dusty and dim. I searched every shelf until I found a rolled map at the *bottom* of a heavy wooden chest. Old Helm lifted it carefully, brushing away years of grey dust. 'This is the one,' he said softly. The map showed an island none of us had ever seen.
bottom:0.cnHint: 我在一个沉重木箱的____找到了一张从未见过的地图。
bottom:0.hook: The island on the map had no name — only a question mark.
bottom:0.line: Old Helm: 'Look at the *bottom* of the chest — that is where the old ones hid things.'

breed:0.en: Bell pointed to a small creature sleeping on the archive shelf — round, pale, and softly glowing. 'This is a rare *breed*,' she whispered, 'found only near the oldest islands.' Old Helm nodded slowly. The creature opened one silver eye, blinked at us, then tucked its head back under its wing.
breed:0.cnHint: 小铃在书架上发现了一种罕见的____，只在最古老的岛屿附近出现。
breed:0.hook: The creature's silver eye had reflected something none of us could explain.
breed:0.line: Bell: 'I have never seen this *breed* outside the oldest charts.'

classify:0.en: Old Helm spread dozens of map fragments across the long table. 'We need to *classify* these by colour and shape before we can read them together,' he said firmly. Bell sorted the pale blue ones to the left. I handled the gold-edged pieces. Slowly, a pattern began to appear across the table.
classify:0.cnHint: 团长要求我们把地图碎片____，颜色和形状各归其类。
classify:0.hook: When the last piece landed, the pattern looked like a door.
classify:0.line: Old Helm: 'Help me *classify* these fragments — colour first, then shape.'

comment:0.en: I pinned my rough sketch of the new island to the wall and stepped back. Old Helm studied it for a long moment without a word. Silverfang leaned in, arms crossed. Finally Old Helm gave his *comment*: 'The coastline is wrong, but the centre — the centre is exactly right.' I felt my heart lift.
comment:0.cnHint: 团长看完我的草图后，给出了他的____，说中心部分画得完全正确。
comment:0.hook: If the centre was right, we already knew where to land.
comment:0.line: Old Helm: 'My *comment* is simple — fix the coast and keep everything else.'

component:0.en: Bell laid the brass navigation tool on the table in pieces. 'Each *component* must be clean before we reassemble it,' she explained, holding a tiny gear up to the lamplight. I counted seven parts in total. Without all seven, she said, the tool could not find true north over open sky.
component:0.cnHint: 小铃把导航仪器拆开，说每个____都必须清洁后才能重新组装。
component:0.hook: One component was missing, and none of us had touched it.
component:0.line: Bell: 'This *component* is the smallest, but lose it and we are lost too.'

contrary:0.en: Silverfang argued that the storm would pass by morning. Old Helm held a *contrary* view — the clouds were turning green at the edges, a sign the sky would not settle for days. The two stood on opposite sides of the table, maps between them, neither willing to move first.
contrary:0.cnHint: 船长和团长持____意见，一个说风暴明早会过，另一个说要等好几天。
contrary:0.hook: Outside, the first green cloud drifted silently past the window.
contrary:0.line: Silverfang: 'My reading is *contrary* to yours, Old Helm, and I trust my sky.'

deny:0.en: I found a second signature at the corner of the oldest map — not Old Helm's. When I asked him about it, he was quiet for a moment. He did not *deny* that someone else had drawn it first. 'She was a better cartographer than I ever was,' he said, and turned back to the window.
deny:0.cnHint: 团长没有____那张最古老地图上的另一个签名，只是沉默地转身看向窗外。
deny:0.hook: Whoever she was, her route led straight to the edge of the world.
deny:0.line: Old Helm: 'I will not *deny* it — that signature belongs to someone I once followed.'

depth:0.en: Bell lowered a thin measuring line through a gap in the archive floor — an old trapdoor that opened onto open sky below the island. She read the number quietly. 'The *depth* to the next island beneath us is less than forty metres,' she said. We all gathered to peer into the blue darkness below.
depth:0.cnHint: 小铃测量了脚下岛屿到下方另一座岛的____，只有不到四十米。
depth:0.hook: In that blue darkness below, something was slowly moving upward.
depth:0.line: Bell: 'The *depth* is nothing — we could drop a rope and reach it before dark.'

distinguish:0.en: The archive room smelled of old paper and lamp oil. Dozens of rolled maps covered every shelf. Old Helm held two charts side by side. 'Only a trained eye can *distinguish* the real route from a decoy,' he said, tracing a faint line with one finger.
distinguish:0.cnHint: 老舵手在档案室里教我如何____两张看似相同的航图。
distinguish:0.hook: One chart led to treasure; the other led to a trap.
distinguish:0.line: 'Can you *distinguish* the true path from the false one?'

document:0.en: Bell spread a worn *document* across the reading table. It bore an official seal and a list of island names, each crossed out except the last. 'This is our only proof that the final island exists,' she said softly, smoothing a torn corner with care.
document:0.cnHint: 领航员展示了一份重要____，上面记录着最后一座岛屿的名称。
document:0.hook: Someone had already crossed out every name but one.
document:0.line: 'This *document* is the only proof we have left.'

dozen:0.en: The storage room held a *dozen* glass jars, each sealed with wax and filled with a faint glowing dust. Old Helm said each jar contained one forgotten word from a vanished island. We had only opened three. Nine more secrets waited on the shelf.
dozen:0.cnHint: 储藏室里摆着____个装有发光尘埃的玻璃罐，每罐封存着一个失落的词语。
dozen:0.hook: The ninth jar rattled on its own in the dark.
dozen:0.line: 'There is a *dozen* jars, and each one hides a secret.'

dull:0.en: The old compass on the shelf looked *dull* and forgotten, its brass case scratched and its needle stuck. Yet when Bell breathed on the glass, the needle spun wildly and stopped, pointing at a wall where no door had ever been. We stared in silence.
dull:0.cnHint: 那枚看起来____的旧罗盘突然转动，指向了一面没有门的墙。
dull:0.hook: Behind that wall, something was already listening.
dull:0.line: 'It looks *dull*, but this compass still knows the way.'

fortune:0.en: A locked box sat beneath the map table, half buried under old charts. Bell pried it open to find not gold but folded letters, each one signed with a different island name. 'Real *fortune* here is knowledge, not coins,' Old Helm said, lifting one letter to the light.
fortune:0.cnHint: 那只上锁的箱子里装的不是金币，而是老舵手所说的真正的____。
fortune:0.hook: The last letter was addressed to someone still on board.
fortune:0.line: 'True *fortune* is what you learn, not what you carry.'

fulfil:0.en: Bell read the old charter aloud by lamplight. It said every member of the troupe must *fulfil* one promise before the final island could be found. I looked around the room. Old Helm was quiet. No one had yet said which promise they still owed.
fulfil:0.cnHint: 古老的航行章程要求每位成员都必须____一个承诺，才能找到最后的岛屿。
fulfil:0.hook: Old Helm folded his hands and would not meet my eyes.
fulfil:0.line: 'We each must *fulfil* our promise before the journey ends.'

gradually:0.en: The star map on the ceiling of the archive room was painted in pale ink. At first I saw only swirls. Then, as the lamp warmed the room, the colours *gradually* grew brighter, and a clear route appeared among the stars overhead, connecting island to island.
gradually:0.cnHint: 随着油灯使房间变暖，天花板上的星图____变得清晰，显示出完整的航路。
gradually:0.hook: The final destination glowed brightest of all.
gradually:0.line: 'Watch — the path will *gradually* show itself if you wait.'

incentive:0.en: Old Helm placed a single glowing word-shard on the table between us. 'This is your *incentive*,' he said with a small smile. Whoever decoded the old logbook by morning could keep it. I pulled the logbook close and did not look up again for a long time.
incentive:0.cnHint: 老舵手把一块发光的词语碎片放上桌，作为我解读旧航海日志的____。
incentive:0.hook: The logbook's first page showed my own name.
incentive:0.line: 'Let this shard be your *incentive* to solve it tonight.'

lower:0.en: Inside the map room, shelves of folded charts lined every wall. Old Helm pointed to the *lower* shelf, where older, worn maps lay forgotten beneath newer ones. 'Those are the ones we need,' he said quietly. I pulled them out, dust rising like tiny clouds around my fingers.
lower:0.cnHint: 老舵在地图室里指着____层的架子，那里藏着我们真正需要的旧地图。
lower:0.hook: The oldest map trembled in my hands, edges glowing faint gold.
lower:0.line: 'Check the *lower* shelf — the answers are always buried deeper.'

naturally:0.en: Bell spread the star charts across the wide table and *naturally* began to hum as she worked, as though the maps and the music were part of the same thought. Old Helm watched her from the doorway, a small smile on his face. I understood then — this was simply who she was.
naturally:0.cnHint: 小铃在整理星图时____地哼起歌来，老舵在门口看着她微笑。
naturally:0.hook: Her humming stopped — she had found something the others had missed.
naturally:0.line: 'I *naturally* think better when I hum — you should try it sometime.'

passionate:0.en: Old Helm laid the final chart flat and began to speak about the floating islands with a *passionate* fire in his voice. His hands moved across the map like wings. Even Bell set down her tools to listen. I had never seen a person love a thing so completely before.
passionate:0.cnHint: 老舵用____的语气讲述浮岛的故事，连小铃也放下工具侧耳倾听。
passionate:0.hook: He paused at one island's name, his voice suddenly dropping to a whisper.
passionate:0.line: 'I am *passionate* about every island on this map — each one changed me.'

pop:0.en: We were sorting old word-fragments when a small folded note seemed to *pop* out from between two heavy charts. No one had placed it there — or so we thought. Old Helm picked it up carefully, turned it over once, and raised an eyebrow at Bell, who shook her head slowly.
pop:0.cnHint: 整理地图碎片时，一张折叠的纸条突然从两张图之间____出来，没人知道它从哪里来。
pop:0.hook: The note held a single word none of us had ever seen before.
pop:0.line: 'Things that *pop* up without warning are usually the most important clues.'

possibly:0.en: Bell studied the strange symbol at the map's edge for a long time. 'This could *possibly* be the entrance to the final island,' she said at last, her finger resting lightly on the mark. Old Helm leaned in close. The room felt smaller, tighter, full of held breath and quiet hope.
possibly:0.cnHint: 小铃看着地图边缘的奇怪符号，说那____是通往最后一座岛的入口。
possibly:0.hook: Old Helm reached out and the symbol began to shine beneath his touch.
possibly:0.line: 'This mark could *possibly* lead us somewhere no troupe has ever reached.'

previously:0.en: I had *previously* thought the back room was just storage, full of broken lanterns and old rope. But Bell pushed open the low door and showed me a second map table, covered in fresh notes and pinned charts. 'We have been working here for weeks,' she said with a quiet smile.
previously:0.cnHint: 我____以为那间小屋只是杂物间，但小铃推开门，里面竟是一张铺满新笔记的地图桌。
previously:0.hook: One pinned chart showed an island that matched no name in our records.
previously:0.line: 'I *previously* assumed it was nothing — I was very wrong about that.'

profession:0.en: Old Helm set down his pen and looked at me steadily. 'Navigation is not just a *profession*,' he said. 'It is a way of seeing the world.' Bell nodded from across the table without looking up. I turned the word over in my mind, feeling its weight settle into something like a decision.
profession:0.cnHint: 老舵告诉我，导航不只是一种____，而是一种看待世界的方式。
profession:0.hook: His next words would change the direction of my entire journey.
profession:0.line: 'Our *profession* is to find what the world has quietly hidden from itself.'

readily:0.en: When Old Helm asked for a volunteer to carry the recovered maps through the narrow lower passage, I *readily* stepped forward before anyone else could speak. Bell looked surprised. Old Helm simply nodded, as though he had expected it all along. I picked up the roll of charts and felt oddly ready.
readily:0.cnHint: 老舵问谁愿意搬运地图，我____地第一个站了出来，小铃露出惊讶的神情。
readily:0.hook: The passage was darker than I had imagined, and something moved ahead.
readily:0.line: 'I *readily* take on any task this troupe needs — that is why I am here.'

relax:0.en: Inside the map room, papers covered every wall. Old Helm dropped into a wide chair and let out a long breath. 'We found the northern fragment,' he said quietly. 'Tonight we can *relax*.' The lanterns burned low, and the whole troupe settled into the warm hush of a well-earned rest.
relax:0.cnHint: 老舵手让大家在地图室里好好____，因为今天找到了北方碎片。
relax:0.hook: But one fragment on the wall had begun to glow.
relax:0.line: 'For once, just *relax* — the stars are not going anywhere tonight.'

release:0.en: Bell stood at the brass tube in the corner of the chart room. She had wound the message scroll tight all day, waiting. At last Old Helm nodded, and she pressed the lever to *release* it into the sky-post. A soft chime rang as the scroll lifted away into the dark above the island.
release:0.cnHint: 领航员在海图室里____了一份重要的消息卷轴。
release:0.hook: The reply arrived in less than a minute — far too fast.
release:0.line: 'Ready. I will *release* the message the moment you give the word.'

route:0.en: The troupe gathered around the long table where Bell had laid out the newest fragment. She traced her finger across the glowing lines. 'This *route* takes us east, past the Hollow Arch, then up to the Silver Shelf,' she said. Everyone leaned in, following the path with wide, hopeful eyes.
route:0.cnHint: 领航员在室内向大家展示新碎片上标注的____。
route:0.hook: The route crossed a place none of them had ever named.
route:0.line: 'Trust me — this *route* is the safest path through the eastern gap.'

sight:0.en: Old Helm opened the inner shutter of the observatory dome and waved me forward. Through the thick lens, the next island floated like a lantern in the dark. The *sight* of it — glowing amber, ringed by slow clouds — made my chest feel suddenly full, too big for ordinary words.
sight:0.cnHint: 在观测室里，我透过镜头看到了令人震撼的____。
sight:0.hook: Then something on that distant island moved toward us.
sight:0.line: 'Come here — the *sight* through this lens will change how you see everything.'

speaker:0.en: The troupe crowded into the small hall where maps lined every shelf. A lantern hung above the centre chair, casting a warm circle of light. Old Helm sat beneath it as the *speaker* for the evening, unrolling the newest fragment and reading each clue aloud in his steady, unhurried voice.
speaker:0.cnHint: 老舵手作为今晚的____，在小厅里向大家宣读新碎片上的线索。
speaker:0.hook: His voice stopped at the last line, and he read it twice.
