The fog thinned, then thinned again. We *eventually* broke through into clear sky, and a whole new chain of islands hung above us like lit lanterns.
eventually:1.cnHint: 穿越重重迷雾后，我们____冲破阻碍，看见了一串如灯笼般悬挂的新岛屿。
eventually:1.hook: One of those islands was already moving slowly toward us.
eventually:1.line: 'If you keep going, you will *eventually* find the sky you are looking for,' Silverfang said.

match:1.en: Old Helm set two word-fragments on the stone table and asked me to find which one would *match* the symbol on the northern gate. I turned them both slowly, held them to the starlight, and felt a faint hum when I brought one close to the gate's carved edge. It locked into place with a clean, bright click.
match:1.cnHint: 老舵主让我找出能与北门符文____的碎片，我在星光下仔细辨认。
match:1.hook: The gate swung open onto a sky nobody in the troupe had ever mapped.
match:1.line: 'Find the piece that will *match* the gate, and the last island will show itself,' Old Helm said.

safe:1.en: At the edge of the map, Old Helm knelt beside a mossy stone wall and brushed the dirt away. Behind a loose brick sat a small iron *safe*, no bigger than a bread loaf. Inside, a folded paper glowed faintly — another word, another island waiting to be found.
safe:1.cnHint: 老舵在石墙缝里发现了一个装有发光纸片的____。
safe:1.hook: But the lock had already been broken from the inside.
safe:1.line: 'Whatever was in this *safe*, someone reached it before us,' Old Helm said quietly.

speed:1.en: Bell stood at the prow of the sky-boat, eyes wide, her scarf snapping behind her. The wind had shifted, and the islands were drifting apart fast. She adjusted the sail with calm hands. 'We match the *speed* of the current,' she said, 'or we lose the passage forever.'
speed:1.cnHint: 贝尔告诉我们必须配合气流的____，否则会错失航道。
speed:1.hook: The gap between the islands was already wider than the boat was long.
speed:1.line: 'Match the *speed* of the wind, or we fall behind,' Bell said.

burden:1.en: Old Helm carried the word-chest on his back all morning across the cracked stone plaza. By midday he sat down on a fountain's edge, breathing hard. I offered to carry it next. He smiled and shook his head. 'It is my *burden*,' he said, 'and also my joy.'
burden:1.cnHint: 老舵独自背着装满词语的箱子，说这份____也是他的快乐。
burden:1.hook: Then the fountain behind him began to rise, stone by stone, into the sky.
burden:1.line: 'This chest is my *burden* to carry — do not worry for me,' said Old Helm.

former:1.en: Two roads crossed the open market square. One was wide and paved with white stone; the other was narrow and covered in soft grass. Bell pointed to both and asked which way we should go. Old Helm chose the *former* without hesitation, saying the stone road always leads to the next word.
former:1.cnHint: 面对两条路，老舵选择了____，也就是宽阔的石板路。
former:1.hook: But at its far end, the white road simply stopped — in mid-air.
former:1.line: 'Of the two paths, I trust the *former* — the stone one,' said Old Helm.

oppose:1.en: Silverfang's crew had reached the market first and blocked the only gate. They crossed their arms and said no one else would pass. Old Helm walked straight toward them without slowing. 'You may *oppose* us all you like,' he said pleasantly, 'but the word has already chosen its reader.'
oppose:1.cnHint: 银牙的船员封锁了城门，但老舵毫不畏惧地____他们。
oppose:1.hook: The gate swung open on its own the moment Old Helm finished speaking.
oppose:1.line: 'You can *oppose* us, but the map does not answer to you,' Old Helm said.

unable:1.en: The word-fragment hovered just above the old clock tower, spinning slowly in the morning light. I climbed every step, stretched as far as I could, and still I was *unable* to reach it. Bell watched from below, then pulled out a small silver whistle and blew one soft note. The fragment floated down.
unable:1.cnHint: 我爬上钟楼却____够到漂浮的词语碎片，最终靠贝尔的口哨解决了问题。
unable:1.hook: The whistle's note was still hanging in the air, shaped like a door.
unable:1.line: 'I was *unable* to reach it, but your whistle did what my arms could not,' I told Bell.

unusual:1.en: The open-air market on the floating island sold things I had never seen: jars of frozen laughter, hats that changed colour with your mood, maps drawn in starlight. But the most *unusual* stall had nothing on it at all — just a sign that read: 'Bring a word, take a wonder.'
unusual:1.cnHint: 集市上有个____的摊位，空空如也，只写着用词换奇迹的告示。
unusual:1.hook: Old Helm walked straight to that empty stall without even looking at the others.
unusual:1.line: 'That empty stall is the most *unusual* thing I have seen on any island,' I said.

apart:1.en: The troupe stood at the very edge of the last mapped island. Ahead, two smaller rocks drifted slowly *apart*, leaving a growing gap of open sky between them. Bell measured the distance with her eyes. 'We jump now,' she said, 'before it is too wide.' We jumped. We made it. Barely.
apart:1.cnHint: 两块小岩石渐渐____，我们必须在缝隙变大前纵身一跳。
apart:1.hook: On the far rock, scratched into the stone, was a single new word.
apart:1.line: 'They are drifting *apart* — we jump on three, and we do not look down,' said Bell.

advice:1.en: The market square on Thistledown Island buzzed with traders calling from every stall. Old Helm stopped beside a lamp-post and studied the crowd. 'You look lost,' said a friendly map-seller. Old Helm smiled and asked for *advice* on which road led to the edge of the island. The seller pointed west, and a new word glowed on our map.
advice:1.cnHint: 在市集广场，老舵向一位地图商人寻求____，找到了通往岛屿边缘的道路。
advice:1.hook: But the road west ended at nothing but open sky.
advice:1.line: 'My *advice* is simple: always ask the one who sells the maps.'

attempt:1.en: The wind bridge between Coral Isle and the next island swayed dangerously. Bell studied the ropes and shook her head twice. Then she took a deep breath and began to *attempt* the crossing anyway, testing each plank with one careful foot before trusting it with her full weight. By the time she reached the other side, the rest of us had already stopped breathing.
attempt:1.cnHint: 小铃面对摇晃的风桥，鼓起勇气____过桥，每一步都走得小心翼翼。
attempt:1.hook: The last plank cracked just as she stepped off it.
attempt:1.line: 'We should *attempt* the crossing before the wind gets stronger,' Bell said.

draw:1.en: After a full morning of racing clouds across the sky-lanes, Silverfang and Bell arrived at Windhook Island at exactly the same moment. Old Helm checked both anchor ropes and declared it a *draw*, then laughed so hard the whole deck shook. The tied result meant the new word on the map belonged equally to both of them, and neither could quite stop smiling.
draw:1.cnHint: 银牙和小铃同时抵达，老舵宣布比赛以____收场，两人共同获得了地图碎片。
draw:1.hook: Then the map fragment split itself cleanly in two.
draw:1.line: 'A *draw* is fair enough — you are both the best I have ever seen,' said Old Helm.

facility:1.en: High on Amber Ridge floated a small island built entirely for learning. Every corner held a shelf, a lens, or a strange spinning tool. Bell called it the finest *facility* she had ever visited, running her fingers along a brass telescope that could read star-names from ten islands away. Old Helm found the word we needed carved above the main door.
facility:1.cnHint: 小铃参观了一座专为学习而建的岛屿____，那里的每个角落都充满了奇妙的工具。
facility:1.hook: The telescope suddenly swung on its own and pointed south.
facility:1.line: 'This *facility* has everything a navigator could ever dream of,' Bell said quietly.

firm:1.en: A sudden gust tried to push our ship off course near the Pale Cliffs. Old Helm gripped the wheel and stayed *firm*, not giving a single degree to the wind. His arms did not shake and his eyes did not move from the horizon ahead. When the gust passed, Bell marked the safe path on our map, and a new word appeared in gold beside it.
firm:1.cnHint: 狂风袭来，老舵____地握紧船轮，一步不让，引领船只安全通过。
firm:1.hook: Ahead, the Pale Cliffs were moving closer together.
firm:1.line: 'Stay *firm* at the wheel — this wind will pass in sixty seconds,' Old Helm called out.

innovation:1.en: The island of Gearlight was unlike any place we had seen. Its people had built sky-bridges out of folded paper and starlight glass. Old Helm called the whole place a wonder of *innovation*, marvelling at how simple ideas had grown into something that kept an entire island floating above the clouds. A glowing word waited for us at the centre of the bridge.
innovation:1.cnHint: 在Gearlight岛，老舵对当地人用简单材料建造天桥的____赞叹不已。
innovation:1.hook: One paper bridge was already holding three more islands above it.
innovation:1.line: 'Real *innovation* comes from asking what nobody else thought to ask,' said Old Helm.

multiple:1.en: The map showed one path to Sunspire, but Bell discovered *multiple* routes spiralling out from the same starting point, each one marked with a different star symbol. She spread them on the deck and counted seven in total. Old Helm let me choose, and the one I picked was the only route still lit by the evening star, so we followed its light north.
multiple:1.cnHint: 小铃发现地图上通往目的地的路线不止一条，而是有____条，最终由叙述者来选择。
multiple:1.hook: Six of the seven paths had been quietly crossed out in red.
multiple:1.line: 'There are *multiple* ways forward — the question is which star you trust,' said Bell.

path:1.en: Fog rolled in thick across the garden island of Mossbell just as we landed. The stone *path* that cut through the flower beds was the only thing still visible, glowing faintly with a soft blue light. I followed it slowly while Old Helm and Bell waited at the ship. At the end of the path stood a small stone pillar, and a new word was carved deep into its face.
path:1.cnHint: 浓雾中，叙述者独自沿着唯一可见的发光石____前行，在终点找到了新的地图文字。
path:1.hook: The pillar had a second face, and something was already carved there too.
path:1.line: 'Every great journey is really just one *path* chosen one step at a time,' said Old Helm.

announce:1.en: The wind carried Old Helm's voice across the whole market square. He climbed onto a crate and *announced* to every traveller and trader present: our troupe had found the edge of the map. Strangers looked up from their stalls, eyes wide, feet already turning toward us.
announce:1.cnHint: 老赫姆站在箱子上，向广场上所有人____了我们找到地图尽头的消息。
announce:1.hook: But one hooded figure did not turn — they simply smiled.
announce:1.line: 'I *announce* to all of you: the edge of the map is real!'

appropriate:1.en: Bell spread the map across a low stone wall and studied it carefully. Old Helm wanted to fly straight into the storm clouds ahead, but Bell shook her head. 'The southern wind route is more *appropriate*,' she said, tracing a gentle arc with her finger. She always found the right path.
appropriate:1.cnHint: 贝尔认为绕行南风路线比直飞风暴更____。
appropriate:1.hook: Then the southern wind suddenly reversed direction.
appropriate:1.line: 'A slower route is *appropriate* when the sky is angry.'

chief:1.en: Silverfang's ship docked beside ours just as the sun touched the horizon. He stepped off with his crew behind him, arms crossed. His *chief* reason for following us, he admitted at last, was not the treasure — it was the word written at the very edge of the map.
chief:1.cnHint: 银牙承认，追随我们的____原因并非财宝。
chief:1.hook: He read that word aloud, and the stars above shifted.
chief:1.line: 'My *chief* reason for being here is that single word on the map.'

clearly:1.en: The fragment glowed the moment Old Helm placed it on the ground. Strange lines of light spread outward, forming paths and peaks none of us had seen before. *Clearly*, the map was alive in ways we had never guessed. Even Silverfang stepped back and said nothing for a full minute.
clearly:1.cnHint: 碎片散发的光芒____表明，这张地图是有生命的。
clearly:1.hook: One glowing path led straight off the island's edge.
clearly:1.line: 'This map is *clearly* trying to tell us something urgent.'

communicate:1.en: The stone pillars at the square's centre were carved with tiny pictures — ships, stars, hands reaching out. Bell knelt and touched one gently. 'These were used to *communicate* between islands long ago,' she said softly. Each picture was a message from someone who had stood here before us.
communicate:1.cnHint: 广场石柱上的图案曾被用来在各岛之间____信息。
communicate:1.hook: The last picture showed a troupe exactly like ours.
communicate:1.line: 'Ancient people used these carvings to *communicate* across the sky.'

emphasis:1.en: Old Helm gathered us under the lamp at the crossroads and spoke slowly. He put great *emphasis* on one rule above all others: we must never trade a word fragment away, no matter what anyone offered. His eyes moved to Silverfang's ship in the distance as he said it.
emphasis:1.cnHint: 老赫姆特别____了一条规矩：绝不能转让地图碎片。
emphasis:1.hook: A stranger was already approaching with a very generous offer.
emphasis:1.line: 'I place *emphasis* on this rule: no fragment leaves our hands.'

emphasize:1.en: Bell drew a circle around the outermost island on the map and tapped it twice. 'I want to *emphasize* that we have very little time,' she said, looking at the pale sky. The stars were fading faster than they should. Old Helm nodded and began folding the map without another word.
emphasize:1.cnHint: 贝尔____说，留给我们到达最外岛屿的时间已经不多了。
emphasize:1.hook: The last star on the horizon blinked out.
emphasize:1.line: 'Let me *emphasize* this: the stars will not wait for us.'

england:1.en: An old trader at the corner stall smiled when he saw our map. 'I once knew a navigator from *England*,' he said, 'who drew sky-maps just like this one.' He touched the edge with a careful finger. 'She said every map has a door — you just have to find the right key.'
england:1.cnHint: 角落摊位的老商人提到，他曾认识一位来自____的绘图师。
england:1.hook: He pressed a small brass key quietly into Old Helm's hand.
england:1.line: 'A navigator from *England* once told me maps have hidden doors.'

moment:1.en: The troupe reached the edge of the last island just before sunrise. Old Helm raised one hand, and everyone stopped. For one quiet *moment*, the whole sky turned gold — stars fading, a new horizon glowing. Nobody spoke. The silence itself felt like a gift none of us expected to find here.
moment:1.cnHint: 在地图尽头，团长举手示意大家停下，天空在那一____变成金色。
moment:1.hook: Then the gold faded — and something beneath us began to move.
moment:1.line: 'Hold still — this *moment* belongs to all of us.'

nice:1.en: Bell spread the final map fragment on a flat stone and studied it with care. The lines were so *nice* in their detail — each curve measured to a hair's width — that she used a thin stick rather than her finger to trace them, afraid even a touch might smear the truth hidden inside.
nice:1.cnHint: 领航员在石头上研究地图碎片，被其____的细节所震惊。
nice:1.hook: One line on the map led not outward, but straight down.
nice:1.line: 'Look at this — the lines are too *nice* to be made by hand.'

peer:1.en: A thick morning mist rolled across the bridge of stone connecting the last two islands. I walked to the edge and tried to *peer* through the white cloud below, searching for solid ground. There was none. Old Helm put a hand on my shoulder and said the map had never lied yet.
peer:1.cnHint: 清晨的迷雾遮住了视线，我努力____向云层下方，却看不到任何地面。
peer:1.line: '*Peer* as hard as you like — you won't see the bottom from here.'

pretty:1.en: A market had grown at the very tip of the island, where traders sold fragments of sky-glass shaped into small *pretties* — charms, pendants, and tiny stars on silver wire. Bell chose one shaped like a compass rose and held it up. Light bent through it and painted colours on the stone path.
pretty:1.cnHint: 在岛屿尽头的市集，领航员挑选了一件玻璃____，光线穿过它折射出彩色光斑。
pretty:1.hook: The colours on the path pointed in a direction no compass had ever shown.
pretty:1.line: 'This little *pretty* bends light — that is not normal glass.'

recommendation:1.en: Old Helm unrolled a note left by a traveller who had reached this island before us. It held only one *recommendation*: cross at dawn, not dusk, and carry something that makes sound. He folded the note carefully, tucked it away, and then looked at Bell's small wind-chime with a satisfied nod.
recommendation:1.cnHint: 团长读到前人留下的纸条，上面只有一条____：黎明时分穿越，并随身携带能发声的东西。
recommendation:1.hook: Bell's wind-chime rang once — though the air was perfectly still.
recommendation:1.line: 'There is only one *recommendation* on this note, so we had better follow it.'

strange:1.en: The fruit sold at the last market tasted like nothing I could name — not sweet, not sour, just *strange* in the way a song sounds when you almost recognise it but cannot place the memory. Silverfang bought a whole bag and said that was exactly the kind of taste worth chasing across islands.
strange:1.cnHint: 市集里的水果味道____，像一首似曾相识却无法辨认的歌，竞争船长却买了一整袋。
strange:1.hook: Silverfang offered one to Old Helm, who turned pale at the smell.
strange:1.line: 'It tastes *strange*, yes — but that is what makes it worth finding.'

widespread:1.en: News of the final map fragment had become *widespread* among sky-traders long before our troupe arrived. Every stall keeper knew our name, every dockhand had a theory about what lay beyond. Silverfang walked ahead of us, visibly annoyed that the secret we had carried so far was now everyone's favourite topic.
widespread:1.cnHint: 关于最后一块地图碎片的消息已经____流传，市集里每个人都知道我们的名字。
widespread:1.hook: One trader knew a detail about the fragment that only we should have known.
widespread:1.line: 'The rumour is *widespread* — someone in our troupe has been talking.'

wonderful:1.en: When Bell placed the last fragment into the map and the whole picture clicked into place, a low hum rose from the stone table. The completed map glowed soft blue. Old Helm looked at it for a long time before he spoke. 'What a *wonderful* problem,' he said, smiling. 'We have run out of edges.'
wonderful:1.cnHint: 领航员将最后的碎片拼入地图，地图发出蓝光，团长看了许久才开口说了一句____的话。
wonderful:1.hook: The map showed one more island — on the back.
wonderful:1.line: 'What a *wonderful* problem — the map has no more edges to find.'

male:1.en: At the edge of the map, a long rope bridge stretched between two islands. Old Helm checked each plank carefully. 'Only the *male* goats cross first,' he said, watching the horned animals test the bridge. 'They are heavier. If it holds them, it holds us.'
male:1.cnHint: 老舵主让____山羊先过桥，测试桥板是否牢固。
male:1.hook: The last plank cracked before the final goat stepped off.
male:1.line: 'Only *male* goats are heavy enough to test this bridge.'

fish:1.en: The market island smelled of salt and smoke. Stalls lined the narrow path, each one piled high with the morning catch. Bell pointed at a silver pile near the end. 'That *fish* still has frost on its scales,' she said. 'Someone flew it in from the ice islands tonight.'
fish:1.cnHint: 贝儿在市场摊位上发现一条来自冰岛的____，鳞片上还带着霜。
fish:1.hook: Beneath the frost, the scales spelled out half a map.
fish:1.line: 'This *fish* came from somewhere we have never been.'

fashion:1.en: The island tailor worked in an open courtyard. Bright cloth hung from every pole. Old Helm watched him stitch in quick, neat loops. 'He sews in the old *fashion*,' Old Helm said quietly, 'the way mapmakers once bound their charts.' I looked closer and saw thread patterns that matched our route.
fashion:1.cnHint: 老舵主发现裁缝缝制的____与地图路线惊人地吻合。
fashion:1.hook: The next stitch traced exactly where our map went blank.
fashion:1.line: 'He works in a *fashion* I have not seen for many years.'

weather:1.en: We landed on the high bridge island just before noon. The wind had turned sharp and cold. Bell spread her hands and read the air like a page. 'The *weather* here changes without warning,' she said. 'The clouds move in circles, not lines. That means the next island is hiding itself from us.'
weather:1.cnHint: 贝儿通过观察____变化，判断下一座岛屿正在刻意隐藏自己。
weather:1.hook: Then the clouds locked into a perfect ring and stopped.
weather:1.line: '*Weather* like this only appears near an island that does not want to be found.'

device:1.en: Near the edge of the platform, a brass ring turned slowly on its own. No hand touched it. Old Helm crouched and studied it for a long moment. 'This *device* reads the pull of the islands below,' he said. 'Someone built it to find what falls off the map. Someone was here before us.'
device:1.cnHint: 老舵主发现一个能探测岛屿引力的____，说明有人捷足先登。
device:1.hook: The ring suddenly spun fast and pointed straight down.
device:1.line: 'This *device* was made to find what maps cannot show.'

farm:1.en: The lower island was quiet and wide. Rows of pale blue plants stretched from edge to edge, tied to wires to stop them drifting off into the sky. 'It is a floating *farm*,' Bell said softly, stepping between the rows. 'They grow food up here and lower it down in baskets. Look, the ropes still move.'
farm:1.cnHint: 贝儿带我们发现了一座用绳索固定作物的空中____。
farm:1.hook: One basket came up from below, and it was not empty.
farm:1.line: 'A *farm* this high means someone has lived here a long time.'

drug:1.en: The old healer's cart stood at the crossroads of four rope paths. Jars of powder and dried leaves covered every shelf. She held one small bottle up to the starlight. 'This *drug* cures sky-sickness,' she told us kindly, 'but only if you take it while the stars are still out. Wait for sunrise and it loses its power.'
drug:1.cnHint: 老药师向我们介绍一种必须在星光下服用的____。
drug:1.hook: Old Helm reached for the bottle, then pulled his hand back.
drug:1.line: 'One drop of this *drug* and the dizziness will be gone.'

heat:1.en: The forge island glowed orange from a distance. We landed on hot stone and felt the air push back against us. A maker in a thick coat hammered a word-plate near a wide fire. 'The *heat* here never drops,' Silverfang said, appearing at our side. 'That is why the word sealed itself into the metal. Cold air would have erased it.'
heat:1.cnHint: 竞争船长解释说，持续的____使文字永久封印在金属板中。
heat:1.hook: Silverfang smiled and slid the word-plate into his coat.
heat:1.line: 'Only this level of *heat* can fix a word into pure metal.'

extreme:1.en: The bridge between two islands was cracked and thin. Old Helm looked at the gap below — nothing but open sky for miles. 'We cross now,' he said. The wind was *extreme*, pushing us sideways with every step. Bell gripped the rope and moved forward anyway.
extreme:1.cnHint: 断桥上，狂风让队伍举步维艰，老舵决定继续穿越____的风。
extreme:1.hook: One rope snapped before Bell reached the other side.
extreme:1.line: 'This *extreme* wind will not stop us — keep moving!'

style:1.en: We landed on a market island where every stall glowed with lanterns. Old Helm moved through the crowd with an easy, unhurried *style* that made people step aside and smile. Bell whispered to me that he had walked like that since before either of us was born.
style:1.cnHint: 集市岛上，老舵独特的____让他在人群中格外引人注目。
style:1.hook: Then a stranger copied his walk — step for step, shadow for shadow.
style:1.line: 'That is his own *style* — no one else can wear it.'

color:1.en: At the edge of the island, a great mural covered the entire cliff face. Each section showed a different sky — sunrise, storm, deep night. Bell ran her fingers along the painted stone. 'Every *color* here is a word the island remembers,' she said softly, and the mural began to glow.
color:1.cnHint: 悬崖壁画上，每一种____都藏着小岛记忆中的一个词语。
color:1.hook: The glow spelled out a name none of us had spoken aloud.
color:1.line: 'Each *color* holds a word — touch the right one.'

meeting:1.en: A circular stone platform stood at the island's centre, worn smooth by years of use. Old Helm said it was built for a *meeting* between the first troupe leaders long ago. Now it was empty — except for a single sealed box sitting exactly in the middle, waiting.
meeting:1.cnHint: 小岛中央的石台曾是早期领队____之地，如今只剩一个神秘封箱。
meeting:1.hook: The box had Old Helm's name carved into its lid.
meeting:1.line: 'This stone marks the *meeting* where everything began.'

volunteer:1.en: The rope bridge needed repair before anyone could cross. Old Helm looked at the group without a word. After a long silence, Bell stepped forward. 'I will *volunteer*,' she said, already tying the work rope around her waist. Nobody argued, because she was already halfway across.
volunteer:1.cnHint: 绳桥需要修缮，小铃主动____，独自系上绳子出发了。
volunteer:1.hook: Halfway across, she stopped and looked down for too long.
volunteer:1.line: 'I *volunteer* — someone has to fix it first.'

deliver:1.en: Old Helm climbed onto the flat rock above the camp and cleared his throat. The whole troupe went quiet. He had gathered us here to *deliver* the plan for reaching the final island — a route none of us had heard before. His voice was steady, but his hands were not.
deliver:1.cnHint: 老舵站上营地岩石，向大家____前往最终小岛的计划。
deliver:1.hook: The route he described had been declared impossible for ten years.
deliver:1.line: 'I will *deliver* the plan — listen carefully, all of you.'

engineering:1.en: The gate to the next island was locked by a puzzle of gears and levers. Bell studied it quietly, then smiled. 'This is *engineering* from the old sky-builders,' she said, reaching for a small lever at the bottom. Three turns later, the gate swung open with a deep, satisfied hum.
engineering:1.cnHint: 通往下一座岛屿的齿轮大门难住了众人，小铃凭借对古代____的了解将它打开。
engineering:1.hook: Beyond the gate, the path split into five directions at once.
engineering:1.line: 'Good *engineering* — whoever built this knew exactly what they were doing.'

tiny:1.en: Tucked behind the market stalls, Bell found a *tiny* door no taller than her knee, set into the base of a great stone pillar. She knelt and pushed it open. Inside was a single folded map, still warm, as though someone had just placed it there moments before we arrived.
tiny:1.cnHint: 小铃在石柱根部发现一扇____的小门，里面藏着一张还有余温的地图。
tiny:1.hook: The map showed an island that should not exist yet.
tiny:1.line: 'Behind this *tiny* door — that is where the answer hides.'

intelligence:1.en: Old Helm spread the old map across a flat rock at the edge of the island. 'This part of the sky is blank,' he said, tapping the empty space. 'Finding the next island takes more than luck — it takes *intelligence*.' Bell nodded, already studying the star patterns above.
intelligence:1.cnHint: 老船长说，找到下一座岛屿靠的不是运气，而是____。
intelligence:1.hook: The blank space on the map began to glow faintly.
intelligence:1.line: '*Intelligence* gets us further than any compass ever could,' said Old Helm.

uk:1.en: Bell pulled a small coin from her coat and held it up to the starlight. 'I found this on the last island,' she said. 'See that tiny stamp? A traveller from the *UK* must have passed through here once.' Old Helm turned the coin slowly, his eyes full of questions.
uk:1.cnHint: 小铃发现一枚带有____印记的硬币，说明曾有远方的旅行者到过此处。
uk:1.hook: On its other side was a map no one had ever seen.
uk:1.line: 'Someone from the *UK* walked this island long before us,' said Bell.

user:1.en: At the edge of the landing dock stood an old machine covered in moss. A small sign read: FOR THE *USER* OF THIS STATION — SPEAK YOUR DESTINATION. Bell leaned close and whispered the name of the next island. A low hum filled the air, and a drawer slid open.
user:1.cnHint: 老旧机器上有一块牌子，提示____按指示说出目的地，机器随即有了反应。
user:1.hook: Inside the drawer lay a folded piece of sky-blue paper.
user:1.line: 'Every *user* of this station leaves a little of themselves behind,' Old Helm said softly.

park:1.en: The troupe landed on a wide green island where neat rows of trees lined a quiet path. 'They *park* their sky-boats here during the star festivals,' Old Helm explained, pointing to a row of empty docks. Bell walked between the trees, fingers trailing across the bark, listening.
park:1.cnHint: 老船长解释说，节日期间人们会把飞船____在这片树木整齐的地方。
park:1.hook: One of the docks still held a boat — its lantern still lit.
park:1.line: 'We can *park* here safely; no one has been back for years,' said Old Helm.

reward:1.en: Silverfang leaned against the stone gate, arms crossed. 'I found the word fragment first,' he said. 'Where is my *reward*?' Old Helm smiled and placed a small glowing tile in his hand. Silverfang stared at it, surprised — it was exactly the piece his own map was missing.
reward:1.cnHint: 竞争船长要求得到____，老船长给了他一块恰好能补全其地图的发光碎片。
reward:1.hook: Silverfang's expression shifted from pride to something closer to wonder.
reward:1.line: 'A true *reward* is the piece you didn't know you needed,' said Old Helm.

credit:1.en: Bell finished marking the new route and stepped back. Silverfang cleared his throat. 'That path was partly my idea,' he said. Old Helm looked at the map, then at Bell. 'Then the *credit* belongs to both of you,' he said warmly. Bell smiled; Silverfang looked almost pleased.
credit:1.cnHint: 老船长说，新航路的____应该由小铃和竞争船长共同分享。
credit:1.hook: The route glowed gold the moment both of them touched the map.
credit:1.line: 'Give Bell the *credit* — she made the final call,' said Old Helm.

progress:1.en: The troupe had been walking the ridge path for an hour. 'Are we getting anywhere?' I asked. Old Helm watched the horizon slowly shift. 'Look behind you,' he said. I turned — the dock was a tiny dot far below. 'That is how *progress* feels,' he said. 'Quiet, then suddenly visible.'
progress:1.cnHint: 老船长让我回头看，用眼前的景象告诉我什么是真正的____。
progress:1.hook: Ahead, the ridge opened onto something none of us expected.
progress:1.line: 'We *progress* best when we stop rushing and start noticing,' Old Helm said.

snack:1.en: We stopped at a small open stall near the island's edge. A cheerful vendor handed Bell a paper cone of warm seeds. 'Best *snack* on any floating island,' he said proudly. Bell offered some to Old Helm, who chewed one thoughtfully. 'He's not wrong,' Old Helm admitted with a grin.
snack:1.cnHint: 我们在路边摊停下，小贩自豪地说这是所有浮岛上最好的____。
snack:1.hook: Tucked inside the paper cone was a tiny folded map.
snack:1.line: 'Never skip a *snack* stop — the best clues hide in the smallest places,' said Old Helm.

immediately:1.en: The edge island had no bridge, only a narrow rope crossing over open sky. Old Helm stepped onto the rope, and *immediately* the wind picked up, pushing us sideways. Bell grabbed the guide line and steadied us. We crossed in silence, hearts loud, eyes fixed on the far platform where a glowing word waited.
immediately:1.cnHint: 绳桥上，风一刮，老舵____采取了行动，让队伍安全抵达对岸。
immediately:1.hook: But the glowing word began to sink before we arrived.
immediately:1.line: '*Immediately* after you hear my signal, move — do not wait.'

improvement:1.en: Old Helm unrolled the map on a flat rock at the island's edge. He traced the new route we had found and nodded slowly. 'This is a real *improvement*,' he said. The old path had curved for days; this one cut straight through morning cloud. Bell marked it in ink, smiling wide.
improvement:1.cnHint: 老舵在岩石上对照地图，认为新路线是一次真正的____。
improvement:1.hook: Then Bell's ink line crossed a section marked with a warning sign.
improvement:1.line: 'Every *improvement* we find brings us one step closer to the final island.'

afternoon:1.en: We landed on Dustwhirl Island just as the sun leaned low and golden. The *afternoon* light turned the sandy paths copper and warm. Market stalls lined the main street, selling bottled echoes and pressed starlights. Bell bought a small compass that spun in colours. Old Helm said we had one hour before dusk closed the gates.
afternoon:1.cnHint: 我们在____时分降落在尘旋岛，赶在城门关闭前逛了一圈集市。
afternoon:1.hook: The gate keeper was already lifting the heavy lock toward the bolt.
afternoon:1.line: 'By *afternoon* tomorrow, this whole island may have drifted east.'

expand:1.en: Old Helm held the new word-fragment up to the starlight. Before our eyes, the map began to *expand*, its edges pushing outward like a slow breath, revealing a cluster of islands that had been blank space only a moment before. Bell leaned in close, counting the new shapes, her voice barely a whisper.
expand:1.cnHint: 老舵将词语碎片举向星光，地图随之____，显现出新的岛群。
expand:1.hook: One of the newly revealed islands had no name, only a question mark.
expand:1.line: 'Watch the map *expand* — every word we collect grows our world.'

regardless:1.en: A sudden gust tilted our vessel sharply to the left. Half the crew grabbed ropes; the other half froze. Bell kept calling out headings, *regardless* of the chaos around her. Her voice was steady, clear, almost calm. Because of her, we held course and cleared the edge of the storm cloud with the hull intact.
regardless:1.cnHint: 风暴突然袭来，小铃____混乱，继续大声报告航向，稳住了船。
regardless:1.hook: A second gust, far stronger than the first, was already building.
regardless:1.line: 'We press on, *regardless* — this troupe does not turn back from wind.'

rid:1.en: The old word-fragment we carried had grown heavy and dark, dragging our vessel lower with each hour. Old Helm said we needed to *rid* ourselves of it before crossing the deep sky. We placed it on a drifting stone platform and pushed off. The ship rose at once, light as a lantern.
rid:1.cnHint: 旧词语碎片越来越沉，老舵决定____它，船才能继续飞行。
rid:1.hook: The dark fragment pulsed once on the stone, then cracked open.
rid:1.line: 'We must *rid* the ship of dead words — they pull us toward the void.'

dog:1.en: At the busy crossing between two rope bridges, a small *dog* sat perfectly still, staring at us. It wore a collar made of tiny brass letters. Old Helm crouched down and read them aloud. The letters spelled a word we had been searching for all morning. The dog then trotted away without looking back.
dog:1.cnHint: 在两座绳桥交叉口，一只____的项圈上藏着我们苦寻已久的词语。
dog:1.hook: We followed, but the dog vanished around a corner of pure mist.
dog:1.line: 'That *dog* knew exactly where we needed to go — follow it, quickly.'

busy:1.en: The market street of Windfall Island was *busy* at midday — voices layered over music, colours spilling from every stall. Old Helm moved through the crowd with ease, nodding left and right. Bell stayed close, notebook open, writing down every strange word she heard. I tried to keep up, stepping around barrels, crates, and stray cats.
busy:1.cnHint: 午间的集市街道____而热闹，小铃边走边记录听到的每一个奇特词语。
busy:1.hook: Then every voice on the street stopped at exactly the same moment.
busy:1.line: 'Stay close in a *busy* place — words hide in the noise between people.'

analysis:1.en: At the edge of the island, Bell spread the old map across a flat rock. She traced each ink mark slowly. 'My *analysis* shows a hidden bridge just past that cloud wall,' she said. Old Helm nodded, his eyes following her finger to where the sky turned silver.
analysis:1.cnHint: 小铃对地图进行____，发现了云墙之后隐藏的桥。
analysis:1.hook: But the cloud wall began to move toward them.
analysis:1.line: 'My *analysis* shows a hidden bridge just past that cloud wall.'

application:1.en: Old Helm pulled a folded paper from his coat and smoothed it on his knee. 'This *application* asks the Sky Guild for passage through the final gate,' he said. Bell stamped it with the troupe's seal. I watched the ink dry and felt a door about to open somewhere far above us.
application:1.cnHint: 老舵长填写____，请求天空公会开放最终的大门。
application:1.hook: The Guild's reply bird was already circling overhead.
application:1.line: 'This *application* asks the Sky Guild for passage through the final gate.'

living:1.en: We landed on a narrow ledge where small lanterns lined the path like stars fallen to earth. A woman there sold warm bread and spoke of island life with pride. 'Everything here is a *living* map,' she said, sweeping her arm across the glowing rooftops. Old Helm smiled and bought the whole basket.
living:1.cnHint: 一位卖面包的女人说这里的一切都是____的地图。
living:1.hook: One lantern flickered and revealed a door no one had noticed.
living:1.line: 'Everything here is a *living* map of the world above.'

proposal:1.en: Silverfang climbed down from her ship and walked straight to Old Helm. She held out a rolled note tied with blue string. 'Read my *proposal*,' she said, calm as the morning sky. 'We reach the map's end together, or neither of us reaches it at all.' The wind went quiet around us.
proposal:1.cnHint: 银牙船长向老舵长提出一个____，要求两队合作前往地图尽头。
proposal:1.hook: Old Helm unrolled the note very, very slowly.
proposal:1.line: 'Read my *proposal* — together we reach the end, or neither does.'

relevant:1.en: I found a pile of old notes in the waystation near the cloud gate. Most were useless lists of supplies and complaints about the wind. Bell leaned over my shoulder. 'Only the ones about star patterns are *relevant* to our path,' she said, pulling three pages free and tucking them into her coat.
relevant:1.cnHint: 小铃告诉我只有关于星象的笔记与我们的路线____。
relevant:1.hook: The third page had today's date already written on it.
relevant:1.line: 'Only the star-pattern notes are *relevant* to where we are going.'

senior:1.en: Outside the gate, a group of young navigators were arguing over a chart. An older man in a faded blue coat stepped forward and settled the dispute with two quiet sentences. Bell told me he was the most respected *senior* of the Sky Guild, someone who had flown every route twice. He glanced at me and nodded.
senior:1.cnHint: 天空公会中最受尊敬的____用两句话平息了一场争论。
senior:1.hook: Then he handed me a chart no one else had seen.
senior:1.line: 'The most respected *senior* of the Guild once flew this very route.'

table:1.en: In the open square at the island's edge, Old Helm set the word-fragments on a low stone *table* one by one. Each piece glowed faintly where it touched the others. Bell held her breath. When the last fragment clicked into place, a new island rose on the horizon like a slow, quiet breath.
table:1.cnHint: 老舵长在石____上将碎片拼合，一座新岛屿随即升起。
table:1.hook: The new island was shaped exactly like the missing piece.
table:1.line: 'Place the last fragment on the *table* — gently, now, gently.'

campus:1.en: The floating *campus* of the Guild drifted into view just after dawn — wide green paths between stone towers, students carrying charts like wings under their arms. Old Helm said he had studied here once, long ago. I looked at the towers reaching into the clouds and felt the word 'beginning' hum somewhere in my chest.
campus:1.cnHint: 天空公会的____在黎明后缓缓出现，老舵长曾在此求学。
campus:1.hook: One tower had our troupe's symbol carved above its door.
campus:1.line: 'I walked this very *campus* forty years ago, and here I am again.'

retire:1.en: The last lantern on Driftstone Square flickered low. Old Helm stretched his arms wide and announced it was time to *retire* for the night. The troupe rolled out blankets under a canopy of stars, but I lay awake, watching a distant island drift slowly into the dark like a sleepy thought.
retire:1.cnHint: 老团长宣布今晚该____了，但叙述者望着远处漂移的岛屿久久无法入眠。
retire:1.hook: Something on that drifting island had just lit up.
retire:1.line: 'Time to *retire*, young one — tomorrow the map grows longer.'

sea:1.en: We stood at the very edge of the lowest island, where the stone dropped away into open sky. Below, where the clouds parted, I saw it: a shimmering expanse the old charts called the Cloud *Sea*. Bell pressed a brass scope to her eye and said the next island floated somewhere inside it.
sea:1.cnHint: 站在岛屿边缘，叙述者俯视云层，第一次看见了传说中的云____。
sea:1.hook: The Cloud Sea swallowed the path whole.
sea:1.line: 'That *sea* of clouds hides the word we need most,' Bell said quietly.

town:1.en: After three hours of walking a rope bridge, we arrived at a *town* built entirely on the back of a slow, enormous creature. Lanterns swayed with each of its deep breaths, and market stalls sold things I had no names for. Old Helm bought a warm pastry and called it research.
town:1.cnHint: 旅团踏上一座建在巨大生物背上的____，集市上摆满了叙述者叫不出名字的东西。
town:1.hook: The creature beneath us suddenly changed direction.
town:1.line: 'Every *town* on a living island must follow the island's own will,' Old Helm said.

gap:1.en: The bridge between Twin Spires had cracked overnight, leaving a *gap* wide enough to swallow our wagon whole. Bell measured it with a length of rope, frowned, and measured it again. We gathered every plank we could find and built a crossing that looked impossible but held every single step.
gap:1.cnHint: 两座石塔之间的桥断裂，出现了一道____，旅团只好自己动手搭建临时通道。
gap:1.hook: The last plank groaned as Old Helm stepped across.
gap:1.line: 'A *gap* like this is just an invitation to be clever,' Bell said, knotting the rope.

generation:1.en: Carved into the wall of the canyon pass were names — hundreds of them, layer by layer. Old Helm traced the oldest letters gently. Every *generation* of travellers who crossed here had added their mark, and the stone was nearly full. He handed me a small chisel without a word.
generation:1.cnHint: 峡谷石壁上刻满了历代旅人的名字，老团长递给叙述者一把凿子，示意他也留下印记。
generation:1.hook: There was just enough space left for one more name.
generation:1.line: 'Each *generation* leaves a word here — what will yours be?' Old Helm asked.

guide:1.en: The fog rolled in so thick we could not see our own boots. Then a small creature, no bigger than a lantern, appeared at the edge of the path. It chirped once and began to walk. Old Helm nodded as though he had expected it. 'Let it *guide* us,' he said, and we followed.
guide:1.cnHint: 浓雾中，一只小生物出现在路边，老团长让大家跟着它作为____穿越迷雾。
guide:1.hook: The creature stopped at a door no map had ever shown.
guide:1.line: 'Let it *guide* us — this island sends help when help is needed,' Old Helm said.

household:1.en: We were welcomed into a *household* perched on the very tip of a needle-thin spire. There were six family members, two pet birds, and more tea than I thought possible. They spoke a dialect Old Helm half-understood, but warmth needs no translation. We left with full cups and a hand-drawn map scrap.
household:1.cnHint: 旅团被一个住在细塔顶端的____热情招待，离开时还收到了一张手绘地图碎片。
household:1.hook: The map scrap showed an island none of us recognised.
household:1.line: 'Every *household* on the high spires guards a piece of the old chart,' Silverfang noted.

luxury:1.en: Silverfang's rival vessel had a galley of polished wood, cushioned seats, and hot meals served on real plates — a *luxury* our patched-up wagon could never match. Silverfang gave us a slow, proud tour. Old Helm just smiled, patted our wagon's dented side, and said character was worth more than comfort.
luxury:1.cnHint: 银牙骄傲地展示自己船上的____设施，老团长却拍着旅团破旧的车厢，说性格比享受更有价值。
luxury:1.hook: Then Silverfang's fancy galley stove cracked clean in two.
luxury:1.line: '*Luxury* fades — a good crew and an open sky last forever,' Old Helm said, still smiling.

campaign:1.en: Old Helm unrolled the new map fragment on a flat stone. 'Every word we collect is part of a bigger *campaign*,' he said, sweeping his arm across the sky. The floating islands ahead glittered like scattered coins. I understood then: we were not just travelling. We were fighting for something.
campaign:1.cnHint: 老赫姆说，我们收集每个词都是一场更大____的一部分。
campaign:1.hook: But the map showed an island none of us had named.
campaign:1.line: 'This *campaign* has no end, only the next horizon.'

hurt:1.en: Bell landed badly on the mossy edge of the dock, one ankle twisted under her. She stood up quickly and waved us off. 'It does not *hurt*,' she said, though her face told a different story. Old Helm handed her his walking stick without a word. She took it.
hurt:1.cnHint: 贝尔落地时扭了脚踝，却说一点也不____。
hurt:1.hook: She kept her eyes fixed on the island ahead, not on the pain.
hurt:1.line: 'It does not *hurt*,' Bell said, smiling too quickly.

initiative:1.en: Nobody told me to fix the broken rope on the dock ramp. I just picked up the loose end and tied it before the others noticed. Old Helm gave a slow nod. 'Good *initiative*,' he said quietly. Silverfang raised an eyebrow from the wheel. I felt, for the first time, like part of the troupe.
initiative:1.cnHint: 没人吩咐我，但我主动修好了绳子，老赫姆夸我有____。
initiative:1.hook: Silverfang's raised eyebrow was either approval or a warning.
initiative:1.line: 'Good *initiative* — now do not make it a habit of stealing my jobs.'

jump:1.en: The gap between our deck and the stone pier was wider than it looked. Silverfang went first, clearing it easily. Then he turned and called to me. My heart lifted into my throat. I took three steps back, breathed out, and *jumped*. The wind caught me for one bright second.
jump:1.cnHint: 石码头和甲板之间有段距离，我鼓起勇气____了过去。
jump:1.hook: My feet hit stone — but the map fragment was no longer in my pocket.
jump:1.line: 'You *jumped* well enough. Next time, hold on to the map.'

lie:1.en: The oldest island on the chart was said to *lie* at the very edge of the known sky, past the curtain of low clouds where no wind blew. Bell traced the route with one finger and said nothing for a long moment. I leaned over her shoulder and felt the distance like a weight.
lie:1.cnHint: 传说最古老的岛屿____在已知天空的尽头。
lie:1.hook: Bell's finger stopped, and she slowly shook her head.
lie:1.line: 'The island does not *lie* where the old maps say it does.'

lunch:1.en: We ate *lunch* on a wide stone terrace that jutted out over the clouds. Silverfang had traded a word fragment for a bag of spiced bread and dried fruit at the last island market. The bread was warm. Below us, nothing but white mist. I decided this was the finest meal I had ever tasted.
lunch:1.cnHint: 我们在悬于云端的石台上吃____，景色壮阔。
lunch:1.hook: Then a second ship appeared below us, rising fast through the mist.
lunch:1.line: '*Lunch* on the edge of the world — not bad for a new member.'

necessarily:1.en: Old Helm studied the glowing word fragment we had just found. 'A longer path does not *necessarily* mean a wrong one,' he said, setting it back on the stone. Bell looked relieved. I was not sure I agreed, but I was learning that his calm always had a reason hiding inside it.
necessarily:1.cnHint: 老赫姆说，路途更长不____意味着方向有误。
necessarily:1.hook: The fragment pulsed once, then pointed away from the main route.
necessarily:1.line: 'More difficult does not *necessarily* mean impossible, young one.'

psychologist:1.en: Among the islanders at the busy terrace market was a quiet woman who read people like open books. Silverfang leaned over and whispered, 'She is a *psychologist* — studies how fear and hope move inside a person.' She glanced at me just then, and I felt oddly, pleasantly seen.
psychologist:1.cnHint: 市集上有位____，专门研究人内心的恐惧与希望。
psychologist:1.hook: She pressed a small word fragment into my hand without speaking.
psychologist:1.line: 'A good *psychologist* knows what you feel before you do,' Silverfang said.

destroy:1.en: The wind hit the edge of the island so hard that morning. Old Helm grabbed the map before it flew off the rail. 'One bad gust could *destroy* everything we have found,' he said quietly. I held the lantern close and watched the sky turn a deep, warning red.
destroy:1.cnHint: 一阵狂风险些将队伍所有的努力____掉，团长及时抓住了地图。
destroy:1.hook: The red sky meant something far worse was still coming.
destroy:1.line: 'One bad gust could *destroy* everything we have found.'

drop:1.en: Bell leaned over the edge of the floating island and let one small seed fall from her fingers. We all watched in silence as that single *drop* of living green disappeared into the clouds far below. 'Every new island begins like that,' she said with a small, warm smile.
drop:1.cnHint: 领航员让一粒种子从岛边____下，消失在云层之中。
drop:1.hook: But something far below caught the seed before it vanished.
drop:1.line: 'Every new island begins with a single *drop* like this.'

efficiency:1.en: Silverfang's crew unloaded the supply crates in perfect order, each box placed exactly where it was needed. Old Helm watched with clear admiration. 'Their *efficiency* puts our troupe to shame,' he whispered to me. I had to agree — we had spent all morning just finding our own rope.
efficiency:1.cnHint: 银牙船长的船员们以极高的____卸货，令团长深感钦佩。
efficiency:1.hook: Then Silverfang glanced our way, and his smile held a challenge.
efficiency:1.line: 'Their *efficiency* puts our whole troupe to shame, I think.'

italian:1.en: At the open-air market on the cloud-edge platform, an old trader spread out a hand-drawn chart and spoke in a warm, rolling tongue. Bell leaned close. 'That sounds like *Italian*,' she said softly, eyes wide with wonder. Far from any sea, that familiar language felt like a small, impossible gift.
italian:1.cnHint: 在空中集市上，一位老商人说着听起来像____语的话，令领航员大为惊讶。
italian:1.hook: The trader smiled and slipped the chart under the table.
italian:1.line: 'That sounds like *Italian* — but how did it reach here?'

newspaper:1.en: Pinned to the notice board at the island's main gate was a single sheet of printed paper — a *newspaper*, yellowed and old. The headline read: LAST ISLAND FOUND. Old Helm went still. 'That date,' he said slowly, tapping the paper, 'is from before any of us were born.'
newspaper:1.cnHint: 岛门口的布告板上贴着一张泛黄的____，头条令团长神情凝重。
newspaper:1.hook: Someone had circled one word in the headline with red ink.
newspaper:1.line: 'This *newspaper* is older than every map we own combined.'

piece:1.en: The map fragment we had carried for weeks turned out to be only a small *piece* of a much larger chart spread across the market floor. Bell knelt and fit our fragment into place. The whole northern sky route appeared at once, glowing faintly at every joined edge.
piece:1.cnHint: 队伍带了数周的地图碎片原来只是更大地图的一____，拼合后北方航线显现出来。
piece:1.hook: One piece of the route was still missing — and someone had torn it away.
piece:1.line: 'Our fragment is only one *piece* of something far greater.'

target:1.en: Bell drew a small circle on the new chart and tapped it twice. 'This island is our next *target*,' she said clearly, tracing the air-path with one steady finger. Old Helm nodded, already rolling up his pack. I felt the familiar pull in my chest — that good ache of a journey about to begin.
target:1.cnHint: 领航员在新地图上画圈，将下一座岛定为队伍的____。
target:1.hook: But the island on the chart had no recorded name at all.
target:1.line: 'This island right here is our next *target*, no question.'

actual:1.en: I had imagined the edge of the map as a faint, quiet line. The *actual* border was nothing like that — it was a wall of slow silver light, humming low, stretching from cloud to star. Old Helm put one hand near it and pulled back fast. 'Now you understand,' he said simply.
actual:1.cnHint: 我以为地图的边界只是一条细线，但____情况令所有人都震惊。
actual:1.hook: Something on the other side of the light moved toward us.
actual:1.line: 'The *actual* edge is nothing like any of us imagined it.'

pursue:1.en: The troupe landed on a narrow island where two roads split in opposite directions. Old Helm knelt and studied the cracked stone beneath our boots. 'We must *pursue* the road that leans toward the light,' he said, pointing east. Bell marked the direction on her chart with a careful stroke.
pursue:1.cnHint: 老团长研究石路，决定____光线方向的那条路。
pursue:1.hook: But both roads seemed to glow at exactly the same hour.
pursue:1.line: 'We *pursue* the light, and the map will answer us.'

site:1.en: Bell led us down a spiral staircase carved into the island's edge until we reached a wide flat stone platform open to the sky. 'This is the *site* where old travellers once gathered to trade words,' she said softly. Tiny grooves in the stone still held the shape of long-forgotten letters.
site:1.cnHint: 贝尔带领大家来到一个古老的____，地面上刻有神秘字迹。
site:1.hook: One groove was still warm to the touch.
site:1.line: 'Every great journey has a *site* where it truly begins.'

absorb:1.en: At the market square of Driftmoor Island, a storyteller stood at the centre reciting words aloud. I watched the youngest children in the crowd *absorb* each sound with wide, still eyes, as if the words were water and they were dry earth. Old Helm smiled and said nothing. He simply listened too.
absorb:1.cnHint: 漂流岛集市上，孩子们全神贯注地____着讲故事人的每一个词。
absorb:1.hook: One word made every child in the crowd go completely silent.
absorb:1.line: 'Let yourself *absorb* every word — they are the real treasure.'

advance:1.en: Silverfang's ship pulled ahead of ours as we crossed the Pale Gap, a stretch of open sky between two island chains. 'His *advance* was planned,' Bell said quietly, her eyes fixed on the rival vessel. Old Helm folded his arms and watched the gap between the two ships slowly, steadily grow wider.
advance:1.cnHint: 银牙的船在空中率先____，贝尔意识到这是早有预谋的。
advance:1.hook: Then Silverfang's ship suddenly stopped and turned to face us.
advance:1.line: 'His *advance* means nothing if we hold the better map.'

capable:1.en: The rope bridge across Windhook Gorge swayed hard in the gusts. I gripped the ropes and froze. Old Helm put a steady hand on my shoulder. 'You are *capable* of this,' he said simply. I took one breath, then one step, and the bridge steadied beneath me as though the island itself agreed.
capable:1.cnHint: 面对摇晃的绳桥，老团长告诉叙述者他是____做到的。
capable:1.hook: Halfway across, the bridge snapped one of its outer ropes.
capable:1.line: 'You are *capable* — your feet already know the way.'

dollar:1.en: At the floating bazaar above Crestfall Island, a merchant held up a single gold coin stamped with a star. 'One *dollar* of sky-silver buys one word fragment,' he said, grinning broadly. Old Helm reached into his coat, paused, then traded a small carved button instead. The merchant accepted it without question.
dollar:1.cnHint: 在空中集市，商人开价一枚____换取一片地图碎片。
dollar:1.hook: The carved button began to glow the moment it changed hands.
dollar:1.line: 'One *dollar* of sky-silver, and the word is yours.'

double:1.en: The word fragment we found at Sunpeak Terrace was strange — it showed a path that looped back on itself, making the journey *double* in length before opening to a hidden ledge. Bell traced the loop twice with her finger, then laughed with surprise. 'It is not a mistake,' she said. 'It is a test.'
double:1.cnHint: 贝尔发现地图碎片上的路径将旅程变为____长，这其实是一个考验。
double:1.hook: The hidden ledge held a second map, older than the first.
double:1.line: 'A *double* road is the island's way of asking if you are sure.'

federal:1.en: Near the edge of Goldmere Island stood a carved pillar marked with the seal of the old Sky Council — a *federal* body of island leaders that had once kept peace across the whole chain. Moss covered half the seal now. Bell pressed her palm against the stone. 'They agreed on one language,' she murmured. 'Words.'
federal:1.cnHint: 古老的石柱上刻着天空议会的印章，那是曾经管理群岛的____机构。
federal:1.hook: Below the seal, someone had scratched a single question mark.
federal:1.line: 'The *federal* seal means every island once shared the same words.'

disadvantage:1.en: The edge of the map was a crumbling stone road. Old Helm spread the newest fragment on a flat rock and frowned. 'Every other troupe travels by wind-ship,' he said. 'Walking puts us at a clear *disadvantage*.' Bell looked at the dusty path ahead and smiled anyway.
disadvantage:1.cnHint: 老舵主担心步行会让我们处于____，但领航员仍然微笑着。
disadvantage:1.hook: Something on that road had already seen us coming.
disadvantage:1.line: 'Walking puts us at a clear *disadvantage*, but I know a shortcut.'

discuss:1.en: Bell called us to gather near the iron signpost where three roads met. She laid out two map fragments side by side and asked us to *discuss* which path led closer to the next island gate. The wind carried our voices upward, into the bright open sky.
discuss:1.cnHint: 领航员让大家在路口____该走哪条路。
discuss:1.hook: Only one road was safe — and none of us agreed on which.
discuss:1.line: 'Let us *discuss* this calmly before the fog rolls in.'

psychological:1.en: The bridge ahead looked solid, but Old Helm warned us that the island's old builders had laid *psychological* traps — paths that felt wrong on purpose, meant to turn travellers back with nothing but doubt. Bell stepped forward first, proving the bridge was real.
psychological:1.cnHint: 老舵主提醒大家，前方的障碍是____上的陷阱，并非真实危险。
psychological:1.hook: Past the bridge, the air tasted like forgotten fear.
psychological:1.line: 'It is only a *psychological* trick — do not let doubt win.'

request:1.en: A small painted sign hung on the gate at the island's rim. It carried a single *request*: leave one word on the stone shelf before you pass. Old Helm placed the word 'home.' Bell placed 'star.' I stood there a long moment, then added my own.
request:1.cnHint: 路口的牌子上写着一个____，每位旅人需留下一个词才能通过。
request:1.hook: No one had warned us the shelf remembered every word left behind.
request:1.line: 'My only *request* is that you each choose honestly.'

symptom:1.en: Halfway along the rim road, Old Helm stopped walking. He pressed one hand to the old compass on his belt. 'A needle spinning with no north is a *symptom* of a broken map fragment nearby,' he said quietly. Bell was already scanning the low stone walls around us.
symptom:1.cnHint: 罗盘失灵是____，说明附近有受损的地图碎片。
symptom:1.hook: Behind the nearest wall, something small was glowing.
symptom:1.line: 'A spinning needle is always the first *symptom* — stay close.'

upon:1.en: Bell climbed the highest point of the rim road and looked out. *Upon* the far horizon floated a thin ribbon of island, pale green and barely visible. 'That is where the last fragment waits,' she said softly. Old Helm shielded his eyes and nodded without a word.
upon:1.cnHint: 在地平线____，大家隐约看见了下一座岛屿。
upon:1.hook: The ribbon of island flickered once, then held steady.
upon:1.line: 'Look — *upon* that horizon sits the place we have sought.'

argument:1.en: Old Helm and Bell stood at the fork in the rim road, neither moving. Their *argument* was quiet but firm: one wanted the high cliff path, the other the low river track. I listened to both sides, then pointed at the sky. A single bright star hung directly above the river.
argument:1.cnHint: 老舵主和领航员在岔路口发生了____，我指着星星化解了僵局。
argument:1.hook: The star moved — just once — before going still.
argument:1.line: 'Our *argument* ends here; the star has chosen for us.'

crisis:1.en: The outer rim road began to crack beneath our feet — a slow, grinding sound rising from below the island's edge. Old Helm called it a map *crisis*: when a fragment is missing too long, the land it describes starts to forget its own shape. We ran for the centre path.
crisis:1.cnHint: 岛屿边缘开始碎裂，老舵主说这是地图____，我们拼命向中心跑去。
crisis:1.hook: The ground behind us fell away into silent sky.
crisis:1.line: 'This is a map *crisis* — we have minutes, not hours.'

insist:1.en: The morning wind carried the smell of rain across the docking platform. Old Helm studied the torn map fragment we had just found, turning it slowly in his hands. 'We go north,' Bell said. But Old Helm would *insist* on waiting until the clouds lifted and every path was clear.
insist:1.cnHint: 老舵 ____要等云散之后再出发，让大家都有些着急。
insist:1.hook: The clouds, however, showed no sign of moving.
insist:1.line: 'I *insist* we wait — one wrong step here and the island is lost.'

investigation:1.en: A crowd had gathered around a cracked stone pillar at the edge of the market. Someone had scratched strange marks into it overnight. Bell pulled out her compass and began a quiet *investigation*, moving around the pillar and measuring each mark with careful fingers.
investigation:1.cnHint: 小铃对石柱上的奇怪刻痕展开了一番____。
investigation:1.hook: The last mark pointed straight down, into the island itself.
investigation:1.line: 'This *investigation* will tell us who — or what — was here before us.'

limited:1.en: Our supply bag was lighter than it should have been. Old Helm spread everything on the ground: three candles, half a loaf, and one coil of rope. 'Our time and our supplies are both *limited*,' he said, counting each item twice before packing it away again.
limited:1.cnHint: 老舵提醒大家，资源____，必须谨慎行动。
limited:1.hook: Somewhere ahead, the next island was already drifting away from us.
limited:1.line: 'We have *limited* rope, so choose the shorter path.'

listen:1.en: The old market square was loud with traders calling and bells ringing. Bell touched my arm and pointed up. Above all the noise, a faint musical hum rose from the flagstones beneath our feet. 'Stop and *listen*,' she said softly. 'The island is trying to tell us something.'
listen:1.cnHint: 小铃让大家停下来____，因为脚下的石板似乎发出了声音。
listen:1.hook: The hum grew louder the moment everyone fell silent.
listen:1.line: 'Just *listen* — do you hear the stones singing under your feet?'

master:1.en: At the top of the hill stood a small workshop with a sign above the door. An old woman inside was shaping a new compass lens by hand, her movements quick and sure. Old Helm bowed low. 'She is a *master* of her craft,' he whispered. 'We are lucky to find her here.'
master:1.cnHint: 老舵向大家介绍山顶工坊里的那位____，说她能修好我们的罗盘。
master:1.hook: She looked up, and her eyes were already on the torn map in my hand.
master:1.line: 'A true *master* never stops learning — remember that on your travels.'

newly:1.en: We reached the far platform just as the sun broke through. A bridge of pale stone stretched ahead, its surface still bright and unscuffed. Silverfang jumped onto it first, then laughed. 'This is *newly* laid,' he said, knocking his boot against the stone. 'Someone built this for us — or just before us.'
newly:1.cnHint: 银牙发现前方的石桥是____建好的，感到既惊喜又警惕。
newly:1.hook: Fresh chisel marks on the first stone still held traces of warm dust.
newly:1.line: 'It is *newly* built — which means someone knew we were coming.'

north:1.en: Bell unrolled the map fragment on the platform railing and traced a thin dotted line with her finger. Every other path curved away toward the bright southern islands we already knew. Only one line ran straight and cold toward the edge of the paper. 'The next word lies to the *north*,' she said quietly.
north:1.cnHint: 小铃查看地图后告诉大家，下一个目标在____方向。
north:1.hook: No one had ever brought back a story from the northern edge of the sky.
north:1.line: 'Head *north* — and keep the star cluster on your left shoulder.'

obviously:1.en: We found the word carved into a low wall behind the floating market, half-hidden by a hanging cloth. Silverfang pulled the cloth aside and stepped back with a grin. The carving glowed a soft gold in the afternoon light. 'It is *obviously* meant to be found,' he said, 'by someone who knows where to look.'
obviously:1.cnHint: 银牙认为这个词的位置____是故意留给寻找它的人的。
obviously:1.hook: But the cloth had been hung there very, very recently.
obviously:1.line: 'This is *obviously* a message — now we just have to read it right.'

pose:1.en: At the edge of the first floating island, Old Helm stopped and struck a wide *pose*, arms out, chin high, as if he owned the whole sky. 'Map fragments love a confident traveller,' he said. The stars above seemed to lean in, curious.
pose:1.cnHint: 老赫姆在岛边____，仿佛整片天空都属于他。
pose:1.hook: But something beneath the island shifted, slowly.
pose:1.line: 'Strike a bold *pose*, and the island will trust you.'

stimulate:1.en: Bell rang a small silver bell at the cloud-gate, and the sound seemed to *stimulate* the sleeping vines around it. They uncurled, glowing faintly green, and a hidden path revealed itself between two drifting rocks. The troupe stepped forward, breath held.
stimulate:1.cnHint: 贝尔的铃声____了沉睡的藤蔓，一条隐秘小路就此现身。
stimulate:1.hook: The path only stayed open for thirty seconds.
stimulate:1.line: 'A clear tone will *stimulate* the gate — ring it once, firmly.'

switch:1.en: Halfway across the sky bridge, the lanterns suddenly went dark. Old Helm reached for a stone panel on the rail and pressed it, trying to *switch* the lights back on. Nothing happened. Below us, clouds churned. Bell checked her compass and pointed left, calm as ever.
switch:1.cnHint: 天桥上灯光突然熄灭，老赫姆试图____电源，但毫无反应。
switch:1.hook: Something had cut the power from the other side.
switch:1.line: 'Press the stone to *switch* the lanterns — hurry, the bridge is fading.'

treatment:1.en: We landed on a herb island where a quiet old keeper tended rows of blue flowers. She offered the troupe warm tea as a *treatment* for the cold winds we had crossed. Sipping it, I felt the chill leave my bones. Old Helm smiled and placed a map fragment on her table.
treatment:1.cnHint: 草药岛上的守护人用热茶作为____，驱走了我们身上的寒意。
treatment:1.hook: The keeper asked for nothing — except one small favour.
treatment:1.line: 'Warm tea is the finest *treatment* after a journey through the cold.'

union:1.en: On the stone plaza of Midsky Island, rival crews from east and west stood apart, arms crossed. Silverfang stepped between them and announced a *union* of all island travellers, one voice, one map. A silence fell. Then, slowly, hands reached across the gap and met.
union:1.cnHint: 银牙船长在广场上宣布建立旅行者____，东西两队慢慢伸出了手。
union:1.hook: Yet one figure in the crowd did not move at all.
union:1.line: 'This *union* means every crew shares the map — and the risk.'

acknowledge:1.en: Silverfang passed us on the rope walkway without a word. Old Helm stopped and waited. After three long steps, Silverfang slowed, turned, and gave a single nod to *acknowledge* that we had beaten his crew to the fragment. It was small, but it was enough. We walked on, lighter.
acknowledge:1.cnHint: 银牙终于停下脚步，点头____我们比他的队伍先找到了碎片。
acknowledge:1.hook: That nod would mean something very different by nightfall.
acknowledge:1.line: 'I *acknowledge* your find — do not expect it to happen again.'

alike:1.en: Bell laid two map fragments side by side on the plaza stone. They looked almost *alike* — same colour, same worn edges — but one had a tiny star in the corner that the other lacked. 'One is real,' she said softly. Old Helm leaned close, squinting at the star.
alike:1.cnHint: 贝尔将两块碎片并排放好，它们看起来几乎____，只差一颗小星。
alike:1.hook: Choosing the wrong one would send us off the edge.
alike:1.line: 'They appear *alike*, but only one will open the next gate.'

analyze:1.en: At the crossroads island, three paths curved away into fog. Bell sat down with her compass and a sheet of bark paper to *analyze* the wind directions at each turning. After a quiet minute she circled one path firmly. 'The stars confirm it,' she said, and stood up.
analyze:1.cnHint: 在三叉路口，贝尔用罗盘和树皮纸____风向，圈出了正确的路。
analyze:1.hook: The fog on that path began to thin — then thickened again.
analyze:1.line: 'Give me one minute to *analyze* the wind before we choose a path.'

gather:1.en: The market square of Edgecloud Island buzzed at dawn. Traders, pilots, and wandering map-hunters began to *gather* around a stone post where someone had pinned a glowing word-fragment. Old Helm reached it first, smoothed the folds of his travel coat, and held the fragment high. 'One more piece,' he said quietly. The crowd leaned in, holding its breath.
gather:1.cnHint: 清晨，云边岛集市上的人们纷纷____在一块发光的词语碎片周围，老舵手率先拿到了它。
gather:1.hook: But the post beneath it had begun to crack and sink.
gather:1.line: 'Everyone should *gather* here before we read the word aloud,' said Old Helm.

imagine:1.en: Bell stood at the very edge of Windtip Platform, her charts spread over a low wall. She asked me to close my eyes. 'Now *imagine* the next island,' she said softly, 'not as a dot on paper, but as a real place with wind and colour.' When I opened my eyes, the horizon looked different — wider, somehow, and full of invitation.
imagine:1.cnHint: 小铃让我闭上眼睛，____下一座岛屿真实的模样，睁眼后地平线仿佛变得更宽广了。
imagine:1.hook: Then a shape appeared there, exactly as I had pictured it.
imagine:1.line: '*Imagine* the island is already beneath your feet,' Bell said, eyes bright.

instance:1.en: Old Helm kept a small leather book full of word-fragment records. 'Look at this *instance*,' he said, tapping a faded entry. 'We found a fragment shaped like a key, and the door it opened led to the Saltmist Terraces.' He closed the book with a soft snap. Every record in there was a reminder that words were never just letters — they were doorways.
instance:1.cnHint: 老舵手翻开记录本，指着某个____说明词语碎片如何打开了通往盐雾台地的大门。
instance:1.hook: The next entry in the book had no ending — only a question mark.
instance:1.line: 'This *instance* proves that every word leads somewhere real,' Old Helm said.

numerous:1.en: From the crow's nest of our sky-raft I counted the islands spread below the star-lit clouds. There were *numerous* ones I had never noticed before — tiny, moss-covered platforms barely large enough for a single tree. Bell handed me her looking-glass. 'Each one has a name,' she said. 'We just haven't earned those names yet.' I felt wonderfully small.
numerous:1.cnHint: 从高处望去，星云下方有____座我从未留意过的小岛，小铃说每一座都有名字等待我们去发现。
numerous:1.hook: One of them was lit from underneath by a pale blue glow.
numerous:1.line: 'There are *numerous* paths forward — we only need to choose one,' said Bell.

puzzle:1.en: The locked gate of Stormring Arch was covered in carved symbols. Nobody in the troupe could open it until Silverfang knelt down and studied the lowest row. 'This is a *puzzle* built from word-fragments,' he said, almost to himself. He pressed three symbols in order, and the gate swung inward on a breath of warm, flower-scented air. Beyond it, a whole new sky waited.
puzzle:1.cnHint: 风环拱门上刻满符号，是个用词语碎片构成的____，竞争船长蹲下来仔细研究后将其解开了。
puzzle:1.hook: Something on the other side of the gate was already moving toward us.
puzzle:1.line: 'Every *puzzle* here has a word at its heart — find the word, find the door,' said Silverfang.

remind:1.en: Before we crossed the Bridge of Echoes, Old Helm stopped and turned to me. 'Let me *remind* you,' he said, with a small, steady smile, 'the bridge only holds if you keep moving forward. No looking down.' I nodded and kept my eyes on the far side, where a lantern swung in the wind. My feet found their rhythm and the bridge held, just as he said it would.
remind:1.cnHint: 越过回声桥前，老舵手____我只要一直向前走桥就不会断，我照做了，桥果然稳稳的。
remind:1.hook: Behind us, the bridge dissolved into starlight the moment I stepped off.
remind:1.line: 'I must *remind* you — forward steps only on this bridge,' said Old Helm, calm and sure.

truly:1.en: After a long cold crossing, we landed on Hearthstone Isle. The ground was warm underfoot, lit from below by deep amber stone. Silverfang sat beside a fire pit and looked up at the stars. 'This,' he said slowly, 'is *truly* the strangest and finest place I have ever rested.' I could not argue. The stars here seemed closer, as if the island had floated up to meet them.
truly:1.cnHint: 在暖石岛落脚后，竞争船长望着繁星感叹这里____是他休憩过的最奇妙之地。
truly:1.hook: Then the amber stone beneath us pulsed once, like a heartbeat.
truly:1.line: 'I am *truly* glad the word brought us here,' Silverfang said, his voice low and warm.

valuable:1.en: We found the word-fragment locked inside a glass case at the top of Cairn Peak. Old Helm examined it carefully. 'More *valuable* than any coin we carry,' he said, wrapping it in cloth. 'This one opens the eastern sea-lane — islands no troupe has charted.' Bell was already updating her charts, her pen moving fast. The world, once again, had just grown larger.
valuable:1.cnHint: 老舵手在峰顶找到词语碎片后说它比任何金币都____，因为它将开启无人标记过的东部海路。
valuable:1.hook: Bell's pen stopped — there was something already drawn on that part of the chart.
valuable:1.line: 'Keep it safe — this fragment is the most *valuable* thing we own right now,' said Old Helm.

belong:1.en: At the edge of the map, Old Helm held up a torn fragment and turned it slowly in the starlight. 'Every piece *belongs* somewhere,' he said. We spread the fragments across the flat stone and watched the outline of a new island take shape before our eyes.
belong:1.cnHint: 老舵把地图碎片拼在一起，一座新岛屿的轮廓慢慢____于它应在的位置。
belong:1.hook: But one fragment glowed faintly, and no island matched it.
belong:1.line: 'Every scrap *belongs* in its place — find the place, find the path.'

beneficial:1.en: Bell climbed the tall signal post at the island's edge and checked the wind flags one by one. She told us that the steady eastern wind was *beneficial* for crossing the wide gap to the next island. Old Helm nodded and began folding the sail with quiet confidence.
beneficial:1.cnHint: 小铃观测到东风对渡过大峡谷非常____，老舵立刻开始准备帆船。
beneficial:1.hook: Then the wind shifted without warning, and Bell's face went still.
beneficial:1.line: 'A steady eastern wind is *beneficial* — we leave before the hour turns.'

characteristic:1.en: The stone archway at the island's entrance was covered in small spiral carvings. Bell ran her finger along one and smiled. 'That spiral is a *characteristic* of the old builders,' she said. 'Wherever you see it, you know they passed through here and left something behind.'
characteristic:1.cnHint: 小铃指着拱门上的螺旋纹样说，那是古代建造者____的标志。
characteristic:1.hook: Deep inside the arch, a second set of carvings pointed downward.
characteristic:1.line: 'The spiral is a *characteristic* of their work — follow it and you will find more.'

director:1.en: A crowd had gathered around a crumbling open-air stage on the lower terrace. An old woman stood at the centre, pointing and calling out in a clear voice. Old Helm leaned over and whispered, 'She is the *director* of the island's memory theatre — they perform the history of every word they have ever collected.'
director:1.cnHint: 露天舞台旁，这座岛屿记忆剧场的____正在指挥一场关于词语的演出。
director:1.hook: She suddenly pointed straight at us, and the whole crowd turned.
director:1.line: 'I am the *director* here — and you three are just in time for the final act.'

emerge:1.en: We waited by the dark cave mouth for what felt like a long while. Then colours began to *emerge* from the shadows — pale blue, then gold, then a deep green — as a flock of tiny lantern-birds flew out one by one and lit the stone path ahead of us like a moving torch.
emerge:1.cnHint: 洞口的黑暗中，一群提灯鸟慢慢____，用柔光照亮了前方的石径。
emerge:1.hook: The last bird paused, looked back at us, and then flew the wrong way.
emerge:1.line: 'Watch the colours *emerge* — the first shade tells you which path is safe.'

exact:1.en: Old Helm spread the map on the ground and pressed each corner flat with a small stone. He studied it for a long moment. 'I need the *exact* position of that tower,' he said, 'not a guess — one wrong step on a floating island and you step off the edge.'
exact:1.cnHint: 老舵盯着地图说，他需要那座塔____的位置，差一步就会踏空。
exact:1.hook: Bell measured twice, then quietly erased her first mark.
exact:1.line: 'Give me the *exact* spot — floating ground forgives no mistakes.'

guest:1.en: A small shelter stood at the crossroads of two sky-bridges, run by a quiet man named Pip who said almost nothing. He set out warm cups without being asked. 'Every traveller is a *guest* of this crossroads,' he said at last, and placed a tiny map fragment beside each cup.
guest:1.cnHint: 十字天桥处的小屋主人说，每一位旅人都是这里的____，并在茶杯旁留下了地图碎片。
guest:1.hook: The fragments, once touched, began to hum the same soft note.
guest:1.line: 'You are a *guest* of this crossroads — the road will remember your name.'

massive:1.en: We had expected a hill, but what rose above the morning mist was something else entirely. A *massive* stone anchor, taller than ten men standing, was driven deep into the island's surface. Bell said the old charts called it the Root — the single point that stopped the island from drifting away.
massive:1.cnHint: 晨雾散去后，一枚巨大的____石锚出现在我们面前，正是它牢牢固定住了这座浮岛。
massive:1.hook: Around its base, fresh scratch marks showed something had been trying to pull it free.
massive:1.line: 'That *massive* anchor is the only thing keeping this island where it belongs.'

mix:1.en: At the edge of the market island, Bell spread out her tools and began working. She ground three kinds of star-dust together into a fine *mix*, pressing it into the shape of a tiny island. Old Helm leaned over her shoulder. 'That pattern,' he said softly, 'matches the blank corner of our map.'
mix:1.cnHint: 小铃将三种星尘研磨成____，压成小岛的形状，恰好与地图空白处吻合。
mix:1.hook: The dust glowed — and the blank corner of the map began to move.
mix:1.line: 'This *mix* of dusts is the only thing that reveals hidden paths,' Bell said.

necessity:1.en: The bridge between two islands had cracked in the night. Old Helm looked at our nearly empty supply box and then at the gap below. 'Crossing is not a choice,' he said. 'It is a *necessity*.' We tied ropes to the railings and went one by one, the wind pulling at our coats, the stars watching in silence.
necessity:1.cnHint: 桥断了，老船长说渡桥是____，大家一个接一个地爬了过去。
necessity:1.hook: The last rope snapped just as the final person reached the other side.
necessity:1.line: 'A *necessity* drives us forward even when the road looks impossible,' Old Helm said.

translate:1.en: The stone gate was covered in symbols none of us could read. Bell ran her fingers along each line, thinking hard. Then she smiled. 'I can *translate* this,' she said. 'It says: the one who arrives with wonder may enter.' Old Helm looked at me — I was the newest member — and gave a quiet nod toward the gate.
translate:1.cnHint: 小铃能____石门上的符文，内容是"怀抱好奇之心者方可入内"。
translate:1.hook: The gate did not open outward — it dissolved into a staircase of light.
translate:1.line: 'I can *translate* these old symbols — they hold the island's oldest secret,' Bell said.

wander:1.en: Old Helm told me not to *wander* past the silver trees, but I did anyway. The path looped back on itself, and each turn showed a different sky — purple, gold, deep green. When I found my way back, he was waiting with a cup of warm tea and a look that said he had already known. 'Well?' he asked. 'What did you see?'
wander:1.cnHint: 我无视警告独自____到银树林深处，每一转弯都是不同颜色的天空。
wander:1.hook: The sky I had seen in the trees was not on any map — not yet.
wander:1.line: 'If you *wander* too far alone, the stars may rearrange and you will lose the way,' Old Helm said.

warn:1.en: A young island-keeper met us at the dock and raised one hand to stop us. 'I must *warn* you,' she said, 'the stone path shifts at night — step only on the lit squares.' Old Helm thanked her with a small bow. That night, we crossed safely, each step landing on soft gold light while the dark squares sank silently into the clouds.
warn:1.cnHint: 岛上的守门人____我们夜间只能踩亮着的石板，否则会坠入云中。
warn:1.hook: At the far end of the path, a door opened that the keeper had not mentioned.
warn:1.line: 'I *warn* every traveller: the islands keep secrets that only patience can unlock,' she said.

advocate:1.en: Around the fire, the troupe debated which route to take next. Bell wanted the long way around; Silverfang wanted to cut straight through the storm belt. Old Helm listened, then stood. 'I am an *advocate* for the slower road,' he said, 'because the things we find along the way are usually the things we needed most.' Nobody argued after that.
advocate:1.cnHint: 老船长表示自己是慢行路线的____，因为沿途的发现往往正是大家最需要的。
advocate:1.hook: He then unfolded a map none of us had seen before — and the slow road glowed on it.
advocate:1.line: 'I am an *advocate* for caution, but tonight caution and wonder point the same way,' Old Helm said.

cite:1.en: Bell pulled out her small notebook, full of careful notes from every island we had visited. When Silverfang doubted the new route, she opened it calmly. 'I can *cite* three times we followed a faint signal and found a whole new island,' she said. Silverfang looked at the notebook, then at the horizon, and finally smiled. 'Set the course,' he said.
cite:1.cnHint: 小铃翻开笔记本，____三次跟随微弱信号最终发现新岛屿的记录，说服了银牙。
cite:1.hook: As she closed the notebook, a fourth signal appeared — stronger than any before.
cite:1.line: 'I can *cite* every island we almost missed — doubt is just a map we haven't read yet,' Bell said.

content:1.en: At the edge of the market square, Old Helm spread our collected words across a flat stone like a map made of light. Each word glowed faintly. He looked over them, crossed his arms, and let out a long breath. 'We are *content*,' he said, 'not because the journey is over, but because today we found exactly what we needed.'
content:1.cnHint: 在集市广场边缘，老舵手将收集到的词语摊开，对今天的收获感到____。
content:1.hook: But one word at the edge of the stone was still dark.
content:1.line: 'We are *content* — not because the journey is over, but because today we found what we needed.'

divide:1.en: A wide crack ran through the middle of the island's open street, deep enough that we could not see the bottom. Bell knelt at its edge, tracing it with one finger. 'This crack will *divide* the island in two by morning,' she warned. Old Helm studied the sky and nodded slowly. We had minutes, not hours.
divide:1.cnHint: 贝尔发现一道裂缝将____这座岛屿，众人必须赶快行动。
divide:1.hook: The far side of the crack held the only word we had come for.
divide:1.line: 'This crack will *divide* the island in two by morning — we move now.'

generate:1.en: In the center of the open plaza stood a tall spinning stone that hummed without stopping. Bell said the old builders had placed it there to *generate* the warm light that kept the island alive through the cold nights. Without it, the floating rock would go dark and drift.
