moral:1.line: 'The *moral* of every journey is simple: share what you find,' Old Helm said.

nor:1.en: The Windglass Market had no ceiling *nor* walls — just a ring of tall poles strung with coloured lanterns and canvas roofs that flapped in the breeze. Traders called out from every direction. I could not tell where to look first, and I loved that feeling entirely.
nor:1.cnHint: 风玻璃集市没有顶棚____四壁，是一个完全开放的露天市场。
nor:1.hook: Then one lantern swung loose and drifted off the edge of the island.
nor:1.line: 'There is no lock *nor* key on this gate — anyone may enter,' Bell said.

pick:1.en: The word-vendor had dozens of small glass bottles, each holding a glowing letter inside. Old Helm told me I could *pick* one for the troupe's collection. I held each bottle up to the starlight, watching the letters pulse. I chose the one shaped like a tiny flying fish, and it sang softly when I uncorked it.
pick:1.cnHint: 字词摊的老板让我从许多发光小瓶中____一个加入队伍的收藏。
pick:1.hook: The moment the cork came free, a new island lit up on the map.
pick:1.line: 'Take your time and *pick* the word that feels right to you,' Old Helm said.

pollution:1.en: The island of Ashhollow had once been a forge-hub, and the old smoke still stained its lower cliffs orange and grey. Bell said the *pollution* from the ancient furnaces had soaked into the stone over centuries, turning even the rainwater rusty. We collected our word-fragment quickly and climbed back to cleaner air above.
pollution:1.cnHint: Ashhollow岛因古代冶炼炉留下的____，连石头和雨水都变了颜色。
pollution:1.hook: Yet at the very top, a single white flower was blooming.
pollution:1.line: 'The *pollution* here is old, but the wind above the cliffs is still clean,' Bell said.

quit:1.en: Halfway across the rope-bridge to Spindle Peak, the wind picked up hard and the whole bridge began to sway. My hands went white on the rope. For one breath I wanted to *quit* and turn back. Then Silverfang called from the far side: 'Halfway is already brave.' I kept moving, one step at a time.
quit:1.cnHint: 过绳桥时风突然变大，我几乎想____，但队友的鼓励让我坚持了下来。
quit:1.hook: The last plank cracked under my boot but held.
quit:1.line: 'Do not *quit* now — the best view on the island is just ahead,' Silverfang called.

recall:1.en: At the edge of Lastlight Pier, Old Helm paused and stared at the horizon for a long moment. 'I *recall* standing at a pier just like this when I found my first word,' he said quietly. 'It was dark and I was alone.' He smiled and handed me the map. 'Your turn to add to it.'
recall:1.cnHint: 在码头边，老舵____起自己第一次找到字词碎片时的情景，然后把地图交给了我。
recall:1.hook: The map trembled in my hands as a new glow appeared at its edge.
recall:1.line: 'I *recall* every island we have ever landed on — each one changed us a little,' Old Helm said.

threaten:1.en: Storm clouds gathered at the edge of Crestholm Island, dark and low. 'Those clouds *threaten* to swallow the whole dock,' Bell said, eyes fixed on the sky. Old Helm told us to tie every rope tight and move the word-lanterns inside. We worked fast, and when the storm passed, the air smelled like new beginnings.
threaten:1.cnHint: 暴风云____着要吞没整个码头，老舵手命令大家迅速固定好一切。
threaten:1.hook: But one word-lantern was already gone — taken by the wind.
threaten:1.line: 'Those clouds *threaten* to swallow the whole dock before we can tie down.'

throw:1.en: Old Helm called it a *throw* of luck — tossing a word-token into the Wishing Pool to see which island it pointed to next. The token spun in the air, caught the starlight, and landed with a soft ring. It pointed north. Everyone cheered, because north meant the Crystal Shelf.
throw:1.cnHint: 老舵手把这次____称为一次冒险，将字符投入许愿池以指引下一段旅程。
throw:1.hook: The token rang once more — and then began to glow.
throw:1.line: 'Every good journey starts with a *throw* of luck, so here we go.'

unlike:1.en: The market on Driftwood Square was *unlike* anything I had seen before. Stalls hung from ropes between cloud-pines, selling bottled echoes, pressed starlight, and jars of frozen laughter. Bell pressed a jar into my hands and smiled. I held it up, and something warm hummed against my palms.
unlike:1.cnHint: 漂木广场的集市与我见过的任何地方____，贝尔递给我一瓶冻结的笑声。
unlike:1.hook: The humming grew louder — as if the jar recognized me.
unlike:1.line: 'This place is *unlike* any market we have docked at before, trust me.'

vast:1.en: We stepped onto the Skyfloor Terrace and looked out. The space between the islands was *vast*, a deep blue bowl full of slow-drifting clouds and distant lights. Old Helm stood at the rail and said nothing for a long moment. Then he pulled out the map and added three new lines to it.
vast:1.cnHint: 踏上天台，眼前____的空间令老舵手沉默良久，随后他在地图上新添了三条路线。
vast:1.hook: One of those distant lights blinked — once, twice, then went dark.
vast:1.line: 'The sky out there is *vast*, but every piece of it has a name waiting.'

absolutely:1.en: Bell spread the charts across the stone table and tapped one with her finger. 'I am *absolutely* certain this route passes over the Salt-Glass Bridge,' she said. Silverfang crossed his arms, but Bell did not flinch. She pointed to the star markings, and one by one his doubts fell quiet.
absolutely:1.cnHint: 贝尔____确定路线经过盐玻璃桥，她用星象标记一一打消了竞争船长的疑虑。
absolutely:1.hook: Then Silverfang pointed to a mark none of them had noticed before.
absolutely:1.line: 'I am *absolutely* certain this bridge is on the route — look at the stars.'

accumulate:1.en: Word-fragments did not arrive all at once. Over three days at Lantern Wharf, we watched them *accumulate* — one tucked under a loose tile, one traded for a warm meal, one humming inside an old bell jar. By sunset on the third day we had enough to open the next island gate.
accumulate:1.cnHint: 在灯笼码头，字符碎片逐渐____，三天后我们终于凑够了开启下一座岛门所需的数量。
accumulate:1.hook: But the gate demanded one more fragment we had not yet found.
accumulate:1.line: 'Let the small finds *accumulate* — every fragment counts toward the gate.'

breakfast:1.en: We chose to *breakfast* on the open platform above the cloud-line, where the air tasted faintly sweet. Old Helm laid out dried fruit and warm grain cakes. Below us, islands drifted like slow ships. A new word-fragment glinted on the tray beside the teapot, left by nobody we could name.
breakfast:1.cnHint: 大家在云层之上的平台____，老舵手的托盘旁神秘地出现了一枚新的字符碎片。
breakfast:1.hook: The fragment carried an address — for an island not on any map.
breakfast:1.line: 'We *breakfast* above the clouds today — let the sky wake us up properly.'

capacity:1.en: The old gate at Rimstone Plaza had a *capacity* for only three word-tokens at a time. Bell read the carved numbers aloud while Old Helm chose our three best tokens carefully. Silverfang watched, arms folded, then gave a quiet nod. The gate accepted them, shivered, and swung open onto golden light.
capacity:1.cnHint: 边石广场的旧门____仅能容纳三枚字符，老舵手精心挑选后，门扉向金色光芒敞开。
capacity:1.hook: Beyond the gate, something enormous shifted in the golden haze.
capacity:1.line: 'This gate has a *capacity* of three tokens only, so choose them well.'

consideration:1.en: Old Helm spread the star-chart across a flat rock and studied every line with care. 'Choosing our next island takes *consideration*,' he said slowly. 'Wind, weight, and how much dried fruit we have left.' Bell nodded, tapping two possible routes. I watched them both and felt, for the first time, like a real member of the troupe.
consideration:1.cnHint: 老舵手在认真____每一条航线后，终于指向了远方那座闪光的岛屿。
consideration:1.hook: Then Bell's finger stopped on a route none of us had noticed before.
consideration:1.line: 'Choosing our path takes careful *consideration*, so don't rush me.'

disaster:1.en: A sudden gust flipped our cooking pot clean off the deck. Hot soup sprayed across the charts, and Bell let out a sharp cry. 'Small *disaster*,' Old Helm muttered, already mopping with his sleeve. Silverfang tossed me a dry cloth without a word. Working together, we saved every map before the ink ran.
disaster:1.cnHint: 一阵狂风掀翻了锅，差点酿成一场____，幸好大家齐心协力保住了地图。
disaster:1.hook: But one corner of the oldest chart was already beginning to blur.
disaster:1.line: 'A *disaster* like this can ruin a map in seconds — move fast!'

emergency:1.en: A crack split across the rear mast just as clouds swallowed the stars. Bell shouted for rope while Silverfang steadied the boom with both hands. '*Emergency* on deck!' Old Helm called, his voice cutting through the wind. I threw the coil to Bell, and somehow, together, we held the mast in place until the storm passed.
emergency:1.cnHint: 桅杆突然开裂，甲板上爆发了一场____，所有人立刻各就各位。
emergency:1.hook: The storm had passed, but a strange light now blinked from the island ahead.
emergency:1.line: '*Emergency* on deck — grab that rope and don't let go!'

familiar:1.en: We drifted toward an island wrapped in silver mist, and something about its shape felt *familiar* to me. Then I remembered: Old Helm had sketched it once on a scrap of paper during my very first night with the troupe. I had not believed it was real. Now it floated right in front of us, glowing softly in the dark.
familiar:1.cnHint: 那座岛屿的轮廓让我感到____，原来老舵手曾经画过它。
familiar:1.hook: And at its highest peak, a door stood open, spilling golden light into the mist.
familiar:1.line: 'This sky looks *familiar* to me — I think we have been near here before.'

furthermore:1.en: Old Helm listed three reasons to land on the pale island: fresh water, a resting place, and a carved stone he had heard about from other travellers. '*Furthermore*,' Bell added quietly, 'the word we need next may be written on that stone.' That settled it. I pulled in the sail, Silverfang steered, and we began our slow, hopeful descent.
furthermore:1.cnHint: 老舵手说出三条登岛理由，领航员____补充了最关键的一点。
furthermore:1.hook: The pale island rose to meet us, and something on it began to hum.
furthermore:1.line: 'The water is clean, and *furthermore*, the stone marker is right here.'

hardly:1.en: The new island was so quiet I could *hardly* hear my own footsteps on the pale grass. No wind, no birds, only the faint hum of starlight above. Bell whispered that the silence meant the island was still sleeping. Old Helm pressed one hand to the ground and smiled. 'It is waking up,' he said. 'It knows we brought the right word.'
hardly:1.cnHint: 岛上静得____能听见脚步声，但老舵手说它正在慢慢苏醒。
hardly:1.hook: Under our feet, the pale grass began to glow, one blade at a time.
hardly:1.line: 'I can *hardly* hear anything — this island is holding its breath.'

hinder:1.en: A dense wall of star-vines had grown across the only path to the stone marker at the island's heart. Silverfang tried to push through and got tangled at the elbows. 'They *hinder* anyone who rushes,' Old Helm said calmly. He showed us how to lift each vine gently instead of forcing it aside. The path opened without a struggle.
hinder:1.cnHint: 密密的星藤____住了去路，老舵手教大家用温柔而非蛮力通过。
hinder:1.hook: Beyond the vines, the stone marker pulsed with a soft blue light.
hinder:1.line: 'Don't force it — those vines will *hinder* you if you push too hard.'

injury:1.en: I slipped on a wet stone near the island's edge and scraped my palm — a small *injury*, but it stung. Bell tore a clean strip from a spare cloth and wrapped my hand without being asked. 'You keep the next word safe in that hand,' Bell said with a gentle smile. Somehow the sting faded the moment I held the new map fragment.
injury:1.cnHint: 我在湿石上滑倒，手掌受了点____，领航员立刻为我包扎。
injury:1.hook: The map fragment in my bandaged hand was already pointing toward the next island.
injury:1.line: 'It is only a small *injury*, but let me wrap it before we move on.'

housing:1.en: The troupe landed on a market island where rows of small wooden shelters filled every corner. Old Helm pointed at a crumbling block of *housing* near the edge. 'The map fragment is hidden somewhere inside those walls,' he said. I felt the old planks shift beneath my feet.
housing:1.cnHint: 老舵指着岛边破旧的____说，地图碎片就藏在那片墙壁里面。
housing:1.hook: The floor cracked, and something below us stirred.
housing:1.line: 'That *housing* looks ready to fall — step lightly, everyone.'

behaviour:1.en: A crowd had gathered on the market street to watch a street performer. His strange *behaviour* — spinning, shouting, then suddenly freezing — confused everyone around him. Bell leaned close to me and whispered that she had seen this act before, and that it always ended with a secret door opening.
behaviour:1.cnHint: 小铃低声说，那个表演者奇怪的____其实是一种暗号。
behaviour:1.hook: The performer froze, stared right at us, and pointed up.
behaviour:1.line: 'His *behaviour* is a signal — get ready to move.'

husband:1.en: An old woman sat alone at a flower stall, arranging bright blooms with quiet care. She told us her *husband* had once sailed these very skies and hidden a word-fragment inside a yellow flower pot. Bell bought every yellow pot on the stall. Only one of them hummed.
husband:1.cnHint: 老妇人说她的____曾把地图碎片藏在一只黄色花盆里。
husband:1.hook: The humming pot grew warmer and warmer in Bell's hands.
husband:1.line: 'My *husband* always said the stars would send good travellers here.'

tourist:1.en: The island's main street was busy with visitors snapping pictures of the glowing sky. Old Helm dressed me up as a *tourist* so I could walk past the guards without raising questions. I kept my eyes low and my bag close, where the map fragment sat wrapped in cloth.
tourist:1.cnHint: 老舵让我装扮成____，这样就能悄悄混过守卫。
tourist:1.hook: One guard stepped forward and asked to see my bag.
tourist:1.line: 'Look like a *tourist* — smile wide and walk slow.'

agent:1.en: A quiet figure waited beside a lamp post at the end of the street. Old Helm called her an *agent*, someone who traded information for star-coins. She slid a small folded paper across the stone bench toward us without a word. It showed the exact path to the next island.
agent:1.cnHint: 老舵说那个沉默的人是____，专门用情报换取星币。
agent:1.hook: She was gone before I could even say thank you.
agent:1.line: 'Our *agent* never stays long — read the paper now.'

cash:1.en: At the island bazaar, every stall had a sign: no star-coins, no trade. Bell searched her coat and pulled out a handful of *cash* just enough to buy one clue from the old map-seller. He took the coins, smiled, and told us the next word was hiding inside the well at the square.
cash:1.cnHint: 小铃掏出仅剩的____，从地图商人那里换来了一条关键线索。
cash:1.hook: The well at the square was surrounded by a strange green glow.
cash:1.line: 'I have just enough *cash* for one answer — make it count.'

competition:1.en: Two crews had arrived at the island at the same time: our troupe and Silverfang's ship. The *competition* between them for the map fragment was already drawing a crowd in the street below. Old Helm rolled up his sleeves and grinned. 'Let's remind them who finds words fastest,' he said.
competition:1.cnHint: 我们的队伍和银牙的船同时抵达，____随即在街头展开。
competition:1.hook: Silverfang was already running toward the old tower gate.
competition:1.line: 'This *competition* ends when we reach the gate first — run!'

farmer:1.en: Near the edge of the market district, a sun-worn *farmer* was selling small bundles of sky-herbs from a wooden cart. He had the quiet, steady eyes of someone who had watched a thousand sunrises. When I asked about the map fragment, he simply lifted a herb bundle and placed a glowing shard in my hand.
farmer:1.cnHint: 市集边缘那位饱经风霜的____默默把发光的地图碎片放进了我的手里。
farmer:1.hook: He turned away before I could ask him his name.
farmer:1.line: 'A *farmer* sees everything that grows here — trust me on that.'

egg:1.en: At the edge of the map, Old Helm spotted a giant *egg* resting in a nest of silver moss. It was the size of a barrel, warm to the touch, and softly glowing. 'This island is alive,' he whispered. Bell pressed her ear close and heard a faint tap from inside.
egg:1.cnHint: 老舵手在地图边缘发现一枚巨大的____，里面传来轻轻的敲击声。
egg:1.hook: Something inside was about to break free.
egg:1.line: 'That *egg* is warm — whatever is inside has been waiting a long time.'

hire:1.en: Old Helm spread a sign on the dock at the edge of the floating market: NAVIGATOR WANTED. By noon, twenty islanders had lined up. He chose Bell on the spot. 'We *hire* only those who can read the wind,' he told the others kindly, and Bell smiled like she had known all along.
hire:1.cnHint: 老舵手在码头张贴告示，决定____一位能读懂风向的领航员。
hire:1.hook: Bell's first wind-reading would lead somewhere no map showed.
hire:1.line: 'We *hire* only those brave enough to trust the sky.'

aid:1.en: A storm had knocked the bridge-post loose, leaving two younger troupe members stranded on a far ledge. Bell threw a rope while I held the anchor stone. Old Helm called out, 'Every kind of *aid* matters right now — pull together!' We did, and the ledge creaked but held until they crossed.
aid:1.cnHint: 桥柱松动，团员被困，老舵手呼吁大家齐心____被困的伙伴。
aid:1.hook: The anchor stone was already starting to slide.
aid:1.line: 'Even the smallest *aid* can tip the balance — give all you have.'

bill:1.en: At the sky-market stall, the vendor slid a folded *bill* across the counter: a long list of goods, with the total written in star-shaped ink. Old Helm studied it carefully, raised an eyebrow, and then laughed. 'Fair enough,' he said, paying with three blue coins and a story about the southern winds.
bill:1.cnHint: 在空中市集，老舵手仔细查看摊贩递来的____，最后痛快付账。
bill:1.hook: The ink on the bill seemed to shift when no one looked.
bill:1.line: 'Check the *bill* twice — sky-market prices hide small surprises.'

paint:1.en: Bell chose the tallest boulder on the island's rim and began to *paint* a wide mural: every island the troupe had visited, connected by thin golden lines. She worked until the stars came out, brush moving fast and sure. When Old Helm saw it, he was quiet for a long moment, then nodded slowly.
paint:1.cnHint: 贝尔在悬崖边的巨石上____出了整张旅途地图，令团长久久无言。
paint:1.hook: One island on the mural no one in the troupe had ever named.
paint:1.line: 'I *paint* what I remember, and I remember every island we have touched.'

bean:1.en: The tiny stall sold only one thing: a single roasted *bean*, dark and fragrant, sealed in a paper twist. 'One per traveller,' the old seller said. I bit into mine and tasted something like thunderstorm and cinnamon at once. Old Helm chuckled. 'That flavour means the next island will surprise you.'
bean:1.cnHint: 小摊只卖一粒烤____，老舵手说那味道预示着前方的惊喜。
bean:1.hook: My tongue still tingled as the next island rose into view.
bean:1.line: 'One *bean*, one truth — chew slowly and listen to what it tells you.'

birthday:1.en: Nobody had planned anything, but somehow everyone in the troupe knew it was Bell's *birthday*. By the time she returned from her morning watch, Old Helm had arranged small lanterns along the deck rail. The whole floating island seemed brighter. Bell looked around, laughed softly, and said it was the best sky she had ever seen.
birthday:1.cnHint: 贝尔生____那天，团长悄悄在甲板上挂满灯笼，让她大吃一惊。
birthday:1.hook: One lantern drifted loose and floated toward an unknown island.
birthday:1.line: 'Happy *birthday*, Bell — the sky put on its best colours just for you.'

flight:1.en: The troupe watched the messenger bird launch from Bell's wrist and climb in a wide spiral. Its *flight* carried a rolled map fragment to Silverfang's ship, drifting half a sky away. Old Helm tracked every wingbeat. 'If it lands,' he said quietly, 'Silverfang will reach the edge before us.' It landed.
flight:1.cnHint: 信使鸟的一次____将地图碎片送到了竞争对手银牙船长那里。
flight:1.hook: Silverfang's ship was already turning toward the horizon.
flight:1.line: 'That *flight* was too straight and too fast — someone trained that bird against us.'

facilitate:1.en: At the edge of the last island, Old Helm spread the map flat on a stone table. 'This bridge,' he said, pointing to a thin line, 'will *facilitate* our crossing to the next fragment.' Bell checked the ropes while the stars above reflected in the still water below.
facilitate:1.cnHint: 老舵手说这座桥将____我们前往下一块碎片的旅程。
facilitate:1.hook: But the bridge had only half its planks remaining.
facilitate:1.line: 'This bridge will *facilitate* our crossing — if we are quick.'

insight:1.en: Bell knelt beside a cracked stone marker at the island's rim, tracing its carvings with one finger. Her *insight* into old symbols was something the rest of us could only admire. 'This sign means the next island moves,' she said quietly. We all went still.
insight:1.cnHint: 小铃凭借她的____，读懂了石碑上古老的符号。
insight:1.hook: A moving island — how could anyone land on it?
insight:1.line: 'My *insight* tells me this island does not stay in one place.'

preparation:1.en: Old Helm called us together before dawn. Every rope was coiled, every bag packed tight. 'Our *preparation* tonight will save us tomorrow,' he said, his voice low and steady. The last star faded as Bell lit a small lantern and we waited for first light.
preparation:1.cnHint: 老舵手说，今晚的____将在明天拯救我们。
preparation:1.hook: Yet none of us had prepared for what the dawn revealed.
preparation:1.line: 'Good *preparation* tonight means no regrets in the morning.'

separate:1.en: The wind split our small group at the crossing fork. Old Helm took the high path; Bell and I took the low one. To *separate* like this felt strange, almost like losing a piece of the map itself. We agreed to meet at the far lantern post by noon.
separate:1.cnHint: 在岔路口，我们不得不____，各走一条路。
separate:1.hook: By noon, only Bell and I reached the lantern post.
separate:1.line: 'We must *separate* here, but the lantern post will find us together again.'

tie:1.en: Silverfang and Old Helm reached the word-stone at the same moment, hands almost touching. The crowd of island folk around them held their breath. A *tie* — neither first, neither last. Old Helm laughed softly and offered his hand. Silverfang looked away, then shook it.
tie:1.cnHint: 两位队长同时抵达目标，以____告终。
tie:1.hook: The word-stone glowed twice — once for each of them.
tie:1.line: 'A *tie* is not a loss — it is the map asking us to work together.'

jam:1.en: The narrow lane between the market stalls was a *jam* of carts, baskets, and island traders all pushing forward at once. Bell grabbed my sleeve and pulled me sideways into a quiet doorway. 'Wait,' she whispered. 'The crowd will thin in a moment.' She was right.
jam:1.cnHint: 集市小道上发生了严重的____，我们被困在人群中。
jam:1.hook: Through the crowd, a hooded figure watched us carefully.
jam:1.line: 'This *jam* of carts will clear — patience is faster than pushing.'

supermarket:1.en: On the central island there was a great open hall the locals called the *supermarket* — shelves rising to the ceiling, lit by glowing stones, stacked with dried fruit, rope, and ink. Old Helm moved through the rows quietly, filling his pack with quiet purpose.
supermarket:1.cnHint: 中心岛上有一个巨大的____，货架一直延伸到天花板。
supermarket:1.hook: One shelf, sealed behind glass, held jars we could not name.
supermarket:1.line: 'A *supermarket* like this — I have not seen one since the eastern islands.'

debate:1.en: Bell and Silverfang stood on either side of the old map table, pointing at different routes. Their *debate* lasted through two cups of tea and half a candle. Old Helm listened without speaking. At last he set a single coin on the table — right between their two chosen paths.
debate:1.cnHint: 小铃和竞争船长就路线展开了一场激烈的____。
debate:1.hook: The coin balanced on its edge, spinning slowly in the still air.
debate:1.line: 'This *debate* has one answer — and the map already knows it.'

female:1.en: At the edge of Windspar Market, a vendor held up a small creature with silver wings. 'This one,' Bell said softly, 'is a *female* — see how her wingtips catch the starlight differently.' Old Helm nodded and paid three word-coins. The little animal blinked at me, and I felt the map fragment hum in my pocket.
female:1.cnHint: 小铃在市场上发现了一只银翼小生物，她解释说这是一只____，翼尖反光方式与雄性不同。
female:1.hook: The creature's wings began to glow, tracing a path none of us had seen before.
female:1.line: 'She is a *female*, and her wings will guide us better than any compass.'

holiday:1.en: The whole island smelled of roasted seeds and coloured smoke. 'It is a *holiday* here,' Old Helm announced, spreading his arms wide. 'Every lamp lit means a word hidden nearby.' Bell was already dancing between the paper lanterns, and I ran after her, my map fragment tugging me toward the loudest drum.
holiday:1.cnHint: 整座岛屿正在庆祝____，老舵说每盏亮着的灯笼附近都藏着一个"词语"。
holiday:1.hook: Behind the last lantern, a locked door pulsed with golden light.
holiday:1.line: 'On a *holiday* like this, the islands always hide their best secrets.'

pain:1.en: I slipped on the wet stepping-stone and scraped my knee hard. The *pain* was sharp but short, and Silverfang reached down with a steady hand. 'Up you get,' he said, almost gently. Old Helm pressed a small leaf to the cut; it cooled the sting at once. I stood, and the sky ahead opened into a new ribbon of islands.
pain:1.cnHint: 叙述者在湿石头上滑倒，感受到了____，但银牙和老舵迅速给予了帮助。
pain:1.hook: Silverfang's eyes lingered on my map fragment just a moment too long.
pain:1.line: 'A little *pain* now means you remember the path later — trust me.'

player:1.en: A circle of children sat around a glowing board etched with island shapes. The best *player* among them — a girl with ink-stained fingers — had collected six word-tiles already. Bell watched, fascinated. Old Helm whispered that every tile she won was a real fragment of our map. I challenged her, heart thudding, and she grinned.
player:1.cnHint: 一群孩子在玩岛屿形状的棋盘游戏，其中最厉害的____已经赢得了六个"词语"碎片。
player:1.hook: The girl slid her final tile across the board and looked straight at me.
player:1.line: 'Any *player* who beats me gets to keep my best word-tile — do you dare?'

production:1.en: Deep in the island's hollow core, a line of workers poured glowing resin into word-shaped moulds. 'This is the *production* of new map fragments,' Bell explained, eyes wide. Old Helm said the troupe had traded here for years. The warm smell of the resin filled my lungs, and I watched a fresh word cool into solid light.
production:1.cnHint: 在岛屿内部，工人们正在进行词语碎片的____，将发光树脂倒入模具中。
production:1.hook: One mould held a shape none of the workers could read aloud.
production:1.line: 'The *production* here never stops — day and night, new words are born.'

secure:1.en: Bell looped a second rope around the anchor post and pulled it tight. 'The platform must be *secure* before we sleep,' she said, checking each knot with careful fingers. Stars pressed close overhead, and the wind rocked us gently. Old Helm handed out blankets. I lay back, listening to the hum of the island beneath us, finally at ease.
secure:1.cnHint: 小铃仔细检查每个绳结，确保平台____，这样大家才能安心入睡。
secure:1.hook: A soft creak beneath the boards suggested the island had its own plans.
secure:1.line: 'Keep every rope *secure* — out here, a loose knot is a lost night.'

audience:1.en: Old Helm stepped onto a flat rock and held up a glowing word-shard. An *audience* of islanders gathered quickly, sitting on steps and windowsills, all eyes bright. He told the story of our journey in three short sentences, and at the end, someone in the crowd tossed us a new fragment. It landed perfectly in my open hand.
audience:1.cnHint: 老舵站在石头上展示词语碎片，吸引了一群____，讲完故事后有人抛来了新碎片。
audience:1.hook: One face in the crowd already knew the story before Old Helm finished telling it.
audience:1.line: 'An *audience* this warm means the island wants us to stay a little longer.'

borrow:1.en: We were one rope short for the crossing. Silverfang looked over at a neighbouring vessel and called out, 'May I *borrow* your long line, just till the far ledge?' The other captain tossed it without a word. We crossed safely, and Silverfang returned it with a small word-coin tucked in the knot as thanks.
borrow:1.cnHint: 渡桥时绳子不够，银牙向旁边的船长____了一根长绳，安全过桥后还归还了。
borrow:1.hook: The other captain unfolded the word-coin and smiled in a way that felt like a warning.
borrow:1.line: 'I only need to *borrow* it once — and I always, always give things back.'

burn:1.en: The market square of Cinder Isle smelled of roasting nuts and warm bread. An old lamp post stood at its centre, its flame so close to a paper lantern that I feared a *burn* on the coloured silk. Old Helm noticed my worry and gently nudged the lantern aside. 'Every island teaches caution,' he said, smiling.
burn:1.cnHint: 在市集广场，灯柱的火焰差点在丝灯笼上留下____，老舵手及时移开了灯笼。
burn:1.hook: But the lamp post's flame flickered once — and the whole map shook.
burn:1.line: 'One *burn* on that lantern and we lose our only light for the next crossing.'

cook:1.en: On the open deck of Saffron Isle's night market, Bell spread our newest word-fragment flat and weighed its corners with spice jars. Nearby, a vendor began to *cook* flat bread on a stone griddle, and the warm smell drifted right over our map. 'Perfect thinking weather,' Bell said, tracing a new route with one finger.
cook:1.cnHint: 在夜市的露天摊位旁，贝尔展开地图碎片，摊贩开始在石板上____食物，香气弥漫。
cook:1.hook: Then the bread lifted off the griddle — and floated upward like a tiny island.
cook:1.line: 'Bell, watch the map — I need to *cook* this batch before the wind shifts.'

corporate:1.en: High above Ledger Isle hung a great iron sign stamped with the words JOINT *CORPORATE* SEAL. Old Helm said it meant the five island councils had once signed a single agreement here, binding all their trade together. I pressed my palm to the cool metal and felt the weight of all those old promises. 'One word unlocked all five gates,' Old Helm said quietly.
corporate:1.cnHint: 在账本岛上方悬挂着写有联合____印章的铁牌，老舵手讲述了五个岛屿议会共同签署协议的历史。
corporate:1.hook: Behind the fifth gate, a corridor of floating lanterns stretched beyond sight.
corporate:1.line: 'This *corporate* seal means every council owes us safe passage — use it wisely.'

dangerous:1.en: The rope bridge connecting Twin-Peak Isle's two summits swayed badly in the night wind. Silverfang planted a flag and called back to us: 'This crossing is *dangerous* — step only where I step.' I held my breath and matched every footfall to his, and the bridge stopped swaying just as I reached the other side.
dangerous:1.cnHint: 连接双峰岛两座山顶的绳桥在夜风中摇晃，银牙警告说这段路____，让大家踩着他的脚步走。
dangerous:1.hook: The moment my foot left the last plank, the bridge quietly detached and drifted away.
dangerous:1.line: 'I have crossed a hundred bridges — this one is the most *dangerous* I have seen.'

debt:1.en: At the toll arch of Copper Isle, a keeper in a brass coat blocked our path and read from a long scroll. Our troupe had borrowed a lantern here seasons ago and never returned it. 'One unpaid *debt*, however small, closes the gate,' the keeper said. Old Helm bowed, placed a fresh lantern on the counter, and the arch swung open with a warm chime.
debt:1.cnHint: 在铜岛关卡，守门人拦住了我们，说我们队伍之前借了灯笼从未归还，这份____让大门关闭。
debt:1.hook: Inside the arch, a second scroll unrolled — and it listed many more names than ours.
debt:1.line: 'A *debt* this small should never be allowed to grow — pay it and walk free.'

discipline:1.en: Bell drilled us on star-reading every dawn before the sky brightened. I yawned through the first lesson, but she was patient and firm. 'Navigation is a *discipline*,' she said. 'You learn a little each day and one morning it all fits together.' That morning came sooner than I expected: I named three constellations on my own, and Bell gave a quiet, proud nod.
discipline:1.cnHint: 贝尔每天黎明前训练我们辨认星象，她说导航是一门____，每天学一点，终有融会贯通的一天。
discipline:1.hook: On the horizon, a fourth constellation appeared that none of our charts had ever named.
discipline:1.line: 'Star-reading is a *discipline* — skip one dawn and the sky starts to feel like a stranger.'

error:1.en: I had copied the new word-fragment by hand, but when Bell laid my copy beside the original she frowned. 'There is an *error* in the third symbol,' she said, pointing to a curling line I had drawn backward. I fixed it with a careful stroke, and the fragment's edges glowed faintly, as if the map itself felt relieved to be whole again.
error:1.cnHint: 我手抄的地图碎片上有一处____，贝尔指出第三个符号画反了，修正后碎片的边缘微微发光。
error:1.hook: As the glow faded, a new island outline appeared that had not been there before.
error:1.line: 'One small *error* in a map can send a whole crew to the wrong island — check it again.'

gym:1.en: Tucked between two market stalls on Ironweight Isle was a tiny open-air *gym*: a few stone rings hanging from a beam and a worn mat on the deck. Silverfang stopped, grabbed a ring, and pulled himself up with a grin. 'Strong arms, strong ship,' he said. I tried next, managed three pulls, and the stone rings chimed softly like a small bell of approval.
gym:1.cnHint: 在铁锤岛的两个摊位之间有一个露天的小____，银牙抓住石环向上撑起，说强臂才能驾好船。
gym:1.hook: Under the worn mat, folded small and waiting, lay the next word-fragment.
gym:1.line: 'Every island has a *gym* of some kind — muscles and maps are both worth keeping sharp.'

collection:1.en: At the edge of Driftstone Market, Old Helm opened a wide wooden case. Inside lay our *collection* of words — each one a glowing shard pressed onto a scrap of bark. 'Forty-three fragments,' he said softly, counting them like old friends. I leaned in, and the whole case smelled of wind and faraway places.
collection:1.cnHint: 老赫姆在市场边展示了旅行队积累的____，每一块都散发着远方的气息。
collection:1.hook: But one shard was missing, and its empty slot pulsed with faint blue light.
collection:1.line: 'Every word in this *collection* was earned on a different island,' said Old Helm.

depression:1.en: A wide hollow sat in the centre of Cloudmere Square — a natural *depression* in the stone, deep enough to hold rainwater from three storms. Bell knelt at its rim, reading ripple patterns the way others read maps. 'The water remembers every wind,' she murmured. I watched the stars reflected below and felt very small.
depression:1.cnHint: 贝尔在广场中央一处地面____旁蹲下，从水面的涟漪中辨认风向。
depression:1.hook: Then the reflection showed a shape that was not in the sky above us.
depression:1.line: 'This *depression* fills before every big storm,' Bell warned quietly.

foot:1.en: The rope bridge swayed as I placed one careful *foot* after the other. Below, clouds rolled like slow white rivers between the islands. Old Helm had already crossed without looking down, which I found both impressive and unhelpful. I focused on the wooden planks, counted my steps, and made it to the other side breathing hard but grinning.
foot:1.cnHint: 叙述者小心翼翼地将____踏上摇晃的绳桥，终于走到对岸。
foot:1.hook: Old Helm pointed ahead — the next island had no bridge at all.
foot:1.line: 'Put your *foot* flat on each plank and you will be fine,' said Old Helm.

graduate:1.en: A young woman sat alone on the steps of the Sky Library, her blue sash marking her as a fresh *graduate* of the island's Chart School. She had the look of someone who knew many things but had tested none of them yet. Bell greeted her warmly. 'Good,' said Old Helm under his breath. 'We could use someone who still asks questions.'
graduate:1.cnHint: 旅行队在图书馆台阶上遇到一位刚从制图学校毕业的____，老赫姆觉得她正是队伍需要的人。
graduate:1.hook: The graduate unrolled a map of a place none of us had ever heard of.
graduate:1.line: 'I am a new *graduate*, but I have studied every chart of the outer islands,' she said.

intake:1.en: The wind engine at Harbour Neck ran on breath — or so it looked. A wide funnel caught the island's constant breeze, and Bell adjusted a brass ring to control the *intake* of air. The engine hummed, the propeller turned, and our little vessel eased forward. I had never seen anything so clever made from so few parts.
intake:1.cnHint: 贝尔调整黄铜环，控制风力引擎的气流____，让船平稳前行。
intake:1.hook: Silverfang's faster ship appeared on the horizon, its own engine roaring loudly.
intake:1.line: 'Reduce the *intake* now or the engine will spin too fast,' Bell said calmly.

screen:1.en: A tall frame of woven reeds stood at the mouth of the alley — a *screen* that split the market wind into soft, slow currents on the sheltered side. Traders hung word-shards from its edges, and each one swayed and caught the starlight. I found our next fragment dangling near the bottom, quiet and patient, as if it had been waiting for us.
screen:1.cnHint: 旅行队在一道芦苇编成的____旁找到了下一块词语碎片，它静静挂在边缘等待着他们。
screen:1.hook: When I reached for the shard, the whole screen rang like a soft bell.
screen:1.line: 'The *screen* keeps the strong wind off the delicate charts,' said Bell.

chair:1.en: At the top of Pillar Crest sat an old carved stone seat — the island's *chair* of honour, given only to the troupe leader who could name every island in the eastern ring. Old Helm walked up to it, sat down without hesitation, and named all thirty-seven. The small crowd watching broke into surprised applause. I clapped the hardest.
chair:1.cnHint: 老赫姆坐上石柱顶端的荣誉____，流利地说出东环所有岛屿的名称，赢得了掌声。
chair:1.hook: A voice from the crowd challenged him to name the islands of the western ring too.
chair:1.line: 'The *chair* belongs to whoever knows the map best,' Old Helm said proudly.

court:1.en: Silverfang had docked at the open-air stone yard they called the Wind *Court*, where captains settled disputes by racing paper boats across a wide shallow pool. He challenged Old Helm with a smirk. Old Helm folded his boat in four calm moves. Silverfang's was faster at the start, but Old Helm's held its line and won by half a length.
court:1.cnHint: 老赫姆和银牙在户外石台____上用纸船比赛，老赫姆的船沿直线行驶最终获胜。
court:1.hook: Silverfang folded his arms and said there would be a rematch at the next island.
court:1.line: 'Everyone who docks here must race in the Wind *Court*,' Silverfang said with a grin.

couple:1.en: Old Helm spread the new map across a flat rock at the edge of the island. A *couple* of lines glowed faintly near the border, tracing a path neither Bell nor I had noticed before. Bell leaned in close, her finger following the light, and whispered that the path forked just ahead.
couple:1.cnHint: 老舵主在悬崖边展开地图，发现边缘有____条发光的线索。
couple:1.hook: The fork in the path meant only one of us could go first.
couple:1.line: 'There are only a *couple* of glowing marks, so we move carefully,' said Old Helm.

definition:1.en: The edge of the island dropped away into open sky. From up here the horizon had a perfect *definition*—a sharp, clean line where the pale sky ended and the deep blue dark began. Bell said the old charts called this place the Map's End, and I finally understood why.
definition:1.cnHint: 在岛屿边缘，小铃指出地平线有着惊人的____，轮廓清晰如刀割。
definition:1.hook: Beyond that clean line, something vast was slowly rising.
definition:1.line: 'The *definition* of the sky here is sharper than any chart I have drawn,' said Bell.

imagination:1.en: Old Helm asked me to sketch what I thought lay beyond the last island. I closed my eyes and let my *imagination* run. I drew towers made of cloud and bridges made of starlight. When I opened my eyes, Old Helm was nodding slowly, as if the drawing matched something he already knew.
imagination:1.cnHint: 老舵主让我用____画出地图尽头的景象，他看后若有所思地点头。
imagination:1.hook: He had seen that place before, and never spoken of it.
imagination:1.line: 'Your *imagination* has drawn something very close to the truth,' said Old Helm.

journey:1.en: We had been sailing for three weeks, hopping from island to island, collecting word-fragments that slowly filled the blank spaces on our map. Bell told me that every *journey* toward the map's edge feels longer than it looks, because the islands drift a little each night. I believed her.
journey:1.cnHint: 小铃告诉我，每一段通往地图边缘的____都比看起来更漫长。
journey:1.hook: Tonight the islands had drifted further than usual.
journey:1.line: 'Every *journey* to the edge teaches us something the map cannot show,' said Bell.

nearby:1.en: We anchored just outside a cluster of small islands and decided to rest. Bell spotted a light *nearby*, blinking in a slow rhythm from a rocky platform no bigger than a cart. Old Helm said it was a word-beacon—a fragment waiting to be claimed. We exchanged a quick, hopeful look.
nearby:1.cnHint: 小铃发现____有一盏灯在岩石台上缓缓闪烁，那是一个词语信标。
nearby:1.hook: Word-beacons do not blink unless something is already watching you.
nearby:1.line: 'There is a beacon *nearby*; we should reach it before the light fades,' said Bell.

perspective:1.en: I climbed to the top of the tallest rock on the island to get a better *perspective* of the route ahead. From up there I could see three more islands stacked in a loose chain, each one smaller than the last. The final one was barely a shadow at the edge of the star-filled sky.
perspective:1.cnHint: 我爬上最高的岩石，从新的____俯瞰前方，发现三座岛屿排成一列。
perspective:1.hook: The last shadow at the end of the chain was moving.
perspective:1.line: 'From this height the *perspective* changes everything—I can see the whole chain,' I said.

requirement:1.en: Old Helm unrolled the ancient sailing code and read aloud. One *requirement* stood clearly above all others: before any ship may cross the final boundary on the map, every member of the crew must hold a word-fragment in hand. We looked at each other. Bell was still one fragment short.
requirement:1.cnHint: 古老航行规则中有一条____：越过地图终界前，每位船员必须持有一块词语碎片。
requirement:1.hook: Bell reached into her coat and found only an empty pocket.
requirement:1.line: 'The first *requirement* is that we each carry a word before we cross,' read Old Helm.

signal:1.en: Silverfang's ship appeared on the far side of the island without warning. He stood at the bow and raised one silver lantern high. Bell grabbed my arm and said that in the old sailor's code, a raised lantern *signals* a challenge—he wanted to race us to the map's final edge.
signal:1.cnHint: 银牙船长高举银灯，小铃说这个动作在古老水手暗语中____着一场挑战。
signal:1.hook: Old Helm's jaw tightened, and he reached for the helm.
signal:1.line: 'One raised lantern *signals* a race—Silverfang wants to reach the edge first,' said Bell.

salary:1.en: The market on Goldpetal Island stretched across three rope bridges, sellers calling out prices from every side. Old Helm stopped at a coin-scale stall and told us that our *salary* as new troupe members was paid not in gold but in words — one new word per island crossed. I held my first word-fragment tight and felt richer than I ever had.
salary:1.cnHint: 老舵手解释说，加入剧团的新成员会以「____」的形式获得报酬，不是金币，而是文字碎片。
salary:1.hook: But the coin-scale stall had one price tag that bore no number at all.
salary:1.line: 'Your *salary* here is a word that opens the next sky,' Old Helm said.

shopping:1.en: Bell led me through the Lantern Bazaar, a floating square where merchants hung glowing jars from every awning. She called it *shopping* for map pieces — each stall keeper held a syllable, and only by trading a small story could you earn it. By the time we left, my pockets were full of syllables and my heart was full of colour.
shopping:1.cnHint: 小铃带着叙述者在漂浮集市里进行____，用故事换取地图碎片的音节。
shopping:1.hook: One stall keeper smiled and said the last syllable cost something we had not yet found.
shopping:1.line: '*Shopping* here means trading stories, not coins,' Bell said with a grin.

tendency:1.en: Old Helm studied the wind above the Drift Cliffs and muttered to himself. He said the clouds had a *tendency* to lean east just before a new island surfaced from the mist. Sure enough, within an hour a green shape rose on the horizon, draped in vines and humming with some quiet life of its own.
tendency:1.cnHint: 老舵手观察到云层有一种____，预示着新岛屿即将从迷雾中浮现。
tendency:1.hook: The green island groaned once, as if it had been waiting a very long time.
tendency:1.line: 'The sky has a *tendency* to show us the way when we stop rushing,' Old Helm said.

tough:1.en: The rope path to the Salt Arch was *tough* going — wind from three directions, planks slick with morning dew, and a drop of pure white cloud below. Silverfang crossed first without a word, hands steady, eyes forward. I watched and copied every step, and when my foot touched solid stone I let out a breath that felt a week old.
tough:1.cnHint: 通往盐拱门的绳索小路极为____，叙述者模仿竞争船长的步伐才安全通过。
tough:1.hook: On the far side, Silverfang pointed to a second arch hidden inside the first.
tough:1.line: 'The path is *tough*, but the view at the top belongs to those who cross,' Silverfang said.

tour:1.en: Bell had made this *tour* of the Amber Ring islands twice before, yet she still paused at every overlook and pointed out details I would have missed — a crack shaped like a river, a stone that caught light like a small sun. Her excitement was not performance; it was just how she moved through the world, and I was glad to follow.
tour:1.cnHint: 小铃已经____过琥珀环群岛两次，但她依然对每一处景色充满惊喜。
tour:1.hook: At the last overlook she went quiet and pointed to an island that was not on any map.
tour:1.line: 'Every *tour* teaches me something the last one missed,' Bell said softly.

wake:1.en: We sailed out before dawn, and I stood at the back of the deck watching our *wake* fan out across the dark water below the clouds. The white lines curved and disappeared into the dark, and Old Helm said each one was a road we had already made — proof we had been somewhere, even if the sky closed behind us.
wake:1.cnHint: 叙述者站在船尾，望着船行过后留下的____，老舵手说那是我们走过的证明。
wake:1.hook: Then a second wake appeared beside ours, from a ship no one could see.
wake:1.line: 'A ship's *wake* is its signature on the sea,' Old Helm said, eyes on the horizon.

annual:1.en: At the top of Sundial Peak, the whole troupe had gathered for what Silverfang called the *annual* word count — a tradition where every member reads aloud every word they had collected in the past year. The sound of all those words together was like a key turning slowly in a very large lock, and somewhere below us, a new island shuddered into the light.
annual:1.cnHint: 在日晷山顶，竞争船长主持了一年一度的____词语盘点，所有收集的文字齐声朗读。
annual:1.hook: This year the lock did not just click — it swung wide open with a sound like bells.
annual:1.line: 'The *annual* count reminds us how far the words have carried us,' Silverfang said.

charity:1.en: A small cloud-ferry had run aground on the edge of Pale Ledge, its crew of three sitting cold in the wind. Old Helm did not hesitate — he called it simple *charity* and had us pull them aboard, share our bread, and offer the warmest corner of the deck. That night one of the rescued crew pressed a word-fragment into my hand without a word, eyes bright with thanks.
charity:1.cnHint: 老舵手毫不犹豫地援救了搁浅的云渡船船员，他说这只是出于____之心。
charity:1.hook: The word-fragment the stranger gave me glowed a colour I had never seen before.
charity:1.line: '*Charity* costs us very little and opens doors we did not know were there,' Old Helm said.

strength:1.en: At the edge of the map, the wind pulled hard at our balloon. Old Helm gripped the rope and leaned forward, teeth pressed together. 'We move when I say,' he told me. The whole troupe drew on every last piece of *strength* to keep us level above the crumbling stone pier.
strength:1.cnHint: 在地图尽头的悬崖边，团队用尽全力稳住了气球，____让大家得以坚持下来。
strength:1.hook: Below us, the pier cracked and fell into silence.
strength:1.line: Old Helm: 'Every bit of *strength* counts when the sky fights back.'

survive:1.en: The old stone platform at the map's edge had seen storms, fires, and forgotten wars. Only a single carved gate still stood. Bell ran her hand along it and said that not many things *survive* so long without a reason. I wondered what reason this gate had kept so quietly all these years.
survive:1.cnHint: 小铃在地图尽头发现了一座古老的石门，感叹它____了那么多岁月，一定有其原因。
survive:1.hook: Behind the gate, something breathed in the dark.
survive:1.line: Bell: 'How does anything *survive* out here at the edge of the world?'

touch:1.en: Bell guided us onto a narrow stone bridge at the map's outermost point. The air felt strange, almost alive. When my boot made the first *touch* with the bridge surface, a soft chime rang across the whole sky, as if the island itself had been waiting for someone to arrive.
touch:1.cnHint: 在地图最边缘的石桥上，我踏上桥面的那一____让整片天空响起了钟声。
touch:1.hook: Every island within sight began to glow at once.
touch:1.line: Bell: 'That *touch* just woke something very, very old.'

trap:1.en: Silverfang led his crew to the same crossroads we had found first. Old Helm studied the ground and spotted a hollow beneath the centre stone. 'Classic *trap*,' he said softly, steering us around the edge. Silverfang's first mate stepped right onto it, and a burst of coloured smoke swallowed the entire crossroads.
trap:1.cnHint: 在路口，老舵识破了一个____，带领大家绕道而行，而对手却踩了上去。
trap:1.hook: When the smoke cleared, Silverfang's crew had vanished.
trap:1.line: Old Helm: 'Walk wide — that stone is a *trap* if I ever saw one.'

tv:1.en: We found a ruined market stall near the map's last road, covered in old signs from islands we had never visited. One sign showed a glowing box with a tiny moving picture inside. Bell laughed and said the islanders once called it a *tv*, a window that showed you the whole world without leaving home.
tv:1.cnHint: 在废弃的集市上，小铃向大家解释了一块古老招牌上画的____是什么东西。
tv:1.hook: The picture on the sign was still moving.
tv:1.line: Bell: 'They watched a *tv* to see the world — we just fly to it.'

victim:1.en: A small crowd of stone statues stood frozen at the far end of the last road. Each figure wore a look of surprise. Old Helm read the carved sign beside them: anyone who spoke a false word here became a *victim* of the island's oldest law and was turned to stone on the spot.
victim:1.cnHint: 在路的尽头，老舵读出了石碑上的警告：说谎者将成为这条法则的____，被化为石像。
victim:1.hook: Old Helm glanced at me and said nothing more.
victim:1.line: Old Helm: 'No one wants to be a *victim* of a law they cannot see.'

zone:1.en: Just past the final marked street, the colour of the sky changed from deep blue to pale gold. Bell opened her chart and drew a careful circle around the area. 'This is the drift *zone*,' she said, 'where the island's edge floats a little free of the map.' We stepped in slowly, one foot at a time.
zone:1.cnHint: 在地图尽头，小铃在海图上标出了一个特殊的____，那里的岛屿边缘不再固定。
zone:1.hook: The ground beneath us swayed like a boat at sea.
zone:1.line: Bell: 'Stay close — the drift *zone* plays tricks on your feet.'

afraid:1.en: I stood at the very last point the map showed, and nothing but open sky lay ahead. The troupe waited behind me. I told Old Helm my boots would not move. He put a hand on my shoulder and said it was all right to be *afraid*, as long as fear did not do the steering. I took one breath and stepped forward.
afraid:1.cnHint: 在地图的终点，我告诉老舵我迈不开脚，他说____是正常的，但不能让它做主。
afraid:1.hook: The sky ahead rippled like water touched by a stone.
afraid:1.line: Old Helm: 'Being *afraid* is honest — just don't let it steer.'

behave:1.en: The market square of Cinderstone Island was full of noise and colour. Old Helm stopped beside a fruit stall and looked at me with calm, steady eyes. 'Every island judges the whole troupe by you,' he said. I straightened my coat. Out here, how you *behave* tells strangers everything about who you are.
behave:1.cnHint: 老舵手告诉叙述者，在陌生的岛屿上，一个人的____代表着整个剧团的形象。
behave:1.hook: A hooded figure at the stall's edge watched my every move.
behave:1.line: '*Behave* well out there, and every door on this island will open for you.'

cent:1.en: Bell spread the troupe's coins across a low wall and counted carefully. The island's gate toll was steep, and we had nearly nothing left. 'Not a single *cent* to spare,' she said quietly, lifting one small copper piece to the starlight. Even so, a tiny smile crossed her face — she had a plan.
cent:1.cnHint: 领航员数完所有硬币后发现，队伍里已经没有多余的一____了。
cent:1.hook: Then she pulled a folded map scrap from inside the copper piece's hollow centre.
cent:1.line: 'We don't have a single *cent* to waste, so listen closely to my plan.'

commercial:1.en: The harbour boulevard of Trestfall Island was lined with banners and bright signs. Old Helm shook his head at the noise. 'Too *commercial*,' he said. 'Every corner is trying to sell you something.' But tucked between two loud stalls, Bell spotted a quiet door — behind it, someone was whispering the name of our next word.
commercial:1.cnHint: 老舵手觉得这座岛的港口大街太____，但领航员却在嘈杂中发现了一扇神秘的门。
commercial:1.hook: The quiet door had no handle — only a keyhole shaped like a star.
commercial:1.line: 'This street feels too *commercial*; the real secret must be hidden somewhere simpler.'

death:1.en: We crossed the Bridge of Hollow Stone just as a cold wind rose from below. Old Helm walked without slowing. Carved into each stone pillar were small figures mid-fall. Bell read the old words aloud: the bridge was once called the Road of *Death*, built to remind travellers how precious the next island truly was.
death:1.cnHint: 石桥上的古老铭文记载着这座桥曾被称为____之路，提醒旅人珍视前方的土地。
death:1.hook: One pillar was freshly carved — and the date on it was today's.
death:1.line: 'They named it the Road of *Death* so no one would cross it without a grateful heart.'

escape:1.en: A sudden fog rolled across the open plaza of Driftmere Island, swallowing the lamp-posts one by one. I heard running footsteps and then silence. Old Helm grabbed my arm and pointed — a figure in grey had just made an *escape* through the market alley, dropping a folded paper as it vanished into the white mist.
escape:1.cnHint: 浓雾弥漫之中，一个灰衣人从集市小巷____了，并留下了一张折叠的纸。
escape:1.hook: The folded paper bore our troupe's name written in someone else's hand.
escape:1.line: 'That was no accident — whoever planned that *escape* knew exactly when the fog would come.'

expose:1.en: Bell climbed the old signal tower at the edge of Saltwind Market and pulled back the canvas covering the top platform. The strong sea wind moved to *expose* a wide view of three hidden coves below, each one sheltering a small ship. Old Helm studied them in silence, then nodded — one of those ships carried the next word.
expose:1.cnHint: 领航员揭开帆布，海风____了山崖下三处隐秘的海湾，其中一艘船藏着下一个单词。
expose:1.hook: The middle ship's flag was the same colour as Old Helm's old coat.
expose:1.line: 'Let the wind *expose* what the canvas hides — truth always finds a way to the surface.'

floor:1.en: The entrance hall of Gridstone Waystation was enormous. Our boots echoed on the wide stone *floor* as we walked in, each step sending a soft ring up to the high ceiling. Bell looked down and noticed the stones were not plain — they were a map, each tile a different island, laid out in the shape of the whole sky-sea.
floor:1.cnHint: 驿站入口大厅的____上铺着一幅完整的地图，每一块石砖都代表一座岛屿。
floor:1.hook: One tile was missing, and the empty gap matched exactly where we were going.
floor:1.line: 'Look at the *floor* — someone built the whole world into these stones for us to follow.'

foundation:1.en: Outside the old Cartographer's Hall, the ground had cracked and tilted. Bell knelt and pressed her hand to the broken earth. 'The *foundation* is giving way,' she said softly. Beneath the crumbling stone, I could see the edge of something enormous — a carved disk, older than the building above it, waiting to be read.
foundation:1.cnHint: 制图师大厅外的地面开裂了，领航员发现____正在下沉，石板下藏着一块古老的刻盘。
foundation:1.hook: The carved disk began to turn, slowly, all on its own.
foundation:1.line: 'If the *foundation* breaks, everything the old mapmakers knew will be lost with it.'

frame:1.en: At the edge of the island, Old Helm held up a broken wooden *frame* — the kind used to mount a map behind glass. 'Every piece of the old chart was once held in one of these,' he said. Around the empty border, faint words still glowed.
frame:1.cnHint: 老船长举起一个破旧的____，边框上隐约发光的字迹让众人屏息。
frame:1.hook: But the words faded the moment I reached out.
frame:1.line: 'This *frame* once held the key to every island on the route.'

friday:1.en: Bell checked her small journal and looked up with wide eyes. 'It is *Friday*,' she said quietly. The troupe had learned long ago that on this one day of the week, the floating islands drifted closer together — close enough to leap between them if you were brave.
friday:1.cnHint: 领航员翻开日志，发现今天是____，这一天各岛之间的距离会神奇地缩短。
friday:1.hook: We had only until sunset to make the crossing.
friday:1.line: 'Every *Friday*, the islands lean in — tonight is our chance.'

grain:1.en: The narrow street between two market stalls was covered in golden dust. Old Helm knelt and pinched a single *grain* of it between his fingers. 'Sky-wheat,' he whispered. 'It falls only where the wind carries a true word.' He stood and followed the trail of dust northward.
grain:1.cnHint: 老船长捡起街道上一粒金色的____，说它只会落在真正的"词语"附近。
grain:1.hook: The trail of golden dust led straight to a locked door.
grain:1.line: 'One *grain* of sky-wheat tells us more than a whole map.'

implication:1.en: Silverfang spread the torn chart on a stone table outside the inn. 'Look at where this path ends,' he said, tapping the blank edge. Bell frowned. The *implication* was clear to everyone — the map did not end because the road did. It ended because the maker had stopped, or been stopped.
implication:1.cnHint: 竞争船长指着地图的空白边缘，那个____令所有人心头一紧。
implication:1.hook: Someone had not wanted this map to be finished.
implication:1.line: 'The *implication* is simple — someone hid what comes next.'

incredible:1.en: We turned the corner and stopped. The street opened onto a platform hanging in open sky, and below it — nothing but stars, stretching in every direction. It was *incredible*: standing there felt like standing inside the night itself. Old Helm laughed softly and said, 'Now you understand why we travel.'
incredible:1.cnHint: 转过街角，众人看到了____的景象——脚下是无边无际的星空。
incredible:1.hook: Then the platform gave a small, slow tilt.
incredible:1.line: '*Incredible* — I have crossed a hundred islands and still this stops me.'

net:1.en: Bell had tied a wide *net* between two lamp-posts at the island's windy edge. As we watched, a glowing slip of paper — carried on the high wind — caught in the mesh. She climbed up, freed it carefully, and unfolded it: a single word, written in blue ink.
net:1.cnHint: 领航员在路边张起一张____，成功捕获了风中飘来的发光纸条。
net:1.hook: The word on the paper was none of us had ever seen before.
net:1.line: 'I set this *net* at dawn — the wind always brings something worth reading.'

obtain:1.en: The old vendor at the open-air stall shook his head slowly. 'You cannot buy this word-stone,' he said. 'You must *obtain* it by trade — something you carried far, something the island does not already know.' Old Helm reached into his coat and placed a dried sky-flower on the counter.
obtain:1.cnHint: 摊贩告诉众人，这块词石无法用钱购买，必须以特别的方式____。
obtain:1.hook: The vendor's eyes went wide at the sight of the flower.
obtain:1.line: 'To *obtain* the stone, give something the island has never seen.'

pair:1.en: Hanging above the street were two lanterns, shaped and painted to match exactly. Bell pointed at the *pair* and said that in the old island custom, matching lanterns marked a place where two roads — and sometimes two fates — crossed. Old Helm studied them for a long moment, then took the left road.
pair:1.cnHint: 街道上方挂着一____灯笼，领航员说这是两条命运之路交叉的标志。
pair:1.hook: Old Helm never explained why he chose the left.
pair:1.line: 'That *pair* of lanterns is a sign — one road remembers, one road forgets.'

mile:1.en: The market street of Crestfall Island stretched ahead, stall after stall of glowing lanterns and dried starfruit. Old Helm pointed to a faded sign at the far end. 'Every *mile* of this road holds a word,' he said quietly. I counted my steps, wondering how many miles — and how many words — still lay between us and the edge of the map.
mile:1.cnHint: 老船长说这条路每隔一____就藏着一个词语碎片，我忍不住开始数步伐。
mile:1.hook: The sign at the road's end was not a sign at all.
mile:1.line: 'Every *mile* of this road holds a word,' Old Helm said.

movement:1.en: Bell stood at the centre of the open plaza, eyes closed, arms slow and wide. 'Watch the wind *movement* in the flag,' she told me. 'That is how the island breathes.' Around her, the whole troupe went still. Even the vendors paused. The flag curled once to the left, and Bell smiled — she had found the word hidden in the air.
movement:1.cnHint: 小铃说旗帜的____能告诉她岛屿的呼吸，她就这样找到了藏在风里的词语碎片。
movement:1.hook: The flag curled a second time, pointing somewhere no map had marked.
movement:1.line: 'Watch the wind *movement* in the flag,' Bell told me.

party:1.en: A loud crowd filled the harbour road — drums, ribbons, someone tossing flower petals from a high window. Old Helm leaned close. 'This island holds a *party* every time a new word is found,' he said. I felt a warm flush of pride. Somewhere in the noise, Silverfang caught my eye and raised a small cup of juice in a quiet toast.
party:1.cnHint: 老船长解释说，每当有人找到一个新词语碎片，这座岛就会举行一场____。
party:1.hook: Then Silverfang pointed — the cup had a word carved into its base.
party:1.line: 'This island holds a *party* every time a new word is found,' Old Helm said.

rescue:1.en: The word had fallen into a deep canal crack between two bridges, glowing faintly below dark water. Bell tied a rope around my waist without a word. 'Your first *rescue* mission,' Silverfang called out, grinning from the bank. I took a breath, reached down, and pulled the small glowing tile free. The crowd on the bridge cheered, and the next island flickered into view on our map.
rescue:1.cnHint: 那个词语碎片掉进了运河裂缝里，银牙笑着说这是我的第一次____任务。
rescue:1.hook: But the tile was warm — and it was already pointing somewhere new.
rescue:1.line: 'Your first *rescue* mission,' Silverfang called out, grinning.

writing:1.en: The old post-office wall was covered in layered notes, messages left by travellers over many years. Bell traced one with her finger. 'This *writing* is at least a hundred years old,' she whispered. Hidden beneath the newest layer, pressed flat under faded paper, was a word-tile still bright as a fresh coin. Old Helm peeled it free and held it to the starlight.
writing:1.cnHint: 小铃指着那面布满____的墙，最深处藏着一枚依然光亮的词语碎片。
writing:1.hook: The tile's glow matched the colour of an island none of us had visited.
writing:1.line: 'This *writing* is at least a hundred years old,' Bell whispered.

bite:1.en: The street cook pressed a small pastry into my hand — warm, golden, smelling of star-anise. 'One *bite* and you will remember this island forever,' she promised. I took that bite. Something sweet and sharp rushed over my tongue, and for a moment I saw the whole floating archipelago laid out in my mind, every island bright and connected. Old Helm laughed softly. 'She was right, wasn't she?'
bite:1.cnHint: 街边厨师说，只需____一口她的糕点，你就会永远记住这座岛。
bite:1.hook: Old Helm was already pulling out the map — it had gained a new detail.
bite:1.line: 'One *bite* and you will remember this island forever,' she promised.

capture:1.en: Silverfang moved through the morning stalls with a small sketch-book, drawing everything fast — the stall shapes, the flag patterns, the way light hit the stone. 'I *capture* each street so we can find our way back,' she explained, not slowing her hand. I looked over her shoulder and saw the drawings were more than maps: they were alive with tiny notes and arrows, a second language only she could read.
capture:1.cnHint: 银牙用速写本____下每条街道的样子，那些画像是只有她才懂的第二种语言。
capture:1.hook: On the last page, she had already drawn a street none of us had walked.
capture:1.line: 'I *capture* each street so we can find our way back,' she explained.

cope:1.en: The outer ring of the market was loud, crowded, and full of sharp smells. I stopped walking. Old Helm noticed. 'New places are hard at first,' he said. 'You learn to *cope* by choosing one thing to focus on.' I picked the sound of a single wind-chime above all the noise. It rang clear and steady. My breath slowed. The market became manageable, and at the chime's base hung a glowing word-tile.
cope:1.cnHint: 老船长说，面对陌生嘈杂的地方，你要学会____——选一件事专注其上。
cope:1.hook: The chime rang once more, and the word-tile swung toward the east.
cope:1.line: 'You learn to *cope* by choosing one thing to focus on,' Old Helm said.

persuade:1.en: The market on Windspire Island buzzed with traders and bright cloth. Old Helm wanted to trade our last star-coin for a worn map. I tried to *persuade* him to wait — a seller nearby had a fresher one — but he was already reaching into his coat.
persuade:1.cnHint: 我试图____老团长，让他等一等，因为附近有更好的地图。
persuade:1.hook: The seller's eyes narrowed at the mention of star-coins.
persuade:1.line: 'I'll *persuade* him to lower the price — just give me a moment.'

preference:1.en: Bell spread three route-charts across the dock railing, each leading to a different island. Old Helm said the choice was mine. I studied the colours and shapes, then pointed to the northern one. 'Your *preference* is noted,' Bell said softly, marking it with a small ink star.
preference:1.cnHint: 面对三条路线，老团长让我说出自己的____，小铃在地图上做了标记。
preference:1.hook: The northern route had no return mark drawn on it.
preference:1.line: 'My *preference* is the northern path — the stars look clearer there.'

reliable:1.en: Silverfang docked beside us at the Edge Pier and tossed over a roll of charts without a word. Old Helm caught it and checked every line with his finger. 'This one is *reliable*,' he said at last, and the whole troupe let out a slow breath of relief.
reliable:1.cnHint: 银牙送来一份地图，老团长仔细检查后说这份地图是____的。
reliable:1.hook: Yet one small island on the chart had been carefully erased.
reliable:1.line: 'A *reliable* map is worth more than a fast ship out here.'

suspect:1.en: We found a word-fragment glowing under a loose stone near the Ladder Bridge. It seemed too easy. Old Helm pocketed it, but I began to *suspect* someone had placed it there on purpose. Bell watched the empty lane behind us the whole walk back to the ship.
suspect:1.cnHint: 在桥边轻易找到碎片后，我开始____这是有人故意设下的局。
suspect:1.hook: Footsteps echoed in the lane long after we had gone.
suspect:1.line: 'I *suspect* we were meant to find that — but by whom?'

yield:1.en: The old vine-covered gate on Amber Shelf had not been opened in years. Old Helm pushed once, then again. Finally it gave a long groan and began to move. 'These ancient locks *yield* slowly,' he said, 'but they do yield.' Beyond it lay a courtyard full of carved stone letters.
yield:1.cnHint: 锈蚀的古门在老团长的推动下终于____了，门后是刻满字母的庭院。
yield:1.hook: The last stone letter in the courtyard was still warm to the touch.
yield:1.line: 'Patience — even the strongest gates will *yield* in the end.'

abandon:1.en: Rain swept across Drift Terrace without warning. We had set up our word-display on the open square, but the crowd scattered like birds. Old Helm shook his head. 'We cannot *abandon* the show just because of a little rain,' he said, and Bell lit the lanterns higher.
abandon:1.cnHint: 大雨突然降临，老团长坚决不肯____演出，小铃把灯笼举得更高了。
abandon:1.hook: One stranger stayed behind in the rain, watching very closely.
abandon:1.line: 'We never *abandon* a show — not even in a storm like this.'

anxious:1.en: The bridge between Twin Peaks Island and the next platform was made of woven rope and old wood. I stepped onto it and felt it sway. Old Helm walked ahead without slowing, but I could tell even he was *anxious* — his hand kept touching the rope rail as he moved.
anxious:1.cnHint: 走在摇晃的绳桥上，老团长虽然步伐稳定，但他____的心情还是藏不住。
anxious:1.hook: A single plank near the centre looked darker than the rest.
anxious:1.line: 'Try not to look down — being *anxious* only makes your feet less sure.'

assess:1.en: Old Helm knelt at the base of the Word-Pillar on Cloud Step Street and ran his fingers across the carvings. He closed his eyes for a moment, then stood. 'I need a little time to *assess* what these marks mean,' he said. Bell and I waited, watching the sky turn gold.
assess:1.cnHint: 老团长在石柱前闭目沉思，说需要时间来____这些奇怪的刻文。
assess:1.hook: When he opened his eyes, his expression had completely changed.
assess:1.line: 'Let me *assess* the marks carefully — one wrong reading could lead us astray.'

beautiful:1.en: At the edge of the chart, where the last island floated above open sky, I stopped walking. The view was almost too much to hold — colours spreading wide like a quiet song. 'This is *beautiful*,' I whispered. Old Helm placed a worn hand on my shoulder and said nothing. Some sights need silence more than words.
beautiful:1.cnHint: 在地图的尽头，我第一次看见了那片令人屏息的____景色。
beautiful:1.hook: But something moved beneath those colours, rising fast.
beautiful:1.line: Old Helm said, 'Every *beautiful* place hides a door you have not yet found.'

combine:1.en: Bell spread three torn chart pieces across a flat stone. Each piece alone showed only fog, but when she pressed them together, the fog cleared. 'We must *combine* all the fragments,' she said firmly. Old Helm nodded. The joined image revealed a bridge of pale light stretching toward an island none of us had ever named.
combine:1.cnHint: 小铃把碎裂的地图拼在一起，才____出了通往新岛屿的路。
combine:1.hook: The bridge began to glow the moment the edges touched.
combine:1.line: Bell said, 'If we *combine* these pieces now, the way opens before dark.'

complicated:1.en: Silverfang unrolled a chart covered in lines that crossed and looped back on themselves. I stared until my eyes ached. 'The route looks *complicated*,' I admitted. Silverfang tapped one of the loops and smiled. 'Only because you read it like a road. Read it like a wind, and it becomes simple as breathing.'
complicated:1.cnHint: 竞争船长展开了一张____的航线图，让初来乍到的我看得头晕目转。
complicated:1.hook: Then one of the lines on the chart began to move on its own.
complicated:1.line: Silverfang said, 'The map is *complicated*, but the sky always tells the truth.'

crash:1.en: We heard it before we saw it — a sharp, shattering sound rolling up from below the island's edge. I ran to look. One of the smaller supply crates had slipped from the rope and was falling, its *crash* against the rocks below sending small stones skipping into the open air like startled birds.
crash:1.cnHint: 一只货箱滑落，____声在整个小岛上回荡，众人急忙跑去查看。
crash:1.hook: Inside the broken crate, something was still moving.
crash:1.line: Old Helm said, 'That *crash* means we have very little time left to load and leave.'

creature:1.en: Near the stone steps at the island's outer rim, a small *creature* sat watching us with wide, pale eyes. It had four thin legs, ears like folded paper, and fur the colour of early morning. None of us moved. It tilted its head, stood up slowly, and walked straight toward Bell as if it already knew her.
creature:1.cnHint: 在岛屿边缘的台阶旁，一只陌生的小____径直走向小铃。
creature:1.hook: Bell knelt down, and the creature placed something in her hand.
creature:1.line: Bell said, 'This little *creature* has been waiting here longer than we have.'

crime:1.en: Old Helm found a notice nailed to the post at the island's market gate. It listed a long *crime*: stealing a word-fragment from the common map and hiding it for private gain. The crowd around the post was quiet and uncomfortable. I read it twice. Somewhere on this island, someone had kept a piece of the world from the rest of us.
crime:1.cnHint: 市场门口张贴的告示揭露了一桩关于地图碎片的____。
crime:1.hook: Old Helm folded the notice and slipped it into his coat without a word.
crime:1.line: Old Helm said, 'A *crime* against the map is a crime against every traveller here.'

deeply:1.en: After the troupe gathered at the outer platform, Bell read the new word aloud. The sound settled over us like warm rain. I breathed in *deeply* and felt the word enter me the way a key enters a lock — with a small, satisfying click somewhere behind the ribs. The stars above seemed to lean in a little closer.
deeply:1.cnHint: 小铃读出新词的那一刻，我____地感受到了某种奇妙的共鸣。
deeply:1.hook: The nearest star then blinked — once, deliberately, straight at me.
deeply:1.line: Bell said, 'Breathe *deeply* and listen; the word will show you where it belongs.'

demonstrate:1.en: A crowd had gathered around a young islander at the open square. She held a small glass rod that hummed faintly. 'I will *demonstrate* how a single word can light the whole rod,' she said, and pressed the rod against the carved letters on the platform stone. A soft gold glow ran from letter to letter like a slow wave.
demonstrate:1.cnHint: 广场上，一位年轻岛民正向众人____词语如何点亮那根发光的玻璃棒。
demonstrate:1.hook: When the glow reached the last letter, the ground gave a quiet shudder.
demonstrate:1.line: She said, 'Watch closely; I will *demonstrate* this only once before the light fades.'

employment:1.en: The market square on Crestholm Island was loud with colour and noise. Old Helm stopped at a stall piled high with glowing jars and spoke to the keeper. 'We offer honest *employment* — navigator, cook, scout — in exchange for passage and a word.' The keeper smiled and pointed east, where a new island had just risen from the clouds.
employment:1.cnHint: 老舵在市集摊位前，用提供____的方式换取一个"词语"地图碎片。
employment:1.hook: The jar in the keeper's hand began to hum a name none of us knew.
employment:1.line: 'We offer honest *employment* and a fair share of every word we find.'

entire:1.en: Bell laid the latest map fragment on the stone table outside the wind-tower. The *entire* surface of the island was drawn on it — every path, every root bridge, every hidden hollow — yet one corner stayed blank. Old Helm tapped it gently. 'That blank piece is where we go next,' he said, and the stars above us seemed to lean in and listen.
entire:1.cnHint: 小铃把地图碎片铺开，发现岛屿____区域都已标注，唯独一个角落空白。
entire:1.hook: Whatever filled that blank corner had no name on any chart we carried.
entire:1.line: 'The *entire* island is mapped — except the one place that matters most.'

gift:1.en: An old woman sat outside the archive tower, weaving star-thread into bracelets. She held one out to me without a word. Old Helm leaned close and murmured, 'A *gift* here is never simple — it carries a memory of where it was made.' I slipped it onto my wrist and felt a faint pull, like the bracelet already knew which island it wanted to visit next.
gift:1.cnHint: 档案塔外的老妇人送给叙述者一件____，老舵手说这份____藏有某处地方的记忆。
gift:1.hook: The bracelet tugged my wrist toward the dark gap between two islands.
gift:1.line: 'A *gift* on this island is a map you wear on your skin.'

kitchen:1.en: Tucked behind the docking platform was a small open *kitchen* built from sky-oak planks, smelling of spice and warm bread. Silverfang was already there, bartering a rare wind-coin for a bowl of cloud-pepper soup. The cook pressed a folded word-card into his hand with the change. 'Every meal here,' Silverfang told me with a grin, 'comes with a destination.'
kitchen:1.cnHint: 停机坪后藏着一间露天____，银牙在那里用稀有风币换到了一张"词语"地图卡。
kitchen:1.hook: The word on that card pointed to an island no one at the table had ever heard of.
kitchen:1.line: 'The best secrets on this island come straight out of the *kitchen*.'

mystery:1.en: The stone arch at the centre of the island was covered in carvings no one could read. Bell circled it three times, head tilted, lips moving. 'The *mystery* is not the writing,' she said at last, 'it is why every carving faces away from the sun.' Old Helm pressed his palm to the arch, and a new word lit up under his hand like a quiet answer.
mystery:1.cnHint: 小铃研究石拱上的神秘雕刻，她发现真正的____不在文字本身，而在雕刻的朝向。
mystery:1.hook: The word Old Helm uncovered was not in any language the troupe had collected before.
mystery:1.line: 'The *mystery* is never the shape of the thing — it is what the thing is hiding from.'

opposite:1.en: The island was split by a deep sky-gorge. On our side, the trees were silver and the air smelled of rain. On the *opposite* shore, the trees were gold and the air shimmered with heat. Bell said a single bridge used to connect them, but the word that named the bridge had been lost. Old Helm smiled slowly. 'Then that,' he said, 'is the word we are here to find.'
opposite:1.cnHint: 峡谷____两岸的景色截然不同，老舵说他们正是来寻找那座消失的桥的"词语"的。
opposite:1.hook: Somewhere in the gorge between the two shores, something was still waiting to be named.
opposite:1.line: 'The *opposite* shore holds the half of the word we are missing.'

permanent:1.en: At the edge of the observation deck, someone had carved names into the railing — dozens of them, deep and clean. Old Helm ran a finger along the grooves. 'These travellers wanted something *permanent*,' he said quietly, 'proof they had been here, that this place was real.' I pulled out my own small knife, then stopped. Some marks, I thought, are better left as feelings than as cuts.
permanent:1.cnHint: 观景台栏杆上刻满了旅人的名字，老舵说他们渴望留下____的印记，叙述者却决定不刻。
permanent:1.hook: One name on the railing was still warm to the touch, as if carved only moments ago.
permanent:1.line: 'Nothing on these islands is *permanent* — except the words we carry away.'

plenty:1.en: The harvest platform on the cloud-farm was stacked with baskets of sky-fruit, each one glowing faintly orange. The farmer waved us toward the table with both arms. 'We have *plenty* — take what you need and leave a word in return.' We shared out slices of fruit, and Old Helm placed our newest word-card on the table like a coin. Above us, the stars seemed brighter after a good meal.
plenty:1.cnHint: 云端农场的收获台上堆满了天空果实，农夫说他们有____，欢迎用"词语"交换食物。
plenty:1.hook: The word Old Helm left behind began to glow the moment the farmer touched it.

strike:1.en: At the edge of the map, the wind changed. Old Helm stepped off the rope ladder and landed hard on the cobblestones. 'A lucky *strike*,' he said, brushing dust from his coat. Somewhere below the island, something groaned — as if the ground itself had been hit back.
strike:1.cnHint: 老舵主降落时踏出了有力的一____，脚下的大地似乎也在回应。
strike:1.hook: The groan came again, louder this time.
strike:1.line: Old Helm: 'That *strike* landed just where the old map marked the fault.'

television:1.en: Bell found it half-buried in the soil at the edge of the island — an old *television*, its glass cracked, its frame covered in moss. No one could explain how it got here. Old Helm knelt beside it and said it must have floated up from a world far below.
television:1.cnHint: 领航员在岛边的土里发现了一台旧____，没人知道它从何而来。
television:1.hook: Its cracked screen flickered with a faint, impossible glow.
television:1.line: Bell: 'A *television* this old should not still be warm to the touch.'

youth:1.en: Old Helm stopped at a stone marker carved with dates and names. He ran his fingers over the oldest line. 'My *youth* was spent on islands just like this,' he said softly. The rest of the troupe stood quiet, watching the way his eyes caught the starlight.
youth:1.cnHint: 老舵主在石碑前停下，低声回忆起他____时在这样的岛屿上度过的岁月。
youth:1.hook: Then he pointed to a name none of us recognized — his own.
youth:1.line: Old Helm: 'In my *youth* I buried a word-fragment somewhere on this very path.'

alter:1.en: Bell spread the map on the stone ground. The moment she placed it under the open sky, its lines began to shift. 'The stars *alter* it,' she whispered, watching the ink move like water. Old Helm nodded — this island only showed itself when the map agreed with the sky above.
alter:1.cnHint: 领航员发现星空会____地图上的线条，让岛屿的轮廓悄悄改变。
alter:1.hook: One new path appeared where there had been only open air.
alter:1.line: Bell: 'Every time the stars *alter* the map, a door we missed comes back.'

approximately:1.en: Old Helm counted his paces from the stone arch to the edge of the market square. '*Approximately* forty steps,' he announced, marking the number in his little book. Bell checked the map. Forty steps was exactly the distance between the word they carried and the next island on the route.
approximately:1.cnHint: 老舵主测量广场的距离，____四十步，与地图上标注的数字吻合。
approximately:1.hook: The market square began to rise, very slowly, into the air.
approximately:1.line: Old Helm: '*Approximately* forty steps should bring us to the hidden entrance.'

attractive:1.en: The market at the edge of the map was small but full of colour. Every stall offered something strange: jars of frozen sound, bottles of pressed starlight. Bell called it the most *attractive* place she had ever seen. Even Silverfang, leaning against a post with arms folded, could not hide a smile.
attractive:1.cnHint: 地图边缘的集市色彩缤纷，领航员觉得这是她见过的最____的地方。
attractive:1.hook: Then every trader turned at once and looked straight at us.
attractive:1.line: Bell: 'This is the most *attractive* market I have seen in three sky-seasons of travel.'

bag:1.en: Silverfang tossed a worn leather *bag* onto the stone table. It landed with a heavy thud and split at the seam, spilling out small tiles — each one carved with a letter. 'My whole collection,' she said. 'Every word I ever found. Now they belong to the troupe.'
bag:1.cnHint: 竞争船长把装满字母石片的旧____摔在桌上，宣布将收藏全部交给队伍。
bag:1.hook: Old Helm stared at one tile and went completely still.
bag:1.line: Silverfang: 'Everything in this *bag* cost me a year of searching the outer islands.'
