beat:1.en: Bell tapped the old drum at the centre of the square. One slow *beat* rolled out across the cobblestones, and the floating lanterns above them swayed in time. Old Helm smiled. 'When the island hears that rhythm,' he said, 'it knows we have arrived and it opens its last door.'
beat:1.cnHint: 领航员敲响广场中央的鼓，一声____让漂浮的灯笼随之摇曳，岛屿似乎也听见了。
beat:1.hook: The last door at the far end of the square swung open on its own.
beat:1.line: Bell: 'One *beat* of this drum is all the island needs to let us in.'

preserve:1.en: The market street on Amber Isle smelled of dried herbs and old wood. A trader handed Old Helm a sealed clay jar. 'We *preserve* rare seeds in salt and honey,' the trader said, 'so the next island can grow them.' Old Helm tucked the jar under his arm and smiled at me. The map fragment glowed warm in my pocket.
preserve:1.cnHint: 集市上，商人向老舵展示用盐和蜂蜜____珍稀种子的方法，地图碎片随之发光。
preserve:1.hook: But the jar's seal had already been broken by someone else.
preserve:1.line: 'We *preserve* rare seeds in salt and honey, so the next island can grow them.'

procedure:1.en: Bell laid the star-charts flat on the dock and tapped each one in order. 'There is a *procedure* for crossing the Drift Gap,' she said firmly. 'Miss one step and the wind throws you sideways.' I watched her careful hands and copied every move into my notebook. The gap ahead looked narrow but very, very deep.
procedure:1.cnHint: 小铃在码头向众人解释穿越漂流裂缝的____，我认真地把每个步骤抄进笔记本。
procedure:1.hook: Then Bell found a step missing from every chart.
procedure:1.line: 'There is a *procedure* for crossing the Drift Gap — miss one step and the wind throws you sideways.'

reasonable:1.en: Silverfang blocked the gate to the Copper Quarter and named his price for safe passage. Old Helm stroked his chin. 'That sounds *reasonable*,' he said quietly, which surprised me, because his eyes were already reading the wall for another way through. Silverfang relaxed just long enough. We were past the gate before he counted the coins.
reasonable:1.cnHint: 银牙开出过路费，老舵表示这个价格____，但他的眼睛早已在寻找别的出路。
reasonable:1.hook: The coins Old Helm left behind were painted wood.
reasonable:1.line: 'That sounds *reasonable*,' Old Helm said, though his eyes were already elsewhere.

reduction:1.en: Storm clouds had swallowed two of the seven bridge-lanterns above the Valley Street. Bell frowned at her instrument. 'A *reduction* in light means the bridge stones lose warmth and start to drift,' she said. We had maybe twenty minutes. Old Helm told us to run, and I have never run so happily in my life.
reduction:1.cnHint: 小铃发现桥灯数量____，警告大家桥石会开始漂移，众人拔腿就跑。
reduction:1.hook: The seventh lantern flickered out just as my boot left the bridge.
reduction:1.line: 'A *reduction* in light means the bridge stones lose warmth and start to drift.'

season:1.en: Old Helm called it the amber *season* — that short time each year when the floating islands drift closest together and the gaps between them narrow to a single leap. We stood on the edge of Ridgeback Isle, watching the next island inch toward us through the haze. 'Now,' said Old Helm, and we jumped together into the warm air.
season:1.cnHint: 老舵说这是琥珀____，岛屿彼此靠近，众人站在边缘等待跳跃的时机。
season:1.hook: The next island stopped moving three feet short of us.
season:1.line: 'This is the amber *season* — the islands will never be closer than right now.'

setting:1.en: We came over the ridge and stopped. Below us, a village of paper lanterns floated above a silver lake, their reflections trembling in the still water. 'What a *setting*,' I breathed. Old Helm nodded slowly, as if the beauty hurt a little. Bell was already sketching it, her pencil moving fast before the clouds could change it.
setting:1.cnHint: 翻过山脊，众人看见一座灯笼村庄倒映在银湖中，这片____美得令人屏息。
setting:1.hook: Then we noticed the village had no doors.
setting:1.line: 'What a *setting*,' I breathed. 'I did not know places like this were real.'

shrink:1.en: The fog on Glass Bridge Lane was so thick I could barely see my own hands. With each step toward the centre, the path seemed to *shrink*, pressing us into a single-file line. 'Keep moving,' Silverfang called from somewhere behind us, his voice smaller than usual. Then the fog broke open and the whole sky appeared at once.
shrink:1.cnHint: 玻璃桥巷的大雾中，小路似乎不断____，众人只能排成一列前行，直到雾散天开。
shrink:1.hook: Silverfang was no longer behind us when we turned around.
shrink:1.line: 'The path will *shrink* as we go deeper — stay close and do not stop moving.'

bottom:1.en: We landed on a narrow ledge halfway down a cliff. Old Helm pointed his lantern toward the *bottom* of the ravine, where pale light gathered like water in a cup. 'The word is down there,' he said. I leaned over the edge and felt the stars pull at my back.
bottom:1.cnHint: 老舵手指着峡谷的____，那里聚集着奇异的光芒。
bottom:1.hook: Something in the dark below us blinked back.
bottom:1.line: 'The map fragment sits at the *bottom* — we must climb down.'

breed:1.en: A flock of cloud-birds circled our island, each one glowing faintly gold. Bell opened her notebook and sketched their wing-span. 'This *breed* only appears where a new word is close,' she said quietly. Old Helm smiled and turned the compass. The birds banked left, and we followed.
breed:1.cnHint: 贝尔认出这种云鸟的____，说明新的词语就在附近。
breed:1.hook: Every bird vanished at once, leaving only one feather falling.
breed:1.line: 'I have never seen this *breed* fly so low before.'

classify:1.en: Rows of glowing stones lined the path up the hill, each carved with a symbol. Bell knelt to study them. 'If we can *classify* these marks by shape, we can read the order,' she said. Old Helm handed her a cloth, and together they sorted the stones while the wind held still.
classify:1.cnHint: 贝尔试图____这些发光石块上的符号，以找出正确顺序。
classify:1.hook: The last stone had no symbol — only a question mark.
classify:1.line: 'Help me *classify* these shapes before the light fades.'

comment:1.en: We gathered at the market square of a drifting island. A stone board on the wall held dozens of small chiselled notes — travellers had left their *comment* on the path ahead. Old Helm read each one aloud. Most warned of fog. One simply said: 'Worth every step.'
comment:1.cnHint: 广场石板上满是旅行者留下的____，老舵手一条条大声朗读。
comment:1.hook: The newest note was still warm to the touch.
comment:1.line: 'Every *comment* on this board is a breadcrumb someone left for us.'

component:1.en: Bell spread the map pieces across a flat rock and studied the gaps between them. 'Each word is one *component* of the larger chart,' she explained, pressing two edges together until they clicked. A new island shape rose from the surface like smoke. Old Helm exhaled slowly and pointed north.
component:1.cnHint: 贝尔说每个词语都是整张地图的一个____，拼合后浮现出新岛屿。
component:1.hook: The shape that rose looked nothing like any island we knew.
component:1.line: 'This word is the missing *component* — the map can breathe now.'

contrary:1.en: Everyone in the troupe expected the bridge to lead east. On the *contrary*, it curved sharply back toward the sunrise cliff we had just left. Old Helm laughed and walked forward without pause. 'The best roads argue with you,' he said. Bell and I exchanged a glance, then followed his lantern.
contrary:1.cnHint: 大家以为桥通向东方，结果____，它弯回了出发的悬崖。
contrary:1.hook: At the far end, the sunrise cliff had grown a new door.
contrary:1.line: 'On the *contrary*, the difficult road is the one worth taking.'

deny:1.en: A toll-keeper blocked the road at the edge of the sky-market, arms folded. He claimed our map fragment was a forgery. Old Helm stepped forward calmly and said, 'You can *deny* its colour, its shape — but can you deny the word it carries?' The keeper looked down, and stepped aside.
deny:1.cnHint: 守门人拦住去路，老舵手质问他是否能____词语本身的存在。
deny:1.hook: As we passed, the keeper whispered a word I almost caught.
deny:1.line: 'I will not *deny* what the map clearly shows to all of us.'

depth:1.en: We lowered a lantern on a long rope into the well at the island's centre. The light shrank to a pin and still had not touched bottom. Bell measured the rope and shook her head. 'The *depth* of this place is beyond our line,' she said. Old Helm smiled. 'Then we found the right word.'
depth:1.cnHint: 贝尔测量古井的____，发现绳子到头了井底仍不见踪影。
depth:1.hook: A voice from below finished Old Helm's sentence perfectly.
depth:1.line: 'The *depth* of this well matches the depth of the word inside it.'

distinguish:1.en: The market at the edge of the map was a blur of colour and noise. Old Helm handed me two coins that looked almost identical. 'You must learn to *distinguish* the real tokens from the false ones,' he said, 'or we will never find the next island.'
distinguish:1.cnHint: 老团长让叙述者在嘈杂的市集中____两枚几乎一模一样的硬币。
distinguish:1.hook: One coin was warm; the other was ice-cold.
distinguish:1.line: 'You must learn to *distinguish* the real tokens from the false ones.'

document:1.en: A gust of wind scattered papers across the floating bridge. Bell snatched one from the air and held it up with wide eyes. It was an old *document*, stamped with a seal none of us had seen before, showing a route to an island that did not appear on any of our maps.
document:1.cnHint: 小铃在桥上捡到一份盖有神秘印章的____，上面标有未知岛屿的航线。
document:1.hook: The seal was still faintly warm to the touch.
document:1.line: 'This *document* shows a path no map has ever marked.'

dozen:1.en: We landed on a wide stone plaza where a *dozen* lanterns hung in a perfect circle, each one a different colour. Old Helm walked slowly around them, counting under his breath. He stopped at the pale-blue one and smiled. 'This is the one,' he said quietly.
dozen:1.cnHint: 广场上悬挂着____盏各色灯笼，老团长在其中找到了关键线索。
dozen:1.hook: The blue lantern flickered once, then spelled out a single letter.
dozen:1.line: 'A *dozen* lanterns, and only one holds the word we need.'

dull:1.en: The path leading out of the harbour town was long and grey, and the sky above was heavy with cloud. Bell kicked a pebble along the road. 'Even the air feels *dull* here,' she said. Then the clouds broke apart and beneath them floated a bright island none of us had mapped before.
dull:1.cnHint: 离港小镇的路灰暗____，但乌云散开后，一座新岛屿突然出现在众人眼前。
dull:1.hook: The island carried the sound of distant bells.
dull:1.line: 'Even the air feels *dull* here — something must be hiding.'

fortune:1.en: At the crossroads market, an old vendor spread a cloth covered in small carved tiles. 'Each tile holds a word,' she told us. Old Helm chose three without hesitation. 'Is that *fortune* or skill?' Bell whispered to me. I honestly had no idea, but all three tiles glowed the moment he touched them.
fortune:1.cnHint: 老团长在集市摊位上挑选刻字石块，小铃小声问叙述者这到底是____还是技巧。
fortune:1.hook: The three tiles together formed a name none of us knew.
fortune:1.line: 'Is that *fortune* or skill that guides his hand?'

fulfil:1.en: The bridge to the next island would only lower if someone read aloud the word carved on the gate. Bell stepped forward without hesitation. Her voice was steady and clear, and the moment she finished, the bridge swung down with a deep hum. 'You *fulfil* the condition,' Old Helm said, looking proud.
fulfil:1.cnHint: 小铃大声读出城门上的刻字，____了降桥的条件，桥随即缓缓落下。
fulfil:1.hook: Beyond the bridge, lights blinked on one by one.
fulfil:1.line: 'You *fulfil* the condition — the way forward is open.'

gradually:1.en: We climbed the long staircase cut into the side of the floating cliff. With each step the wind grew softer and the stars above *gradually* came closer, or so it seemed, until at the top we stood in a silence so complete I could hear my own heartbeat and the faint hum of the island beneath us.
gradually:1.cnHint: 攀登悬崖石阶时，星空____靠近，直到顶端一片寂静令人屏息。
gradually:1.hook: At the top, a door stood open with no wall around it.
gradually:1.line: 'The stars *gradually* grow closer — we are nearly there.'

incentive:1.en: Old Helm unrolled a small chart and pointed to a glowing dot far beyond the current island chain. 'Whoever finds the word hidden in the night market gets to name our next destination,' he announced. That was all the *incentive* Bell and I needed. We were already running before he had rolled the chart back up.
incentive:1.cnHint: 老团长宣布谁找到夜市里藏的词语就能命名下一站，这个____让小铃和叙述者立刻冲了出去。
incentive:1.hook: The night market stretched farther than the map had promised.
incentive:1.line: 'That offer is all the *incentive* anyone here should need.'

lower:1.en: The path split at the edge of the island. Bell pointed to the *lower* bridge — the one closer to the clouds below — and said it was safer than the high road. Old Helm trusted her judgment. We crossed slowly, the wind tugging at our coats, stars drifting just beneath our feet.
lower:1.cnHint: 小铃建议走____的那座桥，老舵手信任她的判断，我们小心翼翼地走了过去。
lower:1.hook: Something moved in the clouds directly below us.
lower:1.line: 'Take the *lower* bridge — the high road is not safe today.'

naturally:1.en: The island had grown without any plan. Trees curved around the stone paths, flowers pushed through old wooden boards, and vines wrapped every railing. Bell said the place had been empty for a hundred years. Everything here had happened *naturally*, shaped only by wind, rain, and time. It felt quietly alive.
naturally:1.cnHint: 这座岛屿上的一切都是____生长的，没有任何人为规划。
naturally:1.hook: Then we saw a light inside the oldest tree.
naturally:1.line: 'It all grew *naturally* — nobody planted a single seed here.'

passionate:1.en: Old Helm spread the new map fragment across a flat rock. His eyes lit up in a way I had never seen before. He was *passionate* about maps the way some people are about music — completely, almost helplessly. He traced every line with one finger and whispered the name of each island like a small prayer.
passionate:1.cnHint: 老舵长对地图充满____，他用手指描摹每一条线，轻声念出每座岛的名字。
passionate:1.hook: One island on the map had no name at all.
passionate:1.line: 'I am *passionate* about maps — each one holds a world nobody has seen yet.'

pop:1.en: We were resting quietly when a small glowing bottle seemed to *pop* out of nowhere, landing with a soft bounce on the stone path ahead. Bell jumped back. Old Helm caught it before it rolled off the edge. Inside was a folded word-fragment, still warm, as if someone had just sent it across the sky.
pop:1.cnHint: 一个发光的小瓶子____出现，落在我们面前的石路上，里面装着一张地图碎片。
pop:1.hook: The word inside the bottle was not in any language we knew.
pop:1.line: 'Did you see that *pop* out of the air just now — right in front of us?'

possibly:1.en: The bridge ahead was old, its boards thin and grey. Bell crouched down and studied the ropes. She said it could *possibly* hold all three of us if we crossed one at a time and moved without stopping. Old Helm went first. I held my breath and counted his steps until he reached the other side.
possibly:1.cnHint: 小铃说这座桥____能撑住我们，但必须一个一个地过。
possibly:1.hook: Halfway across, Old Helm stopped and looked down.
possibly:1.line: 'This bridge can *possibly* hold us — but go one at a time, and do not stop.'

previously:1.en: Bell unrolled the map and pointed to a small island marked with a circle. She said the troupe had *previously* visited it, years before I joined. The paths had changed since then, she warned — what was once open ground was now covered in tall grass and new stone. I listened carefully and updated my own notes.
previously:1.cnHint: 小铃说他们____曾来过这座岛，那时的路和现在已经大不相同。
previously:1.hook: Her voice was steady, but her hand on the map was not.
previously:1.line: 'We *previously* came through here — but nothing looks the same now.'

profession:1.en: At the edge of the market square, an old man carved tiny maps into pieces of wood. I asked Old Helm what the man did. Old Helm smiled and said map-carving was the man's *profession* — one of the oldest on the floating islands, passed from parent to child for generations. I bought one before we left.
profession:1.cnHint: 老舵长告诉我，那位老人的____是雕刻地图，这门手艺已传承了好几代。
profession:1.hook: The tiny map the old man sold me showed an island no chart had ever named.
profession:1.line: 'Map-carving is his *profession* — he has done it longer than I have been sailing.'

readily:1.en: I expected Old Helm to argue when Silverfang offered to share his island charts. Instead, Old Helm *readily* agreed, rolling out our own maps on the deck without hesitation. Silverfang looked surprised. Bell whispered to me that this was how trust between rival crews began — not with words, but with open hands and open maps.
readily:1.cnHint: 老舵长____同意了银牙的提议，毫不犹豫地拿出了我们自己的地图。
readily:1.hook: Silverfang stared at our map for a long time before he spoke.
readily:1.line: 'I *readily* agree — open maps are the only honest language between sailors.'

relax:1.en: After three days crossing storm clouds, our troupe finally landed on a wide, grassy platform above the mist. Old Helm spread his coat on the soft ground and told us to *relax* for a while. The island hummed quietly, as if it too needed rest before the next leg of our journey.
relax:1.cnHint: 历经风暴后，老舵带领大家在草地上____，享受片刻宁静。
relax:1.hook: But the grass beneath us slowly began to rise.
relax:1.line: '*Relax*, everyone — the next island is not going anywhere,' said Old Helm with a wide grin.

release:1.en: Bell discovered a stone cage half-buried at the edge of the platform. Inside, a small cloud-bird beat its wings against the bars. She knelt, found the old latch, and with a careful turn, chose to *release* it. The bird spiralled upward, leaving a trail of silver light across the sky.
release:1.cnHint: 小铃在石笼旁发现了一只被困的云鸟，决定将它____。
release:1.hook: The silver trail pointed straight toward the map's blank edge.
release:1.line: 'We have to *release* it — a caged bird is a bad sign on any island,' said Bell.

route:1.en: Old Helm unrolled the map on a flat boulder and studied it closely. The word we had collected glowed faintly, drawing a thin line through the clouds. 'This is our *route*,' he said, tracing the line with one finger. It curved sharply left, away from every path we had considered before.
route:1.cnHint: 老舵在石台上展开地图，为我们指出了前往下一座岛的____。
route:1.hook: The line on the map ended at a question mark no one had noticed before.
route:1.line: 'Follow this *route* exactly and do not trust shortcuts,' Old Helm warned, his voice steady.

sight:1.en: We rose above the cloud layer at dawn, and the whole crew fell silent. An endless field of floating islands stretched before us, each one lit by its own quiet glow. It was the most astonishing *sight* I had ever witnessed — more islands than words in any map we carried, disappearing into the far blue.
sight:1.cnHint: 破云而出的一刻，眼前壮阔的____让全体成员都屏住了呼吸。
sight:1.hook: Then one island blinked out of sight entirely.
sight:1.line: 'What a *sight* — I never imagined there could be so many islands,' Bell whispered softly.

speaker:1.en: A crowd had gathered around a tall post at the centre of the market island. A travelling *speaker* stood on a wooden box, describing distant islands no chart had ever named. Old Helm listened from the edge of the crowd, arms folded, eyes sharp. He believed maybe one word in ten, he told me later.
speaker:1.cnHint: 集市中心，一位____正在描述地图上从未标注过的神秘岛屿。
speaker:1.hook: One of those unnamed islands matched our map fragment perfectly.
speaker:1.line: 'That *speaker* knows something we do not — stay close and listen,' Old Helm murmured quietly.

species:1.en: Bell stopped beside a row of strange trees whose roots floated free in the open air. She had never seen anything like them. 'A new *species*,' she said softly, running a finger along one pale root. Old Helm marked the spot on the map with a small star, the sign we used for discoveries worth returning to.
species:1.cnHint: 小铃在岛边发现了一种根系悬浮在空中的奇特植物____。
species:1.hook: The roots twitched the moment she let go.
species:1.line: 'This *species* does not grow in soil at all — look, the roots reach for starlight,' Bell said.

specifically:1.en: Silverfang landed her vessel on the far dock and walked over without greeting anyone. She pointed to one small island circled in red on her own chart. 'I am here *specifically* for that one,' she said, her voice calm and certain. Old Helm tilted his head; that same island was circled on our map too.
specifically:1.cnHint: 竞争船长登岛后，明确表示她____是为地图上某座特定的岛屿而来。
specifically:1.hook: Two maps, one island, and only one troupe could claim it.
specifically:1.line: 'I came *specifically* for that island, and I intend to reach it first,' said Silverfang coolly.

unfortunately:1.en: We reached the far dock just before sunset, ready to follow our new route. But the bridge of woven cloud-rope that connected the two islands had come loose and drifted away. '*Unfortunately*,' said Old Helm, staring at the gap, 'the path has decided to leave before we did.' He did not sound worried, which worried me.
unfortunately:1.cnHint: 就在大家准备出发时，连接两座岛屿的桥____已经断开漂走了。
unfortunately:1.hook: Somewhere below the gap, something large was moving upward.
unfortunately:1.line: '*Unfortunately*, our bridge is gone — but every problem hides a better road,' said Old Helm calmly.

somewhat:1.en: The edge of the map was a wide platform of pale stone, open to every wind. Old Helm spread the last chart flat and held it down with both hands. The star above us burned *somewhat* brighter than the others, as if it were pointing at something just beyond the known world.
somewhat:1.cnHint: 老赫姆展开最后一张海图，发现头顶那颗星比其他星____亮。
somewhat:1.hook: Whatever the star pointed to, it had no name yet.
somewhat:1.line: 'This star is *somewhat* brighter — it is trying to tell us something.'

stable:1.en: At the very edge of the last island, Bell found a low *stable* cut into the rock. Inside, a row of old wind-runners — creatures like horses made of cloud — stood quiet. Their breath rose in slow silver puffs. Old Helm said nothing; he just placed one hand on the nearest creature's neck.
stable:1.cnHint: 贝尔在最后的岛屿边缘发现了一座嵌入岩石中的____，里面有几头云雾般的生灵。
stable:1.hook: The cloud-runners lifted their heads, all at once, toward the dark beyond.
stable:1.line: 'Keep the lantern *stable* — one flicker and they will bolt.'

vigorous:1.en: At the edge of the map, Old Helm planted his walking stick into the cracked soil and stretched both arms wide. 'We move at dawn,' he called, his voice *vigorous* and full, rolling across the empty plain like a bell. Even the tired horses lifted their heads.
vigorous:1.cnHint: 老舵主用____的声音宣布黎明出发，连疲惫的马儿都抬起了头。
vigorous:1.hook: But the plain beyond had no path marked on any chart.
vigorous:1.line: 'Keep that *vigorous* pace — the next island will not wait for slow feet.'

wide:1.en: The troupe stood at the rim of the highest island and looked out. The sky was *wide* beyond all imagining — star after star stitched into blue-black cloth, with other islands floating like quiet boats far below. Bell spread her arms as if she could hold it all.
wide:1.cnHint: 贝尔站在岛屿边缘，望向那片____的星空，张开双臂想把它都揽入怀中。
wide:1.hook: Then one distant island flickered, and something on it moved.
wide:1.line: 'A sky this *wide* means there are still places none of us have named.'

agriculture:1.en: The first terrace we found was carved right into the side of a floating island. Rows of low green plants climbed toward the light. Old Helm knelt and pressed the soil. 'Somebody studied *agriculture* up here,' he said quietly, surprised that someone had carried the knowledge of farming into the clouds.
agriculture:1.cnHint: 老舵主发现浮岛上刻有梯田，惊讶地说有人把____带到了云端。
agriculture:1.hook: Tucked under one plant was a folded piece of map, still fresh.
agriculture:1.line: '*Agriculture* this high up tells me someone planned to stay — for a very long time.'

assign:1.en: Old Helm spread the latest map fragment on a flat stone. He studied it for a long moment, then looked at each of us in turn. 'I will *assign* each person one path,' he said. Bell got the river road; I got the ridge trail that wound into pale morning mist.
assign:1.cnHint: 老舵主把新地图碎片铺开，决定____每个人不同的路线。
assign:1.hook: My ridge trail led straight toward a sound no one could explain.
assign:1.line: 'I *assign* the ridge to you — your eyes are sharpest in low light.'

broad:1.en: We crossed a *broad* stone bridge that connected two islands no rope-ladder had ever linked before. The bridge had no rail, only open air on either side, and the wind pushed at us sideways. Silverfang walked ahead without slowing, boots loud on the ancient rock.
broad:1.cnHint: 船队走过一座____的石桥，连接了两座从未相通的浮岛。
broad:1.hook: Halfway across, one stone shifted under Silverfang's foot.
broad:1.line: 'On a road this *broad*, there is no reason to crowd each other — spread out.'

careful:1.en: The old word-stone near the village gate was cracked clean down the middle. Bell crouched beside it, brush in hand, and began to copy the marks one by one. 'Be *careful*,' Old Helm said softly, watching from behind her shoulder. A wrong copy could send us to the wrong island entirely.
careful:1.cnHint: 贝尔蹲下来描摹裂开的文字石，老舵主提醒她要____。
careful:1.hook: Her brush paused over a mark none of us had ever seen before.
careful:1.line: 'Be *careful* with that last symbol — one wrong stroke and the map changes completely.'

combination:1.en: The locked gate at the island's edge had no key — only three spinning rings carved with small pictures. Bell turned each ring slowly, thinking out loud. 'A *combination* of cloud, star, and open hand,' she said at last. The rings clicked; the gate swung open onto a trail of silver light.
combination:1.cnHint: 贝尔找到了石门上三个转环的____，大门应声而开。
combination:1.hook: The silver trail beyond the gate was already fading fast.
combination:1.line: 'That *combination* — cloud, star, open hand — I have seen it once before, long ago.'

constant:1.en: Three days on the ridge, and the wind never stopped. It was a *constant* companion — not cruel, just always present, tugging sleeves and scattering sparks from the camp fire each night. Old Helm said the old islanders believed such a wind was the map's way of keeping travellers moving forward.
constant:1.cnHint: 山脊上的风____地吹了三天，老舵主说这是地图催促旅人前行的方式。
constant:1.hook: On the fourth morning, the wind stopped — and the silence felt like a warning.
constant:1.line: 'A *constant* wind is a gift; it means the map still wants us to move.'

himself:1.en: Old Helm stepped off the rope bridge and looked around slowly. He had drawn every mark on the old map *himself*, tracing each island edge by hand over years of travel. Now the map showed nothing ahead — only blank paper and open sky.
himself:1.cnHint: 老舵主亲自检查地图，发现前方已是一片空白。
himself:1.hook: The blank page trembled, as if waiting to be written.
himself:1.line: 'I drew every line *himself* — and still the map runs out.'

landscape:1.en: From the edge of the final island, the whole floating world spread below us. The *landscape* was breathtaking — silver clouds, tiny green islands stitched together by rope bridges, and far below, a darkness that swallowed all sound. Bell whispered that no chart had ever shown this view.
landscape:1.cnHint: 站在岛屿边缘，眼前出现了从未有人描绘过的壮阔____。
landscape:1.hook: Somewhere in that silver mist, a new island slowly rose.
landscape:1.line: 'No map has ever held a *landscape* this wide,' Bell said softly.

mentally:1.en: Bell stood at the bow and said nothing for a long time. She was *mentally* tracing the star lines above us, matching each bright point to a gap in the old chart. Her eyes moved fast while her body stayed perfectly still. Then she smiled and reached for her pencil.
mentally:1.cnHint: 领航员在____上推演星图，试图找到下一条航路。
mentally:1.hook: Her pencil stopped — right above the one blank island.
mentally:1.line: 'I am *mentally* mapping every star above us right now.'

onto:1.en: Silverfang unrolled a long cloth map and pressed it flat against the stone. He painted a bright trail *onto* the blank spaces, connecting three islands that no one had linked before. The paint glowed faintly in the starlight, like a living path.
onto:1.cnHint: 竞争船长把新航线涂画____空白区域，开辟出一条发光的路。
onto:1.hook: The glowing trail pulsed once — then pointed further on.
onto:1.line: 'I am painting our route *onto* the future,' Silverfang said.

plus:1.en: Bell counted quietly on her fingers. 'Three safe stops, *plus* the hidden ridge Old Helm found last season — that gives us four anchor points.' She sketched small circles on the chart, linking them with a clean line. The route suddenly looked possible for the first time.
plus:1.cnHint: 领航员将已知的停靠点____新发现的山脊加在一起，规划出完整路线。
plus:1.hook: Four circles on the map — but only supplies for three stops.
plus:1.line: 'Three known stops *plus* one new ridge — we have a route.'

root:1.en: At the edge of the island, a great old tree gripped the floating rock with thick, pale *roots* that curled over the edge and reached down into empty air. Old Helm touched one gently. He said the tree had grown here long before any map named this place.
root:1.cnHint: 岛屿边缘一棵古树的____悬在空中，比任何地图都更古老。
root:1.hook: Deep inside one root, something faintly glowed.
root:1.line: 'These *roots* are older than every map we carry,' Old Helm said.

satisfy:1.en: I had hoped the edge of the map would *satisfy* my hunger for answers, but standing here only made the questions bigger. More sky. More silence. More blank paper. Old Helm put a hand on my shoulder and said that was exactly the right feeling for a traveller.
satisfy:1.cnHint: 来到地图的尽头，却发现这里的景象并不能____对答案的渴望，反而带来更多疑问。
satisfy:1.hook: Old Helm smiled — then unrolled a second, larger blank map.
satisfy:1.line: 'The edge will never *satisfy* you — that is why we keep going.'

consultant:1.en: The market square on Bridgeport Island was loud with traders. Old Helm stopped at a small booth where a grey-haired woman sat behind stacks of maps. 'She is our *consultant*,' he said, meaning she knew things none of us could find in any book. She studied our fragments and pointed straight at the next island.
consultant:1.cnHint: 在嘈杂的市集上，老舵找到了一位熟悉地图的____，她指出了下一座岛的方向。
consultant:1.hook: But the woman's finger trembled over one corner of the map.
consultant:1.line: 'A good *consultant* saves you from three wrong turns,' Old Helm said quietly.

direct:1.en: Bell spread the new fragment on the deck and traced two routes to the Amber Cliffs. One wound through fog banks for two days. The other was *direct*, cutting straight across open sky in half a morning. Old Helm looked at the stars and chose the shorter path without a word.
direct:1.cnHint: 小铃研究地图碎片后，发现有一条____路线，可以在半个上午内直达目的地。
direct:1.hook: What Old Helm had not said was why he looked uneasy.
direct:1.line: 'The *direct* path is faster, but the sky there is never quiet,' Bell warned.

discourage:1.en: Fog rolled in thick around Greystone Ledge, and my lantern barely lit my own hands. Silverfang crossed his arms. 'Weather like this would *discourage* most crews,' he admitted. But Old Helm was already tying a guide-rope to the mast, his movements calm and sure, and somehow that was enough to keep us moving.
discourage:1.cnHint: 浓雾让大多数船队都会感到____，但老舵平静的举动让大家重新鼓起勇气。
discourage:1.hook: Then something large moved in the fog just beyond the rope.
discourage:1.line: 'I will not let a little fog *discourage* us today,' Old Helm said firmly.

essentially:1.en: Bell finished reading the fragment aloud, then set it down. 'This island,' she said, 'is *essentially* a library — every stone wall has words carved into it and every word is a door.' Old Helm smiled as if he already knew. I looked at the cliffs ahead and felt the whole place humming like a held breath.
essentially:1.cnHint: 小铃解释说，那座岛____上是一座石刻图书馆，每个词都是一扇门。
essentially:1.hook: The first wall we touched shivered, and a door opened on its own.
essentially:1.line: 'It is *essentially* a living map,' Bell said, eyes wide with wonder.

extent:1.en: From the top of Windspire Peak I could finally see the *extent* of the sky-sea — islands dotting the blue in every direction, far more than our map showed. Old Helm stood beside me and said nothing for a long moment. The silence felt like respect, offered to something too large to name.
extent:1.cnHint: 站在山顶，我第一次看清了天空海洋的____，远比地图上显示的要广阔。
extent:1.hook: And somewhere in that vast distance, one island was blinking like a star.
extent:1.line: 'Now you understand the *extent* of what we are looking for,' Old Helm said.

finance:1.en: The harbour master at Saltring Dock held out his hand and named a price that made Silverfang go pale. 'We do not have enough to *finance* a full repair and still buy food,' Silverfang muttered. Old Helm reached into his coat and placed a single glowing word-fragment on the counter. The harbour master's eyes went wide and he waved us through.
finance:1.cnHint: 银牙担心没有足够的钱____修船和购买食物，但老舵用地图碎片解决了难题。
finance:1.hook: The harbour master pocketed the fragment and whispered a name we had never heard.
finance:1.line: 'One good word can *finance* more than gold ever could,' Old Helm said calmly.

freedom:1.en: Past the last chain-gate, the sky opened up and there were no more toll islands, no more border guards, no more rules carved into stone posts. Bell threw her arms wide. 'This is *freedom*,' she laughed, and the wind agreed, filling our sail with one clean push that sent us racing toward the horizon.
freedom:1.cnHint: 越过最后一道关卡，小铃张开双臂，第一次感受到真正的____。
freedom:1.hook: Then Bell spotted something on the horizon that had no name on any map.
freedom:1.line: 'Real *freedom* means choosing which star to follow,' Bell said with a grin.

highlight:1.en: Old Helm unrolled all our fragments together for the first time on the grass of Ember Flat. He used a thin stick of pale chalk to *highlight* one central path — a bright line connecting every island we had visited, curving like a river through the sky. Seeing it whole made my chest feel full.
highlight:1.cnHint: 老舵将所有碎片拼在一起，用粉笔____出一条连接所有岛屿的核心路径。
highlight:1.hook: The chalk line ended not at an island, but at an empty stretch of open sky.
highlight:1.line: 'Let me *highlight* the one path that ties everything together,' Old Helm said.

invite:2.en: At the edge of the last known island, Bell found a folded note pinned to a lantern post. She read it aloud to the troupe: someone — or something — had chosen to *invite* us deeper into the unmapped dark. Old Helm smiled and said nothing. I felt my heart lift.
invite:2.cnHint: 小铃在路灯柱上发现了一张折叠的纸条，上面写着有人要____我们前往未知之地。
invite:2.hook: The note was signed with a symbol none of us recognised.
invite:2.line: 'They *invite* us forward — and I think we should go,' Bell said.

million:2.en: Old Helm unrolled a chart so large it covered the whole deck. Bell traced her finger across a field of tiny dots — each one an island. 'There could be a *million* places we have never touched,' she whispered. The stars above seemed to nod in quiet agreement.
million:2.cnHint: 老舵展开一张巨大的地图，小铃数着上面密密麻麻的小点，感叹岛屿的数量可能有____之多。
million:2.hook: One dot at the chart's edge was circled in red ink.
million:2.line: 'A *million* islands, and we have found maybe twelve,' Old Helm said softly.

represent:2.en: Deep in a sea-cave, we discovered a mosaic of coloured stones on the floor. Bell knelt and studied it carefully. 'Each colour may *represent* a different wind,' she said. Old Helm pressed his boot gently against a blue tile, and somewhere above us a door swung open.
represent:2.cnHint: 在海洞里，小铃仔细研究地板上的彩色石块，认为每种颜色可能____一种不同的风。
represent:2.hook: Behind the door, a soft golden light was already moving.
represent:2.line: 'These colours *represent* the four great winds — I am almost certain,' Bell said.

surprise:2.en: We landed on a tiny island that did not appear on any chart. To our *surprise*, it held a full market — bright tents, warm smells, laughing voices. Old Helm spread his arms wide. I had expected empty rock and found an entire small world instead.
surprise:2.cnHint: 我们降落在地图上没有标记的小岛，令大家____的是，岛上竟然有一个热闹的集市。
surprise:2.hook: A merchant waved at Old Helm as though they were old friends.
surprise:2.line: 'What a *surprise* — I had given up hoping to find company out here,' Old Helm said.

topic:2.en: Around the fire that night, every member of the troupe had a different idea about the glowing door we had passed through. Old Helm raised a hand. 'Let us agree on one *topic* at a time,' he said, and the voices settled into a single, careful thread of thought.
topic:2.cnHint: 篝火旁，大家七嘴八舌地讨论白天经过的发光门，老舵请大家一次只聊一个____。
topic:2.hook: When they finally agreed, the fire burned suddenly, strangely brighter.
topic:2.line: 'One *topic* at a time — that is how we find real answers,' Old Helm said.

meat:2.en: Silverfang's cook brought out a small pot and set it between the two crews without a word. The smell of slow-cooked *meat* drifted across the deck. For a moment every old rivalry was forgotten. Bell leaned over to me and murmured that good food was worth more than any truce paper.
meat:2.cnHint: 银牙的厨师端出一锅慢炖的____，两支船队之间的竞争气氛因这香味而暂时消散了。
meat:2.hook: Silverfang watched our faces and allowed herself one small smile.
meat:2.line: 'The *meat* is ready — come, both crews eat together tonight,' Silverfang said.

drink:2.en: At the market fountain, a girl handed each of us a small clay cup without being asked. 'You must *drink* before you may read the map,' she said. The water tasted of cold stars. Bell blinked twice, then laughed — the words on the old chart had rearranged themselves into a clear path.
drink:2.cnHint: 市场喷泉旁，一个女孩递给我们小杯水，说必须先____，才能读懂那张旧地图。
drink:2.hook: The girl was gone before any of us could ask her name.
drink:2.line: '*Drink* first — the map will only speak to those who have tasted the water,' she said.

sleep:2.en: We anchored between two quiet cliffs and agreed to rest. But Old Helm did not *sleep*. I found him at the bow in the early dark, holding the new word-fragment up to the starlight, turning it slowly. He heard my step and said the best maps were read when the world was still.
sleep:2.cnHint: 大家停船休息，但老舵没有____，我发现他独自在船头对着星光研究新得到的词语碎片。
sleep:2.hook: The fragment glowed faintly, as if it, too, was waiting for morning.
sleep:2.line: 'You should *sleep* — tomorrow the fragment will show us more,' Old Helm said quietly.

shop:2.en: The island market was unlike any *shop* I had ever seen. Every stall sold a single word, carved on stone or pressed into bark. Old Helm handed the seller three star-coins and received a smooth tile with letters glowing faintly gold. 'One word closer,' he said, tucking it into the map bag.
shop:2.cnHint: 在漂浮岛的集市上，老船长在一家____里用星币买到了一块发光的文字石板。
shop:2.hook: But the seller's eyes said that tile was never meant to be sold.
shop:2.line: 'This *shop* sells only words — choose the wrong one and the map leads nowhere.'

electronic:2.en: Bell knelt beside a humming panel near the island's edge. 'This is *electronic*,' she whispered, pressing her ear to it. Tiny lights blinked in a pattern — dot, dash, dot — like a message no one had decoded yet. Old Helm copied each blink into his notebook with careful strokes.
electronic:2.cnHint: 贝尔在岛边发现了一块____装置，它发出的闪光似乎藏着某种未解开的信息。
electronic:2.hook: The pattern changed the moment she copied the last symbol.
electronic:2.line: 'The *electronic* signals match the rhythm of the star map — this is no accident.'

wild:2.en: The outer ridge of the island was *wild* — no path, no marker, just tangled silver grass bending in a wind that smelled of open sky. I almost turned back, but then I spotted it: a word-stone half-buried in the roots, glowing a steady blue. My heart jumped.
wild:2.cnHint: 在岛屿边缘____的荒地里，叙述者发现了一块半埋在草根下、发着蓝光的文字石。
wild:2.hook: The grass closed behind me as if the island wanted that stone kept secret.
wild:2.line: 'Only someone *wild* enough to cross that ridge ever finds the hidden words.'

rich:2.en: The soil on this island was deep red and *rich*, and flowers grew so tall they brushed the underside of passing clouds. Tucked inside the largest bloom, Silverfang found a rolled leaf. On it, a single word was written in pollen-yellow ink — and on the back, a coordinate.
rich:2.cnHint: 银牙船长在这座土壤____肥沃的岛上，从一朵大花里找到了写着坐标的卷叶。
rich:2.hook: The coordinate pointed to an island that did not appear on any known chart.
rich:2.line: 'This island is *rich* in more than flowers — every root here hides a word.'

special:2.en: Old Helm laid out seven tiles on the deck. Six were ordinary; one had a faint silver border. 'This one is *special*,' he said quietly. When Bell touched it, the whole map bag began to glow, and a new island outline appeared at the very edge of the cloth. We all leaned in.
special:2.cnHint: 老舵手发现七块文字板中有一块与众不同，它____的银色边框让整张地图都亮了起来。
special:2.hook: The new island outline pulsed once, then shifted to a different corner of the map.
special:2.line: 'Keep this tile safe — a *special* word can rewrite the whole map.'

text:2.en: The cave wall was covered in old *text* — columns of tiny letters carved by someone long ago with a very steady hand. Bell read aloud slowly, and with each line the air around us grew a little warmer. At the end of the last column, one word was circled: an island name we had never heard.
text:2.cnHint: 山洞石壁上布满了古老的____，贝尔大声朗读后，发现最后一列圈出了一个从未听说过的岛屿名称。
text:2.hook: Saying that island name aloud made the torch flame bend toward the east.
text:2.line: 'Read the *text* backwards — the island name only appears when you reverse the order.'

front:2.en: The message had been left in plain sight — pinned to the *front* of the troupe's door, on a square of bark, in handwriting none of us recognised. It said only: 'The next word is where the wind forgets to blow.' Silverfang crossed both arms and studied it for a long time.
front:2.cnHint: 一张写着神秘提示的树皮纸条被钉在了大门____，没有人认出那笔迹。
front:2.hook: Silverfang finally uncrossed their arms and pointed — not east, but straight down.
front:2.line: 'Whoever left this note at the *front* of our door knew exactly when we would arrive.'

law:2.en: The old stone sign read: BY *LAW* OF THE ISLAND COUNCIL, ALL WORDS FOUND HERE MUST BE LOGGED BEFORE SUNRISE. Old Helm read it twice, then pulled out his ink brush without a word. We logged every tile we carried, and the gate ahead of us swung open on its own.
law:2.cnHint: 石碑上刻着岛屿议会的____，要求所有找到的文字必须在日出前登记，老舵手照做后大门自动开启。
law:2.hook: Behind the open gate, a second sign pointed to a vault no map had ever shown.
law:2.line: 'The *law* here is simple: log your words honestly, and the island lets you pass.'

thinking:2.en: Old Helm spread the new map fragment across the worn table and fell quiet. I watched his eyes move slowly across the faded lines. 'Good *thinking* gets us farther than any wind,' he said at last. The word on the fragment glowed once, and a new island shimmered into view at the edge of the chart.
thinking:2.cnHint: 老船长仔细研究地图碎片，说正确的____比任何风都能带我们走得更远。
thinking:2.hook: The glowing island had no name — only a question mark.
thinking:2.line: 'Good *thinking* gets us farther than any wind.'

cover:2.en: Bell found the small box half-buried under a *cover* of dry leaves near the island's edge. Inside lay a folded map fragment, still crisp, as if someone had hidden it carefully long ago. Old Helm held it to the starlight and smiled. A new route unfolded before us like a slow, quiet breath.
cover:2.cnHint: 小铃在一层落叶的____下发现了藏有地图碎片的小盒子。
cover:2.hook: Whose careful hands had hidden it there, and why?
cover:2.line: 'There is something under this *cover* — come and look.'

earth:2.en: The island's centre was soft with dark *earth*, unlike the pale stone we had walked for days. Bell knelt and pressed her palm flat against it. 'Things grow here,' she said quietly. Old Helm added the word to our collection, and somewhere below us the roots of the next island began to appear on the map.
earth:2.cnHint: 小岛中央有一片深色的____，小铃感觉到这里有生命存在。
earth:2.hook: Whatever grew here had been waiting a very long time.
earth:2.line: 'This *earth* is soft — something is alive beneath us.'

paper:2.en: Tucked inside a cracked lantern near the dock, I found a roll of thin *paper* covered in careful handwriting. Each line named an island we had never heard of. Old Helm unrolled it slowly, his breath catching. 'This is older than our map,' he whispered, and Bell began to trace the new names with her finger.
paper:2.cnHint: 我在破旧灯笼里找到一卷写满岛屿名字的____，比我们的地图还古老。
paper:2.hook: One island name at the bottom had been crossed out twice.
paper:2.line: 'This *paper* is older than anything we carry — read it carefully.'

art:2.en: The cave wall was covered in painted figures — boats, stars, and creatures I could not name. 'This is *art* left by those who sailed before us,' Old Helm said softly, touching nothing. Bell found a small symbol in the corner that matched our next target word exactly. We copied it down and stepped back out into the open sky.
art:2.cnHint: 洞穴墙壁上布满壁画，老舵说这是前人留下的____，小铃从中找到了线索。
art:2.hook: The smallest figure in the painting seemed to be pointing outward.
art:2.line: 'This *art* was made by those who knew the sky better than we do.'

street:2.en: The abandoned island had one long *street* running from shore to shore, lined with empty lantern posts. At the far end, Bell spotted a stone pillar with a map fragment sealed inside a glass box at its top. Old Helm read the fragment aloud, and the lanterns along the street lit one by one, guiding us toward the next departure point.
street:2.cnHint: 废弃小岛上有一条长____，小铃在尽头的石柱上发现了封存的地图碎片。
street:2.hook: The last lantern lit up before Old Helm even finished reading.
street:2.line: 'Follow this *street* to its end — that is where the next clue waits.'

talent:2.en: Silverfang watched Bell decode the tangled symbols on the fragment in under a minute and crossed her arms slowly. 'That kind of *talent* is rare,' she said, and it sounded almost like a compliment. Bell looked up, surprised. Old Helm added the word quietly to our collection, and a distant island rose gently on the horizon.
talent:2.cnHint: 小铃飞速破解了地图符号，银牙罕见地称赞她拥有这样的____。
talent:2.hook: Silverfang turned away quickly, but I caught her small smile.
talent:2.line: 'That kind of *talent* does not come from practice alone.'

overall:2.en: We laid all the collected fragments on the deck and stepped back to see the *overall* shape they made together. It was not just a map — it was a message, each word a piece of one long sentence written across the sky. Old Helm traced the final line with one finger. 'Now we know where we are going,' he said, and we did.
overall:2.cnHint: 将所有碎片拼在一起后，我们终于看清了____的地图形状，那是一条横跨天空的信息。
overall:2.hook: The final destination had been hidden in plain sight all along.
overall:2.line: 'The *overall* shape tells us more than any single piece could.'

satisfaction:2.en: Old Helm unrolled the newest map fragment on the deck. Every island name we had found glowed faintly, like tiny lanterns. He pressed his thumb against the last blank space. 'Almost complete,' he said with quiet *satisfaction*, the kind that comes after a long and worthy journey. One gap remained.
satisfaction:2.cnHint: 老舵主展开地图，看着已填满的岛名，露出一种深深的____。
satisfaction:2.hook: But the final blank space had begun to move.
satisfaction:2.line: 'There is real *satisfaction* in knowing we found each piece ourselves.'

cultivate:2.en: Bell had claimed a small patch of soil near the ship's bow, pressing seeds into the dark earth each morning. 'You can *cultivate* more than plants,' she told me, smoothing the soil with one careful hand. 'Patience grows here too.' Around us, the floating island drifted softly through pale cloud.
cultivate:2.cnHint: 小铃在船头的土地上耕作，说这里____的不只是植物。
cultivate:2.hook: Then one seedling glowed a colour no plant should be.
cultivate:2.line: 'We *cultivate* good habits the same way — slowly, every single day.'

productive:2.en: Silverfang spread charts across his own deck and called the morning meeting to order. In two hours we had named four islands, traced two wind routes, and found a hidden current. 'Now that,' he said, folding the last chart with a sharp snap, 'was a *productive* morning.' Old Helm simply smiled.
productive:2.cnHint: 银牙船长宣布这个上午非常____，众人都颇为满意。
productive:2.hook: Old Helm's smile, however, held a private secret.
productive:2.line: 'A *productive* crew asks questions before they sail, not after.'

vision:2.en: High on the observation post, Bell handed me her small brass telescope. Through it the edge of the world curved away in a bright arc. 'Good *vision* is not only about seeing far,' she said softly. 'It is about knowing what matters when you look.' A new island shimmered at the rim.
vision:2.cnHint: 小铃借给我望远镜，说真正的____不只是看得远。
vision:2.hook: The shimmering island was not on any chart.
vision:2.line: 'My *vision* for this voyage stretches far beyond that last cloud.'

distance:2.en: The word-fragment we needed was written on a stone marker at the far end of Driftmoss Island. Old Helm studied it from where we stood. 'See the *distance* between us and that stone,' he said. 'Every step you take teaches you something the map cannot.' We started walking in single file.
distance:2.cnHint: 老舵主指着远处的石碑，说____本身也是一种教导。
distance:2.hook: Halfway there, the stone marker quietly turned around.
distance:2.line: 'Keep the right *distance* and you see the whole picture clearly.'

forward:2.en: The rope bridge swayed over a canyon of open sky. Silverfang tested the first plank with one boot, then looked back at us with calm eyes. 'The only safe direction here is *forward*,' he said. He stepped out, steady and unhurried, and the bridge held. One by one we followed him across.
forward:2.cnHint: 银牙船长踏上摇晃的绳桥，说此刻唯一安全的方向是____。
forward:2.hook: The bridge dissolved behind the last person to cross.
forward:2.line: 'Moving *forward* together is safer than standing still alone.'

harmful:2.en: We found the old signal fire built of strange violet wood. Bell knelt and sniffed it carefully. 'Do not light this,' she said, standing back up. 'The smoke would be *harmful* to the root-plants that feed the whole island.' We left it cold and searched instead for a safer way to send our signal.
harmful:2.cnHint: 小铃发现那堆木柴的烟对岛上植物____，阻止了大家点火。
harmful:2.hook: Something else on the island had already been burning.
harmful:2.line: 'Hiding the truth from the crew is just as *harmful* as a wrong turn.'

impossible:2.en: The final map fragment floated in mid-air above the island's centre, spinning slowly. Old Helm stared at it without blinking. 'Reaching it looks *impossible*,' I whispered. He shook his head, pulled a small folded word-token from his coat, and held it up. The fragment dropped gently into his waiting hand.
impossible:2.cnHint: 漂浮在空中的地图碎片看似____，老舵主却用一个字符将它取下。
impossible:2.hook: The word on the token was the same as our next destination.
impossible:2.line: 'Nothing is truly *impossible* if you carry the right word with you.'

meaning:2.en: Deep inside a hollow cloud-rock, I found a carved stone tablet. Strange symbols covered its face, but Old Helm traced each line with a careful finger. 'Every mark has a *meaning*,' he said softly. The symbols slowly formed a map — pointing toward an island none of us had ever seen.
meaning:2.cnHint: 老船长在石板上发现了隐藏的____，那些符号竟然拼出了一张新地图。
meaning:2.hook: The island on the map should not exist.
meaning:2.line: 'Every mark has a *meaning*, if you look long enough.'

strengthen:2.en: The rope bridge to the next island was fraying badly. Bell pulled out a spool of silver cord from her pack and began weaving it through the old fibres. 'This will *strengthen* it enough for all of us,' she said. One by one, we crossed — the bridge holding firm under each step.
strengthen:2.cnHint: 小铃用银色细绳____了破旧的绳桥，让大家得以安全通过。
strengthen:2.hook: But something heavy was already moving on the other side.
strengthen:2.line: 'Weave it tight — *strengthen* the old with the new.'

competitive:2.en: At the Sky Bazaar floating market, Bell spotted a rare wind-compass for sale. Silverfang appeared beside us, eyes bright. The bidding grew fast and *competitive*, each offer climbing higher than the last. In the end, Bell won — but Silverfang gave her a sharp smile, as if this were only the first round.
competitive:2.cnHint: 在天空集市上，一场____激烈的竞价让小铃和银牙之间的较量更加有趣。
competitive:2.hook: Silverfang's smile meant the real contest had just begun.
competitive:2.line: 'Keep your price ready — this crowd is *competitive*.'

recently:2.en: Old Helm unrolled a faded chart on the deck. He pointed to a cluster of small islands near the eastern edge. 'These passages have *recently* shifted,' he told us, tracing new pencil lines over the old ink. Something — wind, or will — was rearranging the world, and our old maps were already wrong.
recently:2.cnHint: 老船长发现地图上的航道____发生了变化，旧地图已经不再准确。
recently:2.hook: Whatever moved the islands might still be moving them now.
recently:2.line: 'The eastern routes have *recently* changed — trust nothing old.'

nation:2.en: We landed on an island covered in coloured banners. An elder explained that long ago, every floating island had been part of one great *nation* — sharing words, songs, and sky-roads. Then the winds scattered them. Our troupe grew quiet, each of us feeling the weight of something once whole, now spread wide across the clouds.
nation:2.cnHint: 岛上的老人讲述了曾经统一的浮岛____，如今却四散于云端。
nation:2.hook: Somewhere, one last sky-road might still connect them all.
nation:2.line: 'We were one *nation* once — before the great wind came.'

perceive:2.en: The fog on Lantern Isle was so thick I could barely see my own hand. But Bell stood still, eyes closed. 'I can *perceive* the lighthouse,' she said quietly, 'by the warmth it puts in the air.' She turned twenty degrees left, and walked straight to it — the beam cutting through the white at last.
perceive:2.cnHint: 在浓雾中，小铃凭借感知____到了灯塔的位置，带领大家找到了方向。
perceive:2.hook: The lighthouse keeper had been waiting for exactly our troupe.
perceive:2.line: 'Close your eyes — you will *perceive* more than you expect.'

pound:2.en: In the bazaar at Copper Step Island, Old Helm traded a heavy bag of goods. The merchant weighed each item on a brass scale, calling out each *pound* in a clear, proud voice. At the final count, Old Helm received a small bronze key — the kind, the merchant whispered, that opens sky-vaults.
pound:2.cnHint: 在集市上，商人用秤称出每件货物的____，老船长换来了一把神秘的铜钥匙。
pound:2.hook: No one on this island knew what the sky-vault held.
pound:2.line: 'Every *pound* of it weighed — nothing is given free here.'

purpose:2.en: I asked Old Helm why he kept collecting words instead of treasure. He looked at the horizon for a long moment. 'Every word we find has a *purpose*,' he said, 'like a key that was made for one specific lock.' He pressed the latest word-fragment into my palm, warm as sunlight, and pointed forward.
purpose:2.cnHint: 老船长告诉我，收集每一个词语都有其特定的____，就像专为某把锁打造的钥匙。
purpose:2.hook: Far ahead, a door stood alone in the open sky.
purpose:2.line: 'Each word has a *purpose* — find the lock it fits.'

respond:2.en: We found a stone door carved with a single question: 'Who seeks the edge of the map?' Old Helm pressed his hand against the cold surface and waited. Slowly, a low hum filled the air. The door had chosen to *respond* — and the whole island trembled as it swung open.
respond:2.cnHint: 石门上刻着一个问题，老舵手触碰它后，门竟然____了。
respond:2.hook: Beyond the door, something was already watching us.
respond:2.line: 'The door will *respond* only to someone with a true heart,' Old Helm said quietly.

welcome:2.en: A lantern swayed above a wooden arch at the island's edge. Beneath it, Bell found a sign so old the paint had nearly faded. She traced the letters with one finger and read them aloud: 'All seekers of words are *welcome* here.' The warmth of those words made the cold wind feel much kinder.
welcome:2.cnHint: 小铃在岛屿边缘发现了一块旧牌子，上面写着寻词者都____。
welcome:2.hook: But the lantern above had not been lit from outside.
welcome:2.line: Bell smiled and said, 'I think we are *welcome* to stay a little longer.'

appeal:2.en: The oldest resident of the island pressed a rolled-up note into my hands. It was an *appeal* — a careful, urgent plea written by a whole village asking someone to carry their last word-fragment to the map's edge before the island drifted too far. My hands would not stop trembling.
appeal:2.cnHint: 老居民交给我一封____，请求我把最后的词语碎片带到地图尽头。
appeal:2.hook: The island had already begun to drift away from the others.
appeal:2.line: Old Helm read it twice and said, 'This *appeal* deserves an answer.'

finally:2.en: We had crossed seven islands, solved riddles in the rain, and traded star-charts with strangers. Now, standing at the very edge of the last floating rock, Bell held up the assembled map and whispered a single word. The full path glowed gold. We had *finally* seen where all the fragments led.
finally:2.cnHint: 小铃将地图碎片拼合后，我们____看清了所有碎片通向的地方。
finally:2.hook: What glowed there was not a place — it was a door.
finally:2.line: 'We have *finally* made it to the edge,' Bell said, her voice full of wonder.

guess:2.en: The stone box had no lock, only a small slot carved with the outline of a single word. 'We have to *guess* which word fits,' said Old Helm, studying the shape. I looked at every fragment we had collected and held one up to the slot. It slid in perfectly, and the box opened with a sigh.
guess:2.cnHint: 石盒上没有锁，老舵手说我们必须____出哪个词语能打开它。
guess:2.hook: Inside was something none of us had expected to find.
guess:2.line: 'Can you *guess* which word the box is asking for?' Old Helm said.

protection:2.en: Beneath a cracked rock pillar we found a bundle of feathers woven into a circle. Bell explained that the island's people used to hang such circles above doorways. 'It is a *protection* charm,' she said, turning it gently in the starlight. We hung it at the entrance of our camp before the night wind rose.
protection:2.cnHint: 小铃发现了一个羽毛编成的圈，说那是一种____符咒。
protection:2.hook: That night, the wind howled — but nothing crossed our doorway.
protection:2.line: 'This charm has given *protection* to many travellers before us,' Bell said.

resident:2.en: An old woman was sitting alone on the highest rock, feeding crumbs to small cloud-birds. She was the only *resident* left on this drifting island. She had stayed behind to guard a word carved into the rock's heart. When we asked to see it, she simply nodded and led us up the narrow path.
resident:2.cnHint: 这座漂移岛上只剩下一位____，她独自守护着一个刻在岩心里的词语。
resident:2.hook: The word she guarded was not what any of us had guessed.
resident:2.line: Silverfang said softly, 'Every *resident* who stayed here left something behind.'

willing:2.en: Silverfang had the fastest ship, but she asked nothing in return at first. Later, at the edge of the last island, she told Old Helm she was *willing* to carry us further only if we shared the final word with her. Old Helm looked at me, then back at her, and slowly extended his hand.
willing:2.cnHint: 竞争船长告诉老舵手，只要我们分享最后的词语，她就____带我们继续前行。
willing:2.hook: Old Helm's pause before he shook her hand told me everything.
willing:2.line: 'I am *willing* to help, but only if we go forward together,' said Silverfang.

admit:2.en: At the edge of the map, Old Helm found a sealed stone door. No key, no handle. Bell pressed her ear to the cold surface and heard a faint hum. 'It wants something from us,' she said. Old Helm had to *admit* he had no idea what that something was.
admit:2.cnHint: 老舵主不得不____，他完全不知道石门想要什么。
admit:2.hook: The hum grew louder, and the door began to glow.
admit:2.line: 'I *admit* I have never seen a door like this one.'

association:2.en: Deep in the archive tower, Bell unrolled an old scroll. It showed a ring of islands linked by silver lines, with a name printed at the centre: the Star Wanderers *Association*. Our troupe had been following their maps for weeks without knowing it. We were walking in their footsteps the whole time.
association:2.cnHint: 贝尔发现地图中央标注着一个神秘____的名字。
association:2.hook: Someone had circled our current island in fresh red ink.
association:2.line: 'The *association* left these maps for someone to find — perhaps for us.'

brand:2.en: Old Helm lifted the lantern over the ancient crate. On its side, burned deep into the wood, was a *brand*: a star inside a circle. Bell had seen that same mark on the very first map fragment we ever collected. The crate had been waiting here for a long, long time.
brand:2.cnHint: 木箱上烙着一个____，与我们最初收集的地图碎片上的记号一模一样。
brand:2.hook: Inside the crate lay a map we had never seen before.
brand:2.line: 'That *brand* — I know it. I have seen it on the oldest fragment.'

deep:2.en: The path led us into a cave below the floating island's root. Moss glowed faintly on the walls. Bell held up her compass, but the needle only spun. We pressed *deep* into the silence, step by careful step, until the cave opened into a vast underground sky full of drifting lights.
deep:2.cnHint: 我们深入洞穴____处，发现了一片漂浮着光点的地下天空。
deep:2.hook: One of the lights drifted close and whispered a single word.
deep:2.line: 'We go *deep* enough, and the island shows us its true heart.'

discover:2.en: Bell was cleaning mud from an old sign when she stopped. 'Come look,' she called. We gathered round to *discover* a list of names carved beneath the dirt — every one of them a word we had already collected on our journey. Someone had known our path before we ever took a single step.
discover:2.cnHint: 贝尔清理泥土后，我们____了一份早已预知我们旅程的名单。
discover:2.hook: The last name on the list had not yet been collected.
discover:2.line: 'We *discover* something new, and the map grows one island larger.'

essential:2.en: Silverfang spread her charts across the bow table and tapped one island firmly. 'This stop is *essential*,' she said. 'Without the word fragment locked there, the northern route stays closed — and winter winds are coming.' Old Helm nodded. For once, rivals agreed. We changed course before the next bell rang.
essential:2.cnHint: 竞争船长强调，拿到那个词语碎片是____的，否则北方航线无法开启。
essential:2.hook: A distant storm confirmed she was right about the timing.
essential:2.line: 'Rest is fine, but this detour is *essential* — trust the charts.'

fine:2.en: After the stone door finally opened, we stepped into a bright round room. Everything inside was in perfect order: tidy shelves, a clean floor, a warm lamp still burning. 'Someone kept this place *fine* for years,' Old Helm said softly, running a hand along the dust-free shelf. We all felt it — we were not the first.
fine:2.cnHint: 老舵主感叹，这个房间多年来一直被保持得____。
fine:2.hook: A chair by the lamp was still slightly warm.
fine:2.line: 'The room is *fine*, too fine — someone was just here.'

largely:2.en: Bell spread the completed map across the floor at last. The journey to the island's edge had been *largely* guided by old star charts we barely trusted. Yet here we stood, exactly where the faded lines had promised. Old Helm laughed — a warm, tired sound. The stars, it turned out, had never lied to us.
largely:2.cnHint: 贝尔感慨，我们的旅程____依靠了几乎不敢相信的古老星图。
largely:2.hook: And the map still had one blank corner left to fill.
largely:2.line: 'Our path was *largely* written in stars before we took it.'

machine:2.en: At the edge of the last island, we found a rusted *machine* half-buried in blue moss. Its gears still turned, slowly, driven by starlight through a cracked glass lens. Old Helm wiped the dust from its face and read aloud the word pressed into its side. The map fragment glowed and a new island rose on the horizon.
machine:2.cnHint: 在最后一座岛的边缘，团长从一台古老的____上读出了新的词语碎片。
machine:2.hook: The gears began turning faster — as if something had been waiting.
machine:2.line: 'This *machine* has been counting the stars since before any of us were born,' Old Helm said softly.

observe:2.en: Bell called us to the bow before dawn. She pointed to a cluster of lights in the distance — a festival on a far island. 'We must *observe* their lantern-rising,' she said. 'It happens once a year and it is how they say thank you to the sky.' We watched in silence, and the silence felt full.
observe:2.cnHint: 小铃带大家在黎明前聚集，说必须____当地人的灯笼节，那是他们对星空致谢的方式。
observe:2.hook: As the last lantern rose, a word appeared written in light across the clouds.
observe:2.line: 'We *observe* this tradition every time we pass,' Bell said, her eyes bright.

fat:2.en: Silverfang traded three star-charts for a round jar of golden *fat* skimmed from cloud-honey bees. The island cook spread it on warm bread and handed a piece to each of us. It tasted like summer and altitude all at once. Old Helm laughed — the first real laugh I had heard from him in days.
fat:2.cnHint: 竞争船长用星图换来了一罐蜂蜜____，岛上的厨师把它抹在面包上招待大家。
fat:2.hook: The cook whispered that the bees only made it when a storm was three days away.
fat:2.line: 'A little cloud-honey *fat* on bread,' Silverfang said, 'and any journey feels shorter.'

helpful:2.en: I dropped my notebook between two islands and watched it fall into the fog below. Bell said nothing, only tossed a small rope anchor that caught the spine of the book mid-air. She pulled it back and handed it to me with a steady smile. Being *helpful*, I was learning, was simply what she did, as naturally as breathing.
helpful:2.cnHint: 我的笔记本掉落时，小铃不声不响地用绳锚救了它——这就是她____的方式，自然得像呼吸一样。
helpful:2.hook: On the cover, the fog had left behind a word I had never written there.
helpful:2.line: 'Being *helpful* costs nothing and usually opens a door somewhere,' Bell said with a shrug.

position:2.en: Old Helm unrolled the map on the deck and marked our *position* with a small ink stone. We were further along than I had thought — past the Amber Shelf and nearly level with the Great Drift. 'One more word,' he said quietly, 'and the map fills in the rest.' I leaned over and saw a blank space shaped like a door.
position:2.cnHint: 团长在地图上标出了我们的____，发现只需再找一个词语碎片，地图就会完整。
position:2.hook: The blank space shaped like a door had a tiny handle drawn at its edge.
position:2.line: 'Our *position* is better than it looks,' Old Helm said, pressing the ink stone down firmly.

threat:2.en: A cold wind crossed the deck and the sky turned a deep amber. Bell checked her instruments twice. 'That colour is a *threat*,' she said, 'the islands ahead will shake before morning.' We tied everything down and moved to the lower cabin. By midnight the shaking had passed, and on the wet deck lay a new word, carved into a loose plank.
threat:2.cnHint: 天空变成深琥珀色，小铃说这是一种____，预示着前方岛屿即将震动。
threat:2.hook: The word carved into the plank had not been there when we tied down for the night.
threat:2.line: 'That sky colour is a *threat* — do not let it go unread,' Bell said, tapping her dial.

trend:2.en: Silverfang spread out his old logbooks and traced a line with his finger. 'The *trend* is clear,' he said. 'Every third island we visit gives a word freely. The others make us earn it.' Old Helm studied the line and nodded slowly. I counted the marks and realised we were due for a free one — the next island glittered ahead like a gift.
trend:2.cnHint: 竞争船长从旧航海日志中发现了一个规律____：每隔两座岛，就有一座岛会主动给出词语碎片。
trend:2.hook: The glittering island was closer than the map said it should be.
trend:2.line: 'Study the *trend* long enough,' Silverfang said, tapping the log, 'and the map starts to teach you.'

ultimately:2.en: We argued for an hour about which path to take — the long way around the Storm Shelf or the short cut through the Pale Gap. Old Helm let us talk. Then he folded his hands and said, '*Ultimately*, the word we need is on the far side either way, so choose the path that teaches you something.' We chose the Gap. It did.
ultimately:2.cnHint: 大家争论了很久走哪条路，团长说____两条路都能到达目的地，不如选一条能让你有所收获的。
ultimately:2.hook: The Pale Gap was narrower than the charts showed — and full of quiet light.
ultimately:2.line: '*Ultimately*, the destination is the same,' Old Helm said. 'The path is the part that differs.'

australia:2.en: Bell spread the old map across the deck and pointed to a blank patch shaped like a sleeping animal. 'This island has no name yet,' she said. Old Helm smiled and pressed the word *australia* onto the patch. The blank space shimmered, and a warm golden coast rose slowly out of the clouds below us.
australia:2.cnHint: 小铃在地图上发现一片空白区域，老舵将一个____贴上去后，一片金色海岸从云层中升起。
australia:2.hook: But the coast kept rising, and something enormous moved beneath it.
australia:2.line: 'Old Helm, the word *australia* just filled the last blank on the southern half of the map!'

authority:2.en: The gate to the Crystal Shelf was locked, and a carved stone face above it demanded proof of passage. Old Helm stepped forward without hesitation. He held up our troupe seal and spoke in a calm, steady voice. The gate recognised his *authority* and ground open, letting starlight pour through the gap.
authority:2.cnHint: 通往水晶台地的大门紧闭，老舵凭借自己的____让石门缓缓开启。
authority:2.hook: Beyond the gate, a second door waited — and it had no keyhole at all.
authority:2.line: 'My *authority* as troupe leader should be enough to open this gate.'

confident:2.en: I had never read a sky-chart before, but Bell handed me hers and nodded. My hands were shaking. I traced the star path slowly, then called out the heading. Bell smiled. 'You sound *confident*,' she said, and I realised I actually was — the stars had answered me back, clear as a bell.
confident:2.cnHint: 小铃把星图交给我，我第一次独立辨认航向，竟发现自己出乎意料地____。
confident:2.hook: Then one star on the chart blinked, and the heading changed.
confident:2.line: 'You look *confident* up there — keep your eyes on the twin stars.'

crowd:2.en: We drifted into Lantern Reef just before the festival began. A *crowd* of islanders filled the stone square, each one holding a jar of captured starlight. Old Helm waded in, laughing, and traded our newest word for three warm jars. We lifted them high and the whole square blazed like a second sky.
crowd:2.cnHint: 我们抵达灯笼礁时，广场上____满了手持星光罐的岛民，老舵用新词换来了三个光罐。
crowd:2.hook: One jar in my hands buzzed softly, as though something inside it was still awake.
crowd:2.line: 'Bell, look at this *crowd* — I have never seen so many lanterns in one place!'

highly:2.en: Old Helm pulled a small sealed note from the message tree at Windpost Island. He read it twice, eyebrows rising. 'The Council speaks *highly* of our collection,' he said quietly, folding it back. Bell and I exchanged a grin. Then he turned the note over — there was a second message on the back, written in red ink.
highly:2.cnHint: 老舵在风柱岛的留言树上取到一封信，信中对我们的____评价极高，但背面还有一行红字。
highly:2.hook: The red ink was still wet.
highly:2.line: 'They speak *highly* of every troupe that reaches the Windpost — but few read the back.'

occur:2.en: We were crossing the Pale Drift when Bell suddenly grabbed my sleeve. 'Did it *occur* to you that we have been here before?' she whispered. I looked around — the same bent cloud, the same blue rock. Our map had looped. Old Helm was already tying a new word to the compass rose, and the drift slowly unwound around us.
occur:2.cnHint: 渡越苍白漂流带时，小铃突然意识到一件____过她的事：我们似乎已经绕回原路了。
occur:2.hook: The compass rose spun once more, and pointed somewhere the map did not show.
occur:2.line: 'Bell, did it *occur* to you that the drift moves when we stop reading the stars?'

regularly:2.en: On Echo Shelf, I found a hollow post carved with tiny marks. Bell explained that passing troupe members left words here *regularly*, each one feeding the island's memory. I pressed our newest word into the lowest empty slot. A low hum rose from the ground, and a hidden staircase unfolded toward the next island above.
regularly:2.cnHint: 在回响台地，过往船员____在空心柱上刻字，我刻下新词后，一段隐藏的阶梯向上展开。
regularly:2.hook: The staircase kept unfolding, past the clouds, past the stars, into total darkness.
regularly:2.line: 'Troupe members *regularly* leave a word here — it keeps the shelf from going quiet.'

responsible:2.en: A storm had torn a rope bridge linking two small islands. Old Helm looked at me. 'You tied the last knot,' he said, not unkindly. 'That makes you *responsible* for fixing it.' I felt the weight of it, picked up the rope, and worked until the bridge was stronger than before. He crossed first, testing every step, then gave a slow nod.
responsible:2.cnHint: 吊桥断裂，老舵告诉我，因为是我最后打的结，所以我需____修好它。
responsible:2.hook: Halfway across, Old Helm paused and looked down into the clouds below.
responsible:2.line: 'You tied the last knot, so you are *responsible* — and I think you already know that.'

digital:2.en: At the edge of the map, Bell pressed her palm against a stone pillar. Strange marks lit up beneath her fingers — not carved, but glowing, shifting, alive. 'These are *digital* signals,' she whispered, 'patterns made of light and number, not ink.' Old Helm leaned close, eyes wide with wonder.
digital:2.cnHint: 小铃在石柱上发现了发光的____信号，老舵长目瞪口呆。
digital:2.hook: The pillar hummed, and a hidden door began to open.
digital:2.line: 'These *digital* patterns — they are a message, not a decoration.'

sale:2.en: On a mossy ledge near the island's edge, a small wooden stall stood alone. Jars of glowing seeds, dried star-flowers, and tiny compass charms covered every shelf. A painted sign read: 'Final *sale* — last stop before the beyond.' Old Helm smiled and reached for his coin pouch.
sale:2.cnHint: 地图边缘有一个摊位正在____，老舵长掏出了钱袋。
sale:2.hook: The seller's eyes gleamed — she already knew what we needed.
sale:2.line: 'Everything on this shelf is on *sale*, but only until the stars shift.'

contact:2.en: Bell climbed the tallest crystal spire and held up a small mirror, flashing light in long and short bursts. She was trying to *contact* a distant island spotted earlier through the telescope. Minutes passed. Then, from far across the cloud-sea, a mirror flashed back — slow, steady, deliberate.
contact:2.cnHint: 小铃用镜子闪光，试图____远处岛屿上的人。
contact:2.hook: The reply spelled out two words we did not expect.
contact:2.line: 'We must *contact* them before the cloud-bridge dissolves.'

failure:2.en: Old Helm stared at the torn corner of the map, jaw tight. We had followed every clue, crossed three sky-currents, and still arrived at empty rock. 'This is not a *failure*,' he said quietly, picking up a feather left on the stone, 'it is the map asking us to look harder.'
failure:2.cnHint: 空手而归，但老舵长说这次的____另有深意。
failure:2.hook: The feather trembled, pointing back the way we had come.
failure:2.line: 'A *failure* to find the word only means the word found us first.'

bird:2.en: A copper-coloured *bird* landed on the ship's railing just as we crossed into uncharted sky. It carried a tiny rolled note tied to its leg with blue thread. Bell reached out carefully and the creature stood perfectly still, watching us with one bright, knowing eye.
bird:2.cnHint: 一只____停在船栏上，腿上绑着一张纸条。
bird:2.hook: The note bore no name — only a single strange symbol.
bird:2.line: 'That *bird* has crossed more sky than any of us ever have.'

official:2.en: A carved seal on the cavern wall bore a sun and three interlocked rings — the mark of an *official* of the old Sky Council, Bell said, brushing away dust. Below the seal was a locked iron box. Whoever placed it here had the authority to shape whole islands.
official:2.cnHint: 洞壁上的印章属于某位天空议会____，铁箱就藏在印章之下。
official:2.hook: Old Helm already had a key that matched the lock's shape.
official:2.line: 'Only an *official* of the Sky Council could leave a mark this deep in stone.'

confidence:2.en: Silverfang's ship pulled alongside ours at the misty rim of the known world. She stood at the bow with easy *confidence*, arms folded, grinning at us across the gap. 'Scared of the edge?' she called. Old Helm straightened up, refusing to let her see any doubt in him.
confidence:2.cnHint: 竞争船长满怀____站在船头，向我们发出挑战。
confidence:2.hook: Beyond her ship, the mist parted to reveal something enormous.
confidence:2.line: 'You need *confidence* to sail past the edge — do you have it?'

display:2.en: Inside the hollow island, walls of pale crystal began to *display* moving images — old voyages, lost routes, skies we had never seen. Bell pressed her notebook to her chest and spun slowly, trying to take it all in. The images flickered like memories the island had kept for centuries.
display:2.cnHint: 空心岛的水晶墙壁开始____古老的航行影像，小铃惊叹不已。
display:2.hook: One image showed our own ship — arriving here long before we were born.
display:2.line: 'The walls *display* the past, but I think they are warning us too.'

experiment:2.en: Deep inside a hollow island, we found a stone table covered in symbols. Old Helm traced each one carefully. 'Someone ran an *experiment* here,' he said, 'testing whether wind and light could grow seeds without soil.' Small glass jars still held tiny green shoots, reaching upward in the dark.
experiment:2.cnHint: 在一座空心岛的深处，团长发现有人曾在此进行____，玻璃罐里的嫩芽至今仍在生长。
experiment:2.hook: One jar had already cracked open from the inside.
experiment:2.line: 'This *experiment* is still running — someone meant to come back.'

nature:2.en: Bell led us onto a wide, flat island where no buildings stood. Soft moss covered everything, and strange birds with silver wings landed near our feet without fear. 'This is the *nature* of this place,' Bell said quietly, 'it has never been touched by any troupe before us.' We all held our breath.
nature:2.cnHint: 贝尔带我们走上一座无人踏足的岛，感受这片土地最原始的____。
nature:2.hook: Then something large moved beneath the moss.
nature:2.line: 'The *nature* of this island is to stay wild — we should be careful.'

status:2.en: At the edge of a bridge between two islands, a stone board listed every troupe that had ever passed. Old Helm found our name near the bottom. 'Low *status*,' Silverfang said with a grin, 'for now.' Old Helm just smiled and pointed at all the blank space still left above the top name.
status:2.cnHint: 在一块记录各路船队____的石碑前，竞争船长看到了自己的位置。
status:2.hook: The top name had been scratched out by someone in a hurry.
status:2.line: 'Our *status* on that board will look very different by the end.'

accident:2.en: I knocked a small brass compass off the shelf by *accident*, and it shattered on the floor. Inside, where the needle should have been, there was a folded piece of cloth. Bell unfolded it slowly. It was a map of an island none of us had ever seen, with a single red mark at its centre.
accident:2.cnHint: 我不小心打碎了一个黄铜罗盘，没想到这个____让我们发现了一张神秘地图。
accident:2.hook: The red mark was still slightly warm to the touch.
accident:2.line: 'That *accident* might be the luckiest thing that ever happened to us.'

active:2.en: The island shook every few minutes. Old Helm checked a small notebook and nodded. 'The heat vents below are still *active*,' he said, 'they push warm air up through the rock and keep the whole island floating.' We felt the gentle vibration in our boots and understood, for the first time, how alive the sky truly was.
active:2.cnHint: 老舵长告诉我们，岛下方的热气孔仍然____，这正是岛屿漂浮的秘密。
active:2.hook: The next tremor lasted twice as long as the last.
active:2.line: 'Stay alert — those vents are *active* and the ground can shift fast.'

feed:2.en: At the far rim of the island, Bell found a wide stone bowl filled with seeds. Every morning, she told us, the wind currents carried small sky-birds here to eat. She began to *feed* them by hand, one by one, and each bird left behind a single bright feather that glowed faintly in the dark.
feed:2.cnHint: 贝尔在岛边发现了一个石碗，她开始____前来觅食的空中小鸟，每只鸟都留下了一片发光的羽毛。
feed:2.hook: The last feather spelled out a word none of us could read.
feed:2.line: 'If you *feed* them gently, they trust you — and trust opens every door.'

principle:2.en: Old Helm spread three maps on the ground and stared at them for a long time. 'There is one *principle* behind all of them,' he said at last. 'Every path curves toward the brightest star, never away.' Bell marked the pattern in red ink, and suddenly the blank spaces on each map began to make perfect sense.
principle:2.cnHint: 老舵长研究三张地图后，发现了隐藏其中的同一条____，指引着每一条路的走向。
principle:2.hook: But the brightest star had shifted slightly since last night.
principle:2.line: 'Hold to this *principle* and the map will never truly let you down.'

article:2.en: Inside a sealed tin box, we found a single folded page — an *article* written by a traveller who had reached the very edge of the known sky. The words were faded, but one line was clear: 'Beyond the last island, the stars are close enough to touch.' Old Helm folded it and put it in his coat.
article:2.cnHint: 我们在密封的铁盒里发现了一篇旅行者写下的____，记录了他抵达已知天空尽头时的所见。
article:2.hook: The date on the page was only three weeks ago.
article:2.line: 'This *article* is proof — someone reached that place and came back alive.'
