mood:2.en: A soft rain had settled over the deck, and with it came a strange *mood* — quiet, a little heavy, as if the sky itself was thinking. Old Helm set down his tea and looked out at the grey horizon. Then he smiled and pointed. Far off, catching the last light, a new island had surfaced right where the map said it would. The heavy feeling lifted all at once.
mood:2.cnHint: 甲板上笼罩着一种奇异的____，就连老舵手也沉默下来，直到他发现地图上预言的新岛屿出现了。
mood:2.hook: The island was shaped exactly like the word Old Helm had been holding all week.
mood:2.line: 'The sky has a *mood* today — and I think it is trying to show us something.'

motivation:2.en: Silverfang had raced us to the Isle of First Light before, and I asked Bell why he kept chasing the same map we did. She thought for a moment. 'His *motivation* is not the words,' she said. 'It is the proof that they exist.' That answer surprised me. It also made me look at the next fragment in my hand with much gentler eyes.
motivation:2.cnHint: 小铃解释说，银牙追逐地图的____并不是为了那些词本身，而是为了证明它们真实存在。
motivation:2.hook: Silverfang's ship was already a bright speck on the horizon ahead.
motivation:2.line: 'His *motivation* matters — understanding it might be the only way we reach the next island first.'

worldwide:2.en: Old Helm unrolled the oldest chart in his pack. It showed not one island or one sea, but a *worldwide* web of floating lands, each dot connected by lines of light. 'This map was drawn by every troupe that ever sailed,' he said softly. I traced one line with my finger and felt the whole sky hum.
worldwide:2.cnHint: 老舵手展开一张古老地图，上面记录着____范围内所有浮岛的位置，我轻轻触碰，感受到整片天空的震动。
worldwide:2.hook: One line on the map still had no end.
worldwide:2.line: 'This *worldwide* map belongs to every troupe that ever sailed these skies.'

accomplish:2.en: The sealed door had beaten every troupe before us. Bell studied the carvings for an hour, then smiled and pressed three stones in order. The lock clicked open. 'We *accomplished* what no one else could,' she said, stepping through into a room full of soft golden light. I could barely breathe.
accomplish:2.cnHint: 贝尔研究门上的刻纹后，终于打开了这扇难倒所有人的门，她说我们____了别人未能做到的事。
accomplish:2.hook: Beyond the door, something was still moving in the dark.
accomplish:2.line: 'We *accomplished* what every troupe before us could not.'

address:2.en: Tucked inside a hollow stone was a small folded note. Bell read it aloud: it was an *address* — not a street, but a set of star angles and wind counts that pointed to an island no chart had named. Old Helm copied it into his log with steady hands. I felt a door opening in my chest.
address:2.cnHint: 一块空心石里藏着一张字条，上面写着一个____——用星角和风速指向一座无名浮岛。
address:2.hook: The star angles on the note matched tonight's sky exactly.
address:2.line: 'This *address* will lead us somewhere no map has ever shown.'

barely:2.en: The bridge between the two islands was a single rope, worn thin by years of wind. I crossed it one careful step at a time, arms out wide. I *barely* made it to the far side before the last thread snapped behind me. Silverfang caught my arm. The new island smelled of pine and rain.
barely:2.cnHint: 我小心翼翼地踩过一根细绳索，____勉强抵达对岸，身后绳索随即断裂。
barely:2.hook: Silverfang looked back at the broken rope and said nothing.
barely:2.line: 'You *barely* made it — next time, let me cross first.'

blame:2.en: The word-fragment we needed was gone — the pedestal empty, the dust disturbed. Silverfang crossed his arms. 'Don't look at me,' he said. Old Helm raised a hand: 'No *blame* yet. Something took it recently. That means it is close.' He pointed to a trail of faint sparks drifting toward the east cliff.
blame:2.cnHint: 碎片不翼而飞，老舵手阻止大家互相____，指出有人刚刚带走了它，线索还在。
blame:2.hook: The sparks were moving faster now, toward the cliff edge.
blame:2.line: 'There is no *blame* here — only a trail we need to follow.'

chat:2.en: While Bell fixed the compass, Silverfang and I sat on the edge of the island and let our feet hang over the stars below. We began to *chat* — quietly at first, then laughing about wrong turns and strange skies. By the time Bell called us back, I felt less like a new member and more like someone who belonged.
chat:2.cnHint: 贝尔修理罗盘时，我和银牙坐在岛边____，笑谈一路上的弯路与奇景，我渐渐有了归属感。
chat:2.hook: Bell's voice cut through our laughter with sudden urgency.
chat:2.line: 'Let's *chat* while we wait — there is time, and I want to know your story.'

combat:2.en: The wind-beast was only fog and sound, but it pressed hard against our little ship. Old Helm took the wheel and set the sails at a sharp angle. He said the best *combat* against a storm is not force — it is a smarter path. The beast thinned, the stars returned, and ahead shone a light we had not seen before.
combat:2.cnHint: 面对呼啸的风兽，老舵主说对抗它最好的____不是蛮力，而是更聪明的航线。
combat:2.hook: The new light ahead was blinking in a pattern.
combat:2.line: 'The only *combat* worth winning out here is fought with a clever course.'

danger:2.en: Bell held up her hand and we all stopped. A soft crack ran across the stone path ahead — the island's edge was breaking away. 'Real *danger*,' she said quietly, not in fear but in respect, the way you speak to something large. We backed up, found another route, and arrived at the far tower just as the sun touched the horizon.
danger:2.cnHint: 贝尔发现石路前方出现裂缝，轻声说出____，我们随即退后另寻路线，有惊无险地抵达远塔。
danger:2.hook: The far tower door was already open, waiting for someone.
danger:2.line: 'This kind of *danger* asks for patience, not speed — step back.'

partly:2.en: The old chest we found on Driftmoss Island was *partly* buried under pale roots, as if the island itself had been slowly swallowing it for years. Bell brushed the soil away with careful hands. Inside lay a folded page, and on it, one glowing word — our next destination, waiting all along.
partly:2.cnHint: 贝尔在浮岛上发现了一只____被埋住的旧箱子，里面藏着一张发光的地图碎片。
partly:2.hook: The word on the page pulsed once, then pointed due north.
partly:2.line: 'This box is *partly* open — something inside is still breathing.'

practical:2.en: Old Helm spread the recovered fragments across the deck and frowned. Most maps showed pretty pictures of clouds and dragons. 'A *practical* map,' he said firmly, 'tells you wind speed, landing depth, and where the roots are weak.' He kept only three fragments and let the rest sail away on the breeze.
practical:2.cnHint: 老舵手挑选地图碎片时，只留下____的那几张，其余全部放走。
practical:2.hook: The three chosen fragments clicked together like old friends.
practical:2.line: 'We keep only what is *practical* — beauty without use is just weight.'

profit:2.en: Silverfang once told me she had sailed these skies purely for *profit* — rare stones, glowing seeds, bottled starlight. But on the morning we found the word carved into the bark of a sky-cedar, she stood very still and said nothing about prices at all.
profit:2.cnHint: 竞争船长过去航行是为了____，但那天早晨她在天杉树前沉默了。
profit:2.hook: She reached out and touched the carving as if it were an old name.
profit:2.line: 'I used to count every find as *profit*, but this one feels different.'

promise:2.en: The word was sealed inside a hollow stone, wrapped in a leaf with writing on it: 'To whoever finds this — keep going.' Old Helm read it aloud twice. He called it a *promise* left by some earlier traveller, proof that this sky-road had been walked before and was worth walking still.
promise:2.cnHint: 老舵手在中空石头里发现了一片叶子，他说那是前人留下的一个____。
promise:2.hook: Somewhere ahead, that earlier traveller might have left another.
promise:2.line: 'This note is a *promise* that the road ahead is real.'

rarely:2.en: Bell said she *rarely* felt nervous reading a navigation word for the first time, but her voice was a half-step higher than usual as she lifted the glowing shard from the pool of still water. The word lit her face blue. She smiled anyway, and read it clearly into the night air.
rarely:2.cnHint: 贝尔____会紧张，但这次从水池中取出发光碎片时，她的声音有些不一样。
rarely:2.hook: The word she read sent every compass needle spinning at once.
rarely:2.line: 'I *rarely* shake like this — this word must be something special.'

severe:2.en: The storm over Ashveil Island had been *severe* enough to crack three of the lower deck boards, and it had driven our target word deep into a sea-cave behind the falls. We climbed in anyway, dripping and laughing, and Bell held the word up like a small torch in the dark.
severe:2.cnHint: 阿什维尔岛的风暴十分____，但大家还是爬进海洞找到了那个词。
severe:2.hook: The word glowed brighter the deeper into the cave we went.
severe:2.line: 'The damage is *severe*, but we got what we came for.'

smell:2.en: The word was hidden inside a bunch of dried silver-herbs hanging from the roof of an abandoned sky-cottage. I knew we were close because of the *smell* — sweet and a little sharp, like starlight pressed into a flower. Old Helm said only the right island grows herbs that glow and scent at the same time.
smell:2.cnHint: 我们靠着一种特殊的____找到了藏在废弃小屋里的词语碎片。
smell:2.hook: Old Helm said only two islands in all the sky could grow those herbs.
smell:2.line: 'Follow the *smell* — if it sharpens, the word is very near.'

socialize:2.en: Every time the troupe arrives at a sky-market island, Bell is the first off the ship. She will *socialize* with anyone — traders, cloud-fishers, children with star-nets — and somehow, within an hour, she always learns exactly which vendor is hiding a map fragment under their counter.
socialize:2.cnHint: 贝尔每次靠港都会主动____，然后总能打听到藏着地图碎片的摊主。
socialize:2.hook: This time she came back grinning, holding something that glowed gold.
socialize:2.line: 'You have to *socialize* — the best maps are never on display.'

dinner:2.en: At the edge of the map, we found a long stone table set among the clouds. Old Helm lit the lanterns without a word. 'Every journey deserves a proper *dinner*,' he said, placing the last word-fragment at the centre like a dish. The stars leaned in, as if hungry too.
dinner:2.cnHint: 在地图的尽头，老舵主摆好石桌，为大家举办了一场____。
dinner:2.hook: But the table had been set for one more person than we were.
dinner:2.line: 'Every journey deserves a proper *dinner*, even at the edge of the map.'

embrace:2.en: The fog at the map's edge was thick and cold. I almost turned back. Then Bell reached out and gave my shoulder a quick, firm *embrace*. 'The fog is part of the path,' she said. I stepped forward, and the clouds parted to reveal a whole new island glowing below.
embrace:2.cnHint: 贝尔给了叙述者一个____，鼓励他迈出踏入迷雾的那一步。
embrace:2.hook: The new island below was shaped exactly like the word in my hand.
embrace:2.line: 'The fog is cold, but let it *embrace* you — it means you are close.'

explanation:2.en: Old Helm handed me a glass bottle sealed with wax. Inside was a single folded note. I opened it carefully. The only thing written on it was a new word and a map marking — no *explanation* at all. Bell laughed. 'He never explains. The road does that for him.'
explanation:2.cnHint: 瓶中纸条只有一个词和一处标记，完全没有____，贝尔却觉得这很正常。
explanation:2.hook: The map marking pointed somewhere none of us had ever dared to sail.
explanation:2.line: 'There is no *explanation* — the island will answer your questions itself.'

intend:2.en: I spread the old word-fragments on the deck and tried to match their edges. Silverfang watched with crossed arms. 'What do you *intend* to find out there?' she asked. I told her: the place where the map ends and something new begins. She uncrossed her arms. 'Fair enough,' she said.
intend:2.cnHint: 银牙问叙述者____做什么，得到答案后她的态度改变了。
intend:2.hook: She then pulled out a fragment none of us had ever seen before.
intend:2.line: 'Tell me what you *intend* to do, and I will tell you if the wind agrees.'

leadership:2.en: When the clouds closed in and our compass spun without purpose, the troupe looked at Old Helm. He said nothing for a long moment. Then, quietly, he turned the ship three degrees left. That calm, unhurried *leadership* was worth more than any shouted order. The clouds opened like a door.
leadership:2.cnHint: 在迷失方向的时候，老舵主平静的____让船找到了出路。
leadership:2.hook: Through the gap in the clouds, we saw lights that no map had ever named.
leadership:2.line: 'Good *leadership* is mostly listening — to the wind, and to the crew.'

locate:2.en: The newest word-fragment glowed faintly in my palm: a gold shape like a leaf. Bell leaned over the navigation table and traced three routes before she could *locate* the matching island. It sat just beyond a ring of slow spinning clouds, patient as if it had always been waiting for us.
locate:2.cnHint: 贝尔在航海图上努力____与碎片形状匹配的那座岛屿。
locate:2.hook: The island had no name on any chart, only a small hand-drawn star.
locate:2.line: 'Give me an hour and I will *locate* it — no island hides from a good navigator.'

original:2.en: Bell unrolled a very old chart, its edges brown and soft. 'This is the *original* map,' she said, 'before anyone added the new islands.' I compared it with our current one. Half the places we had already visited were not on it. We had gone further than anyone before us.
original:2.cnHint: 贝尔展示了____地图，叙述者发现他们已经走到了前人从未到达之处。
original:2.hook: One blank space on the original map matched perfectly with the word in my hand.
original:2.line: 'The *original* map ends here — what comes next is ours to draw.'

overcome:2.en: The final gap in the map was a wide stretch of sky with no island, no star, and no wind. The ship drifted. Old Helm sat still with his eyes closed for a long minute. Then he smiled. 'Every map has one blank place to *overcome*,' he said, and set the sails toward the dark.
overcome:2.cnHint: 面对地图上最后的空白，老舵主鼓励大家____眼前这片无路可走的虚空。
overcome:2.hook: A faint light blinked once, far ahead, exactly where the map showed nothing.
overcome:2.line: 'We will *overcome* this empty sky the same way we overcame all the others — together.'

threaten:2.en: The edge of the map island crumbled beneath our feet. Dark clouds began to *threaten* the sky above the stone bridge, and Old Helm pulled us back with one firm hand. 'Not yet,' he said quietly. Bell held up a glowing word-fragment, and the clouds slowly parted, revealing a pale silver path ahead.
threaten:2.cnHint: 乌云____着通往石桥的天空，老舵手把大家拉了回来。
threaten:2.hook: The silver path led somewhere no map had ever shown.
threaten:2.line: 'Those clouds *threaten* the crossing — we wait for Bell's word.'

throw:2.en: Bell found the sealed jar buried under a pile of old star-charts. Inside was a rolled note and a single word-fragment. 'Opening it is a *throw*,' Old Helm admitted, turning the jar slowly in his rough hands. 'But every island we have ever found began with someone being brave enough to try.' I cracked the seal.
throw:2.cnHint: 打开那只神秘罐子是一次____，但老舵手说每座岛都需要勇气。
throw:2.hook: The note inside named a place none of us had ever heard.
throw:2.line: 'Opening this jar is a *throw*, but I say we do it.'

unlike:2.en: Silverfang's ship carried a large iron chest that was *unlike* anything in our troupe's small wagon — its lid was covered in tiny carved words, each one a place already visited. Old Helm traced them with one finger, smiling. 'Every mark is a door we opened,' he said. Bell pressed a new word-fragment into the last empty space, and the chest hummed softly.
unlike:2.cnHint: 银牙的铁箱____我们的旅行车，盖子上刻满了已探索过的地名。
unlike:2.hook: The hum grew louder as the chest pointed toward the north.
unlike:2.line: 'This chest is *unlike* any I have seen — it remembers every word.'

vast:2.en: We landed on an island with no buildings, only an open field of pale blue grass stretching in every direction. The silence was *vast*, pressing gently against my ears like soft cloth. Old Helm knelt and pressed his palm to the ground. Somewhere beneath us, a word-fragment glowed faintly, and the grass bent toward it like a quiet invitation.
vast:2.cnHint: 那座岛上一片____的寂静，老舵手跪地感受到了埋藏其中的词语碎片。
vast:2.hook: The ground itself seemed to be waiting for us to listen.
vast:2.line: 'The silence here is *vast* — the island is trying to speak.'

absolutely:2.en: Bell laid three word-fragments on the table and studied them for a long time. 'I am *absolutely* certain these fit together,' she said at last, pressing them edge to edge. The pieces locked with a soft click, and a new shape appeared — a small island drawn in faint gold light, floating just beyond the edge of our current chart. Old Helm laughed with quiet delight.
absolutely:2.cnHint: 贝尔____确定三块词语碎片能拼在一起，果然拼出了一座新岛屿的轮廓。
absolutely:2.hook: The gold island on the chart had no name — yet.
absolutely:2.line: 'I am *absolutely* certain — press them together and you will see.'

accumulate:2.en: Our map-chest had grown heavy. Over many journeys, word-fragments begin to *accumulate* in ways you do not notice until you try to lift the lid. Silverfang counted them aloud while Bell wrote each one down. Old Helm watched from his chair and smiled at me. 'That weight,' he said, 'is everywhere we have ever been brave enough to go.'
accumulate:2.cnHint: 旅行途中，词语碎片悄悄地____在地图箱里，直到沉得难以抬盖。
accumulate:2.hook: Bell's list ended with a name no one had spoken aloud before.
accumulate:2.line: 'Words *accumulate* faster than you think — count them with me.'

breakfast:2.en: We had planned to leave at first light, but Old Helm insisted we *breakfast* together on the warm deck first. He set out bread and dried fruit while the stars above us slowly faded. Bell found a word-fragment hidden inside the bread basket, wrapped in a dry leaf. 'Someone left it here for us,' she said softly, holding it up to the last of the starlight.
breakfast:2.cnHint: 出发前大家在甲板上____，贝尔在面包篮里发现了一块被藏起来的词语碎片。
breakfast:2.hook: The leaf it was wrapped in showed a tiny map drawn in ink.
breakfast:2.line: 'We *breakfast* first — the stars will still be there when we are ready.'

capacity:2.en: Silverfang's old ship had a hidden lower deck we had never entered. 'Its *capacity* surprised even me,' he admitted, pushing open the narrow door. Inside, row after row of shelves held sealed jars, each one glowing faintly with a stored word-fragment. Old Helm looked at Bell, then at me. 'Well,' he said warmly, 'it seems our map just grew a great deal larger.'
capacity:2.cnHint: 银牙船的隐藏底舱____惊人，里面藏着一排排盛有词语碎片的罐子。
capacity:2.hook: One jar near the back glowed brighter than all the others.
capacity:2.line: 'The *capacity* of this deck is larger than the whole ship above — come and see.'

disaster:2.en: Tucked inside a cracked lantern near the island's edge, I found a folded note. Old Helm read it aloud: the troupe before ours had tried to cross the Voidrift without a full word-map. The result was a *disaster* — their ship came apart between islands, and only one member reached the other side. Old Helm folded the note carefully and said nothing for a while.
disaster:2.cnHint: 一张旧便条记录了上一支队伍的____，老舵读完后陷入了沉默。
disaster:2.hook: He tucked the note into his coat, and I wondered if he recognized the handwriting.
disaster:2.line: 'That crossing was a *disaster* — we will not repeat their mistake.'

emergency:2.en: A sharp whistle cut through the night air. Bell had found a signal stone near the cliff — the kind the island-keepers used only in an *emergency*. Its surface was still warm. Whoever had pressed it had done so recently, then vanished. Silverfang scanned the dark sky above us, her eyes sharp and steady, while I tried to slow my breathing.
emergency:2.cnHint: 小铃发现了一块信号石——只有____时才会使用——而它的表面还是温热的。
emergency:2.hook: Somewhere below the cliff edge, a rope was still swinging.
emergency:2.line: 'A signal stone means *emergency* — someone needed help and we missed them.'

familiar:2.en: Deep in the archive tower, I pulled a dusty roll of charts from the shelf. The coastlines looked *familiar* — too familiar. I had seen this island before, drawn in the margin of Old Helm's own notebook. He had never mentioned it. Bell appeared beside me and quietly took the chart from my hands, her expression careful and unreadable.
familiar:2.cnHint: 我在档案塔里发现了一张____的海图，上面的海岸线出现在老舵从未提起的笔记本里。
familiar:2.hook: Bell rolled the chart back up and slipped it under her coat without a word.
familiar:2.line: 'This coastline looks *familiar* — I think Old Helm has been here before.'

furthermore:2.en: The stone tablet near the island's northern tip held a message carved in neat lines. It listed the rules for reading word-fragments: keep them dry, keep them together, never read one by starlight alone. *Furthermore*, the last line warned, a fragment read in silence always points toward what the reader fears most. I read that line twice and stepped back from the tablet.
furthermore:2.cnHint: 石碑列出了碎片的使用规则，____，最后一条警告说，独自默读碎片会指向读者最恐惧的东西。
furthermore:2.hook: I was very glad I had read it aloud.
furthermore:2.line: 'The map works by day — *furthermore*, reading alone at night brings its own risk.'

hardly:2.en: We found the signal fire on a narrow ledge below the main island. It had *hardly* been burning an hour — the ash was still warm and the smoke still thin. Someone had lit it and left in a hurry. A single word-fragment lay beside the cold ring of stones, as if it had been left on purpose, a small gift or a quiet warning from whoever had stood here before us.
hardly:2.cnHint: 信号火几乎____燃烧了一小时就熄灭了，旁边留下了一块碎片，像是有人故意留下的。
hardly:2.hook: The fragment spelled a word none of us had collected yet.
hardly:2.line: 'The fire had *hardly* cooled — whoever lit it left only moments ago.'

hinder:2.en: The narrow bridge between the two cliff faces was wrapped in thick silver vines that had grown across the path. Bell tested the first step and frowned. 'These will *hinder* us badly if we try to rush,' she said. So we worked slowly, pulling each vine aside with care, until a passage opened — just wide enough to walk through single file under the watching stars.
hinder:2.cnHint: 银色藤蔓缠住了桥面，小铃说这会____队伍前进，所以大家慢慢地清理出了一条路。
hinder:2.hook: The last vine pulled free with a sound like a whispered name.
hinder:2.line: 'These vines will *hinder* us — move slowly and pull each one clear.'

injury:2.en: Old Helm was waiting at the far end of the rope bridge, holding up a small lantern. As I crossed, the middle plank cracked under my foot and I grabbed the side rope hard, scraping my palm. He took my hand and checked it carefully. 'A small *injury*,' he said, with quiet relief, 'but enough to remind us — every bridge deserves attention, no matter how short.' He handed me a strip of clean cloth.
injury:2.cnHint: 我在绳桥上踩断了木板，手掌划破，老舵检查了我的____后叮嘱我要注意每一座桥。
injury:2.hook: He pointed ahead, where the next island was already catching the first pale light of dawn.
injury:2.line: 'A small *injury* like this is the island's way of asking you to pay attention.'

register:2.en: Deep in the Cartographers' Hall, every island ever found is carved onto a stone wall. Old Helm runs his finger along the carvings until he finds a blank patch. 'Here,' he says quietly. He picks up a bone stylus and *registers* our new island, pressing its name into the cold stone for the first time.
register:2.cnHint: 在制图师大厅，老掌舵将新岛屿____在石壁上。
register:2.hook: But the stylus snaps — and the wall begins to shake.
register:2.line: 'We must *register* every island we find, or the map stays blind.'

skin:2.en: The amber lantern of the Warmstone Shelf glows orange across the whole camp. I hold my hand up and watch the light play on my *skin*, warm as a summer afternoon. Bell laughs softly beside me. 'This island likes us,' she says. For one quiet moment, all our tiredness melts away.
skin:2.cnHint: 在暖石台地的琥珀灯光下，叙述者感受到光映照在____上的温暖。
skin:2.hook: Then the light flickers — something large passes overhead.
skin:2.line: 'The island's glow feels kind against my *skin*.'

spirit:2.en: On the Isle of Echoes, voices of old travellers drift through the mist like smoke. Old Helm stands still, eyes shut, listening. 'Each voice is a *spirit* that refused to leave,' he whispers. I strain to hear my own name among them. One soft voice calls back, patient as the stars above.
spirit:2.cnHint: 在回声岛，老掌舵说每个声音都是不愿离去的____。
spirit:2.hook: One voice whispers a warning no living traveller has heard before.
spirit:2.line: 'A strong *spirit* is the only map that never tears, friend.'

spread:2.en: Bell unrolls the great cloth map across the stone table, and the *spread* of islands stretches wider than I ever imagined — dozens of shapes like scattered seeds. She taps a blank corner with two fingers. 'That whole edge is uncharted,' she says. The empty space feels less like a gap and more like an invitation.
spread:2.cnHint: 贝尔展开地图，岛屿的____远比叙述者想象的更广阔。
spread:2.hook: The blank corner suddenly glows faint gold, all on its own.
spread:2.line: 'Look at the *spread* — we have barely touched the edge of it.'

totally:2.en: The Fog Basin is *totally* unlike any place we have crossed before. There is no wind, no sound, not even the creak of the ropes. Old Helm slows the vessel to a drift and peers into the white silence. A single wooden sign floats past, reading only: YOU ARE EXPECTED. None of us speak.
totally:2.cnHint: 雾盆地与任何已知地点____不同，一块木牌从水中漂过。
totally:2.hook: A second sign floats past — this one has our names on it.
totally:2.line: 'I am *totally* certain something here already knows we came.'

tree:2.en: At the heart of Rootspire Island stands one enormous *tree*, its trunk wider than our whole vessel. Old Helm presses his ear against the bark and listens for a long moment. 'It is humming,' he reports, eyebrows raised. Carved into the roots, half hidden by moss, is a map of islands none of us have ever seen.
tree:2.cnHint: 在根尖岛中心，一棵巨大的____树根上藏着从未见过的地图。
tree:2.hook: The humming grows louder the moment I reach out to touch it.
tree:2.line: 'This *tree* has been keeping secrets longer than our troupe has existed.'

weigh:2.en: Silverfang sets three sealed jars on the rail, each one holding a different fog sample from today's crossing. She pulls out a small brass scale and begins to *weigh* each jar with slow, careful hands. 'Heavier fog means older sky,' she says simply. Old Helm watches, arms crossed, plainly impressed despite himself.
weigh:2.cnHint: 银牙船长用小型天平____三个雾气样本，判断天空的年龄。
weigh:2.hook: The third jar is heavier than it should be — far heavier.
weigh:2.line: 'I always *weigh* the fog before I trust a new route, Old Helm.'

alive:2.en: The word we collected today glows faintly in my palm, pulsing like a slow heartbeat. Bell leans over and smiles. 'It is still *alive*,' she says softly. Old Helm explains that a fresh word hums with the energy of the place it was found, and fades only when a traveller stops wondering. Mine has not faded yet.
alive:2.cnHint: 今天收集的词语在叙述者掌心发光跳动，贝尔说它仍然____。
alive:2.hook: Then it pulses once, brightly — and points northeast, all on its own.
alive:2.line: 'Keep wondering, and it stays *alive* in your hand forever.'

lift:2.en: Deep inside the Clockwork Spire, Old Helm found a brass panel on the wall. He pressed a button, and a small platform rose from the floor — a *lift* that carried us slowly upward through layers of gears and soft golden light, until the ceiling opened into a hidden sky-garden above the clouds.
lift:2.cnHint: 在齿轮塔内部，我们乘坐一个古老装置升到了隐藏花园。
lift:2.hook: Something in that garden had been waiting for us a very long time.
lift:2.line: 'Step onto the *lift* — it will carry us where the stairs cannot reach.'

mainly:2.en: Bell spread the new map fragment across the floor of our sky-boat. The island ahead was *mainly* covered in silver forest, with only a narrow strip of open shore along its eastern edge. She tapped that thin line and said it was our only safe landing spot.
mainly:2.cnHint: 小铃查看地图碎片，发现前方岛屿____被银色森林覆盖。
mainly:2.hook: What lived inside that silver forest, the map did not say.
mainly:2.line: 'The island is *mainly* forest — we land on the shore or not at all.'

moral:2.en: Old Helm read aloud from a tiny scroll we found sealed inside a hollow stone. It was a short fable about a crow who collected too many shiny things and could no longer fly. 'Every old story has a *moral*,' he said, folding it carefully, 'and this one is for us.'
moral:2.cnHint: 老舵从石头里找到一卷古老寓言，读出了其中的____。
moral:2.hook: The crow in the fable had worn our troupe's exact symbol on its wing.
moral:2.line: 'The *moral* is simple: carry only what lets you keep moving.'

nor:2.en: We reached the Edge Shelf, a flat rock jutting out beyond the last mapped island. There was no village here, *nor* any sign that people had ever stopped to rest. Only a single lantern hung on an iron post, still lit, swinging gently in the high wind.
nor:2.cnHint: 在地图边缘的岩架上，既没有村庄，____有任何人曾停留的痕迹。
nor:2.hook: A lantern does not light itself.
nor:2.line: 'There is no path forward, *nor* any way back that I can see.'

pick:2.en: The Word-Market of Lens Isle was a circle of coloured stalls, each one holding a single glowing letter-stone. Old Helm told me I could *pick* only one — the stone I chose would open the next gate on our route. I walked the whole circle twice before my hand finally stopped.
pick:2.cnHint: 在Lens Isle的集市上，我必须从众多发光石头中____一个来开启下一道门。
pick:2.hook: The stone I touched grew warm before I even reached for it.
pick:2.line: '*Pick* carefully — each stone opens a different door, and doors do not reopen.'

pollution:2.en: The Isle of Mirrors had once been beautiful, Bell told us, but careless travelers had left smoke-makers burning for years. A grey haze now hung low over its surface. The *pollution* had turned the famous silver pools dark and still. Old Helm wrote the word down in his log without a comment.
pollution:2.cnHint: 小铃告诉我们，镜之岛因长年____而变得灰暗，银色水池已失去光泽。
pollution:2.hook: Somewhere beneath that grey haze, a light was still blinking.
pollution:2.line: 'The *pollution* reached here before us — someone came this way before.'

quit:2.en: Halfway up the Spiral Stair of Vane Peak, Silverfang stopped climbing and sat down hard on a step. 'I nearly want to *quit*,' he admitted, breathing fast. Old Helm sat beside him, said nothing, and simply handed him a small canteen. After a minute, Silverfang stood and kept going.
quit:2.cnHint: 在螺旋石阶上，银牙筋疲力尽，几乎想要____，但老舵默默给了他支持。
quit:2.hook: The top of the stair held something none of us had expected to find.
quit:2.line: 'I do not *quit* — I only stop long enough to start again.'

recall:2.en: Bell held the old compass and closed her eyes. She was trying to *recall* the route her grandmother had once described to her — a hidden current of wind that ran behind the eastern star-cluster and led straight to the map's end. Slowly, a small smile crossed her face.
recall:2.cnHint: 小铃闭上眼睛，努力____祖母曾描述过的隐秘风道，以找到地图的尽头。
recall:2.hook: Her eyes opened, and she turned the compass to a direction no chart had ever shown.
recall:2.line: 'I *recall* it now — follow the wind that smells of cold starlight.'

anyway:2.en: The old bridge was broken, and the fog sat thick below us. Bell studied the gap, then stepped back and pulled out a small folded note from her coat. 'Someone left this here,' she said. The note held a single word: *anyway*. Old Helm smiled. 'It means: don't stop. Keep going no matter what.' We crossed on a rope, one by one.
anyway:2.cnHint: 断桥前，小铃发现一张纸条，纸条上的词让大家决定____继续前行。
anyway:2.hook: The rope swayed, and something below the fog began to move.
anyway:2.line: '*Anyway*, a broken bridge has never stopped this troupe before,' said Old Helm.

arise:2.en: We landed on a quiet island covered in silver moss. Nothing seemed unusual — until a low hum filled the air and a ring of glowing stones lifted from the ground. 'Problems can *arise* from silence too,' Bell warned, stepping back. Old Helm opened the map chest. The stones formed letters. A new word had found us.
arise:2.cnHint: 在银苔岛上，一圈发光石头突然____，小铃警觉地提醒大家注意。
arise:2.hook: The letters shifted, and one stone rolled toward my foot.
arise:2.line: 'Strange things *arise* on islands that have been quiet too long,' Bell said softly.

besides:2.en: Silverfang's ship had more cargo than I expected: star charts, dried fruit, a small drum, and three locked boxes. 'We carry what the journey needs,' she said. *Besides* the maps, she kept a list of every word the troupe had ever collected, written on pale blue paper. I counted sixty-three words. Sixty-three islands waiting.
besides:2.cnHint: 银牙的船上除了地图____，还藏着一份记录所有词语的清单。
besides:2.hook: The sixty-fourth word on the list was blank — and glowing.
besides:2.line: '*Besides* maps, a good navigator always carries a record of where words have led,' said Silverfang.

certainly:2.en: Old Helm held up the jar and shook it gently. A tiny light spun inside like a trapped star. 'Will it show us the next island?' I asked. He looked at me the way a teacher looks at a good question. 'It will *certainly* show us something,' he said. Bell set the jar on the deck, and the light shot north.
certainly:2.cnHint: 我问老舵那个罐子是否能指路，他____地回答说一定会有所指引。
certainly:2.hook: The light stopped just as a shadow crossed the northern sky.
certainly:2.line: '*Certainly* — every word we find has always pointed somewhere true,' Old Helm replied.

challenging:2.en: The climb up Mirror Peak was steep, and the steps were cut small, as if made for someone much shorter than me. Bell moved ahead easily. I slipped twice. 'The path is *challenging* on purpose,' she called back. 'The island tests whether you really want what waits at the top.' I wanted it. I kept climbing.
challenging:2.cnHint: Mirror Peak的攀登路途____，小铃说这是小岛在考验来访者的决心。
challenging:2.hook: At the top, a door stood open — and something inside was already watching.
challenging:2.line: 'A *challenging* path means the reward at the end is worth every hard step,' Bell said.

circumstance:2.en: The letter was addressed to no one. It had been tucked under a rock near the island's edge, as if waiting for years. Old Helm read it aloud: 'Whatever your *circumstance*, the next island is reachable.' We did not know who wrote it, or when. But the words were still warm, as if written for exactly this moment.
circumstance:2.cnHint: 一封无名信里写道，无论处于什么____，下一座岛都可以抵达。
circumstance:2.hook: Old Helm turned the letter over, and a map began to appear on the back.
circumstance:2.line: 'In any *circumstance*, the troupe moves forward — that is our only rule,' said Old Helm.

comfort:2.en: After three days on rough winds, the troupe landed on Hearthstone Island. Someone had left a fire burning in a stone bowl, with warm bread beside it. No note, no name. 'People leave *comfort* for strangers here,' Silverfang said quietly. I sat by the fire and felt, for the first time, that this sky was home.
comfort:2.cnHint: 经过三天颠簸，大家在Hearthstone Island找到了陌生人留下的____，感受到了温暖。
comfort:2.hook: The fire never once went low, though no one added wood all night.
comfort:2.line: 'A little *comfort* at the right moment can carry a troupe further than any wind,' said Silverfang.

enrich:2.en: The word glowed faintly on the stone tablet: *enrich*. Bell traced it with one finger. 'Every word we collect does this,' she said. 'It makes the map bigger, the world wider, the story richer.' Old Helm added it to the chest. The brass lock clicked, and a new passage opened in the cliff face behind us, full of soft gold light.
enrich:2.cnHint: 小铃说每一个收集到的词都能____他们的地图和旅程，话音刚落，石壁上出现了新通道。
enrich:2.hook: The gold light inside the passage formed the shape of an island none of us had ever seen.
enrich:2.line: 'Every word we find will *enrich* the map and carry us somewhere we have never been,' said Bell.

egg:2.en: At the edge of Shellrock Island, Bell knelt beside a nest of glowing stones. Tucked among them was a single *egg*, warm to the touch and faintly humming, as if something inside was already dreaming of the sky. Old Helm pressed his ear close and smiled. 'It knows a word,' he whispered. 'A very old one.'
egg:2.cnHint: 小铃在发光石堆中发现了一枚会嗡嗡作响的____，老舵长说它懂得一个古老的词。
egg:2.hook: The humming grew louder, and the egg began to crack.
egg:2.line: 'This *egg* is no ordinary stone — listen to it sing!'

hire:2.en: A notice was pinned to the mast of a drifting sky-boat: neat letters, crisp paper, a single word at the top. 'It is a *hire* offer,' Bell read aloud, eyes wide. Old Helm stroked his chin. Someone needed a navigator, and the pay was three rare words — exactly the kind our map was missing.
hire:2.cnHint: 一张漂浮船上的告示写明了____条件，报酬竟然是三个地图碎片词语。
hire:2.hook: The boat's lantern flickered, and a shadow moved inside.
hire:2.line: 'Old Helm, the *hire* offer pays in words — we have to take it!'

aid:2.en: The little island of Mossbell was tilting sideways, its roots slowly pulling free of the sky. Bell spread the map flat. 'We have the word for balance,' she said. Old Helm nodded. Offering our *aid* cost us one map fragment, but watching the island right itself, green and steady again, felt like the better kind of treasure.
aid:2.cnHint: 小岛开始倾斜，老舵长决定给予____，用了一张地图碎片换来岛屿的平衡。
aid:2.hook: But the map now showed a blank space where the island had been.
aid:2.line: 'Our *aid* is the only thing standing between this island and the deep sky.'

bill:2.en: Docked at Cloud-Ledge Port, Old Helm slid a folded paper across the counter. The harbour keeper unfolded it slowly. It was a *bill* for three nights of mooring and two barrels of wind-salt, scrawled in ink the colour of storm clouds. Tucked inside was a word — our next map fragment — written in a much lighter hand.
bill:2.cnHint: 靠港后，老舵长收到了一张____，里面夹着一个新的地图碎片词语。
bill:2.hook: The word written in light ink was not one any of us recognised.
bill:2.line: 'Check the *bill* carefully — someone left us a message inside it.'

paint:2.en: The bridge between the Twin Arch Islands was covered in writing, layer upon layer, each troupe that had passed leaving a word behind. Bell handed me a small brush. 'Your turn,' she said. I chose our newest word and began to *paint* it in slow, careful strokes onto the warm stone, adding our line to the long story of the sky.
paint:2.cnHint: 小铃让叙述者在桥上____下新词，为天空旅人的长篇故事添上一笔。
paint:2.hook: When the word dried, the bridge shivered and stretched a little longer.
paint:2.line: 'Go on — *paint* it boldly, so the next troupe can read it from the air.'

bean:2.en: Silverfang won the navigation contest by half a ship-length and grinned all the way to the prize table. The reward was a small cloth bag. He looked inside, then looked again. One single dried *bean*, mottled green and gold. Old Helm laughed. 'Plant it,' he said. 'The map says the plant that grows will point to the next island.'
bean:2.cnHint: 银牙赢得比赛后，奖品竟然是一颗____，老舵长说把它种下就能找到下一座岛。
bean:2.hook: Silverfang planted it, and it sprouted before dawn.
bean:2.line: 'One *bean* — that is my prize? This map had better be worth it.'

birthday:2.en: Old Helm said nothing all morning, which was unusual. At noon Bell produced a small cake made of sky-honey and cloud-flour, one candle burning at the top. 'It is his *birthday*,' she whispered to me with a warm smile. When Old Helm saw it, his eyes went soft. He blew out the candle, and the smoke curled into the shape of a new island.
birthday:2.cnHint: 小铃为老舵长准备了生日蛋糕，烛烟竟然飘出一座新岛屿的轮廓。
birthday:2.hook: The smoke island matched no shape on our current map.
birthday:2.line: 'Happy *birthday*, Old Helm — the sky saved its best gift for you today.'

flight:2.en: The leap between Windspire Peak and the next island was too wide for the ship. 'We go on foot,' Bell said calmly, pointing to a row of broad-winged birds perched on the rail. Each one could carry a single passenger. My *flight* lasted about forty seconds — wind in my face, stars close enough to touch — and I landed laughing, the new word already glowing in my hand.
flight:2.cnHint: 两岛之间距离太远，叙述者乘鸟____飞越，降落时手中已亮起新的词语碎片。
flight:2.hook: The bird circled once, then vanished into the star-bright dark.
flight:2.line: 'My *flight* was short, but I saw three islands no map has named yet.'

facilitate:2.en: Old Helm spread the ancient chart across the bow and placed a glowing stone at each corner. 'These markers *facilitate* our reading of the star-lines,' he said. The chart shimmered, and three new islands rose like ink blooming in water. Bell traced the nearest route with one careful finger.
facilitate:2.cnHint: 老赫姆用发光石块压住星图四角，____了整个船队对星线的判读。
facilitate:2.hook: The third island had no name — only a question mark burned into the paper.
facilitate:2.line: 'These markers *facilitate* our reading of the star-lines, so touch nothing until Bell confirms the heading.'

insight:2.en: Tucked inside a hollow cloud-stone, I found a folded note covered in tiny writing. Reading it gave me sudden *insight* into why the eastern islands kept drifting — they followed the starfish migration, not the wind. Bell looked over my shoulder and let out a slow, impressed breath.
insight:2.cnHint: 我在一块空心云石里发现了一张字条，从中获得了关于东方群岛漂移规律的____。
insight:2.hook: At the bottom of the note, someone had written: 'Do not tell Old Helm. Not yet.'
insight:2.line: 'That note gave me real *insight* — the islands move with the starfish, not the wind.'

preparation:2.en: Bell laid out every compass, every rope-knot chart, and every star-glass on the deck before dawn. 'Good *preparation* means no surprises at the edge,' she said quietly. Old Helm watched from the stern, nodding once — which I had learned was his way of saying he was proud.
preparation:2.cnHint: 贝尔在黎明前把所有航行工具摆满甲板，认真____着前往边缘岛屿的航程。
preparation:2.hook: One tool was missing, and no one mentioned it aloud.
preparation:2.line: 'Good *preparation* means no surprises at the edge — lay everything out now.'

separate:2.en: The fog rolled in and *separate*d our small boat from the rest of the troupe's fleet. I could still hear Silverfang's horn through the white silence, but it sounded distant and strange. I gripped the rail and kept the single star above the mast in sight until the fog finally thinned.
separate:2.cnHint: 浓雾突然涌来，将我们的小船与船队____开来，只剩头顶一颗星可以辨认方向。
separate:2.hook: When the fog cleared, Silverfang's ship was pointed the wrong way entirely.
separate:2.line: 'The fog will *separate* us — watch that star and do not let it leave your sight.'

tie:2.en: At the docking post of the amber island, there was no clear winner — Silverfang's ship and Old Helm's ship reached the pier at exactly the same moment. 'A *tie*,' Silverfang said, with a rare half-smile. Old Helm shrugged, but I noticed he was smiling too as he stepped ashore.
tie:2.cnHint: 两艘船同时抵达琥珀岛的码头，竟然打成了____，两位船长都露出了难得的笑容。
tie:2.hook: The island only unlocked one gate — and it needed both captains to open it.
tie:2.line: 'A *tie* — I suppose that means we open the gate together, Old Helm.'

jam:2.en: The great bronze door of the cloud-vault would not turn. Something inside had *jammed* the lock, and no amount of pushing helped. Bell pressed her ear to the metal, then smiled. She pulled a bent feather-key from her coat and wiggled it once — the door swung open with a sigh of warm light.
jam:2.cnHint: 云库的铜门因为内部卡住而____住了，贝尔用一把弯羽钥匙轻巧地将它打开。
jam:2.hook: Inside the vault, every shelf was empty except for one small, glowing word.
jam:2.line: 'Something has *jammed* the lock — stand back and let me try the feather-key.'

supermarket:2.en: The mid-sky trading post was nothing like the quiet islands we knew — it was loud, bright, and packed with stalls selling star-salts, cloud-cloth, and bottled lightning. Old Helm called it 'the floating *supermarket* of the sky.' I spent ten whole minutes just staring at a jar of frozen moonlight.
supermarket:2.cnHint: 空中贸易站热闹非凡，老赫姆笑称它是天空中的____，摊位上摆满了稀奇古怪的货物。
supermarket:2.hook: One stall had no sign — only a curtain, and a faint glow from behind it.
supermarket:2.line: 'Welcome to the floating *supermarket* of the sky — pick one thing, and choose wisely.'

debate:2.en: Bell said the next word-fragment pointed north. Silverfang said it pointed west. The *debate* lasted until the stars shifted and gave us a third direction entirely. Old Helm laughed, picked up the fragment, and held it to the light. 'It points,' he said, 'wherever the wind is kindest.'
debate:2.cnHint: 贝尔和西尔弗方就下一块碎片的指向展开了一场____，最终老赫姆用风向给出了出人意料的答案。
debate:2.hook: The wind shifted the moment Old Helm finished speaking — straight toward the hidden island.
debate:2.line: 'Enough *debate* — hold the fragment to the light and let it decide for itself.'

collection:2.en: Near the edge of the map, Bell found a hollow stone shelf carved into the cliff face. On it sat a neat *collection* of tiny glass jars, each holding a single glowing letter. Old Helm counted them slowly. 'Someone was here before us,' he said, voice low with wonder.
collection:2.cnHint: 小铃在悬崖边发现了一排石架，上面摆着一组装有发光字母的玻璃瓶——这是某人留下的____。
collection:2.hook: One jar was still warm to the touch.
collection:2.line: Old Helm: 'This *collection* tells me someone mapped these islands long before we did.'

depression:2.en: The island's centre held a wide bowl-shaped *depression* in the rock, as if a giant thumb had pressed down from above. Rainwater had gathered there, perfectly still and dark. Bell knelt at the edge and saw letters floating just below the surface, waiting to be read.
depression:2.cnHint: 岛屿中心有一片低洼的____，积水中漂浮着神秘的字母。
depression:2.hook: The letters began to rearrange themselves.
depression:2.line: Bell: 'This *depression* in the rock was not made by rain or wind, I am sure of it.'

foot:2.en: A narrow rope bridge led to the next island, and at its *foot* stood a wooden post covered in carved symbols. Old Helm traced each one with his finger. 'These are directions,' he said softly. I copied them into my notebook before the morning wind could shake the bridge too hard.
foot:2.cnHint: 绳桥____处的木柱上刻满了符号，老舵长说那是方向指引。
foot:2.hook: The post tilted slightly, pointing somewhere new.
foot:2.line: Old Helm: 'Meet me at the *foot* of the bridge when the stars shift west.'

graduate:2.en: Among the papers inside the old shelter, I found a letter signed by someone called 'the last *graduate* of the Cloud Academy.' The handwriting was careful and proud. Old Helm read it twice, folded it gently, and tucked it into his coat. 'We owe this person a destination,' he said.
graduate:2.cnHint: 废弃小屋中有一封自称是云端学院____写的信，老舵长郑重地将它收起。
graduate:2.hook: The Cloud Academy appeared on no map we carried.
graduate:2.line: Old Helm: 'A *graduate* of that school would never leave clues by accident.'

intake:2.en: The stone door would only open with sound. Bell discovered that a sharp *intake* of breath, drawn in quickly and held, made the carved eye above the lock glow blue. I tried it myself and the door gave a deep click. Beyond it, warm amber light spilled across the floor.
intake:2.cnHint: 石门只会在某种特定的____声后打开，小铃发现了这个秘密。
intake:2.hook: Something inside the room had been waiting a very long time.
intake:2.line: Bell: 'One quick *intake* of breath, hold it steady, and the door should respond.'

screen:2.en: Old Helm unrolled a sheet of pale fabric and hung it between two poles, making a rough *screen*. He shone a lamp behind it, and the shadows of the map fragments we had gathered arranged themselves into a shape — an island none of us had seen before. Silverfang leaned forward in silence.
screen:2.cnHint: 老舵长用一块布做成____，将碎片的影子投影成一座从未见过的岛屿轮廓。
screen:2.hook: Silverfang reached out as if she could touch the shadow island.
screen:2.line: Old Helm: 'The *screen* shows only what we have already found — but look at the gap in the middle.'

chair:2.en: At the top of the signal tower sat a single carved *chair*, facing the open sky. Whoever sat there last had left a folded note on the seat. Bell read it aloud: a list of star names and the hours they rose. Silverfang copied every word without being asked.
chair:2.cnHint: 信号塔顶端有一把____，上面留着一张写满星星名字和时间的纸条。
chair:2.hook: The last star on the list would not rise for another three nights.
chair:2.line: Silverfang: 'Whoever built that *chair* up there never meant to come back down quickly.'

court:2.en: A wide flat platform of pale stone served as a kind of open *court* where three paths crossed. At its centre, a map tile stood upright in a crack in the ground. Old Helm said it was a meeting spot — traders, scouts, wanderers all passed through. I felt the weight of every footstep before mine.
court:2.cnHint: 三条小路交汇的石台广场是一处____，中央竖立着一块地图碎片。
court:2.hook: One of the three paths led off the edge of every chart we had.
court:2.line: Old Helm: 'This open *court* was where deals were made and routes were shared, long ago.'

housing:2.en: The island of Crumblereach greeted us with rows of tiny stone shelters carved right into the cliff face. Bell pointed her lantern at the nearest wall, where someone had pressed a single word into the rock like a seal. 'This *housing* is older than any map we carry,' she said softly. Old Helm reached out and traced the letters, and the cliff hummed — a new path lit up below our feet.
housing:2.cnHint: 小铃在悬崖上的古老____中发现了一个神秘刻字，老舵手触碰后，脚下出现了新的光路。
housing:2.hook: The path below led somewhere no map had ever named.
housing:2.line: 'This *housing* is older than any map we carry.'

behaviour:2.en: The sky-eels of Driftmere circled our deck in slow rings, which Bell said was normal. Then they stopped, hung perfectly still, and stared at Old Helm. He pulled a folded note from his coat — left by a stranger on the last island — and read it aloud. 'Unusual *behaviour* in the eels means the next word is close,' it said. Above us, a single eel glowed gold.
behaviour:2.cnHint: 天空鳗鱼突然停止游动盯着老舵长，一张纸条解释了它们奇怪的____，暗示下一个词语就在附近。
behaviour:2.hook: The glowing eel turned east and began to move.
behaviour:2.line: 'Unusual *behaviour* in the eels means the next word is close.'

husband:2.en: On the island of Saltwhisper we found a locked box nailed to a driftwood post. Inside, wrapped in oilcloth, was a short letter. 'My *husband* carved this word into every island he visited,' it read, 'so I could always follow.' The word inside the cloth glowed faintly — warm, stubborn, alive. Old Helm placed it on our map and a new island rose on the horizon.
husband:2.cnHint: 在一封信里，我们发现一位女士靠着____留下的词语一路追随他，那个词让新的岛屿从地平线升起。
husband:2.hook: Somewhere ahead, the carver was still travelling.
husband:2.line: 'My *husband* carved this word into every island he visited.'

tourist:2.en: Silverfang docked at Glassbell Pier with a wide grin and announced that today we would blend in. The market was thick with travellers, and one vendor spotted us at once. 'Every *tourist* who asks about the hidden word gets the same answer,' she said, sliding a tile across her stall. The tile showed a star chart — and one island marked in red that appeared on none of our maps.
tourist:2.cnHint: 在集市上，一位摊贩告诉每一位____同样的秘密，并递给我们一块标有神秘红色岛屿的星图瓦片。
tourist:2.hook: The red island had no name, only coordinates.
tourist:2.line: 'Every *tourist* who asks about the hidden word gets the same answer.'

agent:2.en: A messenger bird landed on Bell's shoulder at dawn, carrying a tiny scroll sealed in blue wax. 'I am an *agent* for the Wordsmiths' Guild,' the note began, 'and I have hidden your next map fragment under the stone lantern at Pale Crest.' Old Helm read it twice, then looked up with bright eyes. None of us had ever heard of the Wordsmiths' Guild before.
agent:2.cnHint: 一封来自词匠公会____的神秘信件告诉我们，下一块地图碎片就藏在白顶岛的石灯笼下。
agent:2.hook: Old Helm folded the note and said nothing for a long moment.
agent:2.line: 'I am an *agent* for the Wordsmiths' Guild.'

cash:2.en: The toll-keeper of Ironmist Bridge held out her hand and named her price. Silverfang patted every pocket with growing alarm. Old Helm stayed calm. 'We carry no *cash*,' he said, 'but we carry words.' He placed a glowing syllable on the keeper's palm — and her eyes went wide, because that syllable was one she had been searching for herself for twenty years.
cash:2.cnHint: 过桥没有____，老舵长用一个发光的词节代替过桥费，收费员为此震惊不已。
cash:2.hook: The keeper stepped aside and whispered, 'Pass quickly.'
cash:2.line: 'We carry no *cash*, but we carry words.'

competition:2.en: The annual Word Race of Skyveil Island drew a dozen crews, all chasing the same fragment pinned to the tallest cloud-spire. Silverfang rolled her shoulders. 'I have won this *competition* three times,' she said, and leaped off the rail before the horn sounded. She came back two minutes later, fragment in hand, looking entirely too pleased with herself. Old Helm added it to the map without a word.
competition:2.cnHint: 在天幕岛的年度词语比赛中，银牙赢得了____并带回了地图碎片，老舵长默默地将它加入地图。
competition:2.hook: The fragment glowed brighter than any piece we had found before.

farmer:2.en: We landed on a low green island where a figure was tending rows of glowing seedlings. Each plant bore a single letter on its leaf. 'I am a *farmer*,' the old woman said, 'but I grow words, not wheat.' She snipped a full-grown word from the nearest stalk and pressed it into my hand. It felt warm, like bread fresh from an oven, and the map in my coat pocket immediately grew heavier.
farmer:2.cnHint: 在一座绿色小岛上，一位种植词语而非小麦的____剪下一个成熟的词语送给了我，地图随即变沉了。
farmer:2.hook: I looked down and saw a new island had appeared at the map's edge.
farmer:2.line: 'I am a *farmer*, but I grow words, not wheat.'

female:2.en: We found the message carved on a stone arch at the edge of Hollow Peak. Bell pointed to a small drawing beside the words — a *female* bird with one silver wing, the symbol of a guide. 'She flew ahead of every troupe that ever reached this island,' Bell said softly.
female:2.cnHint: 小铃在石拱上发现了一幅雕刻，那只有银翅的____鸟据说为每支到达此地的队伍引路。
female:2.hook: But the stone beneath the drawing was still warm.
female:2.line: 'That *female* bird has been carved here longer than any map we carry.'

holiday:2.en: The island of Lantern Drift looked like a *holiday* from the moment we landed — coloured ribbons on every post, round lamps swaying in the wind, and the smell of sweet bread drifting from open doors. Old Helm spread his arms wide and laughed for the first time in three days.
holiday:2.cnHint: 踏上灯漂岛，眼前的彩带和圆灯让人感觉像是置身____，老舵手也忍不住开怀大笑。
holiday:2.hook: Then every lamp went out at once.
holiday:2.line: 'This feels like a *holiday*, but something here wants us to stay.'

pain:2.en: The map fragment was sealed inside a glass bottle wedged into a crack in the cliff. I pulled until my fingers ached — real *pain*, sharp and clear. Finally it came free, and the bottle held not just paper but a tiny dried flower pressed flat between the folds.
pain:2.cnHint: 我费力从悬崖裂缝中拔出玻璃瓶，手指传来阵阵____，瓶内却藏着地图碎片和一朵干花。
pain:2.hook: The flower was still faintly blue, as though picked yesterday.
pain:2.line: 'A little *pain* now is worth what waits on the other side.'

player:2.en: On the floating stage of Echo Garden, a lone *player* sat at a carved wooden game board, moving pieces without an opponent. She did not look up when we arrived. Old Helm recognised the pattern on the board and went pale — it was a map of islands we had not yet visited.
player:2.cnHint: 在空中舞台上，一位孤独的____正移动棋子，棋盘上的图案竟是我们尚未到达的岛屿地图。
player:2.hook: She moved the last piece and smiled before we spoke a word.
player:2.line: 'Every *player* who reaches this table already knows the ending.'

production:2.en: The workshop on Gear Isle hummed with noise. Bell read the label on the nearest crate: a *production* of star-glass, the rarest material used to make lenses for night navigation. Someone had left an entire crate behind, untouched, as if in a great hurry to leave.
production:2.cnHint: 在齿轮岛的工坊里，小铃发现了一整箱星玻璃的____，货物完好无损，像是有人仓皇离去。
production:2.hook: The dust on the crate was disturbed by only one set of footprints.
production:2.line: 'This *production* took months — no one abandons it without a reason.'

secure:2.en: The bridge between Twin Spires looked narrow, but Old Helm tested each rope and nodded. 'It is *secure*,' he said, pressing a plank with his boot until it held firm. We crossed one by one, the wind pulling our coats, and on the far side found a door carved with our troupe's symbol.
secure:2.cnHint: 老舵手仔细检查了双峰间的吊桥，确认____后，我们一一通过，对岸的门上竟刻着我们的徽记。
secure:2.hook: No one in our troupe had ever been here before.
secure:2.line: 'Stay close — I need to know this rope is *secure* before you step.'

audience:2.en: We climbed to the open-air platform at the top of Cloud Terrace and found rows of empty stone seats. Bell opened the old logbook and read aloud: this place was built for an *audience* of a thousand, gathered once a year to watch the star-crossing. We were three hundred years too late — or perhaps too early.
audience:2.cnHint: 小铃从旧航海日志得知，云台顶端的石座曾为____千人而建，专为观看星辰渡空。
audience:2.hook: Then the seats filled with soft, silver light.
audience:2.line: 'An *audience* once sat here and never forgot what they saw.'

borrow:2.en: Silverfang pulled alongside us at Mist Shelf and called across the gap. 'I need to *borrow* your star-compass — mine shattered on the rocks below. One hour, I promise.' Old Helm hesitated, then passed it over. Silverfang caught it, nodded once, and for the first time looked almost grateful.
borrow:2.cnHint: 银牙船长靠近我们，请求____星罗盘，说自己的已经摔碎，老舵手犹豫片刻后还是递了过去。
borrow:2.hook: Silverfang sailed away fast — far faster than one hour would need.
borrow:2.line: 'I only want to *borrow* it — but I understand why you hesitate.'

mile:2.en: The sealed glass bottle had drifted to our island from somewhere far away. Inside was a rolled note that read: 'Every *mile* of open sky between islands holds one secret — count them and you will find the door.' Old Helm held it up to the starlight, his eyes wide. The word MILE glowed faintly on the paper.
mile:2.cnHint: 漂流瓶里的纸条告诉我们，岛屿间每隔一____都藏着一个秘密。
mile:2.hook: The bottle was still warm, as if someone had dropped it only moments ago.
mile:2.line: 'Every *mile* of sky is a page,' Old Helm said softly, 'and we have not read nearly enough.'

movement:2.en: Bell spotted it first — a slow, silent *movement* behind the crystal wall of the Archive Tower. Something inside was shifting, rearranging rows of glowing word-stones all on its own. We pressed our faces to the cold surface and watched, barely breathing. Old Helm whispered that the tower was choosing our next destination for us.
movement:2.cnHint: 档案塔的水晶墙后有神秘的____，仿佛有什么东西在自行整理发光的文字石。
movement:2.hook: Then one word-stone rolled to the front and spelled out our names.
movement:2.line: 'That *movement* means the tower is awake,' Bell said, stepping back slowly.

party:2.en: Carved above the entrance of the Cloud Vault was a sentence none of us could fully read — except for two words: WELCOME and *PARTY*. Old Helm said a troupe of travellers like ours was exactly the kind of party the vault had been waiting for. We stepped inside together, and the stone doors sealed shut behind us with a deep, friendly hum.
party:2.cnHint: 云穹库门口的铭文写着欢迎这样的____到来，石门随即关闭。
party:2.hook: Every lantern inside flickered on at once, lighting a path deeper into the dark.
party:2.line: 'A *party* of word-seekers,' Old Helm read aloud, grinning, 'is what this place has always wanted.'

writing:2.en: Along the curved wall of the Hollow Bell Tower, someone had left *writing* in a language that shifted each time I blinked — one moment it looked like star charts, the next like a recipe, then like a letter home. Bell ran her fingers over it gently and said it was the oldest kind of message: one that meant something different to every reader.
writing:2.cnHint: 钟楼弯曲的墙壁上留有古老的____，每次眨眼它看起来都不一样。
writing:2.hook: At the very end of the wall, my own name appeared in perfectly clear letters.
writing:2.line: 'Good *writing* never finishes,' Bell said, 'it just waits for the right eyes.'

bite:2.en: Old Helm broke a piece from the edge of the Map-Bread — a flat, golden disc baked with word-dust that the troupe used to read sealed messages. He handed me a small piece. 'One *bite* is enough,' he said. The moment it touched my tongue, a whole island appeared in my mind: green, loud with wind, impossible to forget.
bite:2.cnHint: 老舵让我尝了一小口地图面包，____下去后我脑海中浮现出一座新的岛屿。
bite:2.hook: The island in my mind had a door, and the door was open.
bite:2.line: 'One *bite*,' Old Helm said warmly, 'and the map speaks directly to you.'

capture:2.en: Bell had rigged a small paper lantern with word-dust and thread, and she let it drift toward the cloud cluster where the lost fragment was hiding. It circled twice, then folded shut around the glowing shard — enough to *capture* the word without breaking it. She pulled the lantern back hand over hand, smiling like she had done this a hundred times.
capture:2.cnHint: 小铃用特制的纸灯笼____住了躲在云层里的失落文字碎片。
capture:2.hook: Inside the folded lantern, the word pulsed like a tiny heartbeat.
capture:2.line: 'The trick to *capture* a word,' Bell said, 'is to make it feel welcome, not trapped.'

cope:2.en: My first night on a drifting island was nothing like I had imagined. The ground tilted, the stars spun in unfamiliar patterns, and every sound was strange. Old Helm sat beside me and said that every new member had to *cope* with the strangeness at first, and that the strangeness was the best part once you learned to love it. By morning, I believed him.
cope:2.cnHint: 初到漂流岛的第一夜，老舵告诉我每位新成员都要学会____这里的陌生感。
cope:2.hook: By dawn, the island had drifted somewhere none of us had ever been before.
cope:2.line: 'You learn to *cope*,' Old Helm said gently, 'and then one day you learn to fly with it.'

burn:2.en: The old lighthouse on Cinder Isle held a warning carved deep into its stone door. Bell ran her fingers along the letters slowly. 'Someone pressed a hot iron right here,' she said. The *burn* left behind read: TURN BACK. Old Helm smiled and stepped inside anyway, lantern swinging.
burn:2.cnHint: 小铃在灯塔门上发现了一道____，上面刻着警告的字样。
burn:2.hook: Whatever made that mark was still somewhere inside.
burn:2.line: 'This *burn* is fresh — someone was here not two nights ago.'

cook:2.en: On the island of Ember Shelf, we found a clay kitchen floating all on its own, no walls, just a stove under open stars. Old Helm sat down and began to *cook* a pot of something thick and golden. The smell alone made the next map fragment glow brighter in Bell's hand.
cook:2.cnHint: 老舵在漂浮的厨房里____了一锅食物，地图碎片竟然发出了光。
cook:2.hook: The pot held one ingredient none of us could name.
cook:2.line: 'Let me *cook* — hunger makes brave people foolish,' said Old Helm.

corporate:2.en: Bell pulled a brass plate from the ruins and read it aloud. 'A *corporate* seal,' she said, 'meaning this island once belonged to a whole group, not one person.' The crest showed seven hands joined in a circle. Old Helm copied it into his notebook. Seven islands. Seven hands.
corporate:2.cnHint: 小铃发现了一块____印章，说明这座岛曾属于某个团体。
corporate:2.hook: Six of those seven islands had already vanished from every known map.
corporate:2.line: 'A *corporate* seal this old means someone shared a very big secret,' said Bell.

dangerous:2.en: The rope bridge to Fog Notch swayed hard even with no wind. 'It is *dangerous*,' Silverfang said, testing one plank with his boot, 'but the word we need is on the other side.' He tied a guide rope to my wrist before stepping forward, which told me everything about how serious he was.
dangerous:2.cnHint: 银牙警告说前方的吊桥____，但他们必须过去取得地图碎片。
dangerous:2.hook: Halfway across, two planks dropped silently into the cloud below.
dangerous:2.line: '*Dangerous* is just the cost of finding something worth finding,' said Silverfang.

debt:2.en: The keeper of Pale Shelf Island offered us the map fragment freely. 'No payment,' she said. Old Helm bowed low. 'Then we owe you a *debt* of kindness,' he told her. She shook her head and pointed at the stars. 'Pay it forward to the next troupe that comes lost through here.'
debt:2.cnHint: 地图保管人免费给出了碎片，老舵说他们欠了她一份____。
debt:2.hook: She watched us leave as though she had been waiting a very long time for us.
debt:2.line: 'A *debt* of kindness is the only kind worth carrying,' said Old Helm.

discipline:2.en: Bell made us practice reading star-charts every morning before the ship moved one inch. 'This *discipline* will save your life someday,' she said, tapping the chart. Silverfang grumbled. I grumbled too. But on the third morning I spotted the hidden current that would have sent us straight into the rock shelf.
discipline:2.cnHint: 小铃坚持每天早上练习读星图，她说这种____有一天会救大家的命。
discipline:2.hook: The rock shelf had no name on any map — because no one had survived it before.
discipline:2.line: '*Discipline* now means choices later — that is the whole deal,' said Bell.

error:2.en: The new map fragment showed a path curving left around the Moon Tooth peaks. I copied it carefully, but made one small *error* — I drew the curve right. We flew an hour the wrong way before Bell noticed. Old Helm did not scold me. He just said, 'Good. Now you will never make that one again.'
error:2.cnHint: 叙述者在抄写地图时犯了一个____，导致飞船偏离了方向。
error:2.hook: The wrong path had led us straight above an island that appeared on no chart at all.
error:2.line: 'One *error* is a lesson — the same error twice is a choice,' said Old Helm.

gym:2.en: At the center of Spring-Lock Island stood a round stone hall the locals called the *gym* — not for strength, but for sharpening the mind through movement and balance. Bell walked its beams without looking down. Old Helm said the founders believed a still body made a still imagination, and a still imagination could never read the sky.
gym:2.cnHint: 岛上有一座石制____，当地人在这里通过运动来锻炼思维和平衡力。
gym:2.hook: The final beam led to a hidden door, and behind it was exactly what we had come for.
gym:2.line: 'Every *gym* I have seen on these islands teaches the same thing: pay attention,' said Bell.

strength:2.en: Deep in the map room, Old Helm unrolled a canvas covered in tiny marks. 'Each island has a garrison,' he said quietly. 'Look at these numbers — their *strength* grows the closer we sail to the edge.' Bell traced the figures with one finger, eyes wide.
strength:2.cnHint: 老舵手在地图室里发现，越靠近地图边缘，岛屿守卫的____越强大。
strength:2.hook: Whatever waited at the edge, we were already outnumbered.
strength:2.line: 'Their *strength* doubles on every island past the third.' — Old Helm

survive:2.en: We found a glass bottle wedged in a crack between two sky-stones. Inside was a note, blurred by rain but still readable: 'Only those who share their last lantern will *survive* the dark passage ahead.' Old Helm held it up to the starlight and said nothing for a long moment.
survive:2.cnHint: 一个漂流瓶里的字条警告大家，只有懂得分享的人才能____那片黑暗通道。
survive:2.hook: Our lantern had just enough oil for one person.
survive:2.line: 'Together we *survive*; alone we simply drift.' — Old Helm

touch:2.en: Bell handed me a small stone carved into the shape of a compass. The moment my fingers closed around it, a quiet warmth spread up my arm — a strange *touch* that felt like a welcome from the island itself. 'It chooses its keeper,' Bell said with a soft smile.
touch:2.cnHint: 领航员交给我一块雕刻罗盘，那种奇异的____让我感觉整座岛屿在欢迎我。
touch:2.hook: The stone pulsed once, then pointed somewhere no map showed.
touch:2.line: 'That *touch* means the island trusts you now.' — Bell

trap:2.en: Old Helm stopped us at a glowing archway. Vines had been twisted into a neat path leading through it — too neat. 'Classic *trap*,' he muttered, kneeling to inspect the stones. 'Someone wants us to step inside before we read the word carved above the door.' We all stepped back.
trap:2.cnHint: 老舵手识破了发光拱门下的____，提醒大家先读门上的刻字再行动。
trap:2.hook: The word above the door began to slowly fade away.
trap:2.line: 'A pretty path is the oldest *trap* there is.' — Old Helm

tv:2.en: On a forgotten island shaped like a crescent, we discovered a rusted metal box with a cracked glass front. Bell cleaned the glass and recognised it at once. 'A *tv*,' she said. 'Islanders once gathered around it every evening to receive news from the capital, before the sky-roads broke apart.'
tv:2.cnHint: 在一座废弃的岛上，领航员认出了一台旧____，那是岛民昔日接收消息的设备。
tv:2.hook: The screen flickered, and a single word appeared.
tv:2.line: 'They watched this *tv* the night the last bridge fell.' — Bell

victim:2.en: Tucked under a loose floor stone we found a journal. The final page read: 'I was not the first *victim* of this island's illusions — the mist shows you what you most want, then leads you off the edge.' Old Helm closed the journal gently and marked the island on our chart in red.
victim:2.cnHint: 一本日记揭示，失踪的旅人是这座岛屿幻象的____，迷雾会诱人走向边缘。
victim:2.hook: Red marks already covered a third of our chart.
victim:2.line: 'Let this be the last *victim* this mist ever claims.' — Old Helm

zone:2.en: Bell spread the newest map fragment across the deck. A wide band of cloud stretched across the centre, marked with diagonal lines. 'That shaded strip is a wind *zone*,' she explained. 'Air currents there spin in every direction. Entering without the right word-key means being thrown miles off course.'
zone:2.cnHint: 领航员在新地图碎片上发现了一片危险的风力____，进入那里需要特殊的词语钥匙。
zone:2.hook: We had the map, but not yet the word.
zone:2.line: 'No ship crosses that *zone* without the right word.' — Bell

afraid:2.en: Silverfang's vessel pulled alongside ours just as the stars began to dim. He leaned over the rail and called across the gap. 'I know you are not *afraid* of the dark passage,' he said, 'but I am — and I have sailed these skies twice as long as Old Helm.' The honesty surprised everyone.
afraid:2.cnHint: 竞争船长靠近我们，坦白说自己对黑暗通道感到____，这份诚实让所有人都愣住了。
afraid:2.hook: An honest rival is far more dangerous than a proud one.
afraid:2.line: 'Even I am *afraid* of what waits past the last star.' — Silverfang

couple:2.en: At the edge of the map, Bell found a stone post with two lanterns hanging side by side. 'A *couple* of lights always marks a safe harbour,' she said softly. She pressed both lanterns at once, and a hidden door in the cliff swung open, revealing a stairway that spiralled up into the stars.
couple:2.cnHint: 小铃发现石柱上挂着的一____灯笼，同时按下后，悬崖上的暗门开启了。
couple:2.hook: The stairway had no ceiling — only endless, breathing dark.
couple:2.line: 'A *couple* of lights always marks a safe harbour,' Bell said softly.

definition:2.en: Old Helm unrolled a faded scroll on the navigator's table. Every island on the map had a name, but one square was blank. 'Without a *definition*, a place cannot be found,' he muttered. He dipped his pen and wrote one careful word, and the blank square slowly filled with the shape of a brand-new island.
definition:2.cnHint: 老舵在地图上一片空白的区域写下____，那块空白随即浮现出一座新岛屿的轮廓。
definition:2.hook: The ink was still wet when the island groaned and rose from the clouds.
definition:2.line: 'Without a *definition*, a place cannot be found,' Old Helm muttered.

imagination:2.en: Deep in the island's crystal cave, the walls showed scenes from nowhere — cities of cloud, rivers of light, creatures with a hundred wings. Bell whispered that the cave fed on *imagination*, growing new pictures from every visitor's mind. I thought of home, and a small warm window appeared, glowing gently among the crystals.
imagination:2.cnHint: 水晶洞穴以访客的____为食，我一想起家，墙上便浮现出温暖的窗户光芒。
imagination:2.hook: Then the window opened, and something beyond it waved back.
imagination:2.line: 'This cave feeds on *imagination* — think carefully about what you picture,' Bell warned.

journey:2.en: Silverfang spread a new chart across the ship's deck and traced a long curve with one finger. 'This *journey* will take us past the Rim Rocks and beyond the last marked star,' he said, and there was no fear in his voice, only hunger. Old Helm nodded once, and Bell set the compass to a heading nobody had ever sailed before.
journey:2.cnHint: 银牙描述这段____将带领船队驶过边界岩礁，抵达最后标记星球的彼端。
journey:2.hook: Beyond the last star, the chart was perfectly, terrifyingly blank.
journey:2.line: 'This *journey* will take us past every place we have ever known,' Silverfang said.

nearby:2.en: The word we sought was carved not in some grand tower but in a mossy stone *nearby*, half-hidden under a flowering vine. I almost walked past it. Old Helm laughed and said the best discoveries always hide in plain sight. I brushed away the vine, and the carved letters glowed gold, adding one more island to our growing map.
nearby:2.cnHint: 我们寻找的词语就刻在____一块长满苔藓的石头上，险些被忽视。
nearby:2.hook: The gold glow spread outward and outlined a whole archipelago no one had mapped.
nearby:2.line: 'Check the stone *nearby* before you look to the horizon,' Old Helm advised.

perspective:2.en: From the ground, the island looked like a tangle of broken rock. But Bell climbed the signal mast and called down that the *perspective* up there was completely different — the rocks formed a perfect arrow pointing north. We had been reading the map from the wrong angle the whole morning. I climbed up too, and everything clicked into place.
perspective:2.cnHint: 从高处望去，小铃发现____截然不同——乱石其实构成了一个指向北方的箭头。
perspective:2.hook: North, the arrow pointed at an island none of our charts had ever named.
perspective:2.line: 'Change your *perspective* and the whole island tells a different story,' Bell called down.

requirement:2.en: The gate to the inner island bore an inscription in clear letters: one spoken word is the only *requirement* for entry. Silverfang tried three clever phrases and the gate stayed shut. I stepped forward, thought of the word we had found that morning, and said it quietly. The gate sighed open like it had been waiting all its life for exactly that.
requirement:2.cnHint: 内岛大门的铭文写明入场只有一个____：说出一个特定的词语。
requirement:2.hook: Inside, the air smelled of rain and something older than rain.
requirement:2.line: 'One spoken word is the only *requirement* — choose it well,' the inscription read.

signal:2.en: Bell stood at the bow and raised the blue lantern three times — the agreed sign that we had found the edge of the map. Far below, through the clouds, a second light *signalled* back: another troupe, on another vessel, had reached the same edge from the other side. Old Helm spread his arms wide and said the world was suddenly twice as large.
signal:2.cnHint: 小铃举起蓝色灯笼发出____，云层下方竟有另一支船队从对面抵达了地图的尽头。
signal:2.hook: The other vessel rose slowly through the clouds, and it was beautiful and strange.
signal:2.line: 'When you reach the edge, *signal* with the blue lantern so others can find you,' Bell said.

salary:2.en: Tucked inside a hollow post on Amber Isle, we found a rolled-up notice. It listed every job on the old sky-fleet — cook, rigger, cloud-reader — along with each worker's *salary* paid in star-coins. Old Helm read it twice, then smiled. 'Someone valued their crew well,' he said, and added the word to our map.
salary:2.cnHint: 在一根空心柱子里，我们发现了一份记录各岗位____的旧告示。
salary:2.hook: But one name on the list matched the carving above our own ship's door.
salary:2.line: 'A fair *salary* means a loyal crew,' Old Helm said softly.

shopping:2.en: The market island of Tinspar hung low in the clouds, its stalls bright with lanterns. Bell dragged me from booth to booth — *shopping* for a new compass needle, a spool of silver thread, and a jar of dried sky-berries. She found all three, then held up the jar with a grin. 'Navigation fuel,' she said.
shopping:2.cnHint: 小铃带我在云端集市上____，寻找指南针针头和其他补给。
shopping:2.hook: Then she spotted a vendor selling something that had no name — yet.
shopping:2.line: 'I love *shopping* on a new island,' Bell said, eyes wide.

tendency:2.en: Old Helm spread the star-charts across the deck. 'Every sky-current has a *tendency* to pull west near the solstice,' he told me, tracing a slow arc with his finger. 'Fight it and you drift. Follow it and you glide.' I wrote the word down, and the chart shimmered — a new island blinked into view.
tendency:2.cnHint: 老舵解释说，天空气流有向西偏移的____，顺势而行才能找到新岛屿。
tendency:2.hook: The island at the edge of the arc had no name on any chart we owned.
tendency:2.line: 'Clouds have a *tendency* to hide the best islands,' Old Helm said with a wink.

tough:2.en: The rope bridge to Cinder Ledge was *tough* work — planks missing, wind howling, the whole thing swaying like a slow pendulum. Silverfang crossed first, made it look easy, then called back: 'Fastest way earns the word!' I gritted my teeth and kept moving. The ledge on the other side held a glowing stone carved with our next destination.
tough:2.cnHint: 通往Cinder Ledge的绳桥摇摇晃晃，过桥是一件____的事，但终点藏着下一个目的地。
tough:2.hook: The glowing stone was still warm, as if someone had just set it down.
tough:2.line: 'The path is *tough*, but the view makes it worth it,' Silverfang called out.

tour:2.en: Bell suggested a slow *tour* of Spiral Atoll before we anchored — one full loop around its five connected islands to read the wind and mark the safe coves. We drifted in silence, watching fireflies trace the cliff edges. By the time we completed the circle, I had filled two whole pages with sketches and the map had grown a new ring.
tour:2.cnHint: 小铃建议先绕旋形环礁____一圈，观察风向，记录安全的停泊地。
tour:2.hook: On the final stretch, a second ship appeared, following our exact path.
tour:2.line: 'Every good *tour* teaches you something you did not plan to learn,' Bell said.

wake:2.en: We dropped anchor at dusk and held a quiet *wake* for the word 'horizon' — a fragment lost when our old chart tore in the storm. Old Helm set a single lantern on the water and we watched it float away, carrying the memory. Then he pulled out a new chart and said, 'Grief done. Now we find it again.'
wake:2.cnHint: 我们为一块在风暴中丢失的地图碎片举行了简短的____仪式，然后重新出发。
wake:2.hook: The floating lantern stopped — and slowly turned back toward us.
wake:2.line: 'A *wake* reminds us what mattered,' Old Helm said, voice gentle.

annual:2.en: Carved into the wall of the Tidestone Cave was a record of the troupe's *annual* journey — one line per year, each ending with how many words the team had collected. This year's line was still blank. Silverfang ran a finger along the empty space. 'Our turn to write something worth reading,' they said, and handed me the chisel.
annual:2.cnHint: 山洞石壁上刻着每年____的航行记录，今年那行还空着，等待我们来填写。
annual:2.hook: The chisel was heavier than it looked, and my hand would not stop shaking.
annual:2.line: 'The *annual* record never lies about how hard you worked,' Silverfang said.

charity:2.en: At the Gate of Echoes, a keeper stopped us. 'No coin, no passage,' she said. Old Helm reached into his pack and gave her our spare star-map — pure *charity*, nothing asked in return. She studied it for a long moment, then stepped aside and pressed a small glass word into his palm. It spelled out our next island's name in light.
charity:2.cnHint: 在回声之门，老舵出于____之心将备用地图送给守门人，换来了下一座岛屿的名字。
charity:2.hook: The glass word was still warm, and it hummed like it was alive.
charity:2.line: 'True *charity* asks for nothing back,' Old Helm said, smiling at the keeper.

behave:2.en: The Ink Isle librarian watched us with narrow eyes as we searched the shelves. Old Helm whispered that the word we needed was sealed inside a glass case. 'Touch nothing,' he murmured. I tried hard to *behave*, keeping my hands behind my back, even when a glowing page fluttered right past my nose.
behave:2.cnHint: 在墨水岛图书馆里，老舵提醒大家要注意____，因为我们要找的词藏在玻璃柜里。
behave:2.hook: The glass case creaked open on its own.
behave:2.line: 'You must *behave* in here, or the shelves will seal themselves forever.'

cent:2.en: At the sky market above Cloud-Nine Island, Bell found a coin half-buried in the wooden floor. She held it up: one copper *cent*, stamped with a tiny island on both sides. Old Helm squinted and smiled. 'That is no ordinary coin,' he said. 'That is the map fragment we have been searching for all week.'
cent:2.cnHint: 小铃在天空集市的地板上发现了一枚铜____，老舵认出它其实是一块地图碎片。
cent:2.hook: The coin began to spin on its own.
cent:2.line: 'One *cent* can open a door that gold cannot,' Old Helm said softly.

commercial:2.en: The island of Brass Quay was built for trade. Every sign, every flag, every painted wall carried some *commercial* message selling goods from across the sky. Bell said it felt like the whole island was shouting at once. But tucked behind a noisy market stall, silent and small, was the word we had come to find.
commercial:2.cnHint: 黄铜码头岛是个____气息浓厚的地方，但我们要找的词静静地藏在一个嘈杂摊位的背后。
commercial:2.hook: The word glowed faintly, waiting to be claimed.
commercial:2.line: 'This place is too *commercial*,' Bell said, 'but the word hides where no one is selling anything.'

death:2.en: On the Isle of Still Waters, an old stone tablet stood alone in a quiet garden. It marked the spot where a great navigator had rested his final journey. Bell read the carved words aloud. The tablet spoke of *death* not as an ending but as a doorway, and below the last line, a fresh word shimmered into view, ready for us to take.
